Huangbo was seven chi tall, with a round jewel on his forehead. By nature he understood Chan. In former times the master traveled

text_zh: 黃檗身長七尺。額有圓珠。天性會禪。師昔遊 天台。路逢一僧。與之談笑。如故相識。熟視之 目光射人。頗有異相。乃偕行。屬溪水暴漲。乃 植杖捐笠而止。其僧率師同渡。師曰。請渡。彼 即褰衣。躡波如履平地。回顧云渡來渡來。師 咄云。這自了漢。吾早知揑怪。當斫汝脛。其僧 歎曰。真大乘法器。言訖不見。初到百丈。丈問 云。巍巍堂堂。從什麼處來。檗云。巍巍堂堂從 嶺中來。丈云。來為何事。檗云。不為別事。百 丈深器之。次日辭百丈。丈云。什麼處去。檗 云。江西禮拜馬大師去。丈云。馬大師已遷化 去也。儞道黃檗恁麼問。是知來問。是不知來 問。却云。某甲特地去禮拜。福緣淺薄。不及一 見。未審平日有何言句。願聞舉示。丈遂舉再 參馬祖因緣。祖見我來。便竪起拂子。我問 云。即此用。離此用。祖遂掛拂子於禪床角良 久。祖却問我。汝已後鼓兩片皮。如何為人。我 取拂子竪起。祖云。即此用。離此用。我將拂 子。掛禪床角。祖振威一喝。我當時直得三日 耳聾。黃檗不覺悚然吐舌。丈云。子已後莫承 嗣馬大師麼。檗云。不然。今日因師舉。得見馬 大師大機大用。若承嗣馬師。他日已後喪我 兒孫。丈云。如是如是。見與師齊。減師半德。 智過於師。方堪傳授。子今見處宛有超師之 作。諸人且道。黃檗恁麼問。是知而故問耶。是 不知而問耶。須是親見他家父子行履處始 得。黃檗一日又問百丈。從上宗乘。如何指示。 百丈良久。檗云。不可教後人斷絕去。百丈云。 將謂汝是箇人。遂乃起入方丈。檗與裴相國 為方外友。裴鎮宛陵請師至郡。以所解一編。 示師。師接置於座。略不披閱。良久乃云。會 麼。裴云。不會。檗云。若便恁麼會得。猶較些 子。若也形於紙墨。何處更有吾宗。裴乃以頌 贊云。自從大士傳心印。額有圓珠七尺身。掛 錫十年棲蜀水。浮盃今日渡漳濱。八千龍象 隨高步。萬里香花結勝因。擬欲事師為弟子。 不知將法付何人。師亦無喜色云。心如大海 無邊際。口吐紅蓮養病身。自有一雙無事手。 不曾祇揖等閑人。檗住後。機鋒峭峻。臨濟在 會下。睦州為首座。問云。上座在此多時。何不 去問話。濟云。教某甲問什麼話即得。座云。何 不去問如何是佛法的的大意。濟便去問。三 度被打出。濟辭座曰。蒙首座令三番去問。被 打出。恐因緣不在這裏。暫且下山。座云。子若 去須辭和尚去方可。首座預去白檗云。問話 上座。甚不可得。和尚何不穿鑿教成一株樹 去。與後人為陰涼。檗云。吾已知。濟來辭。檗 云。汝不得向別處去。直向高安灘頭。見大愚 去。濟到大愚。遂舉前話。不知某甲過在什麼 處。愚云。檗與麼老婆心切。為儞徹困。更說什 麼有過無過。濟忽然大悟云。黃檗佛法無多 子。大愚搊住云。儞適來又道有過。而今却 道佛法無多子。濟於大愚脇下。𡎺三拳。愚拓 開云。汝師黃檗非干我事。一日檗示眾云。牛 頭融大師。橫說竪說。猶未知向上關捩子在。 是時石頭馬祖下。禪和子浩浩地。說禪說道。 他何故却與麼道。所以示眾云。汝等諸人盡 是噇酒糟漢。恁麼行脚。取笑於人。但見八百 一千人處便去。不可只圖熱鬧也。可中總似 汝如此容易。何處更有今日事也。唐時愛罵 人。作噇酒糟漢。人多喚作黃檗罵人。具眼者 自見他落處。大意垂一鉤。釣人問。眾中有 不惜身命底禪和。便解恁麼出眾問他道。只 如諸方匡徒領眾。又作麼生。也好一拶。這老 漢果然分疎不下。便却漏逗云。不道無禪。只 是無師。且道意在什麼處。他從上宗旨。有時 擒。有時縱。有時殺。有時活。有時放。有時收。 敢問諸人。作麼生是禪中師。山僧恁麼道。已 是和頭沒却了也。諸人鼻孔在什麼處。良久 云。穿却了也。
text_en: to Tiantai. On the road he met a monk and talked and laughed with him as if they were old acquaintances. Looking closely at him, his gaze shot into people; he had a rather unusual appearance. So they went along together. When the stream suddenly flooded, he planted his staff, tossed aside his hat, and stopped. That monk urged the master to cross with him. The master said, Please, cross. He then hitched up his robe and stepped on the waves as if walking on level ground. Turning back, he called, Cross over, cross over. The master shouted, You self-satisfied fellow! I knew long ago you were making trouble—I ought to have chopped your shins! That monk sighed, A true vessel of the Great Vehicle Dharma! When he finished speaking, he vanished. When Huangbo first arrived at Baizhang, Baizhang asked saying, Majestic and upright—where do you come from? Huangbo said, Majestic and upright, I come from within the mountains. Baizhang said, And why have you come? Huangbo said, For no other matter. Baizhang valued him deeply. The next day he took leave of Baizhang. Baizhang said, Where are you going? Huangbo said, To Jiangxi to pay respects to Master Ma. Baizhang said, Master Ma has already passed away. Tell me: when Huangbo asked like that, did he ask knowing, or did he ask not knowing? Then he said, I specifically went to pay respects, but my blessings and conditions were shallow—I did not make it in time for even one meeting. What were his usual sayings? I wish to hear you raise and show them. Baizhang then brought up again the circumstances of his second interview with Mazu: The Patriarch saw me come and immediately held up a fly-whisk. I asked saying, Use it right here, or apart from this use? The Patriarch then hung the fly-whisk on the corner of the Chan bed for a long while. Then the Patriarch asked me, Later, when you beat the two pieces of hide, how will you teach people? I took the fly-whisk and held it up. The Patriarch said, Use it right here, or apart from this use? I took the fly- whisk and hung it on the corner of the Chan bed. The Patriarch shook the assembly with a single shout. At that time, for three days I was deaf. Huangbo, without realizing it, shuddered and stuck out his tongue. Baizhang said, Later, will you not succeed Master Ma? Huangbo said, No. Today, because you raised this, I got to see Master Ma’s great pivot and great function. If I were to succeed Master Ma, in later days I would lose my children and grandchildren. Baizhang said, So it is, so it is. If your seeing is equal to the master’s, you diminish him by half a virtue. Only when your wisdom surpasses the master are you fit to receive the transmission. Your present seeing truly has something that goes beyond the master. Now tell me, everyone: when Huangbo asked like that, did he ask knowing and therefore ask on purpose, or did he ask because he did not know? You must personally see the conduct and footsteps of that father and son to get it. One day Huangbo again asked Baizhang, In the lineage of the ancestors from the beginning, how is it pointed out? Baizhang was silent for a long while. Huangbo said, You must not let later people cut it off. Baizhang said, I thought you were someone. And then he rose and went into the abbot’s quarters. Huangbo and the Prime Minister Pei were friends outside the world. When Pei was governor of Wanling, he invited the master to the prefecture and presented a volume of his understanding. He showed it to the master. The master took it and set it on the seat, not even opening it. After a long while he said, Do you understand? Pei said, I do not. Huangbo said, If you understood it just like that, it would still be short by a bit. If it takes form in paper and ink, where is there room for our school? Pei then used a verse to praise him, saying, Since the Great Being transmitted the mind-seal, a round jewel on the forehead, a body seven chi tall. Carrying his staff, he dwelt by the waters of Shu for ten years; floating a cup, today he crossed to the banks of Zhang. Eight thousand dragons and elephants follow his lofty steps; for ten thousand li, incense and flowers form splendid causes. I would like to serve the master as a disciple, but I do not know to whom the Dharma will be entrusted. The master showed no joy and said, The mind is like the great sea, without boundary. The mouth spits red lotus to nourish the sick body. I have a pair of hands with nothing to do, and I have never merely bowed to ordinary people. After Huangbo took up residence, his edge was steep and severe. Linji was in the assembly; Muzhou was head seat. He asked, You have been here a long time—why don’t you go ask for a word? Linji said, What should you have me ask? The head seat said, Why not go ask, What is the true great meaning of the Buddha-Dharma? Linji then went to ask. Three times he was beaten and driven out. Linji said to the head seat, Thanks to you ordering me to ask three times, I was beaten and driven out. I fear my conditions are not here; I will go down the mountain for now. The head seat said, If you go, you must first take leave of the master. The head seat went ahead and reported to Huangbo, saying, That monk who goes to ask questions is quite something. Master, why not carve and drill him into a single tree to give later people shade? Huangbo said, I already know. Linji came to take leave. Huangbo said, You must not go elsewhere. Go straight to the Gao’an riverbank and see Dayu. Linji reached Dayu and brought up the earlier matter. I do not know where my fault lies. Dayu said, Huangbo has such an old-woman’s anxious heart—he has gone to the end of hardship for you. What more is there to say about fault or no fault? Linji suddenly had a great awakening and said, Huangbo’s Buddha-Dharma is not much. Dayu grabbed him and said, Just now you said there was fault, and now you say the Buddha-Dharma is not much—how is that? Linji struck three punches under Dayu’s ribs. Dayu pushed him away and said, Your teacher Huangbo is none of my business. One day Huangbo addressed the assembly, saying, Oxen Master Tou Rong, talking horizontally and talking vertically, still did not know where the pivotal turning point of the higher way lies. At that time, under Shitou and Mazu, the Zen fellows in great numbers talked of Zen and talked of the Way. Why did he speak like this? So he instructed the assembly, saying: All of you people are entirely dregs-eating drunks. Wandering about like this, you make yourselves a laughingstock. Whenever you see a place with eight hundred or a thousand people, you head right there. Do not just go looking for excitement. In all cases it is just like you taking it this easily—where else would there be what is happening today? In the Tang there was one who loved to scold people, calling them dregs-eating drunks. Many called him Huangbo the scolder. Those with eyes see for themselves where he lands. In the main he dangled a single hook, fishing for someone to ask. In the crowd there was a Zen fellow who did not begrudge his body and life; he knew to step out and ask him like this, saying: Just like the leaders who guide followers in the various quarters—how is it then? A fine squeeze indeed. This old fellow truly did not hold back in the least; he let it slip and said: It is not that there is no Zen; it is only that there are no teachers. Now tell me—where is his intent? His fundamental principle has, at times, capture; at times release; at times kill; at times enliven; at times let go; at times gather in. I dare ask you all: what counts as a teacher within Zen? This mountain monk speaking like this has already made a muddle of it. Where are your nostrils? After a long pause he said: They have been pierced through.
Bracing, solitary wind—he does not boast; seated upright across the seas, he settles still does not even know it exists. He too is a Yunju arhat.

text_zh: 凜凜孤風不自誇猶自不知有。也是雲居羅漢　端居寰海定 龍蛇也要別緇素。也要皂白分明大中天子曾輕觸說什麼大中天子任 大也須從地起。更高爭奈有天何三度親遭弄爪牙死蝦蟆多口作什麼。未為奇 特。猶是小機巧。若是大機大用現前。盡十方世界。乃至山河大地。盡在黃檗處乞命
text_en: dragons and snakes. One must distinguish monk and lay; one must have black and white clearly separated. The Tianzi of Dazhong once brushed against him lightly; What are you saying about the Son of Heaven of Dazhong bearing greatness? Even the great must rise from the ground. If you go higher, what can you do about there being heaven? three times he personally suffered the play of claws and fangs. What is a dead toad doing with so many mouths? It is not yet strange enough; it is still a small trick. If the great pivot and great function appear right before you, the entire ten-direction world, even mountains, rivers, and the great earth, would all go to Huangbo to beg for their lives.

text_zh: 雪竇此一頌。一似黃檗真贊相似。人却不得作 真贊會。他底句下。便有出身處。分明道。凜凜 孤風不自誇。黃檗恁麼示眾。且不是爭人負 我。自逞自誇。若會這箇消息。一任七縱八橫。 有時孤峯頂獨立。有時鬧市裏橫身。豈可僻 守一隅。愈捨愈不歇。愈尋愈不見。愈擔荷愈 沒溺。古人道。無翼飛天下。有名傳世間。盡情 捨却佛法道理。玄妙奇特。一時放下。却較些 子。自然觸處現成。雪竇道。端居寰海定龍蛇。 是龍是蛇。入門來便驗取。謂之定龍蛇眼擒 虎兕機。雪竇又道。定龍蛇兮眼何正。擒虎兕 兮機不全。又道。大中天子曾輕觸。三度親遭 弄爪牙。黃檗豈是如今惡脚手。從來如此。大 中天子者。續咸通傳中載。唐憲宗有二子。一 曰穆宗。一曰宣宗。宣宗乃大中也。年十三。少 而敏黠。常愛跏趺坐。穆宗在位時。因早朝罷。 大中乃戲登龍床。作揖群臣勢。大臣見而謂 之心風。乃奏穆宗。穆宗見而撫歎曰。我弟乃 吾宗英胄也。穆宗於長慶四年。晏駕。有三子。 曰敬宗文宗武宗。敬宗繼父位。二年內臣謀 易之。文宗繼位。一十四年。武宗即位。常喚大 中作癡奴。一日武宗。恨大中昔日戲登父位。 遂打殺致後苑中。以不潔灌。而復甦。遂潛遁 在香嚴閑和尚會下。後剃度為沙彌。未受具 戒。後與志閑遊方到廬山。因志閑題瀑布詩 云。穿雲透石不辭勞。地遠方知出處高。閑吟 此兩句佇思久之。欲釣他語脈看如何。大中 續云。溪㵎豈能留得住。終歸大海作波濤。閑 方知不是尋常人。乃默而識之。後到鹽官會 中。請大中作書記。黃檗在彼作首座。檗一日 禮佛次。大中見而問曰。不著佛求。不著法求。 不著眾求。禮拜當何所求。檗云。不著佛求。不 著法求。不著眾求。常禮如是。大中云。用禮何 為。檗便掌。大中云。太麁生。檗云。這裏什麼 所在。說麁說細。檗又掌。大中後繼國位。賜黃 檗為麁行沙門。裴相國在朝。後奏賜斷際禪 師。雪竇知他血脈出處。便用得巧。如今還有 弄爪牙底麼。便打。
text_en: a literal portrait. Under his lines there is a way out. He plainly says: Bracing, solitary wind does not boast. When Huangbo instructed the assembly like this, it was not to contend that others owed him anything, nor to show off and brag. If you understand this news, then let it be seven releases and eight sideways moves as you please. Sometimes standing alone on the peak of a solitary mountain; sometimes lying crosswise in the noisy marketplace. How could one narrowly guard one corner? The more you discard, the less you stop; the more you seek, the less you find; the more you shoulder and carry, the more you drown. The ancients said: wingless, it flies through the world; having a name, it is passed on in the world. Completely cast off Buddha-Dharma doctrines, the abstruse, the marvelous, the strange—set it all down at once, and it is better by a bit then. Naturally, wherever you touch it, it is already there. Xuedou said: seated upright across the seas, he settles dragons and snakes. Dragon or snake—when it enters the gate, test it at once. This is called the eyes that settle dragons and snakes, and the knack that seizes tigers and rhinoceroses. Xuedou also said: settling dragons and snakes—how straight those eyes; seizing tigers and rhinoceroses— the mechanism is not complete. He also said: the Tianzi of Dazhong once brushed against him lightly; three times he personally suffered the play of claws and fangs. Huangbo was no crude hack like people today—he has always been like this. As for the Tianzi of Dazhong, the Continuation of the Xiantong Record relates that Tang Xianzong had two sons. One was called Muzong; one was called Xuanzong. Xuanzong was Dazhong. At thirteen years old, as a youth he was quick and clever, and often loved to sit cross-legged. When Muzong was on the throne, after the morning court had ended, Dazhong playfully climbed onto the dragon throne and made gestures of greeting to the assembled ministers. The great ministers saw it and called it a madness of the heart, and reported it to Muzong. Muzong saw it and sighed with admiration, saying: My younger brother is the outstanding scion of our line. In the fourth year of Changqing, Muzong passed away. He had three sons, called Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong. Jingzong succeeded his father; within two years palace eunuchs plotted to replace him. Wenzong succeeded and reigned fourteen years. Wuzong then ascended the throne and often called Dazhong a foolish slave. One day Wuzong resented that Dazhong had once playfully climbed his father’s throne, and had him beaten to death and thrown into the rear garden. They poured filth over him, and he revived again. He then slipped away in secret and was at the assembly of the master Xiangyan Xian. Later he shaved his head and became a novice, not yet having received full precepts. Later, traveling with Zhixian, he arrived at Mount Lu. Because Zhixian inscribed a waterfall poem that said: Piercing clouds and passing through stone, it does not refuse the toil; only at a far distance do you know its source is high. Xian recited these two lines and pondered them for a long time, wanting to fish out his thread of speech and see how it went. Dazhong continued: How could the stream be kept and held? In the end it returns to the great sea to become waves. Xian then knew he was no ordinary person, and silently recognized him. Later, arriving at Yanguan’s assembly, they invited Dazhong to serve as secretary. Huangbo was there as head seat. One day Huangbo was bowing to the Buddha, and Dazhong saw him and asked: Not clinging to Buddha to seek, not clinging to Dharma to seek, not clinging to the assembly to seek—when you bow, what are you seeking? Huangbo said: Not clinging to Buddha to seek, not clinging to Dharma to seek, not clinging to the assembly to seek—always bow just like this. Dazhong said: What use is bowing for? Huangbo then slapped him. Dazhong said: Too rough! Huangbo said: What sort of place is this, to talk of rough or fine? Huangbo slapped him again. Later Dazhong succeeded to the throne and bestowed on Huang- bo the title Rough-Practice Monk. When Minister Pei was at court, he later memorialized that he be granted the Chan title Duanji, Master Duanji. Xuedou knew the source of his lineage and used it skillfully. Nowadays is there still anyone who will play with claws and fangs? Then strike.

text_zh: 垂示云。殺人刀活人劍。乃上古之風規。亦今 時之樞要。若論殺也。不傷一毫。若論活也。喪 身失命。所以道。向上一路。千聖不傳。學者勞 形。如猿捉影。且道。既是不傳。為什麼。却有 許多葛藤公案。具眼者。試說看。
text_en: the pivot of today. If we speak of killing, it does not harm a hair; if we speak of giving life, it loses body and life. Therefore it is said: the single road upward is not transmitted by a thousand sages. Students toil their bodies like monkeys grabbing at shadows. Now tell me—since it is not transmitted, why then are there so many vine-entangled public cases? Those with eyes, try speaking.
Case twelve: A monk asked Dongshan, What is Buddha? Dongshan said: Three An iron caltrop—patch-robed monks under heaven cannot jump out of it.

text_zh: 【一二】舉僧問洞山。如何是佛鐵蒺藜。天下衲僧跳不出山云。麻 三斤灼然。破草鞋。指槐樹罵柳樹。為秤鎚。
text_en: pounds of hemp. Blazing clear. A broken straw sandal. Point at the locust tree and curse the willow tree—taken as a weight on the scale.
How many people misunderstand this public case—truly hard to chew, with nowhere for you to get your teeth into it.

text_zh: 這箇公案。多少人錯會。直是難咬嚼。無爾下 口處。何故淡而無味。古人有多少答佛話。或 云。殿裏底。或云。三十二相。或云。杖林山下 竹筋鞭。及至洞山。却道麻三斤。不妨截斷古 人舌頭。人多作話會道。洞山是時在庫下。秤 麻。有僧問。所以如此答。有底道。洞山問東答 西。有底道。爾是佛。更去問佛。所以洞山遶 路答之。死漢更有一般道。只這麻三斤便是 佛。且得沒交涉。爾若恁麼去洞山句下尋 討。參到彌勒佛下生。也未夢見在。何故言語 只是載道之器。殊不知古人意。只管去句中 求。有什麼巴鼻。不見古人道。道本無言。因言 顯道。見道即忘言。若到這裏。還我第一機來 始得。只這麻三斤。一似長安大路一條相似。 舉足下足。無有不是。這箇話。與雲門餬餅話。 是一般。不妨難會。五祖先師頌云。賤賣擔板 漢。貼秤麻三斤。千百年滯貨。無處著渾身。爾 但打疊得情塵意想。計較得失是非。一時淨 盡自然會去。
text_en: Why is it bland and tasteless? The ancients gave many answers about Buddha—some said: the one in the hall; some said: the thirty-two marks; some said: the bamboo-staff whip from beneath Zhanglei Mountain— and so on. But when it comes to Dongshan, he says: three pounds of hemp. It is enough to cut off the tongues of the ancients. Many people take it as mere talk and say: at that time Dongshan was in the storeroom, weighing hemp, and a monk asked, so he answered like this. Some say: Dongshan was asked east and answered west. Some say: you are Buddha—why ask Buddha? So Dongshan answered by a roundabout route. Dead men even have another kind of saying: this very three pounds of hemp is Buddha. That at least is irrelevant. If you go hunting under Dongshan’s words like this, even if you practice until Maitreya Buddha descends, you still will not have dreamed of it. Why? Words are only vessels that carry the Way. People do not know the ancients’ intent and only keep seeking in the phrase itself—what real nose or face is that? Have you not seen the ancients say: the Way is originally without words; because of words the Way is revealed. When you see the Way, you forget the words. If you reach here, then return my first move to me and only then is it right. This three pounds of hemp is like the single main road in Chang’an: lifting a foot, setting a foot down—none of it is not it. This saying is the same kind as Yunmen’s rice-cake saying; it is not out of place that it is hard to understand. The former master Wuzu composed a verse, saying: He cheap-sells the carrying-board fellow; he posts a price, three pounds of hemp. For a thousand hundred years the goods have sat unsold; there is nowhere to put your whole body. You just need to pack up the dust of feelings and the thoughts of mind, and the calculating of gain and loss, right and wrong, and in one moment make it all clean—then naturally you will understand.

The golden crow is swift, the jade rabbit is quick. The left eye weighs half a jin. Even a swift hawk cannot catch up. Throwing oneself sideways within flames. The right eye weighs eight liang. Making a nest in Chang’e’s palace.

text_zh: 雪竇見得透。所以劈頭便道。金烏急玉兔速。 與洞山答麻三斤。更無兩般。日出月沒。日日 如是。人多情解。只管道。金烏是左眼。玉兔是 右眼。纔問著便瞠眼云。在這裏有什麼交涉。 若恁麼會。達磨一宗掃地而盡。所以道。垂鉤 四海只釣獰龍。格外玄機。為尋知已。雪竇 是出陰界底人。豈作這般見解。雪竇輕輕去 敲關擊節處。略露些子教爾見。便下箇注脚 道。善應何曾有輕觸。洞山不輕酬這僧。如鐘 在扣。如谷受響。大小隨應。不敢輕觸。雪竇一 時。突出心肝五臟。呈似爾諸人了也。雪竇有 靜而善應頌云。覿面相呈。不在多端。龍蛇易 辨。衲子難瞞。金鎚影動。寶劍光寒。直下來 也。急著眼看。洞山初參雲門。門問。近離甚 處。山云。渣渡。門云。夏在甚麼處。山云。湖南 報慈。門云。幾時離彼中。山云。八月二十五。 門云。放爾三頓棒。參堂去。師晚間入室。親近 問云。某甲過在什麼處。門云。飯袋子。江西湖 南便恁麼去。洞山於言下。豁然大悟。遂云。某 甲他日向無人煙處。卓箇庵子。不蓄一粒米。 不種一莖菜。常接待往來十方大善知識。盡 與伊抽却釘。技却楔。拈却膱脂帽子。脫却鶻 臭布衫。各令灑灑落落地。作箇無事人去。門 云。身如椰子大。開得許大口。洞山便辭去。他 當時悟處。直下穎脫。豈同小見後來出世應 機麻三斤語。諸方只作答佛話會如何是佛。 杖林山下竹筋鞭。丙丁童子來求火。只管於 佛上作道理。雪竇云。若恁麼作展事與投機 會。正似跛鼈盲龜入空谷。何年日月尋得出 路去。花簇簇錦簇簇。此是僧問智門和尚。洞 山道麻三斤意旨如何。智門云。花簇簇錦簇 簇。會麼。僧云。不會。智門云。南地竹兮北地 木。僧回舉似洞山。山云。我不為汝說。我為大 眾說。遂上堂云。言無展事。語不投機。承言者 喪。滯句者迷。雪竇破人情見。故意引作一 串頌出。後人却轉生情見道。麻是孝服。竹是 孝杖。所以道。南地竹兮北地木。花簇簇錦簇 簇。是棺材頭邊。畫底花草。還識羞麼。殊不 知。南地竹兮北地木。與麻三斤。只是阿爺與 阿爹相似。古人答一轉語。決是意不恁麼。正 似雪竇道金烏急玉兔速。自是一般寬曠。只 是金鍮難辨。魚魯參差。雪竇老婆心切。要破 爾疑情。更引箇死漢。因思長慶陸大夫。解道 合笑不合哭。若論他頌。只頭上三句。一時頌 了。我且問爾。都盧只是箇麻三斤。雪竇却有 許多葛藤。只是慈悲忒殺。所以如此。陸亘大 夫。作宣州觀察使。參南泉。泉遷化。亘聞喪入 寺下祭。却呵呵大笑。院主云。先師與大夫。有 師資之義。何不哭。大夫云。道得即哭。院主無 語。亘大哭云。蒼天蒼天。先師去世遠矣。後來 長慶聞云。大夫合笑不合哭。雪竇借此意大 綱道。爾若作這般情解。正好笑莫哭。是即是。 末後有一箇字。不妨聱訛。更道咦。雪竇還洗 得脫麼。
text_en: It is no different from Dongshan’s answer, three pounds of hemp. Sunrise, moonset—day after day it is thus. People mostly interpret it emotionally and keep saying: the golden crow is the left eye, the jade rabbit is the right eye. As soon as they are questioned, they stare and say: what does that have to do with anything here? If you understand it like this, Bodhidharma’s lineage is swept away entirely. Therefore it is said: dangling the hook across the four seas, it only fishes for fierce dragons. The extraordinary mysterious mechanism is for seeking a true confidant. Xuedou If one is a person who has stepped beyond the shadowy realms, how could one form views like this? Xuedou lightly taps the gate and strikes the beat, revealing just a little for you to see. Then he adds a footnote saying: Good responding has never been a light touch. Dongshan did not lightly answer this monk, like a bell being struck; like a valley receiving an echo. Great or small, it responds accordingly, not daring to touch lightly. Xuedou, at once, pulls out heart, liver, and the five viscera and presents it to you people. Xuedou has a verse on stillness and good responding: Presented face to face, not in many complications. Dragons and snakes are easy to tell apart; a patched-robed monk is hard to deceive. The golden hammer’s shadow moves; the jeweled sword’s gleam is cold. Come straight down right here—quick, open your eyes and look. When Dongshan first visited Yunmen, Yunmen asked, Recently you left what place? Dongshan said, Zha Crossing. Yunmen asked, Where did you spend the summer? Dongshan said, Baozi in Hunan, Baoci. Yunmen asked, When did you leave there? Dongshan said, The twenty-fifth day of the eighth month. Yunmen said, I’ll let you off with three rounds of blows—go to the hall. That evening the master entered the room; in close attendance, he asked, Where exactly was my fault? Yunmen said, You rice-bag! From Jiangxi to Hu- nan and you just go like that. At these words, Dongshan suddenly had a great awakening. Then he said, Someday I will, in a place where there are no people, set up a small hut. I will not store a single grain of rice. I will not plant a single stalk of vegetables. I will always receive the great good friends of the ten directions who come and go, and I will pull out their nails, knock out their wedges, snatch off their grease-smeared caps, and strip off their rancid cloth shirts, letting each one be clean and unencumbered, and go off as a person with nothing to do. Yunmen said, With a body as big as a coconut, you open such a huge mouth! Dongshan then took his leave. At that time his place of awakening was straight and outstanding—how could it be the same as a shallow view, later on, when he appeared in the world and responded to circumstances with the saying, Three pounds of hemp. Teachers everywhere only take it as an answer about Buddha, as in What is Buddha? A bamboo-whip under Zhanglin Mountain; the lads of Fire come seeking fire. They only go on making reasoning around Buddha. Xuedou said, If you handle it like this, taking it as a display of skill and a meeting with the situation, it’s exactly like a lame turtle and a blind tortoise entering an empty valley—what year and month will they ever find a way out? Flower-clusters, brocade-clusters. This was when a monk asked Master Zhimen: What is the meaning of Dong- shan’s saying, Three pounds of hemp? Zhimen said, Flower-clusters, brocade-clus- ters. Understand? The monk said, I don’t. Zhimen said, Bamboo in the south, timber in the north. The monk went back and told Dongshan. Dongshan said, I won’t explain it for you; I’ll explain it for the great assembly. So he ascended the hall and said: Words do not display the matter; phrases do not fit the situation. Those who take up words are lost; those who get stuck in phrases are deluded. Xuedou breaks people’s emotional views, intentionally drawing out a string of verses. Later people instead turn around and give rise to emotional views, saying hemp is mourning clothes, bamboo is the mourning staff. Therefore they say, Bamboo in the south, timber in the north; flower-clusters, brocade-clus- ters—these are painted flowers and grasses by the head of the coffin. Do you still know shame? Yet they do not know: Bamboo in the south, timber in the north, and three pounds of hemp are just like dad and father—similar. When the ancients answered with a turning word, their meaning certainly was not like that. It is just like Xuedou saying, The golden crow is urgent, the jade rabbit swift—by nature it is broadly open. It’s only that brass and gold are hard to tell apart; “fish” and “Lu” get mixed up. Xuedou, with an old-woman’s anxious heart, wants to smash your knot of doubt, and so he brings up another dead fellow. He recalls Minister Lu of Changqing, who could say one should laugh, not cry. If we speak of his verse, it’s just the first three lines—at once it is versified and done. Let me ask you: all in all it’s only three pounds of hemp, yet Xuedou has so many entangling vines—he is simply far too compassionate, and so it is like this. Official Lu Geng served as the Surveillance Commissioner of Xuanzhou and visited Nanquan. When Nanquan passed away, Lu heard the news and went into the monastery to offer rites, but he laughed loudly. The rector said, The late master and you, sir, had the bond of teacher and student—why don’t you cry? The official said, If you can speak it, I’ll cry. The rector had no reply. Lu then wailed loudly, Blue heaven, blue heaven—my late master has been gone for so long! Later Changqing heard and said, The official should laugh, not cry. Xuedou borrows this meaning and in broad outline says: if you interpret it with this kind of sentiment, then it’s exactly right to laugh and not cry. “It is” is “it is.” At the very end there is one word, not without its harshness—he even adds, Eh? Can Xuedou still wash himself clean of it?

text_zh: 這箇公案。人多錯會道。此是外道宗。有什麼 交涉。第十五祖。提婆尊者。亦是外道中一數。 因見第十四祖。龍樹尊者。以針投鉢。龍樹深 器之。傳佛心宗。繼為第十五祖。楞伽經云。佛 語心為宗。無門為法門。馬祖云。凡有言句。是 提婆宗。只以此箇為主。諸人盡是衲僧門下 客。還曾體究得提婆宗麼。若體究得。西天九 十六種外道。被汝一時降伏。若體究不得。未 免著返披袈裟去在。且道是作麼生。若道言 句是。也沒交涉。若道言句不是。也沒交涉。且 道馬大師意在什麼處。後來雲門道。馬大師 好言語。只是無人問。有僧便問。如何是提婆 宗。門云。九十六種。汝是最下一種。昔有僧辭 大隋。隋云。什麼處去。僧云。禮拜普賢去。大 隋竪起拂子云。文殊普賢盡在這裏。僧畫一 圓相以手托呈師。又拋向背後。隋云。侍者將 一貼茶來。與這僧去。雲門別云。西天斬頭截 臂。這裏自領出去。又云。赤旛在我手裏。西天 論議勝者手執赤旛。負墮者返披袈裟。從偏 門出入。西天欲論議。須得奉王勅。於大寺中。 聲鐘擊鼓。然後論議。於是外道於僧寺中。封 禁鐘鼓。為之沙汰。時迦那提婆尊者。知佛法 有難。遂運神通。登樓撞鐘。欲擯外道。外道遂 問。樓上聲鍾者誰。提婆云。天。外道云。天是 誰。婆云。我。外道云。我是誰。婆云。我是爾。外 道云。爾是誰。婆云。爾是狗。外道云。狗是誰。 婆云。狗是爾。如是七返。外道自知負墮。伏義 遂自開門。提婆於是從樓上持赤旛下來。外 道云。汝何不後。婆云。汝何不前。外道云。汝 是賤人。婆云。汝是良人。如是展轉酬問。提婆 折以無礙之辯。由是歸伏。時提婆尊者。手持 赤旛。義墮者旛下立。外道皆斬首謝過。時提 婆止之。但化令削髮入道。於是提婆宗大興。 雪竇後用此事而頌之。巴陵眾中謂之鑒多 口。常縫坐具行脚。深得他雲門脚跟下大事。 所以奇特。後出世法嗣雲門。先住岳州巴陵。 更不作法嗣書。只將三轉語上雲門。如何是 道。明眼人落井。如何是吹毛劍。珊瑚枝枝撐 著月。如何是提婆宗。銀椀裏盛雪。雲門云。 他日老僧忌辰只舉此三轉語。報恩足矣。自 後果不作忌辰齋。依雲門之囑。只舉此三轉 語。然諸方答此話。多就事上答。唯有巴陵恁 麼道。極是孤峻。不妨難會。亦不露些子鋒鋩。 八面受敵。著著有出身之路。有陷虎之機。脫 人情見。若論一色邊事。到這裏須是自家透 脫了。却須是遇人始得。所以道。道吾舞笏同 人會。石鞏彎弓作者諳。此理若無師印授。擬 將何法語玄談。雪竇隨後拈提為人。所以頌 出。
text_en: does it have to do with us? The fifteenth patriarch, Venerable Deva, was also once counted among the outsiders. Because he met the fourteenth patriarch, Venerable Nagarjuna, and threw a needle into a bowl—Nagarjuna deeply recognized his capacity, transmitted the Buddha-mind tradition, and he became the fifteenth patriarch. The Lankavatara Sutra says: The Buddha takes mind as the principle; no-gate is the Dharma gate. Mazu said, Whatever has words and phrases is Deva’s tradition. Take only this as the main point. You all are guests under the patched-robed monks’ gate—have you ever investigated Deva’s tradition? If you have investigated it, the ninety-six kinds of outside teachings in the West are all subdued by you at once. If you have not investigated it, you won’t avoid having to put on a robe backwards and go off. But tell me—how is it? If you say words and phrases are it, that has nothing to do with it. If you say words and phrases are not it, that also has nothing to do with it. So tell me: where was Master Ma’s meaning? Later Yunmen said, Master Ma had fine words—only no one asked. A monk then asked, What is Deva’s tradition? Yunmen said, Of the ninety-six kinds, you are the very lowest kind. Long ago a monk took leave of Great Sui. Sui said, Where are you going? The monk said, I’m going to pay respects to Samantabhadra. Great Sui raised his whisk and said, Manjushri and Samantabhadra are all right here. The monk drew a circle-sign and held it up to present to the master, then tossed it behind his back. Sui said, Attendant, bring a packet of tea and send this monk off. Yunmen also said, In the West they chop heads and cut arms; here you take yourself out. He also said, The red banner is in my hands. In the West, in debate the winner holds the red banner; the defeated puts on the robe backwards and enters and leaves by a side gate. In the West, to debate one must receive a royal edict, in a great monastery. They ring bells and beat drums, and then they debate. Thus the outsiders, in the monks’ monastery, sealed off and forbade bells and drums, suppressing them. At that time Venerable Kanadeva knew the Buddha Dharma was in trouble, so he used spiritual powers, climbed the tower and struck the bell, wishing to expel the outsiders. The outsiders then asked, Who is the one sounding the bell up there? Deva said, Heaven. The outsiders said, Who is Heaven? Deva said, Me. The outsiders said, Who am I? Deva said, I am you. The out- siders said, Who are you? Deva said, You are a dog. The outsiders said, Who is the dog? Deva said, The dog is you. Like this for seven exchanges, the outsiders themselves knew they were defeated, bowed in submission, and then opened the gate themselves. Deva then came down from the tower holding the red banner. The out- siders said, Why don’t you go behind? Deva said, Why don’t you go ahead? The outsiders said, You are a low person. Deva said, You are a fine person. In this way they exchanged questions and answers back and forth. Deva refuted them with unobstructed eloquence, and thus they submitted. At that time Venerable Deva held the red banner; those who fell in meaning stood beneath the banner. The outsiders all offered their heads to apologize. Then De- va stopped them, and instead transformed them, having them shave their heads and enter the Way. Thus Deva’s tradition greatly flourished. Later Xuedou used this incident and versified it. Among Baling’s community he was called “Mirror- Mouth.” He often sewed sitting-cloths and traveled on foot, deeply grasping Yunmen’s great matter beneath his heel. That is why it is extraordinary. Later, when he appeared in the world, he was Dharma heir to Yunmen. First he resided at Baling in Yuezhou. He did not even make a Dharma-heir letter; he only took three turning phrases up to Yunmen: What is the Way? A clear-eyed person falls into a well. What is the hair-blowing sword? Coral branches, branch after branch, prop up the moon. What is Deva’s tradition? Snow contained in a silver bowl. Yunmen said, On the day of my memorial, just raise these three turning phrases—repaying kindness is enough. From then on he indeed did not hold memorial feasts; following Yunmen’s instruction, he only raised these three turning phrases. Yet teachers everywhere, answering these words, mostly answer on the level of things. Only Baling spoke like this—utterly solitary and steep; it is not amiss that it is hard to understand, and it does not reveal the slightest edge or point. Attacked from eight sides, each move has a way out; each move has a chance to trap a tiger. It strips away human emotional views. If we speak of matters on the side of the one color, when you get here it must be personally penetrated It is shed; only on meeting the right person can it be so. Thus it is said: Daowu danced his baton, meeting with his peers; Shigong bent his bow, and those who act know it well. If this principle lacks a master’s seal of transmission, what Dharma-words could you use for abstruse talk? Xuedou then lifted it up to guide people, and so he composed a verse and brought it forth.

text_en: of a separate transmission outside the scriptures: solely transmitting the mind-seal, directly pointing to the human mind, seeing nature and becoming Buddha. Shakyamuni, the old fellow, lived in the world for forty-nine years, held three hundred sixty assemblies, and opened talks on sudden and gradual, provisional and real—this is called the teaching of an entire lifetime. This monk picked it up and asked: what is the teaching of an entire lifetime? Why didn’t Yunmen explain it to him in detail, but instead said to him: Speaking in response to the One? In Yunmen’s usual single sentence, there must be three sentences: the sentence that encloses heaven and earth; the sentence that follows the waves and chases the currents; the sentence that cuts off all streams. Letting go and drawing in, it is naturally striking—like cutting nails and slicing iron—so that people’s interpretive understanding cannot reckon it. The entire Tripitaka needs only three characters. In all directions, on all sides, there is no place for your picking and drilling. Many people misunderstand it, saying it is a matter of responding to the One as a timely expedient, and so it is spoken thus. Others say: the myriad phenomena and all appearances are all stamped by the One Dharma, and this is called speaking in response to the One. Still others say: it is simply speaking of that One Dharma; what does it have to do with anything? Not only do they not understand, they fall into hell like an arrow—utterly unaware that the ancients’ intent was not like this. Hence it is said: grinding bones to powder and shattering the body is not enough to repay it; one phrase, clearly understood, surpasses a hundred billion. It is indeed striking. What is the teaching of an entire lifetime? You need only say: Speaking in response to the One. If you can realize it on the spot, you can go home and sit securely. If you cannot realize it, then bow and listen for your assignment.

text_en: and perilous, outshining the past and cutting off the future—like a ten-thousand-foot cliff, and also like a million-soldier battle array, with no place for you to stand. It is just too solitary and perilous. The ancients said: if you want intimacy, do not take a question to ask. The question is in the answer; the answer is at the tip of the question. It is utterly solitary and steep. Tell me, where is this solitary steepness? People in the world cannot do anything about it. This monk too was a capable one, and so he asked like this. Yunmen answered like that; it is very much like a holeless iron hammer driving the wedge hard. Xuedou used literary phrasing: he used it quite skillfully. Beneath the Jambu tree he laughs, ha ha. In the Sutra on the Arising of the World it says there must be a vaidurya tree on the southern side of Mount Sumeru, casting its reflection so that all within Jambudvipa appears blue. This continent is named after the great tree, and is called Jambudvipa. The tree extends seven thousand yojanas in length and breadth. Below it is a mass of Jambu gold, twenty yojanas high; because the gold is produced from beneath the tree, it is called the Jambu tree. Thus Xuedou speaks of himself: he is beneath the Jambu tree laughing, ha ha. Tell me, what is he laughing at? He laughs that last night the black dragon had its horn wrenched and snapped. One can only gaze and look up; praising Yunmen has its share. Yunmen said: speaking in response to the One is like what? It is like wrenching and snapping one horn of a black dragon. If there were not such a matter here, how could one speak like this? Xuedou, in one go, finished the verse; at the end he says: distinct, distinct. The old man of Shaoyang got a single peg. Why not say he got it all? Why does he only get a single peg? Tell me, where is that single peg? It directly pierces through the second person.
15 The instruction says: the knife that kills and the sword that gives life are the style and standard of antiquity, and are now

text_zh: 垂示云。殺人刀活人劍。乃上古之風規。是今 時之樞要。且道。如今那箇是。殺人刀活人劍。 試舉看。
text_en: the pivotal key. Tell me, which one today is the knife that kills and the sword that gives life? Try bringing it up and see.

text_zh: 【一五】舉僧問雲門。不是目前機。亦非目前事 時如何𨁝跳作什麼。倒退三千里門云。倒一說平出。款出囚人口。也不得 放過。荒草裏橫身。
text_en: what then? Yunmen said: Inverting the One, speaking. What are you jumping for? Retreat three thousand li. Brought out flatly. Drawing out a convict’s mouth by confession—still you must not let it pass. Lying crosswise in wild grass.
This monk was indeed a capable one, able to ask like this. On the surface it is called requesting

text_zh: 這僧不妨是箇作家。解恁麼問。頭邊謂之請 益。此是呈解問。亦謂之藏鋒問。若不是雲門。 也不奈他何。雲門有這般手脚。他既將問來。 不得已而應之。何故作家宗師。如明鏡臨臺。 胡來胡現漢來漢現。古人道。欲得親切。莫將 問來問。何故。問在答處。答在問處。從上諸 聖。何曾有一法與人。那裏有禪道與爾來。爾 若不造地獄業。自然不招地獄果。爾若不造 天堂因。自然不受天堂果。一切業緣。皆是自 作自受。古人分明向爾道。若論此事。不在 言句上。若在言句上。三乘十二分教。豈是無 言句。更何用祖師西來。前頭道對一說。這裏 却道倒一說。只爭一字。為什麼却有千差萬 別。且道。聱訛在什麼處。所以道。法隨法行。 法幢隨處建立。不是目前機。亦非目前事時 如何。只消當頭一點。若是具眼漢。一點也謾 他不得問處既聱訛。答處須得恁麼。其實雲 門騎賊馬趕賊。有者錯會道。本是主家話。却 是賓家道。所以雲門云倒一說。有什麼死急。 這僧問得好。不是目前機。亦非目前事時如 何。雲門何不答他別語言。却只向他道倒一 說。雲門一時打破他底。到這裏道倒一說。也 是好肉上剜瘡。何故。言迹之興白雲萬里。異 途之所由生也。設使一時無言無句露柱燈 籠。何曾有言句。還會麼。若不會到這裏也須 是轉動始知落處。
text_en: benefit; it is a question that presents understanding, also called a question that hides the edge. If it were not Yunmen, one could not do anything with him. Yunmen had such hands and feet; since he brought the question, Yunmen responded as he must. Why? A capable lineage master is like a bright mirror facing the stand: when a barbarian comes, a barbarian appears; when a Han comes, a Han appears. The ancients said: if you want intimacy, do not take a question to ask. Why? The question is in the answer; the answer is in the question. From the sages above, when was there ever a single Dharma given to people? Where is there any Zen Way brought to you? If you do not create the karma of hell, you naturally will not invite the fruit of hell. If you do not create the causes of heaven, you naturally will not receive the fruit of heaven. All karmic conditions are self- made and self-received. The ancients plainly told you: if we speak of this matter, it is not in words and phrases. If it were in words and phrases, would the three vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teaching be without words and phrases? Then what need was there for the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Earlier he said, speaking in response to the One; here he says, inverting the One, speaking. It differs by only one character—why then are there a thousand divergences and ten thousand distinctions? Tell me, where is the awkwardness? Thus it is said: Dharma follows Dharma in practice; the Dharma banner is raised wherever one is. When it is not the present opportunity, and also not the present matter, what then? It only takes a single point right at the head. If you are a clear-eyed person, even one point cannot fool you. Since the place of questioning is awkward, the place of answering must be like this. In truth, Yunmen rode a thief’s horse to chase a thief. Some misunderstand, saying it was originally the host’s words, but become the guest’s words. Therefore Yunmen said, inverting the One, speaking. What deadly urgency is there? This monk asked well: when it is not the present opportunity, and also not the present matter, what then? Why didn’t Yunmen answer with other words, but only said to him, inverting the One, speaking? Yunmen shattered him at once. Yet here, saying inverting the One, speaking, is also like gouging a sore in good flesh. Why? When verbal traces arise, white clouds stretch ten thousand miles; the ways by which divergent paths are born. Suppose for a time there were no words and no phrases—just pillar and lamp, when were there words and phrases? Do you understand? If you do not understand, when you reach here you still must turn it around before you know where it lands.
Inverting the One, speaking—cut into a single section. You cannot put it down. Seven blossoms, eight splits. South of Sumeru—rolling up all five thousand and forty-eight on your side and on my side.

text_zh: 倒一說放不下。七花八裂。須彌南畔。卷盡五千四十八　分一節在爾邊在我邊。 半河南半河北。把手共行同死同生為君訣泥裏洗土塊。著甚來由。放 爾不得八萬四千非鳳毛羽毛相似。太殺減人威光。漆桶如麻如粟　三 十三人入虎穴唯我能知。一將難求。野狐精一隊別別有什麼別處。 少賣弄。一任𨁝跳擾擾怱怱水裏月青天白日。迷頭認影。著忙作什麼
text_en: Half Henan, half Hebei—hand in hand, walking together. Together in death, together in life—this is the secret for you. Washing a lump of dirt in mud—what reason is there? I will not let you go. Eighty-four thousand are not phoenix down; three Like feathers—far too much diminishing people’s awesomeness. A lacquer bucket, like hemp, like millet. thirteen people enter the tiger’s den. Only I can know. One general is hard to find. A whole troop of wild-fox spirits. Distinct, distinct. Where is there any other place? Stop showing off. Jump as you like. In restless hurry, the moon in the water. Blue sky, bright day—losing your head and taking shadows for real. What are you rushing for?
Xuedou was no less a true adept; with a single line he at once cuts off a section, clearly

text_zh: 雪竇亦不妨作家。於一句下。便道分一節。分 明放過一著。與他把手共行。他從來有放行 手段。敢與爾入泥入水。同死同生。所以雪 竇恁麼頌。其實無他。只要與爾解粘去縛。抽 釘拔楔。如今却因言句。轉生情解。只如巖頭 道雪峯雖與我同條生。不與我同條死。若非 全機透脫得大自在底人。焉能與爾同死同 生。何故。為他無許多得失是非滲漏處。故洞 山云。若要辨認向上之人真偽者。有三種滲 漏。情滲漏。見滲漏。語滲漏。見滲漏。機不離 位。墮在毒海。情滲漏。智常向背。見處偏枯。 語滲漏。體妙失宗。機昧終始。此三滲漏。宜已 知之。又有三玄。體中玄。句中玄。玄中玄。古 人到這境界。全機大用。遇生與爾同生。遇死 與爾同死。向虎口裏橫身。放得手脚。千里萬 里。隨爾銜去。何故還他得這一著子。始得。八 萬四千非鳳毛者。靈山八萬四千聖眾。非鳳 毛也。南史云。宋時謝超宗。陳郡陽夏人。謝 鳳之子。博學文才傑俊。朝中無比。當世為之 獨步。善為文為王府常侍。王母殷淑儀薨。 超宗作誄奏之。武帝見其文。大加嘆賞曰。超 宗殊有鳳毛。古詩云。朝罷香煙携滿袖。詩成 珠玉在揮毫。欲知世掌絲綸美。池上如今有 鳳毛。昔日靈山會上四眾雲集。世尊拈花。唯 迦葉獨破顏微笑。餘者不知是何宗旨。雪竇 所以道。八萬四千非鳳毛。三十三人入虎穴。 阿難問迦葉云。世尊傳金襴袈裟外。別傳何 法。迦葉召阿難。阿難應喏。迦葉云。倒却門前 剎竿著。阿難遂悟。已後祖祖相傳。西天此土。 三十三人。有入虎穴底手脚。古人道。不入虎 穴。爭得虎子。雲門是這般人。善能同死同生。 宗師為人須至如此。據曲彔木床上坐。捨得 教爾打破。容爾捋虎鬚。也須是到這般田地 始得。具七事隨身。可以同生同死。高者抑之。 下者舉之。不足者與之。在孤峯者。救令入 荒草。落荒草者。救令處孤峯。爾若入鑊湯爐 炭。我也入鑊湯爐炭。其實無他。只要與爾解 粘去縛。抽釘拔楔。脫却籠頭。卸却角馱。平田 和尚。有一頌最好。靈光不昧。萬古徽猷。入此 門來。莫存知解。別別。擾擾怱怱水裏月。不妨 有出身之路。亦有活人之機。雪竇拈了。教人 自去明悟生機。莫隨他語句。爾若隨他。正是 擾擾怱怱水裏月。如今作麼生得平穩去。放 過一著。
text_en: letting one move pass, taking you by the hand to walk together. He has always had ways of letting go, daring to enter mud and water with you, to die together and live together. That is why Xue- dou composed this verse. In truth it is nothing else: he only wants to free you from sticking and binding, to pull nails and pry out wedges. Yet now, because of words and phrases, you instead give rise to sentimental interpretations. Just like Yantou said, Xuefeng may share the same branch of life with me, but he does not share the same branch of death. If one is not a person whose whole functioning breaks through, attaining great freedom, how could he die together with you and live together with you? Why? Because he has no place where gain and loss, right and wrong, can seep in. Thus Dong- shan said: if you want to discern the genuine from the false among people of the higher way, there are three kinds of seepage: emotional seepage, perceptual seepage, and verbal seepage. With perceptual seepage, the functioning does not leave its position and falls into a poisonous sea. With emotional seepage, wisdom is always for or against; the place you see from is one-sided and withered. With verbal seepage, the subtle essence loses its source; functioning is darkened from start to finish. These three seepages you should already know. And there are also three mysteries: mystery within the body, mystery within the phrase, and mystery within mystery. The ancients who reached this realm had whole functioning and great activity: meeting life, they lived together with you; meeting death, they died together with you. They lay themselves crosswise in the tiger’s mouth, letting limbs go free; for a thousand miles, ten thousand miles, you may carry them off in your jaws. Why do we still grant him this move? Only then does it work. The eighty- four thousand who are not phoenix feathers: the eighty-four thousand holy assembly at Vulture Peak are not phoenix feathers either. The History of the South says: in the Song, Xie Chaozong, a man of Yangxia in Chen Commandery, the son of Xie Feng, broadly learned and outstanding in literary talent, unmatched at court; in his day he was regarded as without peer. Skilled in writing, he served as a Regular Attendant in a princely household. When the king’s mother, Yin Shuyi, died, Chaozong wrote the funeral eulogy and presented it. Emperor Wu read it and praised it greatly, saying, Chao- zong truly has phoenix feathers. An old poem says: when court is dismissed, fragrant smoke fills your sleeves; when a poem is finished, pearls and jade are in the sweep of the brush. If you want to know the beauty of one who holds the threads of edicts in hand, by the pond today there is phoenix feather. Long ago at the assembly on Vulture Peak, the fourfold community gathered like clouds; the World-Honored One held up a flower—only Kashyapa alone broke into a slight smile; the rest did not know what the message was. Thus Xuedou said: the eighty-four thousand are not phoenix feathers; thirty-three people entered the tiger’s den. Ananda asked Kashyapa: besides transmitting the gold-brocade robe, what other teaching did the World-Honored One transmit separately? Kashyapa called out, Ananda! Ananda answered, Yes! Kashyapa said: knock down the flagpole in front of the gate. Ananda thereupon awakened. Thereafter, patriarch after patriarch transmitted it, from the Western Heaven to this land. These thirty-three people had the hands and feet to enter the tiger’s den. The ancients said: if you do not enter the tiger’s den, how can you get the tiger cub? Yunmen was such a person, well able to die together and live together. A lineage master guiding others must come to this: sitting on the wooden seat with its curved backrest, he dares to let you smash it, allows you to stroke the tiger’s whiskers. You too must reach such ground before it works. With seven things carried on the body, one can live together and die together. Those who are high he presses down; those who are low he lifts up. Those who lack he supplies. Those on a solitary peak he rescues and makes enter the wild grasses; those who have fallen into the wild grasses he rescues and makes dwell on a solitary peak. If you enter the cauldron of boiling soup, the furnace of coals, I too enter the cauldron of boiling soup, the furnace of coals. In truth it is nothing else: it is only to free you from sticking and binding, to pull nails and pry wedges, to remove the halter, to unload the horn-burden. The master Pingtian has a verse that is best: numinous light is not obscured; for ten thousand ages, the splendid model. Enter this gate and do not keep intellectual understanding. Separate, separate. In restless hurry, the moon in the water—there is still no harm in there being a road to step out, and also a pivot for bringing people to life. Xuedou picked this up to teach people to go and clearly awaken to the living pivot themselves—do not follow his words and phrases. If you follow him, that is exactly restless hurry, the moon in the water. So how do you now go in calm steadiness? Let one move pass.
16 The instruction says: the Way has no sideways shortcut; to stand is solitary and perilous. The Dharma is not in seeing and hearing; words and thought are

text_zh: 垂示云。道無橫徑。立者孤危。法非見聞。言思 逈絕。若能透過荊棘林。解開佛祖縛。得箇穩 密田地。諸天捧花無路。外道潛窺無門。終日 行而未甞行。終日說而未甞說。便可以自由 自在。展啐啄之機。用殺活之劍。直饒恁麼更 須知有建化門中一手擡一手搦。猶較些子。 若是本分事上。且得沒交涉。作麼生是本分 事。試舉看。
text_en: far beyond. If you can pass through the thicket of thorns, untie the bonds of Buddha and patriarchs, and gain a stable, tight ground, the gods offering flowers will have no road, and outsiders peering in will have no gate. All day you walk yet have never walked; all day you speak yet have never spoken. Then you can be free and at ease, unfold the peck-and-chirp pivot, and wield the sword of killing and bringing to life. Even if it is so, you must further know that within the gate of teaching there is one hand lifting and one hand grasping—still a bit short of it. But as for the original matter itself, it has nothing to do with it. What is the original matter? Try bringing it up and see.

Case sixteen: A monk asked Jingqing, I chirp; please, Master, peck. Jingqing said, Can you still get to live or not? The monk said, If I do not live, people will laugh at me. Jingqing Raising waves with no wind—what for? You use so

text_zh: 【一六】舉僧問鏡清。學人啐。請師啄無風起浪。作什麼。爾用許 多見解。作什麼。清云。還得活也無剳。買㡌相頭。將錯就錯。不可總恁 麼僧云。若不活遭人怪笑相帶累。撐天拄地。檐板漢。清 云。也是草裏漢果然。自領出去。放過即不可。
text_en: many views—what for? A jab—buying a physiognomy reading. Taking mistake upon mistake—you must not always be like this. Dragging each other down. Propping up heaven and bracing earth—an eaves-plank fellow. said, You are also a fellow in the grass. Indeed. You lead it out yourself. Letting it pass is not allowed.
Jingqing was a successor of Xuefeng, a contemporary of Benren, Xuansha, Shushan, Taiyuan Fu, and the like.

text_zh: 鏡清承嗣雪峯。與本仁玄沙疎山太原孚輩 同時。初見雪峯。得旨後。常以啐啄之機。開示 後學。善能應機說法。示眾云。大凡行脚人。須 具啐啄同時眼。有啐啄同時用。方稱衲僧。如 母欲啄。而子不得不啐。子欲啐。而母不得不 啄。有僧便出問。母啄子啐。於和尚分上。成得 箇什麼邊事。清云。好箇消息。僧云。子啐母 啄。於學人分上。成得箇什麼邊事。清云。露箇 面目。所以鏡清門下。有啐啄之機。這僧亦是 他門下客。會他家裏事。所以如此問。學人啐 請師啄。此問洞下謂之借事明機。那裏如此。 子啐而母啄。自然恰好同時。鏡清也好。可 謂拳踢相應。心眼相照。便答道。還得活也無。 其僧也好。亦知機變。一句下有賓有主。有照 有用。有殺有活。僧云。若不活遭人怪笑。清 云。也是草裏漢。一等是入泥入水。鏡清不妨 惡脚手。這僧既會恁麼問。為什麼却道。也是 草裏漢。所以作家眼目。須是恁麼。如擊石火 似閃電光。構得構不得。未免喪身失命。若恁 麼。便見鏡清道草裏漢。所以南院示眾云。諸 方只具啐啄同時眼。不具啐啄同時用。有僧 出問。如何是啐啄同時用。南院云。作家不啐 啄。啐啄同時失。僧云。猶是學人疑處。南院 云。作麼生是爾疑處。僧云。失。南院便打。其 僧不肯。院便趕出。僧後到雲門會裏舉前話。 有一僧云。南院棒折那。其僧豁然有省。且道 意在什麼處。其僧却回見南院。院適已遷化。 却見風穴。纔禮拜。穴云。莫是當時問先師啐 啄同時底僧麼。僧云。是。穴云。爾當時作麼生 會。僧云。某甲當初時。如燈影裏行相似。穴 云。爾會也。且道是箇什麼道理。這僧都來只 道某甲當初時。如燈影裏行相似。因甚麼風 穴便向他道爾會也。後來翠巖拈云。南院雖 然運籌帷幄。爭柰土曠人稀。知音者少。風穴 拈云。南院當時。待他開口。劈脊便打。看他作 麼生。若見此公案。便見這僧與鏡清相見處。 諸人作麼生。免得他道草裏漢。所以雪竇愛 他道草裏漢。便頌出。
text_en: When he first met Xuefeng and obtained the point, he often used the peck-and-chirp pivot to instruct later students. He was skilled at responding to circumstances to speak the Dharma. He addressed the assembly, saying: in general, a traveling practitioner must have the eye of chirping and pecking at the same time, and the function of chirping and pecking at the same time—only then can he be called a patch-robed monk. For when the mother wants to peck, the chick cannot but chirp; when the chick wants to chirp, the mother cannot but peck. Then a monk came forward and asked: mother pecks and chick chirps—on the master’s side, what sort of matter does this accomplish? Jingqing said, A fine piece of news. The monk said: chick chirps and mother pecks—on the student’s side, what sort of matter does this accomplish? Jingqing said, It reveals a face. Therefore, in Jingqing’s gate there is the peck-and-chirp pivot. This monk too was a guest in his gate, who understood the affairs of the house, and so asked like this: I chirp, please, Master, peck. In the Dongshan school this question is called borrowing an affair to illuminate functioning. It is not like that here. When the chick chirps and the mother pecks, naturally it is exactly simultaneous. Jingqing too was fine; it can be said that fist and kick correspond, mind and eye illuminate each other. So he answered: Can you still get to live or not? That monk too was fine; he also knew adaptive turns. Within a single line there is guest and host, illumination and function, killing and bringing to life. The monk said: If I do not live, people will laugh at me. Jingqing said: You are also a fellow in the grass. All the same, it is entering mud and water; Jingqing is not to be faulted for a rough hand. Since this monk could ask like that, why then did he say, You are also a fellow in the grass? Thus the eyes of a true adept must be like this: like striking stone to make fire, like a flash of lightning—whether you can set it up or cannot set it up, you cannot avoid losing body and life. If it is like this, then you see why Jingqing said fellow in the grass. Therefore Nanyuan addressed the assembly, saying: the various quarters only have the eye of chirping and pecking at the same time, but do not have the function of chirping and pecking at the same time. A monk came forward and asked: what is the function of chirping and pecking at the same time? Nanyuan said: a true adept does not chirp or peck; chirping and pecking at the same time is missed. The monk said: this is still where the student doubts. Nanyuan said: what is it that you doubt? The monk said: missed. Nanyuan then struck him. The monk would not accept it, so Nanyuan drove him out. Later the monk went to Yunmen’s assembly and brought up the earlier exchange. Another monk said: Nanyuan’s staff broke there. That monk suddenly had an awakening. Tell me, where is the intent? That monk went back to see Nanyuan, but Nanyuan had just passed away. He then went to see Fengxue; as soon as he bowed, Fengxue said: are you not the monk who at that time asked the former master about chirping and pecking at the same time? The monk said: yes. Fengxue said: how did you understand it at the time? The monk said: at first, it was like walking within lamplight and shadows. Fengxue said: you understood it. Tell me, what principle is this? All along this monk only said: at first, it was like walking within lamplight and shadows. Why then did Feng- xue at once say to him, you understood it? Later Cuiyan picked it up, saying: although Nanyuan planned within the tent, what can be done that the land was vast and people were few, and those who truly understood were rare? Fengxue picked it up, saying: if at that time Nanyuan had waited for him to open his mouth and then struck him across the back, see what he would do. Yunmen said, If I had been there at the time and saw it, I would have killed him with one blow and fed him to a dog, just to keep the world at peace. In this way one would finally repay it properly. Therefore the timing of pecking and chirping is all the household style of the ancient buddha. If you reach this Way, you can knock down Yellow Crane Tower with a single punch, and with one kick topple Parrot Isle. It is like a great mass of fire: draw near and it scorches your face. It is like the Tai'a sword: try to match it and you lose your body and your life. Only one who has broken through and shed everything into great liberation can be like this. If you are confused about the source and stuck on phrases, you definitely cannot muster talk like this. In raising and responding you meet dismissal and stripping away: that is one guest and one host. One question, one answer; right within question and answer there is stripping away. This is called raising and responding meeting dismissal and stripping away. Xuedou deeply knew this matter, so he only versified it within two lines. At the end it is still falling into the weeds, breaking it open with notes for your sake. The child and the mother do not know each other. Who is it that pecks and chirps together? Though the mother pecks, she cannot bring about the child's chirping; though the child chirps, it cannot bring about the mother's pecking. Each does not know the other. At the moment of chirping and pecking, who is it that chirps and pecks together? If you understand it like this, you still cannot get out from within Xuedou's final line. Why? Do you not see Xiangyan saying: The child chirps, the mother pecks; the child awakens to having no shell; child and mother both are forgotten. Responding to conditions is not mistaken; those on the same path sing in harmony; wondrous mystery, one leg. Xuedou does not mind falling into the weeds, spinning vines with the word peck. This one word is used to versify Jingqing's answer to the question, Is it still alive or not? Awake. He versifies this monk's saying: If it is not alive, you will be mocked and laughed at. Why then does Xuedou immediately say, Still in the shell? Xuedou, in the flash of sparks struck from stone, distinguishes black-robed from white; in the instant of lightning he discerns the beginnings. Jingqing said, He too is a fellow in the weeds. Xuedou said, He gets struck down again; that is the harder point. Since Jingqing said he too is a fellow in the weeds, can you call that Jingqing changing people's eyes? Is this line not Still in the shell? For now, let it go without concern; how could it be like that? If you can understand it, you can wander the world on pilgrimage and have your share of repaying kindness. This mountain monk talking like this is also a fellow in the weeds. The world’s patched-robed monks are named Miaoyue; who is not named Miaoyue? When you come to this point, Xuedou himself cannot escape the name Miaoyue, and instead further burdens all the monks in the world. Tell me: how is Jingqing acting for this monk? The monks of the world cannot jump out of it. Tell me, how was Jingqing acting on behalf of this monk? Monks everywhere leap about They cannot jump out.

text_zh: 香林道。坐久成勞。還會麼。若會得。百草頭 上。罷却干戈。若也不會。伏聽處分。古人行 脚。結交擇友。為同行道伴。撥草瞻風。是時雲 門旺化廣南。香林得得出蜀。與鵝湖鏡清同 時。先參湖南報慈。後方至雲門會下。作侍者 十八年。在雲門處。親得親聞。他悟時雖晚。不 妨是大根器。居雲門左右十八年。雲門常只 喚遠侍者。纔應喏。門云是什麼。香林當時。也 下語呈見解弄精魂。終不相契。一日忽云。我 會也。門云。何不向上道將來。又住三年。雲門 室中。垂大機辯。多半為他遠侍者。隨處入作。 雲門凡有一言一句。都收在遠侍者處。香林 後歸蜀。初住導江水晶宮。後住青城香林。智 門祚和尚。本浙人。盛聞香林道化。特來入蜀 參禮。祚乃雪竇師也。雲門雖接人無數。當代 道行者。只香林一派最盛。歸川住院四十年。 八十歲方遷化。嘗云。我四十年。方打成一片。 凡示眾云。大凡行脚。參尋知識。要帶眼行。須 分緇素。看淺深始得。先須立志。而釋迦老子。 在因地時。發一言一念。皆是立志。後來僧問。 如何是室內一盞燈。林云。三人證龜成鼈。又 問。如何是衲衣下事。林云。臘月火燒山。古來 答祖師意甚多。唯香林此一則坐斷天下人 舌頭。無爾計較作道理處。僧問。如何是祖 師西來意。林云。坐久成勞。可謂言無味句無 味。無味之談。塞斷人口。無爾出氣處。要見便 見。若不見切忌作解會。香林曾遇作家來。所 以有雲門手段。有三句體調。人多錯會道。祖 師西來。九年面壁。豈不是坐久成勞。有什麼 巴鼻。不見他古人得大自在處。他是脚踏實 地。無許多佛法知見道理。臨時應用。所謂法 隨法行。法幢隨處建立。雪竇因風吹火。傍指 出一箇半箇。

When the ancients went on pilgrimage, they made friends and chose companions as fellow travelers on the Way, parting the grass and watching the winds. At that time Yun- men’s flourishing teaching was in Guangnan. Xianglin came out of Shu and, together with Ehu Jingqing, first visited Baozi in Hunan, and only afterward arrived at Yunmen’s assembly, serving as an attendant for eighteen years. At Yunmen’s place he personally received and personally heard. Though his awakening came late, it still does not hinder that he was a great vessel. Staying at Yunmen’s side for eighteen years, Yunmen often only called, Attendant Yuan. As soon as he responded, Yunmen would say, What is it? At that time Xianglin also offered phrases, presenting views and toying with cleverness, but in the end he never matched. One day he suddenly said, I understand! Yunmen said, Why not bring it forth in an upward way? He stayed another three years. In Yunmen’s room he set forth great pivots and discernment, mostly for that Attendant Yuan, letting him enter and work in at every place. Whatever single word or phrase Yunmen had, all of it was gathered into the attendant Yuan. Xianglin later returned to Shu, first residing at the Crystal Palace of Daojiang, and later at Xianglin in Qingcheng. The master Zhimen Zuo, a native of Zhejiang, greatly hearing of Xianglin’s Way and teaching, specially came into Shu to pay respects and inquire. Zuo was Xuedou’s teacher. Though Yunmen guided countless people, among those of the time who truly walked the Way, only Xianglin’s line was the most flourishing. Returning to Sichuan, he stayed as abbot for forty years. Only at eighty did he pass away. He once said, Only after forty years did I finally hammer it into one piece. Whenever he instructed the assembly he said: In general, when you go on pilgrimage and seek out teachers, you must travel with eyes; you must distinguish black-robed from white, and only then see what is shallow and what is deep. First you must set your resolve. And old Shakyamuni, when he was at the stage of causes, whenever he uttered a word or formed a thought, it was all setting resolve. Later a monk asked, What is a lamp inside the room? Xianglin said, Three people confirm a turtle becomes a soft-shelled turtle. Again he asked, What is the matter beneath the patched robe? Xianglin said, In the twelfth lunar month, fire burns the mountain. Since ancient times there have been many answers about the Patriarch’s intent, but only this one case of Xianglin severs the tongues of everyone under heaven, leaving you no place to calculate and make up principle. A monk asked, What is the intent of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Xianglin said, Sitting long becomes toil. It can be said: words without flavor, phrases without flavor. Flavorless talk blocks mouths and shuts them off, leaving you nowhere to breathe out. If you want to see, then see. If you do not see, absolutely do not make interpretations. Xianglin had once met an adept, therefore he had Yunmen’s methods. There are three-phrase modes and tones. Many people mistakenly understand it as: the Patriarch came from the West and faced the wall for nine years, so is that not sitting long becomes toil? What is the point? They do not see where the ancients gained great freedom. He was feet planted on solid ground, without so much Buddhist doctrine, views, and reasoning. He used it as needed in the moment, what is called: the dharma follows the dharma; the dharma-banner is raised wherever you go. Xuedou, because the wind blows the fire, points to one or half of one.

text_zh: 肅宗代宗。皆玄宗之子孫。為太子時。常愛參 禪。為國有巨盜。玄宗遂幸蜀。唐本都長安。為 安祿山僣據。後都洛陽。肅宗攝政。是時忠國 師。在鄧州白崖山住庵。今香嚴道場是也。四 十餘年不下山。道行聞于帝里。上元二年勅 中使。詔入內。待以師禮。甚敬重之。甞與帝演 無上道。師退朝。帝自攀車而送之。朝臣皆有 慍色。欲奏其不便。國師具他心通。而先見 聖奏曰。我在天帝釋前。見粟散天子。如閃電 光相似。帝愈加敬重。及代宗臨御。復延止光 宅寺。十有六載。隨機說法。至大曆十年。遷 化。山南府青銼山和尚。昔與國師同行。國師 甞奏帝令詔他。三詔不起。常罵國師耽名愛 利。戀著人間。國師於他父于三朝中。為國師。 他家父子。一時參禪。據傳燈錄所考。此乃是 代宗設問。若是問國師如何是十身調御。此 却是肅宗問也。國師緣終。將入涅槃。乃辭代 宗。代宗問曰。國師百年後。所須何物。也只是 平常一箇問端。這老漢無風起浪。却道與老 僧造箇無縫塔。且道白日青天如此作什麼。 做箇塔便了。為什麼却道。做箇無縫塔。代宗 也不妨作家。與爾一拶道。請師塔樣。國師良 久云。會麼。奇怪這些子。最是難參。大小大國 師。被他一拶。直得口似匾檐。然雖如此。若不 是這老漢。幾乎弄倒了。多少人道。國師不言 處。便是塔樣。若恁麼會。遶磨一宗掃地而盡。 若謂良久便是。啞子也合會禪。豈不見外道 問佛。不問有言不問無言世尊良久。外道禮 拜。贊嘆曰。世尊大慈大悲。開我迷雲。令我得 入。及外道去後。阿難問佛。外道有何所證。而 言得入。世尊云。如世良馬。見鞭影而行。人多 向良久處會。有什麼巴鼻。五祖先師拈云。前 面是珍珠瑪瑙。後面是瑪瑙珍珠。左邊是觀 音勢至。右邊是文殊普賢。中間有箇旛子。 被風吹著。道胡盧胡盧。國師云。會麼。帝曰。 不會。却較些子。且道這箇不會。與武帝不識。 是同是別。雖然似則似。是則未是。國師云。吾 有付法弟子耽源。却諳此事。請詔問之。雪 竇拈云。獨掌不浪鳴。代宗不會則且置。耽源 還會麼。只消道箇請師塔樣。盡大地人不柰 何。五祖先師拈云。爾是一國之師。為箇什麼 不道却推與弟子。國師遷化後。帝詔耽源問 此意如何。源便來為國師。胡言漢語說道理。 自然會他國師說話。只消一頌祖庭事苑出齊時湘之 南潭之北。中有黃金充一國。無影樹下合同 船。瑠璃殿上無知識。耽源名應真。在國師處 作侍者。後住吉州耽源寺。時仰山來參耽源。 源言重性惡不可犯。住不得。仰山先去參性 空禪師。有僧問性空。如何是祖師西來意。空 云。如人在千尺井中。不假寸繩出得此人。即 答汝西來意。僧云。近日湖南暢和尚。亦為人 東語西話。空乃喚沙彌拽出這死屍著沙彌仰山山 後舉問耽源。如何出得井中人。耽源曰。咄。癡 漢。誰在井中。仰山不契。後問溈山。山乃呼 慧寂。山應諾。溈云。出了也。仰山因此大悟。 云。我在耽源處得體。溈山處得用。也只是 這一箇頌子。引人邪解不少。人多錯會道。相 是相見。譚是譚論。中間有箇無縫塔。所以道。 中有黃金充一國。帝與國師對答。便是無影 樹下合同船。帝不會。遂道瑠璃殿上無知識。 又有底道。相是相州之南。潭是潭州之北。中 有黃金充一國。頌官家眨眼顧視云。這箇是 無縫塔。若恁麼會。不出情見。只如雪竇下四 轉語。又作麼生會。今人殊不知古人意。且道。 湘之南。潭之北。爾作麼生會。中有黃金充一 國。爾作麼生會。無影樹下合同船。爾作麼生 會。瑠璃殿上無知識。爾作麼生會。若恁麼見 得。不妨慶快平生。湘之南潭之北。雪竇道。獨 掌不浪鳴。不得已與爾說。中有黃金充一國。 雪竇道。山形拄杖子。古人道。識得拄杖子。一 生參學事畢。無影樹下合同船。雪竇道。海晏 河清。一時豁開戶牖。八面玲瓏。瑠璃殿上 無知識。雪竇道。拈了也。一時與爾說了也。不 妨難見。見得也好。只是有些子錯認處。隨語 生解。至末後道拈了也。却較些子。雪竇分明 一時下語了。後面單頌箇無縫塔子。
text_en: study Zen. Because the realm had a great bandit threat, Xuanzong then fled to Shu. Tang’s original capital was Chang’an; it was usurped and occupied by An Lushan. Later the capital was at Luoyang, and Suzong served as regent. At that time the National Teacher Zhongguo was living in a hermitage on Baiya Mountain in Dengzhou, where Xiangyan’s practice site is today. For more than forty years he did not come down from the mountain. His conduct and practice became known in the imperial capital. In the second year of Shangyuan, an edict a palace messenger, summoning him to enter within. He was received with the courtesies due a teacher, and was deeply respected. He once expounded with the emperor the unsurpassed Way with the emperor. When the master withdrew from court, the emperor himself held onto the carriage and escorted him. All the court officials showed displeasure and wanted to memorialize that it was improper. The National Teacher had knowledge of others’ minds, and foresaw the imperial memorial in advance, saying: “Before Indra, lord of gods, I see a petty human emperor like a flash of lightning, like lightning’s light.” The emperor respected him even more. When Daizong ascended the throne, he again invited him to reside at Zhiguang Monastery for sixteen years, teaching according to conditions. In the tenth year of Dali, he passed on and transformed. The master of Qingcuo Mountain in Shannan Prefecture had once traveled with the National Teacher. The National Teacher once petitioned the emperor to issue an edict for him. Three summons came and he did not rise. He often cursed the National Teacher for craving fame and loving profit, clinging to the human world. The National Teacher served as national teacher through three reigns for that father and son. That father and son, for a time, studied Zen. According to what is examined in the Transmission of the Lamp Record, this is a question posed by Daizong. But if the question is “National Teacher, what is the tenfold body that tames and guides,” this was instead asked by Suzong. When the National Teacher’s karmic conditions ended and he was about to enter nirvana, he took leave of Dai- zong. Daizong asked: “After the National Teacher’s hundred years, what will be needed?” It is just an ordinary line of questioning. This old fellow raised waves without wind, and said: “Build for this old monk a seamless stupa.” Tell me, under bright day and clear sky, what is this for? Just making a stupa would do. Why did he instead say, make a seamless stupa? Daizong was no slouch either. He pressed him with one shove: “Please, Master, the stupa pattern.” The National Teacher, for a long while, said: “Do you understand?” Strange, this kind of thing is hardest to work on. The great National Teacher, pressed by that one shove, was left with a mouth like a flat eave. Even so, if it were not for this old fellow, he would almost have toppled it. How many people say: “The National Teacher’s not speaking is the stupa pattern.” If you understand it like that, you grind the whole lineage to dust and sweep it all away. If you say the long pause itself is it, then even a mute would be able to understand Zen. Don’t you see the outsider who asked the Buddha, not asking for words, not asking for no words—World-Honored One remained silent for a long while. The outsider bowed in homage and praised: “World-Honored One, with great kindness and great compassion you have parted my cloud of confusion, allowing me to enter.” After the outsider left, Ananda asked the Buddha: “What realization did the outsider attain, that he says he has entered?” The World-Honored One said: “Like a fine horse in the world that moves upon seeing the shadow of the whip.” Many people try to understand at the long pause—what’s the point? Master Wuzu picked it up and said: “In front are pearls and agate; behind are agate and pearls. On the left are Avalokiteshvara and Mahasthamaprapta; on the right are Manjushri and Samantabhadra. In the middle there is a banner.” The wind blows it and it goes hu lu, hu lu. The National Teacher said: “Do you understand?” The emperor said: “I don’t understand.” That’s a bit better. Tell me: is this “don’t understand” the same as Emperor Wu’s “I don’t recognize,” or different? Though it resembles it, it is not actually it. The National Teacher said: “I have a Dharma-heir disciple, Danyuan, who understands this matter. Please issue an edict and ask him.” Xue Dou picked it up and said: “One hand does not make the waves roar.” Set aside Daizong’s not understanding for now—does Danyuan understand or not? Just by saying “Please, Master, the stupa pattern,” people across the whole earth cannot do anything about it. Master Wuzu picked it up and said: “You are the teacher of a nation—why don’t you speak, instead pushing it off onto your disciple?” After the National Teacher passed on, the emperor summoned Danyuan and asked what this meant. Danyuan then came to serve as National Teacher, babbling in mixed talk, explaining principles. Naturally he understood the National Teacher’s words. It only took one verse: “South of the Xiang, When the Ancestors’ Garden Anthology was first compiled, north of the Tan: within it is gold filling a whole nation. Beneath the shadowless tree, they share a boat. In the lapis hall there is no ‘knower.’” Danyuan’s name was Yingzhen. At the National Teacher’s place he served as an attendant. Later he resided at Danyuan Monastery in Jizhou. At that time Yangshan came to study with Danyuan. Danyuan said: “Zhongxing is harsh-natured, fierce, and must not be offended—you can’t stay.” Yangshan first went to study with Master Xing- kong. A monk asked Xingkong: “What is the Patriarch’s meaning in coming from the West?” Xingkong said: “It’s like someone in a thousand-foot well. Without using even an inch of rope, get the person out—then I will answer you about the meaning of coming from the West.” The monk said: “Recently in Hunan, Master Chang also guides people by talking east and speaking west.” Xingkong then called a novice: “Drag this corpse out and throw it on the mountain!” the novice Yangshan, Later he raised it and asked Danyuan: “How do you get the person out of the well?” Danyuan said: “Tch! You foolish fellow—who is in the well?” Yangshan did not accord with it. Later he asked Guishan. Guishan then called: “Huiji!” Yangshan answered. Guishan said: “He’s out.” Because of this, Yangshan had a great awakening. He said: “With Danyuan I got the substance; with Guishan I got the function.” It is just this one verse that leads many into perverse interpretations. Many people mistakenly understand it, saying: “Xiang means meeting face to face; Tan means discussing.” In the middle there is a seamless stupa—so they say. “Within it is gold filling a whole nation” means the exchange between the emperor and the National Teacher. That is the shared boat beneath the shadowless tree. The emperor did not understand, so it says: “In the lapis hall there is no ‘knower.’” Others say Xiang is south of Xiangzhou, and Tan is north of Tanzhou. Within it is gold filling a whole nation. They chant that the ruler blinked and glanced around, saying: “This is the seamless stupa.” If you understand it like that, you never get beyond emotional views. But as for Xue Dou’s four turning phrases below, how will you understand them? People today really do not know what the ancients meant. Tell me: “South of the Xiang, north of the Tan”—how do you understand it? “Within it is gold filling a whole nation”—how do you understand it? “Beneath the shadowless tree they share a boat”—how do you understand it? “In the lapis hall there is no ‘knower’”—how do you understand it? If you can see like that, you may rejoice for your whole life. “South of the Xiang, north of the Tan”—Xue Dou said: “One hand does not make the waves roar.” With no choice, I’ll tell you: “Within it is gold filling a whole nation.” Xue Dou said: “Mountain-shaped staff.” The ancients said: “If you recognize the staff, your lifelong study is finished.” “Beneath the shadowless tree they share a boat”—Xue Dou said: “The sea is calm, the river runs clear.” In one moment the doors and windows are flung open—crystal clear in all eight directions. “In the lapis hall there is no ‘knower’”—Xue Dou said: “Picked up and done.” In one stroke I’ve told it to you. It’s not that it’s impossible to see; seeing it is fine too. It’s just that there are places where you misrecognize—following words, you give rise to interpretations. At the very end he says “picked up and done,” which is a bit better. Xue Dou clearly delivered his remarks all at once. After that, he gives a separate verse just on the seamless stupa.
Seeing the seamless stupa is still hard; the clear pool does not allow this seam—how huge it is! What are you saying? Not something the eye can see. Blind!

text_zh: 雪竇當頭道。無縫塔見還難。雖然獨露無私。 則是要見時還難。雪竇忒殺慈悲。更向爾道。 澄潭不許蒼龍蟠。五祖先師道。雪竇頌古一 𠕋。我只愛他澄潭不許蒼龍蟠一句。猶較些 子。多少人去他國師良久處作活計。若恁麼 會。一時錯了也。不見道。臥龍不鑒止水。無處 有月波澄。有處無風浪起。又道。臥龍長怖碧 潭清。若是這箇漢。直饒洪波浩渺。白浪滔天。 亦不在裏許蟠。雪竇到此頌了。後頭著些子 眼目。琢出一箇無縫塔。隨後說道。層落落影 團團。千古萬古與人看。爾作麼生看。即今 在什麼處。直饒爾見得分明。也莫錯認定盤 星。
text_en: when you want to see it, it is still hard. Xue Dou is overly compassionate, and further tells you: “The clear pool does not allow an azure dragon to coil.” Master Wuzu said: “Of Xue Dou’s verse on the ancients, I only love his one line, ‘The clear pool does not allow an azure dragon to coil.’ Still, it’s a bit better.” How many people go to the National Teacher’s long pause and make a living off it. If you understand it like that, you miss it all at once. Don’t you see it said: “A coiled dragon does not reflect in still water.” Where there is no place for moon-waves to be clear, there are places where waves rise without wind. It also says: “The coiled dragon long fears the emerald pool’s clarity.” If it is this fellow, even if vast floods surge and white waves reach the sky, he still will not coil there. When Xue Dou gets here, he has finished the verse; after that he adds some “eyes,” chiseling out a seamless stupa, and then says: “Tier upon tier, shadows gathered round—through a thousand ages, ten thousand ages, for people to see.” How do you see it? Right now, where is it? Even if you see it clearly, do not misrecognize the fixed pole star.

text_zh: 垂示云。一塵舉大地收。一花開世界起。只如 塵未舉花未開時。如何著眼。所以道。如斬一 綟絲。一斬一切斬。如染一綟絲。一染一切染。 只如今便將葛藤截斷。運出自己家珍。高低 普應。前後無差。各各現成。儻或未然。看取下 文。
text_en: before the mote is raised, before the flower opens, how do you set your eye? Thus it is said: like cutting a single strand of silk—one cut, and all is cut; like dyeing a single strand of silk—one dyeing, and all is dyed. Just now, cut off the tangled vines at once, and bring forth your own family treasure, high and low Universally responsive, with no discrepancy from beginning to end; each is complete in itself. If it is not yet so, look at what follows.
