text_zh: 若向指頭上會。則辜負俱胝。若不向指頭上 會。則生鐵鑄就相似。會也恁麼去。不會也恁 麼去。高也恁麼去。低也恁麼去。是也恁麼去。 非也恁麼去。所以道。一塵纔起大地全收。一 花欲開世界便起。一毛頭獅子。百億毛頭現。 圓明道。寒則普天普地寒。熱則普天普地熱。 山河大地。下徹黃泉。萬象森羅。上通霄漢。且 道。是什麼物得恁麼奇怪。若也識得。不消一 揑。若識不得。礙塞殺人。俱胝和尚。乃婺州 金華人。初住庵時。有一尼名實際。到庵直入。 更不下笠。持錫遶禪床三匝云。道得即下笠。 如是三問。俱胝無對。尼便去。俱胝曰。天勢稍 晚。且留一宿。尼曰道得即宿。胝又無對。尼便 行。胝嘆曰。我雖處丈夫之形。而無丈夫之氣。 遂發憤要明此事。擬棄庵往諸方參請。打疊 行脚。其夜山神告曰。不須離此。來日有肉 身菩薩。來為和尚說法。不須去。果是次日。天 龍和尚到庵。胝乃迎禮。具陳前事。天龍只竪 一指而示之。俱胝忽然大悟。是他當時鄭重 專注。所以桶底易脫。後來凡有所問。只竪一 指。長慶道。美食不中飽人喫。玄沙道。我當時 若見。拗折指頭。玄覺云。玄沙恁麼道。意作麼 生。雲居錫云。只如玄沙恁麼道。是肯伊。是不 肯伊。若肯伊。何言拗折指頭。若不肯伊。俱胝 過在什麼處。先曹山云。俱胝承當處莽鹵。只 認得一機一境。一等是拍手撫掌。見他西 園奇怪。玄覺又云。且道俱胝還悟也未。為什 麼承當處莽鹵。若是不悟。又道平生。只用一 指頭禪不盡。且道曹山意在什麼處。當時俱 胝實然不會。及乎到他悟後凡有所問。只竪 一指。因什麼。千人萬人。羅籠不住。撲他不 破。爾若用作指頭會。決定不見古人意。這般 禪易參。只是難會。如今人纔問著。也竪指竪 拳。只是弄精魂。也須是徹骨徹髓。見透始得。 俱胝庵中有一童子。於外被人詰曰。和尚尋 常以何法示人。童子竪起指頭。歸而舉似師。 俱胝以刀斷其指。童子叫喚走出。俱胝召一 聲。童子回首。俱胝却竪起指頭。童子豁然領 解。且道見箇什麼道理。及至遷化。謂眾曰。吾 得天龍一指頭禪。平生用不盡。要會麼。竪起 指頭便脫去後來明招獨眼龍問國泰深師叔 云。古人道。俱胝只念三行呪。便得名超一切 人。作麼生與他拈却三行呪。深亦竪起一指 頭。招云。不因今日。爭識得這瓜州客。且道。 意作麼生。祕魔平生。只用一杈。打地和尚凡 有所問。只打地一下。後被人藏却他棒。却問 如何是佛。他只張口。亦是一生用不盡。無業 云。祖師觀此土有大乘根器。唯單傳心印。指 示迷塗。得之者不揀愚之與智。凡之與聖且 多虛不如少實。大丈夫漢。即今直下休歇去。 頓息萬緣去。超生死流。逈出常格。縱有眷屬 莊嚴。不求自得。無業一生凡有所問。只道莫 妄想。所以道。一處透。千處萬處一時透。一機 明。千機萬機一時明。如今人總不恁麼。只管 恣意情解。不會他古人省要處。他豈不是無 機關轉換處。為什麼只用一指頭。須知俱胝 到這裏。有深密為人處。要會得省力麼。還他 圓明道寒則普天普地寒。熱則普天普地熱。 山河大地。通上孤危。萬象森羅。徹下嶮峻什 麼處得一指頭禪來。
text_en: it is like being cast from raw iron. Understanding goes like this; not understanding also goes like this. High goes like this; low goes like this. Right goes like this. Wrong goes like this. Therefore it is said: when a single mote of dust arises, the whole earth is gathered in. When a single flower is about to open, the world comes forth. On one hair-tip a lion; on a hundred billion hair-tips it appears. Yuanming said: when it is cold, all heaven and all earth are cold; when it is hot, all heaven and all earth are hot. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth below penetrate to the Yellow Springs; the myriad forms in their profusion above reach the vault of heaven. Tell me, what thing is it that is so strange? If you recognize it, there is no need for a single pinch. If you do not recognize it, it blocks you to death. Master Juzhi was a man of Jinhua in Wuzhou. When he first lived in a hermitage, a nun named Shiji came; she walked straight in. Without removing her hat, holding her staff, she circled the meditation seat three times and said, Speak and I will remove my hat. In this way she asked three times. Juzhi had no reply, so the nun left. Juzhi said, It is getting rather late; stay the night. The nun said, Speak and I will stay. Juzhi again had no reply, so the nun went on. Juzhi sighed, Though I have a man's form, I have no man's spirit. So he roused himself, determined to clarify this matter. He planned to abandon the hermitage and travel to various places to seek instruction, packing for pilgrimage. That night the mountain spirit told him, You need not leave here. Tomorrow a bodhisattva in the flesh will come to teach the Dharma for the master. Do not go. Sure enough, the next day, Master Tianlong came to the hermitage. Juzhi greeted him with bows and fully related what had happened before. Tianlong simply raised one finger to show him. Juzhi suddenly had great awakening. It was because at that time he was earnest and wholly focused that the bottom of the bucket was easy to drop out. After that, whenever he was asked anything, he only raised one finger. Changqing said, Fine food does not satisfy a person who eats it wrongly. Xuansha said, If I had seen it then, I would have twisted off the finger. Xuanjue said, When Xuansha speaks like that, what is his intent? Yunju Xi said, Just consider Xuansha speaking like that: does he approve of him, or does he not? If he approves, why say he would twist off the finger? If he does not approve, where is Juzhi at fault? Formerly Caoshan said, Juzhi's taking up was crude; he only recognized one device and one scene. It is just like clapping and rubbing your hands, seeing his strange spectacle in the western garden. Xuanjue also said, Tell me, did Juzhi awaken or not? Why is his taking up crude? If he did not awaken, yet it is said that all his life he used only the one-finger Zen without exhausting it. Tell me, where is Caoshan's meaning? At that time Juzhi truly did not understand. Yet once he had awakened, whenever he was asked anything, he only raised one finger. Why? A thousand people, ten thousand people cannot net it; they cannot break it down. If you use it as understanding the finger, you will definitely not see the ancients' intent. This sort of Zen is easy to enter, but hard to understand. Nowadays as soon as people are asked, they raise a finger, raise a fist, merely playing with spirit. You must penetrate to the bones and marrow; only then can you see through. In Juzhi's hermitage there was a boy. Outside, someone questioned him, What method does the master usually use to instruct people? The boy raised a finger. Returning, he told the master. Juzhi cut off his finger with a knife. The boy cried out and ran away. Juzhi called out once; the boy turned his head. Juzhi then raised a finger. The boy suddenly understood. Tell me, what principle did he see? When he was about to pass away, he said to the assembly, I obtained Tianlong's one-finger Zen; all my life I have used it without exhausting it. Want to understand? Raise a finger and it slips away. Later, Mingzhao the one-eyed dragon asked his grand-uncle, Master Guotai Shen, The ancients say Juzhi merely recited a three-line spell and thereby gained a name surpassing all people. How would you take away those three lines of spell? Shen also raised one finger. Zhao said, If not for today, how would one recognize this Guazhou traveler? Tell me, what is the meaning? Pimo all his life used only a fork; Master Dadi, whenever he was asked anything, only struck the ground once. Later someone hid his staff; when asked What is Buddha? he only opened his mouth. This too was something used all one's life without exhausting. Wuye said, The patriarchs observed that this land has roots for the Great Vehicle, so they transmitted only the mind-seal, singly. They point out the deluded path. Those who obtain it are not chosen by foolishness or wisdom, by ordinary or sage. Moreover, better a little truth than much emptiness. You great man, right now, directly, rest and let go. At once stop the myriad entanglements; transcend the stream of birth and death; stand far outside the usual pattern. Even if you have family and adornments, without seeking you attain it of yourself. All his life, whenever Wuye was asked anything, he only said, Do not indulge in deluded thinking. Therefore it is said: break through in one place and a thousand places, ten thousand places break through at once. When one device is clear, a thousand devices, ten thousand devices are clear at once. People today are not like this; they only indulge their own emotional interpretations, not understanding the ancients' essential point. Is it not that there is no pivoting and turning? Why use only one finger? You must know that Juzhi at this point had a deep and secret way of benefiting people. Want to understand the labor-saving way? Return to Yuanming's saying: when it is cold, all heaven and all earth are cold; when it is hot, all heaven and all earth are hot. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth connect upward to solitary heights; the myriad forms in their profusion penetrate downward to perilous depths. From what place could a one-finger Zen be obtained?

Raising it up in praise, he deeply loves old Juzhi; though the universe is empty, Leprous children tugging companions—only those on the same path know. It still cannot avoid being one device, one scene.

text_en: who else is there? Two or three—and there is yet another; that one too must be killed. He once set a floating log down upon the vast sea; a log. It is entirely this. Yes, yes—yet it is too solitary and steep. What use is a torn straw sandal? In night waves, together it meets and receives the blind turtle. Fishing up heaven, groping earth—when will it ever end? Even if you catch it, what can you use it for? Act according to the command and drive on into a world with no Buddha. Having caught it, Venerable—one blind fellow.

text_zh: 雪竇會四六文章。七通八達。凡是誵訛奇特 公案。偏愛去頌。對揚深愛老俱胝。宇宙空來 更有誰。今時學者。抑揚古人。或賓或主。一問 一答。當面提持。有如此為人處。所以道。對揚 深愛老俱胝。且道雪竇愛他作什麼。自天地 開闢以來。更有誰人。只是老俱胝一箇。若 是別人須參雜。唯是俱胝老。只用一指頭。直 至老死。時人多邪解道。山河大地也空。人也 空。法也空。直饒宇宙一時空來。只是俱胝老 一箇。且得沒交涉。曾向滄溟下浮木。如今謂 之生死海。眾生在業海之中。頭出頭沒。不明 自己。無有出期。俱胝老垂慈接物。於生死海 中。用一指頭接人。似下浮木接盲龜相似。令 諸眾生得到彼岸。夜濤相共接盲龜。法華經 云。如一眼之龜。值浮木孔。無沒溺之患。大善 知識接得一箇如龍似虎底漢。教他向有佛 世界。互為賓主。無佛世界坐斷要津。接得箇 盲龜。堪作何用。
text_en: unusual gong'an, he especially loved to compose a verse on it. Raising it up in praise, he deeply loves old Juzhi; though the universe is empty, who else is there? Students today either praise or disparage the ancients, sometimes as guest, sometimes as host, question and answer, holding it up face to face. There is such a way of benefiting people. Therefore it is said: raising it up in praise, he deeply loves old Juzhi. Tell me, what does Xuedou love about him? Since heaven and earth were opened up, who else has there been? Only old Juzhi alone. If it were someone else, there would have to be mixture and admixture. Only old Juzhi used only one finger, straight until old age and death. People of the time often had a perverse understanding, saying that mountains, rivers, and the great earth are empty; people too are empty; Dharma too is empty. Even if the universe were empty all at once, still old Juzhi alone would have nothing to do with it. He once set a floating log down upon the vast sea; now it is called the sea of birth and death. Sentient beings are in the sea of karma, heads emerging, heads sinking, not understanding themselves, with no time of escape. Old Juzhi let down compassion and received beings; within the sea of birth and death, he used one finger to receive people, like a floating log receiving a blind turtle, enabling all beings to reach the other shore. In night waves, together it meets and receives the blind turtle. The Lotus Sutra says: like a one-eyed turtle meeting the hole in a floating log, there is no danger of drowning. A great good friend who receives someone like a dragon, like a tiger, teaches him: in a world with Buddhas, they mutually act as guest and host; in a world without Buddhas, they sit and cut off the vital pass. If you receive a blind turtle, what use is it?

text_zh: 【二〇】舉。龍牙問翠微。如何是祖師西來意諸方舊話。 也要勘過微云。與我過禪板來用禪板作什麼。洎合放過。噞牙過 禪板與翠微也是把不住。駕與青龍不解騎。可惜許。當面不承當。微接 得便打着。打得箇死漢濟甚事。也落在第二頭了也牙云。打即任 打。要且無祖師西來意這漢話在第二頭。賊過後張弓牙 又問臨濟。如何是祖師西來意諸方舊公案。再問將來。不 直半文錢濟云。與我過蒲團來曹溪波浪如相似。無限平人被陸沈。一狀領 過。一坑埋却牙取蒲團過與臨濟依前把不住。依前不伶俐。依俙越國。 髣髴揚州濟接得便打著。可惜打這般死漢。一模脫出牙云。打即 任打。要且無祖師西來意灼然在鬼窟裏作活計。將謂得便宜。 賊過後張弓。

Harnessed to the azure dragon yet you cannot ride—what a pity. Face to face you do not accept it. and struck Longya, saying, You may strike, Hit! What does beating a dead fellow accomplish? You have also fallen into the second head. but there is, after all, no meaning of the Patriarch's coming from the West. Longya This fellow’s words are in the second head—drawing the bow after the thief has passed. again asked Linji, What is the meaning of the Patriarch's coming from the West? Linji said, Hand me the sitting cushion. Longya took the cushion and handed it to Linji. Linji took it and struck Longya, saying, You may strike, Old public cases from all quarters—ask them again, and they are not worth half a coin. The waves of Caoxi are like this; countless ordinary people are submerged on dry land. In one batch they are herded through, and buried in a single pit. As before, you cannot grasp it; as before, you are not nimble—vaguely like the state of Yue. Faintly like Yangzhou. Strike! What a pity to beat such a dead fellow—cast from one mold. but there is, after all, no meaning of the Patriarch's coming from the West. text_zh: 翠巖芝和尚云。當時如是。今時衲子。皮下還 有血麼。溈山喆云。翠微臨濟。可謂本分宗師。 龍牙一等是撥草瞻風。不妨與後人作龜鑑。 住院後有僧問。和尚當時還肯二尊宿麼。牙 云。肯即肯。只是無祖師西來意。龍牙瞻前顧 後。應病與藥。大溈則不然。待伊問和尚當時 還肯二尊宿麼。明不明。劈脊便打。非惟扶竪 翠微臨濟。亦不辜負來問。石門聰云。龍牙無 人拶著。猶可。被箇衲子挨著。失却一隻眼。雪 竇云。臨濟翠微。只解把住不解放開。我當 時如作龍牙。待伊索蒲團禪板。拈起劈面便 擲。五祖戒云。和尚得恁麼面長。或云。祖師土 宿臨頭。黃龍新云。龍牙驅耕夫之牛。奪飢人 之食。既明則明矣。因什麼却無祖師西來意。 會麼。棒頭有眼明如日。要識真金火裏看。 大凡激揚要妙。提唱宗乘。向第一機下明得。 可以坐斷天下人舌頭。儻或躊躇落在第二。 這二老漢。雖然打風打雨。驚天動地。要且 不曾打著箇明眼漢。古人參禪多少辛苦。立 大丈夫志氣。經歷山川。參見尊宿。龍牙先 參翠微臨濟。後參德山。遂問學人仗鏌鎁劍。 擬取師頭時如何。德山引頸云。㘞。牙云。師頭 落也。山微笑便休去。次到洞山。洞山問。近離 甚處。牙云。德山來。洞山云。德山有何言句。 牙遂舉前話。洞山云。他道什麼。牙云。他無 語。洞山云。莫道無語。且試將德山落底頭呈 似老僧看。牙於此有省。遂焚香遙望德山禮 拜懺悔。德山聞云。洞山老漢不識好惡。這漢 死來多少時。救得有什麼用處。從他擔老僧 頭遶天下走。龍牙根性聰敏。擔一肚皮禪。行 脚。直向長安翠微。便問。如何是祖師西來 意。微云。與我過禪板來。牙取禪板與微。微接 得便打。牙云。打即任打。要且無祖師西來意。 又問臨濟。如何是祖師西來意。濟云。與我過 蒲團來。牙取蒲團與臨濟。濟接得便打。牙云。 打即任打。要且無祖師西來意。他致箇問端。 不妨要見他曲彔木床上老漢。亦要明自己 一段大事。可謂言不虛設。機不亂發。出在做 工夫處。不見五洩參石頭。先自約曰。若一言 相契。即住。不然即去。石頭據座。洩拂袖而 出。石頭知是法器。即垂開示。洩不領其旨。告 辭而出至門。石頭呼之云。闍黎。洩回顧。石頭 云。從生至死。只是這箇。回頭轉腦。更莫別 求。洩於言下大悟。又麻谷持錫到章敬。遶禪 床三匝。振錫一下。卓然而立。敬云。是是。又 到南泉。依前遶床振錫而立。南泉云。不是不 是。此是風力所轉。終成敗壞。谷云。章敬道 是。和尚為什麼道不是。南泉云。章敬即是。是 汝不是。古人也不妨要提持透脫此一件事。 如今人纔問著。全無些子用工夫處。今日也 只是恁麼。明日也只是恁麼。爾若只恁麼盡 未來際。也未有了日。須是抖擻精神。始得有 少分相應。爾看龍牙發一問道。如何是祖師 西來意。翠微云。與我過禪板來。牙過與微。微 接得便打。牙當時取禪板時。豈不知翠微要 打他。也不得便道他不會。為什麼却過禪板 與他。且道當機承當得時。合作麼生。他不向 活水處用。自去死水裏作活計。一向作主宰。 便道打即任打。要且無祖師西來意。又走去 河北參臨濟。依前恁麼問。濟云。與我過蒲團 來。牙過與濟。濟接得便打。牙云。打即任打。 要且無祖師西來意。且道二尊宿。又不同法 嗣。為什麼答處相似。用處一般。須知古人。一 言一句。不亂施為。他後來住院。有僧問云。和 尚當時見二尊宿。是肯他不肯他。牙云。肯則 肯。要且無祖師西來意。爛泥裏有刺。放過與 人。已落第二。這老漢把得定。只做得洞下 尊宿。若是德山臨濟門下。須知別有生涯。若 是山僧則不然。只向他道。肯即未肯。要且無 祖師西來意。不見僧問大梅。如何是祖師西 來意。梅云。西來無意。鹽官聞云。一箇棺材。 兩箇死漢。玄沙聞云。鹽官是作家。雪竇道。三 箇也有。只如這僧問祖師西來意。却向他道 西來無意。爾若恁麼會。墮在無事界裏。所以 道。須參活句。莫參死句。活句下薦得。永劫不 忘。死句下薦得。自救不了。龍牙恁麼道。不妨 盡善。古人道相續也大難。他古人一言一句。 不亂施為。前後相照。有權有實。有照有用。賓 主歷然。互換縱橫。若要辨其親切。龍牙雖不 昧宗乘。爭柰落在第二頭。當時二尊宿。索禪 板蒲團。牙不可不知他意。是他要用他胸襟 裏事。雖然如是。不妨用得太峻。龍牙恁麼問。 二老恁麼答。為什麼却無祖師西來意。到這 裏須知別有箇奇特處。雪竇拈出令人看。
text_en: blood under your skin? Weishan Zhe said, Cuiwei and Linji can be called masters true to their station. Longya and his like were clearing the grass and watching the wind; they can serve as a mirror for later people. After he became abbot, a monk asked, Master, back then did you approve of those two venerables? Longya said, Approve, yes I approve, but there is no meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West. Longya looked ahead and behind, prescribing medicine to match the illness. But Dawei was not like that. If he were asked, Master, back then did you approve of those two venerables? clear or not clear, he would strike him across the back at once. Not only did he uphold Cuiwei and Linji, he also did not fail the one who came to ask. Shimen Cong said, If no one presses Longya, it is still acceptable; but once that patched-robed fellow crowds him, he loses one eye. Xuedou said, Linji and Cuiwei only know how to seize and hold, not how to let go and open. If I had been there, acting as Longya, when he asked for the sitting mat or the meditation board, I would have snatched it up and straightaway hurled it in his face. Wuzu Jie said, The master has gotten such a long face. Someone said, The Patriarchs and old worthies are bearing down on him. Huanglong Xin said, Longya drives off the plowman’s ox and snatches away the hungry man’s food. If it is clear, then it is clear; so why is there still no meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West? Do you understand? The staff has eyes, bright as the sun; to know true gold, look for it in the fire. In general, to rouse and raise the essential, to lift up and proclaim the tradition, you must understand it at the first pivot. Then you can sit and cut off the tongues of everyone under heaven. If you hesitate, you fall into the second. These two old fellows, though they strike like wind and rain, shaking heaven and earth, still have not yet struck a clear-eyed man. How hard the ancients labored in investigating Chan. They set the resolve of a great man, traversed mountains and rivers, and went to visit venerable elders. Longya first visited Cuiwei and Linji, and later visited Deshan. Then he asked, When a student brandishes the Mo-ye sword and intends to take the master’s head, what then? Deshan stretched out his neck and said... Longya said, The master’s head falls. Deshan gave a faint smile and let it rest. Next he went to Dongshan. Dongshan asked, Where have you just come from? Longya said, From Deshan. Dongshan said, What words does Deshan have? Longya then raised the previous exchange. Dongshan said, What did he say? Longya said, He had no words. Dongshan said, Do not say no words. Try presenting to this old monk the head that Deshan let fall, and let me see. Longya had an awakening here. He then burned incense, bowed toward Deshan from afar, and repented. Deshan heard of it and said, That old fellow Dongshan does not know good from bad. This fellow has been dead for so long; what use is it to save him? Let him carry this old monk’s head around the world. Longya’s natural endowment was keen; he carried a bellyful of Chan and traveled on foot, heading straight to Cuiwei in Chang’an, and asked, What is the meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West? Cuiwei said, Hand me the meditation board. Longya took the meditation board and gave it to Cuiwei. As soon as Cuiwei received it he struck him. Longya said, Strike if you like, but there is still no meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West. Then he asked Linji, What is the meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West? Linji said, Hand me the sitting mat. Longya took the sitting mat and gave it to Linji. As soon as Linji received it he struck him. Longya said, Strike if you like, but there is still no meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West. He set up this line of questioning; it is no harm if he wanted to see those old fellows on their bentwood and plank beds, and also to clarify for himself a great matter. It can be said his words were not empty, his triggers were not fired at random; it came from doing the work. Do you not see Wuxie visiting Shitou? He agreed beforehand: if one word matched, he would stay; otherwise he would leave. Shitou sat on his seat; Wuxie flicked his sleeves and went out. Shitou knew he was a vessel of Dharma, so he offered instruction. Wuxie did not take up its meaning, and took his leave and went to the gate. Shitou called out, Venerable. Wuxie turned his head. Shitou said, From birth to death, it is only this. Do not turn your head and swivel your brain looking for something else. Wuxie had a great awakening upon these words. Also, Magu carried his staff to Zhangjing, circled the meditation platform three times, shook the staff once, and stood upright. Zhangjing said, Yes, yes. Then he went to Nanquan. As before, he circled the platform, shook the staff, and stood. Nanquan said, It is not that it is not so, but this is turned by the force of wind; in the end it becomes ruin and decay. Magu said, Zhangjing said yes; why does the master say not? Nanquan said, Zhangjing is indeed yes; but yes is not you. The ancients were not averse to lifting and sustaining this one matter until it was thoroughly released. Nowadays, as soon as people are questioned, there is not the slightest place where they have applied effort. Today it is only like this; tomorrow it is only like this. If you are only like this all the way to the end of the future, you still will not have a finishing day. You must shake yourself awake and rouse your spirit; only then will you have a small measure of accord. Look at Longya raising a single question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West? Cuiwei said, Hand me the meditation board. Longya handed it over to Cuiwei. Cuiwei received it and struck him. When Longya took up the meditation board at that time, could he not have known Cuiwei meant to strike him? Yet he could not simply say Cuiwei did not understand. Why then did he hand over the meditation board to him? Tell me, if he could have taken responsibility right on the spot, how should it have been? He did not apply it in living water, but went into dead water to make a living scheme, always making himself the master. So he said, Strike if you like, but there is still no meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West. Then he ran off to Hebei to visit Linji, and asked in the same way. Linji said, Hand me the sitting mat . Longya handed it to Linji. Linji received it and struck him. Longya said, Strike if you like. But there is still no meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West. Tell me, those two venerables were not of the same Dharma lineage; why were their replies alike, and their use the same? You must know the ancients: one word, one phrase, they did not act at random. Later, when he was abbot, a monk asked, Master, back then when you met those two venerables, did you approve of them or not? Longya said, Approve, then approve, but there is still no meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West. There are thorns in rotten mud; letting it pass on to others, he has already fallen into the second. This old fellow held it firmly, but only managed to be an elder of the Dongshan line. If he were under Deshan or Linji, you must know there would be another way of life. But if it were this mountain monk, it would not be so: I would only tell him, Approve, and yet not approve; but there is still no meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West. Do you not see a monk asking Damei, What is the meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West? Damei said, Coming from the West has no meaning. Yanguan heard and said, One coffin. Two dead fellows. Xuansha heard and said, Yanguan is a genuine hand. Xuedou said, There are three of them too. If, when this monk asked about the meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West, you instead told him Coming from the West has no meaning, and you understood it like that, you would fall into the realm of nothing-to-do. Therefore it is said: you must investigate the living phrase, do not investigate the dead phrase. If you realize it under the living phrase, through endless kalpas you will not forget. If you realize it under the dead phrase, you cannot even save yourself. Longya speaking like this is not without excellence. The ancients said continuity is very difficult. Those ancients, one word and one phrase, did not act at random. Before and after illuminated each other; there was provisional and there was real; there was illumination and there was function; guest and host were distinct; they exchanged and crossed freely. If you want to discern what is truly intimate, Longya, though he did not obscure the tradition, still fell into the second. At that time those two venerables demanded the meditation board and the sitting mat; Longya could not but know their intent. They wanted to use what was in his own chest and bosom. Even so, their use was not without being too steep. Longya asked like this, the two elders answered like that; why then was there still no meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West? Here you must know there is another special point. Xuedou picked it up and showed it to people.
In Longya Mountain, the dragon has no eyes, in dead water Blind! You can fool others, sure. Washing a clod in mud—everyone under heaven knows it.

The meditation board and sitting mat cannot be used. Who can be made to say it? What do you want a Chan board and cushion for? Is this a charge to you, Venerable? text_zh: 雪竇據欵結案。他雖恁麼頌。且道意在什麼 處。甚處是無眼。甚處是死水裏。到這裏須是 有變通始得。所以道。澄潭不許蒼龍蟠。死 水何曾有獰龍。不見道。死水不藏龍。若是活 底龍。須向洪波浩渺白浪滔天處去。此言龍 牙走入死水中去。被人打。他却道打即任打。 要且無祖師西來意。招得雪竇道死水何曾 振古風。雖然如此。且道。雪竇是扶持伊是減 他威光。人多錯會道。為什麼。只應分付與盧 公。殊不知。却是龍牙分付與人。大凡參請。須 是向機上辨別。方見他古人相見處。禪板蒲 團不能用。翠微云。與我過禪板來。牙過與他。 豈不是死水裏作活計。分明是駕與青龍。只 是他不解騎。是不能用也。只應分付與盧公。 往往喚作六祖非也。不曾分付與人。若道分 付與人要用打人。却成箇什麼去。昔雪竇自 呼為盧公。他題晦迹自貽云。圖畫當年愛洞 庭。波心七十二峯青。而今高臥思前事。添得 盧公倚石屏。雪竇要去龍牙頭上行。又恐人 錯會。所以別頌要剪人疑解。雪竇復拈云。
text_en: Where is the lack of eyes? Where is the dead water? Here you must have adaptability for it to work. Therefore it is said, A clear pool does not allow a blue dragon to coil; dead water has never had a fierce dragon. Do you not see the saying: dead water does not hide a dragon. If it is a living dragon, it must go where the vast floods surge and the white waves billow to the sky. This means Longya ran into dead water. He was struck by others, yet he said, Strike if you like. But there is still no meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West, which drew Xuedou to say, how could dead water ever stir the ancient wind? Even so, tell me: is Xuedou supporting him, or diminishing his authority and radiance? Many people misunderstand, saying, Why should it only be handed over to Elder Lu? They do not realize it is Longya who is handing it over to others. In general, in inquiry and visitation, you must discern it on the pivot; only then do you see where the ancients met. The meditation board and sitting mat It can’t be used at all. Cuiwei said, “Pass me the chan board.” Ya handed it to him. Isn’t this making a living scheme in dead water? Plainly it’s being given a blue dragon to ride—only he doesn’t know how to ride it, so he can’t use it. It should simply be handed over to Lord Lu. It’s wrong to keep calling him the Sixth Patriarch. He never handed it over to anyone. If you say he did hand it over to someone, you’d have to use it to beat people—what would that turn into? Long ago Xuedou called himself Lord Lu. He inscribed “Hiding his tracks, he brings it on himself,” saying: “In paintings back then I loved Dong- ting Lake; in the heart of the waves the seventy-two peaks are green. Now I lie high at ease, thinking of past matters—adding Lord Lu leaning on a stone screen.” Xuedou wanted to walk on Longya’s head, yet feared people would misunderstand, so he made another verse to cut off people’s doubtful interpretations. Xuedou then again brought it up, saying:
“This old fellow still hasn’t been utterly finished off.” He then made another verse: “Though Lord Lu handed it over, what is there to rely on?” Clearly so—how many can know it? On your own

text_zh: 這老漢。也未得勦絕。復成一頌灼然。能有幾人知。自 知較一半。賴有末後句盧公付了亦何憑盡大地討恁麼人也難得。教誰領話 坐倚休將繼祖燈草裏漢。打入黑山下坐。落在鬼窟裏去也堪對暮 雲歸未合一箇半箇。舉著即錯。果然出不得遠山無限碧層 層塞却爾眼塞却爾耳。沒溺深坑。更參三十年。
text_en: knowing is somewhat better. Luckily there is the final line. Across the whole earth it is hard to find such a person—who can be made to take up the words? “Whether sitting or leaning, don’t take up the Patriarchs’ lamp to pass on; it can face the evening A grass-side fellow—strike him down to sit beneath Black Mountain; he falls into a ghost cave. clouds returning before they fully gather—distant mountains, endless blue, layer One and a half of one—raise it and it is wrong; indeed you cannot get out. upon layer.” Plug up your eyes, plug up your ears; drown in a deep pit—study another thirty years.
“Though Lord Lu handed it over, what is there to rely on?” What evidence is there to rely on? You must understand it right here like this—

text_zh: 盧公付了亦何憑。有何憑據。直須向這裏恁 麼會去。更莫守株待兔。髑髏前一時打破。無 一點事在胸中。放教灑灑落落地。又何必要 憑。或坐或倚。不消作佛法道理。所以道。坐倚 休將繼祖燈。雪竇一時拈了也。他有箇轉身 處。末後自露箇消息。有些子好處道。堪對暮 雲歸未合。且道雪竇意在什麼處。暮雲歸欲 合未合之時。爾道作麼生。遠山無限碧層層。 依舊打入鬼窟裏去。到這裏得失是非。一時 坐斷灑灑落落。始較些子。遠山無限碧層層。 且道是文殊境界耶。是普賢境界耶。是觀音 境界耶。到此且道是什麼人分上事。
text_en: and don’t cling to the stump waiting for a rabbit. Smash through it once right in front of the skull; with not a speck of anything in your chest, let it be free and unencumbered—then what need is there to rely on anything? Whether sitting or leaning, there’s no need to make Buddhist doctrines out of it. That’s why it says: sitting or leaning, don’t take up the Patriarchs’ lamp. Xuedou brought it up in one stroke. He has a place to turn around— and at the very end he reveals a bit of news himself. There’s a little something good in it, saying: it can face the evening clouds returning before they fully gather. Tell me—where is Xuedou’s intent? When the evening clouds return, about to gather yet not gathered, what do you say then? Distant mountains, endless blue, layer upon layer. Still you crash right into the ghost cave. When you reach here, gain and loss, right and wrong—all at once are cut off, free and unencumbered—only then is it somewhat close. Distant mountains, endless blue, layer upon layer. Tell me, is this Manjushri’s realm? Samantabhadra’s realm? Avalokiteshvara’s realm? When you get to this point, tell me—whose business is it?

text_zh: 智門若是應機接物。猶較些子。若是截斷眾 流。千里萬里。且道這蓮花。出水與未出水。是 一是二。若恁麼見得。許爾有箇入處。雖然如 是。若道是一。顢頇佛性儱侗真如。若道是二。 心境未忘落在解路上走有什麼歇期。且道 古人意作麼生。其實無許多事。所以投子道 爾但莫著名言數句。若了諸事自然不著即 無許多位次不同。爾攝一切法。一切法攝 爾不得。本無得失夢幻如許多名目不可強 與他安立名字。誑諕爾諸人得麼。爾諸人問 故所以有言。爾若不問。教我向爾道什麼即 得。一切事。皆是爾將得來。都不干我事。古人 道。欲識佛性義當觀時節因緣。不見雲門舉 僧問靈雲云。佛未出世時如何。雲竪起拂子。 僧云。出世後如何。雲亦竪起拂子。雲門云。前 頭打著。後頭打不著。又云不說出與不出。何 處有伊問時節也。古人一問一答。應時應節 無許多事。爾若尋言逐句。了無交涉。爾若能 言中透得言。意中透得意。機中透得機。放令 閑閑地。方見智門答話處。問佛未出世時如 何。牛頭未見四祖時如何。斑石內混沌未分 時如何。父母未生時如何。雲門道。從古至今。 只是一段事。無是無非。無得無失。無生與未 生。古人到這裏。放一綫道有出有入。若是未 了底人。扶籬摸壁。依草附木。或教他放下。又 打入莽莽蕩蕩荒然處去。若是得底人。二六 時中。不依倚一物。雖不依倚一物。若露一機 一境。作麼生摸索他。這僧問道。蓮花未出水 時如何。智門云。蓮花。便只攔問一答。不妨奇 特。諸方皆謂之顛倒語。那裏如此。不見嵒頭 道。常貴未開口已前。猶較些子。古人露機處。 已是漏逗了也。如今學者。不省古人意。只管 去。理論出水與未出水。有什麼交涉。不見僧 問智門。如何是般若體。門云。蚌含明月。僧云 如何是般若用。門云。兔子懷胎。看他如此對 答。天下人討他語脈不得。或有人問夾山道。 蓮花未出水時如何。只對他道。露柱燈籠。且 道與蓮花是同是別。出水後如何。對他道。杖 頭挑日月。脚下太泥深。爾且道是不是。且莫 錯認定盤星。雪竇忒殺慈悲。打破人情解。所 以頌出。
text_en: whole current, it’s a thousand miles, ten thousand miles away. Tell me—this lotus, emerged from the water and not yet emerged from the water—are they one or two? If you can see it like that, I’ll grant you a way in. Even so, if you say it is one, that’s muddled buddha-nature and vague true suchness. If you say it is two, mind and object aren’t forgotten—you fall onto the road of explanation and run along it; when will there ever be rest? Tell me, what was the ancients’ intent? In truth there aren’t so many things. That’s why Touzi said: “Just don’t cling to famous phrases. If you understand all matters, naturally you won’t cling, and then there aren’t so many different ranks and positions. You encompass all dharmas; all dharmas encompass you—yet cannot take hold of you. Originally there is no gain or loss; dreams and illusions—so many labels—you must not force names onto them. Can that kind of deception scare you people?” You people ask— therefore there are words. If you didn’t ask, what could I possibly tell you? Everything is something you bring in yourselves; it has nothing to do with me. The ancients said, “If you want to know the meaning of buddha-nature, you should observe the seasons and conditions.” Haven’t you seen Yunmen cite: A monk asked Lingyun, “What about before the Buddha appeared in the world?” Lingyun held up his whisk. The monk said, “After he appeared in the world, what then?” Lingyun also held up his whisk. Yunmen said, “At the front you hit it; at the back you can’t hit it.” He also said, “Don’t speak of appearing or not appearing—where is there any ‘when’ for him to ask about?” The ancients’ one question, one answer—responding in time, responding in season— there aren’t so many matters. If you chase words and run after phrases, it has nothing to do with it. If you can penetrate words within words, intent within intent, pivot within pivot—then let it be easy and unhurried; only then will you see where Zhimen’s answer lies. Asking “Before the Buddha appeared in the world, what about?” “Before Niutou met the Fourth Patriarch, what about?” “Before chaos within the mottled stone was differentiated, what about?” “Before your parents were born, what about?” Yunmen said, “From ancient times to the present, it’s just one stretch of affair—no right, no wrong; no gain, no loss; no born and not-yet-born. When the ancients got here, they let out a thread, saying there is exit and entry. If you’re someone who hasn’t understood, you prop yourself on fences and grope walls, clinging to grass and leaning on trees. Maybe someone tells you to put it down, and then you’re knocked into a vast, boundless, desolate place. If you’re someone who has gotten it, in the twenty-four hours you don’t rely on a single thing. Though you don’t rely on a single thing, if you reveal a single pivot and a single scene, how will you grope for it? This monk asked, “When the lotus has not yet emerged from the water, what about?” Zhimen said, “Lotus.” It was just a single question, a single answer—no harm in being striking. Everywhere people call it inverted speech—how could that be? Haven’t you seen Yantou say, “It’s always prized before the mouth opens; that’s still somewhat close.” Where the ancients reveal their pivot, they’re already leaking and giving it away. Students nowadays don’t understand the ancients’ intent—they just go on theorizing about emerging from the water and not yet emerging—what does that have to do with it? Haven’t you seen a monk ask Zhimen, “What is the substance of prajna?” Zhimen said, “A clam holds the bright moon.” The monk asked, “What is the function of prajna?” Zhimen said, “A rabbit is with child.” Look at answers like this— no one under heaven can find his verbal thread. Or suppose someone asked Jiashan, “When the lotus has not yet emerged from the water, what about?” You could just answer, “Dewy pillars and lanterns.” Now tell me, are they the same as the lotus or different? After it emerges from the water, what about? Answer him, “On the staff-tip, the sun and moon are carried aloft; underfoot the mud is too deep.” Tell me—is it so or not? For now don’t mistake the fixed star for your reference point. Xuedou is outrageously compassionate—he smashes human-sentiment interpretations, so he brings forth the verse:

text_zh: 智門本是浙人。得得入川參香林。既徹。却回 住隋州智門。雪竇是他的子。見得好窮玄極 妙。直道蓮花荷葉報君知。出水何如未出時。 這裏要人直下便會。山僧道。未出水時如何。 露柱燈籠。出水後如何。杖頭挑日月。脚下太 泥深。爾且莫錯認定盤星。如今人咬人言句 者。有甚麼限。爾且道出水時是什麼時節。未 出水時是什麼時節。若向這裏見得。許爾親 見智門。雪竇道。爾若不見。江北江南問王老。 雪竇意道。爾只管去江北江南。問尊宿出水 與未出水。江南添得兩句。江北添得兩句。一 重。添一重。展轉生疑。且道何時得不疑去。如 野狐多疑。氷凌上行。以聽水聲。若不鳴方可 過河。參學人若一狐疑了一狐疑。幾時得平 穩去。
text_en: and lived at Zhimen in Suizhou. Xuedou was his disciple. He saw it well, plumbing the mysterious to the utmost, reaching the wondrous. He went straight to: “Lotus and lotus leaf report it to you—how is it when it emerges from the water, and when it has not yet emerged?” Here it requires that people understand immediately. This mountain monk says: when it has not yet emerged from the water, what about? Dewy pillars and lanterns. After it emerges from the water, what about? On the staff-tip, the sun and moon are carried aloft; underfoot the mud is too deep. For now don’t mistake the fixed star for your reference point. Nowadays people bite and chew on other people’s phrases— what limit is there? Tell me: when it emerges from the water, what season is that? When it has not yet emerged from the water, what season is that? If you can see it here, I’ll grant you personally meeting Zhimen. Xuedou said: if you don’t see it, north of the river and south of the river, ask Old Wang. Xuedou’s meaning is: you just go north of the river and south of the river, asking venerable elders about emerging from the water and not yet emerging. South of the river you add two lines; north of the river you add two lines—one layer adds another layer, and doubt arises again and again. Tell me, when will you be rid of doubt? Like a wild fox, full of suspicion, walking on ice ridges, listening for the sound of water—only if it doesn’t sound can it cross the river. If a practitioner has one doubt after another doubt, when will they ever get steady and secure?

text_en: Feng traveled together with Yantou and Qinshan. In all, they went three times to Touzi, and nine times up to Dongshan. Later he visited Deshan, and only then smashed the lacquer bucket. One day he led Yantou to call on Qinshan. They were snowed in at the Ao Mountain inn. Yantou spent every day just sleeping. Xuefeng sat in meditation the whole time. Yantou shouted, “Go on, sleep and eat!” On the bed every day, just like the village earth god of seven hamlets. One of these days, you’ll bewitch the men and women of people’s homes and lead them off. Xuefeng pointed to his own chest and said, “In here I’m not yet steady; I dare not deceive myself.” Yantou said, “I thought that later you’d go to the top of a solitary peak and knot together a grass hut, spreading the great teaching—yet you’re still talking like this.” Xuefeng said, “I truly am not steady.” Yantou said, “If it’s really like that, then from your point of view, bring it all out, one by one. Where it’s right, I’ll confirm it for you; where it’s not, I’ll cut it off for you.” So Xuefeng raised the case of Yanguan in the hall expounding the meaning of form and emptiness, and found an entry point. Yantou said, “From this for thirty years—on no account bring it up.” Xuefeng brought up another: Dongshan’s verse on crossing the stream. He found an entry point. Yantou said, “If it’s like that, you can’t save yourself.” Later he went to Deshan. He asked about the matter of the ancestral school: “Does a student still have a share in it or not?” Deshan struck him with his staff. “Say what?” At that moment I felt as if the bottom dropped out of a bucket. Yantou then shouted, “Haven’t you heard: what comes in through the gate isn’t the family treasure.” Xuefeng said, “Afterwards what then is it?” Yantou said, “If someday you want to spread the great teaching, let it all come flowing out from your own chest. For me, cover heaven and cover earth with it.” Xuefeng, on hearing this, had a great awakening. He bowed in homage. Rising, he cried out again and again, “Only today is it that I’ve realized the Way at Ao Mountain! Only today is it that I’ve realized the Way at Ao Mountain!” Later he returned to Fujian and lived at Xianggu Mountain. He composed a verse for himself, saying: “A human life flashes by, only a brief moment; in the floating world, how could one stay long? Leaving the passes, I had just turned thirty-two; entering Fujian, I was already over forty. It’s not that he doesn’t use it—he keeps raising it again and again; but once it’s passed, it should be removed at once. I report to all the court’s crimson-and-purple nobles: King Yama isn’t afraid of your gold fish pendants.” Whenever he ascended the hall to instruct the assembly, he said: “Each and every one covers heaven and covers earth. I won’t talk of the abstruse or the wondrous; nor will I talk of mind or nature. Suddenly it stands alone, revealed—like a great mass of fire: come near and it scorches your face. Like the Tai’e sword: if you so much as aim at it, you lose body and life. If you pause to think and halt your workings, then there’s no connection at all. Take Baizhang asking Huangbo, “Where are you coming and going?” Huangbo said, “Coming and going to pick mushrooms below Mount Daxiong.” Baizhang said, “Did you see a great beast?” Huangbo made a tiger’s roar. Baizhang lifted an axe and made a chopping gesture. Huangbo then slapped Baizhang once. Baizhang, humming and laughing, returned and mounted the seat, telling the assembly, “On Mount Daxiong there is a great beast. All of you must watch carefully. Today this old monk personally ran into it.” Zhaozhou, whenever he saw a monk, would ask, “Have you ever been here?” If they said, “I have,” or if they said, “I haven’t,” Zhaozhou would always say, “Go drink tea.” The prior said, “Master, you regularly ask monks whether they’ve been here or not, and you always say ‘Go drink tea.’ What’s the point?” Zhaozhou said, “Prior.” The prior answered. Zhaozhou said, “Go drink tea.” Zihu set up a sign at his gate. On the sign it read: “Zihu has a dog. It takes people’s heads above, their waists in the middle, their feet below. If you deliberate, you lose body and life.” Or when a newcomer had just met him, the master would shout, “Watch the dog!” As soon as the monk turned his head, the master would return to the abbot’s quarters. Just like Xuefeng saying, “On South Mountain there is a turtle-nosed snake. You people must watch carefully.” Right at such a time, how would you respond? Don’t step in the tracks of those before. Try saying it. Here you must understand a phrase beyond the standards to make it. As for all the language of public cases, once you bring it up, you immediately know where it falls. Look at how he instructed the assembly like this: I won’t talk to you about practice or explanation. Can you still measure it with feelings and intellect? If you are his descendants, naturally you can say it just right. Therefore the ancients said: take up words and you must understand the aim; don’t set up your own rules. Speech must be beyond the standards; phrases must pass through the barrier. If your words don’t leave the ruts and holes, you fall into a sea of poison. Xuefeng instructing the assembly like this can be called tasteless talk—blocking people’s mouths. Changqing and Xuansha were both people of his own household; only then could they understand him speaking like this. Just take Xuefeng’s saying, “On South Mountain there is a turtle-nosed snake.” Do you people know where it lands? Here you must possess the eye of one who comprehends in all directions to manage it. Isn’t there Zhenjing’s verse: “Beating drums, playing the pipa—two who understand meet; Yunmen can sing in response; Changqing can go along with it. The ancient tune has no melody; the turtle-nosed snake of South Mountain—who knows this meaning? Truly it is Xuansha.” Just as for Chang- qing responding like that—tell me, what does it mean? Here it is like striking stone for sparks, like a flash of lightning—only then can you approach it. If even the slightest trace doesn’t go away, then you can’t reach it. What a pity—many people give rise to emotional interpretations under Changqing’s words, saying that as soon as there is something heard in the hall, it’s already losing body and life. Some say, “There wasn’t a single thing to begin with—speaking like this out of the blue just makes people doubt.” When people hear him say “On South Mountain there is a turtle-nosed snake,” you immediately doubt. If you understand it like that, you’ll at least have no connection at all—only making a living calculation on his words. Since you don’t understand it that way, then how do you understand it? Later a monk brought it up to Xuansha. Xuan- sha said, “It must be Brother Leng.” Even so, I’m not like that. The monk said, “Then how are you?” Xuansha said, “What use is South Mountain? Just look—within Xuansha’s words there’s a place to emerge.” He then said, “What use is South Mountain? If it weren’t Xuansha, it would be very hard to answer. Just take him saying like that— “On South Mountain there is a turtle-nosed snake”—tell me, where is it? Here it must be someone of the upward way who can understand such talk. The ancients said, “On the fishing boat you thank Third-Lord Xie; you don’t love the turtle-nosed snake of South Mountain.” Then he went to Yunmen and jabbed his staff toward Xuefeng’s face, making a frightening gesture. Yunmen had the hands and feet of a snake-handler, not offending the sharp edge. He strikes the bright head and strikes the dark head. In his usual guidance of people, it’s like dancing the Tai’e sword. Sometimes it flies toward a person’s eyebrows and eyelashes; sometimes it flies three thousand miles away to take someone’s head. Yunmen jabbed his staff to make a frightening gesture—yet it’s not a trick with spirits. Wouldn’t that also be losing body and life? A true master of the school never makes his living on a single word or phrase. As for the scheme: Xuedou only because he loved that Yunmen had matched and confirmed Xuefeng’s intent, therefore he composed this verse. It comes out:
Elephant-bone crags are lofty; people do not reach there—whoever reaches there must be A thousand or ten thousand cannot grope it out—it is not your realm.

text_en: below there is Xianggu Cliff. Xuefeng’s pivot-words are lofty and steep; few people reach that place. Xuedou was one of his own household, like the same feathers and down: same sound responds, same energy seeks its match. It still requires those of broad understanding to confirm each other. As for this turtle-nosed snake, it’s not that it can’t be hard to handle—you must know how to handle it. If you don’t know how, instead you’ll be injured by the snake. The former master Wuzu said, “This turtle-nosed snake must have not- This is the move that damages hands and feet: grab him right at the seven-inch point, pinch and hold fast, and then the old monk takes you by the hand and walks with you. Changqing and Xuansha had this kind of skill. Xuedou said, Master Leng and Master Bei could do nothing about it. People mostly say Changqing and Xuansha could do nothing about it, so Xuedou alone praises Yunmen, making it seem unrelated. But they do not know that among the three, the pivot has no winning or losing; there is only closeness and distance. Tell me, everyone—what place is it where Master Leng and Master Bei could do nothing? How many lose their bodies and forfeit their lives because of it? In this verse, Changqing said, Today in the hall, many people lose their bodies and forfeit their lives. At this point you must have the hands of a snake-handler; only careful attention will do. Xuedou brings out his Yunmen, so he sweeps the rest aside for the moment and leaves only Yunmen standing, saying Shaoyang knows. He stirs the grass again, because Yunmen knew that Xuefeng said, On South Mountain there is a snouted-snake that falls there—so he stirs the grass again. When Xuedou’s verse reaches this point, there is something even subtler: It cannot be sought in north, south, east, or west. Tell me, where is it? Suddenly it pops out at the tip of the staff. It turns out it is only right here. You must not then go make a living scheme on the tip of the staff. Yunmen jabbed with his staff in front of Xuefeng’s face to put on a frightening display. Yunmen then used the staff as that snouted- snake. Sometimes he would say, The staff transforms into a dragon and swallows heaven and earth. Where do mountains, rivers, and the great earth come from? It is just one staff. Sometimes it is a dragon, sometimes it is a snake. Why is it like this? Only when you reach here do you know. The ancients said, The mind turns along with the ten thousand conditions; where it turns, it truly can be subtle. The verse says: He threw it down before Xuefeng, and Xuefeng opened his mouth wide. Opening the mouth wide is like lightning. Xuedou had talent to spare. He picked up Yunmen’s venomous snake and said: this opening the mouth wide, like lightning is just like it. If you deliberate, you will lose your body and forfeit your life. Even if you lift your eyebrows, you still do not see—where will you go? After Xuedou finished the verse, you must go to the living place to help people. Taking Xuefeng’s snake, he himself picks it up and plays with it; he can kill or bring to life as the moment demands. Want to see? He said, Now it is hidden in front of Ru Peak. Ru Peak is the name of Xuedou’s mountain. Xue- dou has a verse saying: The rocks look around on all sides and the blue sea is cramped; vast and lonely, it does not allow white clouds to be white. Changqing, Xuansha, and Yunmen—though they can handle it, it still cannot be seen. Yet he says, now it is hidden in front of Ru Peak; those who come should each look for themselves by skillful means. Xuedou is still entangled in fine points, not speaking and just using it. Then he shouted loudly, Watch your feet! From above until now, how many people have picked it up and played with it? Tell me—has it ever injured anyone or not? If it has not injured anyone, the master strikes.

text_en: realized together; saw together and heard together; picked up together and used together. One going out, one coming in—they pressed and shoved one another, because they were people from the same line. The moment it was raised, they knew where it landed. In Xuefeng’s community, the everyday questions and answers were just these three. The ancients, in walking, standing, sitting, and lying down, kept this Way in mind. Therefore, when it is raised, they know where it lands. One day while roaming the mountains, Baofu pointed with his hand and said, Right here is the summit of Miao Peak. Nowadays, if a Zen fellow is asked like this, his mouth just hangs open like a signboard eave. Luckily it was Changqing who was asked. Tell me: when Baofu spoke like that, what was he aiming for? The an- cients did this to test whether one has eyes or not. If you are one of his own people, you naturally know where it lands, and so you answer him: It is, it is—what a pity. Tell me, what was Changqing’s meaning in saying that? You must not just go on like this. Similar, indeed similar—rarely is there anything so casual with not the slightest matter. Fortunately Changqing saw through him. Xuedou added a remark: Today, roaming the mountains with this fellow—what are we aiming for? Tell me, where does it land? And again: A hundred or a thousand years later, it is not that there will be none; it is only that there will be few. Xuedou’s way of pointing to the chest is just like Huangbo saying, It is not that there is no Chan, it is only that there are no teachers. For Xuedou to speak like this is indeed steep and perilous. If they were not matching in the same voice, how could it be so solitary, precarious, and strange? This is called adding a remark: it falls on both sides. Though it falls on both sides, it does not stay on either side. Later it was brought up to Jing- qing. Jingqing said, If it were not Lord Sun, you would see skulls covering the wilds. Lord Sun was Changqing’s lay surname. Haven’t you seen a monk ask Zhaozhou, What is the solitary summit of Miao Peak? Zhaozhou said, This old monk will not answer you that. The monk said, Why won’t you answer that? Zhaozhou said, If I answered you, I fear it would fall onto flat ground. In the teachings they speak of the solitary summit of Miao Peak: Bhikshu Deyun never goes down the mountain. Sudhana went to visit him. For seven days he did not meet him; one day they met on another peak. And once they met, he spoke to him of one thought and the three times, all Buddhas, the light of wisdom, universally seeing the Dharma gate. If Deyun does not go down the mountain, why did they meet on another peak? If you say he went down the mountain, the teachings say Bhikshu Deyun never once went down the mountain, always on the solitary summit of Miao Peak. Up to here—where exactly were Deyun and Sudhana? Later, Layman Li tangled up the vines, and did it well, saying the solitary summit of Miao Peak is a single-flavored Dharma gate of equality: each and every one is true, each and every one is complete. It uniquely reveals itself in the place of no gain and no loss, no right and no wrong. Therefore Sudhana did not see it. When you reach the place that accords with nature, it is like the eye not seeing itself, the ear not hearing itself, the finger not touching itself; like a knife not cutting itself, fire not burning itself, water not washing itself. When you reach here, the teachings have a lot of old-woman-like helping. So they let out one thread, saying: in the gate of the second meaning, they set up guest and host, set up pivot and situation, set up questions and answers. Therefore they say, the Buddhas do not come forth into the world, and there is no nirvana; as expedient means to ferry beings, they therefore manifest such matters. Tell me, ultimately how can you avoid Jingqing and Xuedou speaking like this? Back then they could not match each other in crisp claps, so for all the people across the earth skulls cover the wilds. Jingqing realized it like this; how did those two use it like this? Xuedou’s later verse brings it out even more clearly. The verse says:

On the solitary summit of Miao Peak, the grasses are thick; having grasped it clearly, to whom will you hand it over? Sink away with your whole body—beneath your feet it is already several fathoms deep.

text_zh: 妙峯孤頂草離離和身沒却。脚下已深數丈也　拈得分明付 與誰用作什麼。大地沒人知。乾屎橛堪作何用。拈得鼻孔失却口不是孫公辨 端的錯看箭。著賊了也不知髑髏著地幾人知更不再活。如麻似粟。 闍黎拈得鼻孔失却口
text_en: To whom will you give it? What is it used for? No one on the great earth knows. What use is a dry shit-stick? When you pinch the nostrils, you lose the mouth. If it were not Lord Sun, who could discern what is truly so? You misread the arrow; the thief has already struck, and you do not even know it. When skulls hit the ground, how many people know? There is no second chance for life—like hemp and millet. The acharya grabs the nostrils and loses the mouth.
On the solitary summit of Miao Peak, the grasses are thick. Rolling in the grass—what end is there? Having grasped it

text_zh: 妙峯孤頂草離離。草裏輥有什麼了期。拈得 分明付與誰。什麼處是分明處。頌保福道只 這裏便是妙峯頂。不是孫公辨端的。孫公見 什麼道理。便云。是則是可惜許。只如髑髏著 地幾人知。汝等諸人還知麼瞎。
text_en: clearly, to whom will you hand it over? What place is the clear place? The verse is on Baofu saying, Right here is the summit of Miao Peak. If it were not Lord Sun discerning what is truly so—what did Lord Sun see as principle, that he then said, It is, it is—what a pity? Just as for skulls hitting the ground, how many people know? Do you all know or not? Blind!
24 Instruction: Stand on the lofty peak top—demons and outsiders cannot know. Walk on the deep sea bottom—

text_zh: 垂示云。高高峯頂立。魔外莫能知。深深海底 行。佛眼覷不見。直饒眼似流星。機如掣電。未 免靈龜曳尾。到這裏合作麼生。試舉看。
text_en: even the Buddha-eye cannot spy it. Even if your eyes are like shooting stars and your pivot is like a flash of lightning, you still cannot avoid the spirit turtle dragging its tail. When you reach here, what will you do? Try bringing it up.
Case 24: Liu Tiemuo arrived at Weishan. Weishan said, Old cow, It is fine that it is hard to come together. This old woman does not keep to her proper place.

text_zh: 【二四】舉。劉鐵磨到溈山不妨難湊泊。這老婆不守本分山云老牸 牛。汝來也點。探竿影草。向什麼處見聱訛磨云。來日臺山大 會齋。和尚還去麼箭不虛發。大唐打鼓新羅舞。放去太速收來太遲溈 山放身臥中也。爾向什麼處見溈山。誰知遠煙浪別有好思量磨便出 去過也。見機而作。
text_en: you have come. Tiemuo said, Tomorrow at Taishan there is a great A touch: probing with a pole, watching the grass and shadows—where will you see any clumsy error? assembly feast. Will the master go too? Wei- The arrow never misses. Great Tang beats the drum, Silla dances. Letting it go is too fast; drawing it back is too late. shan stretched out and lay down. Tiemuo then went out Hit the mark. Where are you going to see Guishan? Who would know that far-off mist and waves hold other fine reflections? and left. It passes. Act when you see the moment.
Liu Tiemo is like striking sparks from flint, like the flash of lightning. If you try to deliberate, you lose your body A nun, too.

text_zh: 劉鐵磨尼也如擊石火。似閃電光。擬議則喪身 失命。禪道若到緊要處。那裏有許多事。他 作家相見。如隔牆見角便知是牛。隔山見煙 便知是火。拶著便動。捺著便轉。溈山道。老僧 百年後。向山下檀越家。作一頭水牯牛。左脇 下書五字云。溈山僧某甲。且正當恁麼時。喚 作溈山僧。即是喚作水牯牛。即是。如今人問 著。管取分疎不下。劉鐵磨久參機鋒峭峻。人 號為劉鐵磨。去溈山十里卓庵。一日去訪溈 山。山見來便云。老牸牛。汝來也。磨云。來日 臺山大會齋。和尚還去麼。溈山放身便臥。磨 便出去。爾看他一如說話相似。且不是禪又 不是道。喚作無事會得麼。溈山去臺山。自隔 數千里。劉鐵磨因什麼却令溈山去齋。旦道 意旨如何。這老婆會他溈山說話。絲來線去。 一放一收。互相酬唱。如兩鏡相照。無影像可 觀。機機相副。句句相投。如今人三搭不迴頭。 這老婆一點也瞞他不得。這箇却不是世諦 情見。如明鏡當臺。明珠在掌。胡來胡現。漢來 漢現。是他知有向上事。所以如此。如今只管 做無事會。四祖演和尚道。莫將有事為無 事。往往事從無事生。爾若參得透去。見他恁 麼如尋常人說話一般。多被言語隔礙。所以 不會。唯是知音方會他底只如乾峯示眾云。 舉一不得舉二。放過一著落在第二。雲門出 眾云。昨日有一僧。從天台來却往南岳去。乾 峯云。典座今日不得普請。看他兩人。放則雙 放。收則雙收。溈仰下謂之境致。風塵草動。悉 究端倪。亦謂之隔身句。意通而語隔。到這裏。 須是左撥右轉方是作家。
text_en: and your life. When the Way of Chan reaches the crucial point, there are not so many affairs. They who are adepts meet like this: see horns over a wall and you know it is an ox; see smoke beyond a mountain and you know it is fire. Press it and it moves; hold it down and it turns. Guishan said, this old monk after a hundred years will go to a lay donor’s home below the mountain and become a water buffalo. Under the left flank there will be written five characters saying: “Monk so-and-so of Guishan.” Now right at that moment, if you call it a Guishan monk, that is calling it a water buffalo; that is it. When people today are questioned about it, you can be sure they cannot sort it out. Liu Tiemo has long practiced, her edge sharp and steep; people nicknamed her Liu the Iron Grinder. Ten li from Guishan she set up a hermitage. One day she went to visit Guishan; when Guishan saw her coming he said, “Old cow, you’ve come.” Tiemo said, “Tomorrow at Mount Tai there is a great assembly feast. Will the master go?” Guishan let his body go and lay down. Tiemo then went right out. Look at them—just like ordinary talk. Yet it is neither Chan nor the Way. Can you call this “understanding as nothing to do”? Guishan went to Mount Tai—separated by several thousand li. Why did Liu Tiemo make Guishan go to the feast? Just say: what is the meaning? This old woman understood Guishan’s words—thread coming, line going, one release, one gather—answering each other back and forth like two mirrors reflecting one another, with no image to be seen. Move matching move, phrase fitting phrase. People today can be prompted three times and still won’t turn their heads. This old woman could not hide a thing from him. But this is not worldly truth, not emotional views. It is like a bright mirror on its stand, a shining pearl in the palm: when a barbarian comes, a barbarian appears; when a Han comes, a Han appears. It is because they know there is a matter above, so it is like this. People today only keep on trying to make it into an “idle understanding.” Master Si-zu Yan said, “Do not take what has affairs and make it no-affairs; often affairs arise from no-affairs.” If you penetrate your investigation, you’ll see them speaking just like ordinary people. Most get blocked by words, and therefore do not understand. Only those who truly “know the tune” understand it. Consider Qianfeng addressing the assembly, saying, “Raise one and you cannot raise two; let one pass and you land on the second.” Yunmen stepped out from the crowd and said, “Yesterday there was a monk who came from Tiantai and went on to Nanyue.” Qianfeng said, “Today the cook may not do the general labor.” Look at those two: release and both release; gather and both gather. In the Guiyang line this is called “the state of affairs.” Wind, dust, the stirring of grass—all are thoroughly traced to their source. It is also called “a phrase separated by a body”: the intent is clear but the words are blocked. When you reach here, you must deflect left and turn right—only then are you an adept.
Once he rode an iron horse into the fortified city; the imperial decree went out, the news spread A veteran fighter, a true hand; a frontier general, with the seven necessities on his person.

text_zh: 曾騎鐵馬入重城慣戰作家。塞外將軍。七事隨身　勅下傳聞 六國清狗銜赦書。寰中天子。爭奈海晏河清猶握金鞭問歸客是什 麼消息一條拄杖兩人扶。相招同往又同來夜深誰共御街行君向瀟湘我向秦。 且道行作什麼
text_en: the six states are pacified. A dog holds an amnesty edict; the Son of Heaven within the realm—yet what can be done when seas are calm and rivers run clear? Still gripping a golden whip, he asks the returning traveler, What news is this? One staff, supported by two people—calling each other to go together and to return together. deep into the night, who will walk the imperial street together? You head for Xiaoxiang; I head for Qin. Tell me: what are you going for?
Xuedou’s verse: the various places take it as the utmost standard. Among the hundred verses, this one most

text_zh: 雪竇頌。諸方以為極則。一百頌中。這一頌最 具理路。就中極妙。貼體分明頌出。曾騎鐵 馬入重城。頌劉鐵磨恁麼來。勅下傳聞六國 清。頌溈山恁麼問。猶握金鞭問歸客。頌磨云。 來日臺山大會齋。和尚還去麼。夜深誰共御 街行。頌溈山放身便臥。磨便出去。雪竇有這 般才調。急切處向急切處頌。緩緩處向緩緩 處頌。風穴亦曾拈。同雪竇意。此頌諸方皆美 之。高高峯頂立。魔外莫能知。深深海底行。佛 眼覻不見。看他一箇放身臥。一箇便出去。若 更周遮。一時求路不見。雪竇頌意最好。是 曾騎鐵馬入重城。若不是同得同證。焉能恁 麼。且道得箇什麼意。不見僧問風穴。溈山道。 老牸牛汝來也。意旨如何。穴云。白雲深處金 龍躍。僧云。只如劉鐵磨道。來日臺山大會齋。 和尚還去麼。意旨如何。穴云碧波心裏玉兔 驚。僧云。溈山便作臥勢。意旨如何。穴云。老 倒疎慵無事日。閑眠高臥對青山。此意亦與 雪竇同也。
text_en: fully contains the reasoning, and within it is supremely subtle, close to the body and plainly expressed. “Once he rode an iron horse into the fortified city” praises Liu Tiemo coming like that. “The decree went out, the news spread, the six states are pacified” praises Guishan asking like that. “Still gripping a golden whip, he asks the returning traveler” praises Tiemo saying, “Tomorrow at Mount Tai there is a great assembly feast—will the master go?” “Deep into the night, who will walk the imperial street together?” praises Guishan letting his body go and lying down, and Tiemo going right out. Xuedou has this kind of talent: at urgent points he verses urgently; at slow points he verses slowly. Fengxue also once took this up, in the same spirit as Xuedou. Everywhere they praise this verse. “Stand on the highest peak—demons and outsiders cannot know. Walk on the ocean’s deepest floor—the Buddha eye cannot see.” Look at them: one lets his body go and lies down; one goes right out. If you add any fussing around, at once you cannot find the path. Xuedou’s intent in the verse is best: it is “Once he rode an iron horse into the fortified city.” If they were not of the same attainment and the same verification, how could it be like this? Tell me, what is the meaning? Have you not seen a monk ask Fengxue: “Guishan said, ‘Old cow, you’ve come.’ What is the meaning?” Fengxue said, “In the depths of white clouds a golden dragon leaps.” The monk said, “Then as for Liu Tiemo saying, ‘Tomorrow at Mount Tai there is a great assembly feast. Will the master go?’ What is the meaning?” Fengxue said, “In the heart of blue waves, the jade rabbit is startled.” The monk said, “Guishan then made the lying-down posture. What is the meaning?” Fengxue said, “The old fellow—slack and lazy on a day with nothing to do—idly sleeps and lies high, facing the green mountains.” This meaning too matches Xuedou’s.
25 The prefatory instruction says: If the pivot does not leave its place, you fall into the poisonous sea. If words do not startle the crowd, you sink into

text_zh: 垂示云。機不離位。墮在毒海。語不驚群。陷於 流俗。忽若擊石火裏別緇素。閃電光中辨殺 活。可以坐斷十方。壁立千仞。還知有恁麼時 節麼。試舉看。
text_en: common vulgarity. Suddenly—within the sparks from striking flint—distinguish black from white; within the flash of lightning—discern killing and bringing to life. You can sit and cut off the ten directions, stand like a cliff a thousand fathoms high. Do you know there is such a moment? Try bringing it up and see.

Case 25 raised: The hermitage master of Lotus Peak picked up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying, “When the ancients reached here, why were they unwilling to stay?” The assembly was silent, so he answered for them, saying, Look: right atop the head, there is a single eye.

text_zh: 【二五】舉。蓮花峯庵主。拈拄杖示眾云看。頂門上具一隻眼。 也是時人窠窟古人到這裏。為什麼不肯住不可向虛空裏釘橛。 權立化城眾無語千箇萬箇如麻似粟。却較些子。可惜許。一棚俊鶻自代云。 為他途路不得力若向途中辨。猶爭半月程。設使得力堪作什麼。豈可全無一 箇復云。畢竟如何千人萬人只向箇裏坐却。千人萬人中一箇兩箇會又 自代云。楖𣗖橫擔不顧人。直入千峯萬峯 去也好與三十棒。只為他擔板。腦後見腮。莫與往來。
text_en: It is also the den of people today. You must not drive a stake into empty space. Provisionally set up a conjured city. A thousand, ten thousand—like hemp and millet. Yet they still fall short by a bit—what a pity. A whole perch of fine falcons. “Because their road and path lacked power.” Again he said, “Ultimately, how is it?” and again If you try to sort it out on the road, you are still short by half a month’s journey. Even if you gained strength, what could you do? How could there be not even a single one? A thousand people, ten thousand people—just sit right here. Among a thousand or ten thousand, one or two might understand, answered for them, saying, “With a shoulder-pole across the arms, not looking back at people, he goes straight into a thousand peaks, ten thousand peaks and off he goes.” and they still deserve thirty blows—because they carry a plank, and you can see their cheeks from behind. Do not associate with them.
Can you all discern the hermitage master of Lotus Peak? His heels have not even touched

text_zh: 諸人還裁辨得蓮花峯庵主麼。脚跟也未點 地在。國初時在天台蓮花峯卓庵。古人既得 道之後。茅茨石室中。折脚鐺兒內。煮野菜根 喫過日。且不求名利。放曠隨緣。垂一轉語。且 要報佛祖恩。傳佛心印。纔見僧來。便拈拄杖 云。古人到這裏為什麼不肯住。前後二十餘 年。終無一人答得。只這一問。也有權有實。有 照有用。若也知他圈繢。不消一揑。爾且道因 什麼二十年如此問。既是宗師所為。何故只 守一橛。若向箇裏見得。自然不向情塵上走。 凡二十年中。有多少人。與他平展下語呈見 解。做盡伎倆。設有箇道得。也不到他極則處。 況此事雖不在言句中。非言句即不能辨。不 見道。道本無言因言顯道。所以驗人端的處。 下口便知音。古人垂一言半句。亦無他。只要 見爾知有不知有他見人不會。所以自代云。 為他途路不得力。看他道得。自然契理契機。 幾曾失却宗旨。古人云。承言須會宗。勿自立 規矩。如今人只管撞將去便了。得則得。爭柰 顢頇儱侗。若到作家面前。將三要語印空。 印泥印水驗他。便見方木逗圓孔。無下落處。 到這裏討一箇同得同證。臨時向什麼處求。 若是知有底人。開懷通箇消息。有何不可。若 不遇人。且卷而懷之。且問爾諸人。拄杖子是 衲僧尋常用底。因什麼却道途路不得力。古 人到此不肯住。其實金屑雖貴落眼成翳。石 室善道和尚。當時遭沙汰。常以拄杖示眾云。 過去諸佛也恁麼。未來諸佛也恁麼。現前諸 佛也恁麼。雪峯一日僧堂前拈拄杖示眾云。 這箇只為中下根人。時有僧出問云。忽遇上 上人來時如何。峯拈拄杖便去。雲門云。我即 不似雪峯打破狼籍。僧問未審和尚如何。雲 門便打。大凡參問也無許多事。為爾外見有 山河大地。內見有見聞覺知。上見有諸佛可 求。下見有眾生可度。直須一時吐却。然後十 二時中。行住坐臥。打成一片。雖在一毛頭上。 寬若大千沙界。雖居鑊湯爐炭中。如在安樂 國土。雖居七珍八寶中。如在茅茨蓬蒿下。這 般事。若是通方作者。到古人實處。自然不費 力。他見無人搆得他底。復自徵云。畢竟如何。 又柰何不得。自云。楖𣗖橫擔不顧人。直入千 峯萬峯去。這箇意又作麼生。且道指什麼處 為地頭不妨句中有眼。言外有意。自起自倒。 自放自收。豈不見嚴陽尊者。路逢一僧。拈起 拄杖云。是什麼。僧云。不識嚴云一條拄杖也 不識嚴復以拄杖。地上劄一下云。還識麼。僧 云。不識嚴云。土窟子也不識。嚴復以拄杖擔 云會麼。僧云不會。嚴云楖𣗖橫擔不顧人。直 入千峯萬峯去。古人到這裏。為什麼不肯住。 雪竇有頌云。誰當機舉不賺。亦還希。摧殘峭 峻銷鑠玄微。重關曾巨闢。作者未同歸。玉兔 乍圓乍缺。金烏似飛不飛。盧老不知何處去。 白雲流水共依依。因什麼山僧道。腦後見腮 莫與往來。纔作計較。便是黑山鬼窟裏作活 計。若見得徹信得及。千人萬人。自然羅籠不 住。柰何不得。動著拶著。自然有殺有活。雪竇 會他意道直入千峯萬峯去。方始成頌。要知 落處。看取雪竇頌云。
text_en: the ground. In the early days of the state he set up a hermitage on Lotus Peak at Tiantai. After the ancients attained the Way, in that thatched hut and stone chamber, in a three-legged pot, they boiled wild vegetable roots and ate to pass the days. They did not seek fame or profit, but were broad and free, going along with conditions. They offered a turning word, and wished to repay the kindness of Buddhas and patriarchs, transmitting the Buddha’s mind-seal. As soon as they saw a monk come, they would pick up the staff and say, “When the ancients reached here, why were they unwilling to stay?” For more than twenty years, in the end not one person could answer. Just this one question contains both provisional and real, both illumination and function. If you know his boundaries and sketch, you do not need even a pinch. Tell me, why for twenty years did he ask like this? Since it is what a lineage master does, why did he only guard a single stake? If you see within this, naturally you will not run after the dust of feelings. Over those twenty years, how many people laid out flat words for him, presenting their views and understanding, exhausting every trick. Even if someone did speak, it still would not reach his utmost. Besides, though this matter is not in words and phrases, without words and phrases you still cannot discern it. Have you not seen it said: the Way is originally without words; through words the Way is revealed. Therefore, where you test someone’s genuineness, the moment they open their mouth you know whether they know the tune. When ancients offered a word or half a phrase, it was for nothing else—only wanting to see whether you know there is or do not know there is. Seeing people did not understand, he answered for them, saying, “Because their road and path lacked power.” See how he said it—naturally it accords with principle and matches the occasion. How could it ever miss the main point? The ancients said, “Receiving words, you must understand the source; do not set up your own rules.” People today just crash straight in—that’s all. If they get it, they get it; but how can they help being dull and muddled? If you come before an adept, he uses the three essential phrases to stamp emptiness, stamp mud, stamp water, to test you—then you see a square peg shoved into a round hole, with nowhere to land. When you reach here and seek someone of the same attainment and the same verification, where can you look at the moment? If you are someone who knows there is, open your heart and get the message through—what is impossible? If you do not meet the right person, then roll it up and keep it in your breast. Let me ask you all: a staff is what a patch-robed monk uses every day—why then say the road and path lack power? The ancients, upon reaching here, were unwilling to stay. In truth, though gold dust is precious, if it gets into the eye it becomes a film. Master Shandao of Stone Chamber, in his time, suffered dismissal and suppression. He often used his staff to show the assembly, saying, “The Buddhas of the past are also like this; the Buddhas of the future are also like this; the Buddhas of the present are also like this.” One day Xuefeng, in front of the monks’ hall, picked up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying, “This is only for people of middling and lesser capacities.” At the time a monk came forward and asked, “If one suddenly meets a superior person, what then?” Xuefeng picked up the staff and left. Yunmen said, “I am not like Xuefeng, smashing things into a mess.” The monk asked, “Then how is it with you, master?” Yunmen struck him. In general, inquiry and investigation are not so many affairs: because outwardly you see there are mountains, rivers, and the great earth; inwardly you see there are seeing, hearing, awareness, and knowing; above you see there are Buddhas to seek; below you see there are beings to save. You must spit it all out at once. Then, through the twelve double-hours—walking, standing, sitting, lying down—forge it into one piece. Though it is on the tip of a single hair, it is vast as a great thousand-world of sands. Though you dwell in boiling cauldrons and burning coals, it is like being in the Land of Ease. Though you dwell among the seven treasures and eight jewels, it is like being under thatch and weeds. These kinds of matters—if you are a broad and complete adept, when you reach the ancients’ real place, naturally there is no need to expend power. Seeing that no one could get a grip on him, he again questioned himself, saying: Ultimately, how is it? Yet it still can’t be helped. He said to himself: Carry the staff crosswise on the shoulder, paying no mind to anyone, and go straight into a thousand peaks, ten thousand peaks. What then is the meaning of this? Tell me, what place does it point to as the home ground? It’s fine if within the line there is an eye, and beyond the words there is intent. Rising by itself, falling by itself. Letting go by itself, gathering in by itself. Haven’t you seen Venerable Yanyang? On the road he met a monk and lifted up his staff, saying: What is this? The monk said: I don’t recognize it. Yanyang said: You don’t even recognize a single staff, either. Yanyang again jabbed the staff into the ground once and said: Do you recognize it now? The monk said: I don’t recognize it. Yanyang said: You cave-dweller, you don’t recognize it either. Yanyang again shouldered the staff and said: Do you understand? The monk said: I don’t understand. Yanyang said: Carry the staff crosswise on the shoulder, pay no mind to anyone, and go straight into a thousand peaks, ten thousand peaks. When the ancients reached this point, why were they unwilling to stay? Xuedou has a verse, saying: Who can raise it right on the spot without being cheated? Even that is rare. Ravaging the sheer cliffs, it melts away the dark subtlety. The double barrier once opened wide; the doers have not returned together. The jade rabbit suddenly full, suddenly lacking; the golden crow seems to fly and yet not fly. Old Lu, no one knows where he went. White clouds and flowing water, both lingering on. Why does this mountain monk say: If you can see the cheeks behind the head, do not associate with him. The moment you start calculating and comparing, you’re making your living in a ghost cave on Black Mountain. If you see through it and can truly trust it, then among a thousand people, ten thousand people, you naturally cannot be netted in and held. It still can’t be helped. Once you touch it, once you’re pressed up against it, there is naturally killing and there is living. Xuedou understood his meaning in the words, go straight into a thousand peaks, ten thousand peaks, and only then made this verse. If you want to know where it lands, look at Xuedou’s verse:
Dust and sand in the eyes, dirt in the ears, a thousand peaks, Dull and muddled under three hundred eaves; blundering and crashing—what limit is there? There are still fellows like this.

text_zh: 眼裏塵沙耳裏土懞憧三百檐。鶻鶻突突有什麼限。更有恁麼漢　千峯 萬峯不肯住爾向什麼處去。且道是什麼消息落花流水太茫 茫好箇消息。閃電之機。徒勞佇思。左顧千生右顧萬劫剔起眉毛何處 去脚跟下更贈一對眼。元來只在這裏。還截得庵主脚跟麼。雖然如是。也須是到這田地始得。打云。 為什麼只在這裏
text_en: ten thousand peaks, unwilling to stay. Where are you going? Tell me, what news is this? Falling blossoms, flowing water, so vast and boundless. Fine news indeed: the moment of a lightning flash. Waiting and thinking is wasted effort—look left, a thousand lives; look right, ten thousand kalpas. Lift the eyebrows—where do you go? Under the heels, add another pair of eyes. It turns out it is only here. Can you still cut off the hermit’s heel? Even so, you must reach this ground for it to work. He struck and said: Why is it only here?
Xuedou’s verse is extremely good. There is a place to turn the body, not keeping to one corner. So he says: Dust and sand in the eyes,

text_zh: 雪竇頌得甚好。有轉身處。不守一隅。便道眼 裏塵沙耳裏土。此一句頌蓮花峯庵主。衲僧 家到這裏。上無攀仰下絕己躬。於一切時中 如癡似兀。不見南泉道。學道之人。如癡鈍者 也難得。禪月詩云。常憶南泉好言語。如斯癡 鈍者還希。法燈云。誰人知此意。令我憶南泉。 南泉又道。七百高僧。盡是會佛法底人。唯有 盧行者不會佛法。只會道。所以得他衣鉢。且 道佛法與道相去多少。雪竇拈云。眼裏著沙 不得。耳裏著水不得。或若有箇漢。信得及把 得住。不受人瞞。祖佛言教是什麼熱碗鳴聲。 便請高掛鉢囊。拗折拄杖。管取一員無事道 人。又云。眼裏著得須彌山。耳裏著得大海水。 有一般漢。受人商量。祖佛言教。如龍得水。似 虎靠山。却須挑起鉢囊。橫擔拄杖。亦是一員 無事道人。復云。恁麼也不得。不恁麼也不 得。然後沒交涉。三員無事道人中。要選一人 為師。正是這般生鐵鑄就底漢。何故或遇惡 境界。或遇奇特境界。到他面前。悉皆如夢相 似。不知有六根。亦不知有旦暮。直饒到這般 田地。切忌守寒灰死火。打入黑漫漫處去。也 須是有轉身一路始得。不見古人道。莫守寒 巖異草青。坐却白雲宗不妙。所以蓮花峯庵 主道。為他途路不得力。直須是千峯萬峯去 始得。且道喚什麼作千峯萬峯。雪竇只愛他 道楖𣗖橫擔不顧人。直入千峯萬峯去。所以 頌出。且道向什麼處去。還有知得去處者麼。 落花流水太茫茫。落花紛紛。流水茫茫。閃電 之機。眼前是什麼。剔起眉毛何處去。雪竇為 什麼也不知他去處。只如山僧道適來舉拂 子。且道即今在什麼處。爾諸人若見得。與蓮 花峯庵主同參。其或未然。三條椽下。七尺單 前。試去參詳看。
text_en: dirt in the ears. This one line is a verse about the Hermit of Lotus Peak. When a patch-robed monk reaches this point, above there is nothing to cling to, below he cuts off himself. At all times, he is like a fool, like a blockhead. Don’t you see how Nanquan said: People who study the Way—those who are like fools and dullards are hard to come by. Chan-yue’s poem says: I often recall Nanquan’s fine words; such fools and dullards are still rare. Fadeng said: Who understands this meaning, making me recall Nanquan? Nanquan also said: Seven hundred eminent monks all understand the Buddha-dharma; only Layman Lu does not understand the Buddha-dharma—he only understands the Way. Therefore he received the robe and bowl. Now tell me: how far apart are the Buddha-dharma and the Way? Xuedou raised it, saying: You can’t put sand in the eyes, It won’t do. You can’t get water into your ears. If there is some fellow who can truly believe it and take hold of it, hold fast and not be deceived by others. What are the words and teachings of patriarchs and buddhas but the clatter of a hot bowl? Then please hang up your bowl-bag high, snap your staff in two, and I guarantee you’ll be one carefree person of the Way. He also said: Put Mount Sumeru into the eyes; put the water of the great sea into the ears. There is another kind of fellow who accepts others’ judgments: the words and teachings of patriarchs and buddhas are like a dragon getting water, like a tiger leaning on a mountain. Then he should pick up the bowl-bag, shoulder the staff crosswise—he too is a carefree person of the Way. He added: Like this won’t do; not like this won’t do either. Only then is there no involvement. Among these three carefree people of the Way, you must choose one to be your teacher. It must be exactly this sort of man cast from raw iron. Why? Whether he encounters a bad circumstance or an extraordinary circumstance, before him it is all just like a dream. He does not know of the six faculties; he does not know of morning or evening. Even if you reach such a state, you must strictly avoid guarding cold ashes and dead fire and plunging into a pitch-black place. You must have a single road for turning the body. Haven’t you seen the ancients say: Do not guard cold cliffs where strange grasses grow green; sitting out the White Cloud lineage is not good. Therefore the Hermit of Lotus Peak said: Because his road lacked strength, he had to go straight into a thousand peaks, ten thousand peaks for it to work. Now tell me: what do you call a thousand peaks, ten thousand peaks? Xuedou only loved his saying: Carry the staff crosswise on the shoulder, pay no mind to anyone, go straight into a thousand peaks, ten thousand peaks. Therefore he composed the verse. Now tell me: where do you go? Is there anyone who knows the place you go to? Falling blossoms, flowing water—so vast. Blossoms falling in profusion, flowing water boundless. In the instant of a lightning flash, what is right before your eyes? Lift the eyebrows—where do you go? Why does Xuedou not know his whereabouts? Just as this mountain monk just now raised the whisk, tell me: where is it right now? If you people can see it, then together with the Hermit of Lotus Peak, you can study together. If not, then under the three rafters, before the seven-foot bed, go and investigate it.
