text_zh: 陸亘大夫久參南泉。尋常留心於理性中。游 泳肇論。一日坐次。遂拈此兩句。以為奇特。問 云。肇法師道。天地與我同根。萬物與我一體。 也甚奇怪。肇法師。乃晉時高僧。與生融叡。同 在羅什門下。謂之四哲。幼年好讀莊老。後因 寫古維摩經。有悟處。方知莊老猶未盡善。故 綜諸經。乃造四論。莊老意謂。天地形之大也。 我形亦爾也。同生於虛無之中。莊生大意。只 論齊物。肇公大意論性皆歸自己。不見他論 中道。夫至人空洞無象。而萬物無非我造。會 萬物為自己者。其唯聖人乎。雖有神有人有 賢有聖。各別而皆同一性一體。古人道。盡乾 坤大地。只是一箇自己。寒則普天普地寒。熱 則普天普地熱。有則普天普地有。無則普天 普地無。是則普天普地是。非則普天普地非。 法眼云。渠渠渠。我我我。南北東西皆可可。不 可可。但唯我無不可。所以道。天上天下唯我 獨尊。石頭因看肇論。至此會萬物為自己處。 豁然大悟。後作一本參同契。亦不出此意。看 他恁麼問。且道。同什麼根。同那箇體。到這 裏。也不妨奇特。豈同他常人。不知天之高地 之厚。豈有恁麼事。陸亘大夫恁麼問。奇則甚 奇。只是不出教意。若道教意是極則。世尊何 故更拈花。祖師更西來作麼。南泉答處。用衲 僧巴鼻。與他拈出痛處。破他窠窟。遂指庭前 花。召大夫云。時人見此一株花。如夢相似。如 引人向萬丈懸崖上打一推。令他命斷。爾若 平地上推倒彌勒佛下生。也只不解命斷。亦 如人在夢。欲覺不覺被人喚醒相似。南泉若 是眼目不正。必定被他搽糊將去。看他恁麼 說話。也不妨難會。若是眼目定動。活底聞得。 如醍醐上味。若是死底聞得翻成毒藥。古人 道。若於事上見。墮在常情。若向意根下卜度。 卒摸索不著。巖頭道。此是向上人活計。只露 目前些子。如同電拂。南泉大意如此。有擒 虎兕定龍蛇底手脚。到這裏也須是自會始 得。不見道。向上一路千聖不傳。學者勞形如 猿捉影。看他雪竇頌出。
text_en: through Sengzhao’s Treatise. One day while sitting, he raised these two lines, taking them to be extraordinary, and asked He said, Master Zhaolun declared: Heaven and earth and I share the same root; the ten thousand things and I are one body. It is indeed strange. Master Zhaolun was a great monk of the Jin era, together with Sengzhao, Sengrong, and Sengrui, sharing studies under Kumarajiva; they were called the Four Sages. In his youth he loved reading Zhuangzi and Laozi; later, because he copied the old Vimalakirti Sutra and had an awakening, he then realized that Zhuangzi and Laozi were still not fully adequate. Therefore he synthesized the sutras and composed the Four Treatises. The intent of Zhuangzi and Laozi is that heaven and earth are vast in form; my form is likewise, and we are born together within emptiness. Zhuangzi’s main point only argues the leveling of things. Lord Zhao’s main intent discusses nature as all returning to oneself; he does not take up their doctrine of the Middle Way. As for the utmost person: empty and open, without appearance, and the myriad things are none other than what I make. To gather the myriad things as oneself—only a sage can do that. Though there are spirits, there are humans, there are worthies and there are sages—distinct, yet all share one nature, one body. The ancients said: throughout the whole heavens and earth, it is just one single self. When cold, all heaven and all earth are cold. When hot, all heaven and all earth are hot. When there is, all heaven and all earth are. When there is none, all heaven and all earth are none. When it is, all heaven and all earth are it. When it is not, all heaven and all earth are not. Fayan said: You, you, you; I, I, I. North, south, east, and west are all acceptable; not acceptable, acceptable. Yet only I have nothing that is not acceptable. Therefore it is said: in heaven above and earth below, only I alone am honored. Shitou, because he read Zhao’s Treatise, came to this point of taking the myriad things as oneself. He suddenly had a great awakening. Later he wrote a version of the Cantongqi, which also does not depart from this meaning. Look at how he asks: tell me, the same as what root, the same as which body? When you get to here, it is not without its strangeness. How could it be like ordinary people who do not know the height of heaven or the thickness of the earth? How could there be such a thing? Minister Lu Geng asked in this way—strange indeed, very strange—yet it still does not go beyond the meaning of the teachings. If you say the meaning of the teachings is the ultimate standard, then why did the World-Honored One pick up the flower again? Why did the patriarch come from the West? Where Nanquan answered, he used the monks’ noses to point out the sore spot, to smash his nest and burrow. Then he pointed to the flowers in the courtyard and called to the minister. People today see this single flowering plant as if in a dream, as if leading someone to a ten-thousand-zhang cliff and giving a shove, cutting off his life. If you knock down Maitreya’s descent on level ground, you still will not understand life being cut off. It is also like someone in a dream: about to wake yet not waking, when someone calls him awake. If Nanquan had crooked eyes, he would certainly have been smeared over and led away by him. Watch him speak like this—it is not without being hard to grasp. If one’s eyes are steady and lively, the living hear it. It is like the finest flavor of ghee. If the dead hear it, it turns into poison. The ancients said: if you see it in terms of events, you fall into ordinary feelings. If you divine it from the root of thought, in the end you cannot find it. Yantou said: this is the livelihood of one who goes upward; it only reveals a little right before the eyes, like a lightning flash. Nanquan’s main intent is like this: he has the hands and feet to seize tigers and rhinoceroses, to settle dragons and snakes. When you get here, you still must understand for yourself before it works. Haven’t you heard: the one road upward is not transmitted by a thousand sages. Learners toil their bodies like an ape snatching at shadows. Look at Xuedou’s verse.

text_en: to him: Do not permit night-travel; cast yourself into the light and you must arrive. Tell me, what kind of moment is this? A holeless flute strikes a felt clapper-board—this is called a question that tests the host; it is also called a question of the mind’s conduct. Throughout the various places, both Touzi and Zhaozhou were praised for attaining the eloquence that surpasses the crowd. Though the two elders inherited different lines, see how their sharp points meet as if in one boat. Touzi one day, for Zhaozhou’s sake, set out a tea seat to receive him. He personally passed steamed cakes to Zhaozhou; Zhaozhou did not take them. Touzi had an attendant pass over sesame cakes to Zhaozhou; Zhaozhou paid respect to the attendant with three bows. Tell me, what was his meaning? See how it is all aimed at the root itself, lifting up this fundamental matter to work for people. A monk asked: What is the Way? He answered, Way. What is Buddha? He answered, Buddha. Again asked: When the golden lock has not yet been opened, how is it? He answered: Open. When the golden rooster has not yet crowed, how is it? He answered: There is no such sound. After it crows, how is it? He answered: Each knows in their own time. Touzi’s whole life, his questions and answers were always like this. Look at Zhaozhou’s question: When someone who has died the great death comes back to life, how is it? He immediately said: Do not permit night-travel; cast yourself into the light and you must arrive. Straight down, it is like striking flint for fire, like a flash of lightning. Only one who goes upward is fit for it. A person who has died the great death has no Buddha-dharma, no principles, no mysteries, no gain or loss, right or wrong, long or short. When you reach here, you only rest like this. The ancients called it: countless dead people on level ground. To pass through the thorn forest is the skilled hand. You must also penetrate through to the other side before it works. Even so, for people today to reach this kind of field is already hard to come by. If there is reliance or interpretive understanding, then it has nothing to do with it. Master Zhe called this “seeing not pure and clean.” The former teacher, Fifth Patriarch, called it “the life-root not cut off.” You must die the great death once, and only then can you live again. Master Yongguang of Zhe said: if the edge of words is off, it misses by ten thousand li. You must let go at the cliff’s edge, and willingly take responsibility yourself; after utter cutting off, revive again— you cannot deceive anyone. It is an extraordinary meaning—how could a person hide it? Zhaozhou’s question has this intent. Touzi is a master hand and did not fail what was asked. It is just that he cuts off feeling and cuts off traces; it is not without being hard to grasp. He only reveals a bit right in front. Therefore the ancients said: if you want intimacy, do not use a question to question. The question is in the answer; the answer is in the question. If it were not Touzi, faced with Zhaozhou’s one question, it would be very hard to respond. Only because he is a master hand—raise it and he immediately knows where it lands. text_en: Yet this monk would not accept it. If someone now came out and asked Huanglong, tell me how would he dispatch it? After a long pause he said: To settle in Zen you need not have mountains and waters; extinguish the fire in your mind and it naturally becomes cool. Everyone, tell me, where does Dongshan's circling and painting fall? If you can clearly discern it, then you will know that under Dongshan the Five Positions interchange, using upright and inclined to meet people. It is not without its strangeness. Only upon reaching this upward realm can it be like this. There is no need to arrange anything; it is naturally just right. Hence it is said: The inclined within the upright: at the first night of the third watch the moon is bright before you. Do not blame meeting without recognition; faintly there still lingers the old days' dislike. The upright within the inclined is lost: a morning old woman meets an ancient mirror; clearly face to face, yet there is no truth. Do not further lose your head and take shadows for the real. Coming from within the upright: within the empty there is a road that leaves the dust, only do not touch the present taboo, and you surpass the previous dynasty's tongue-cut talent. Reaching within the inclined: two blades cross in combat and there is no need to avoid; a good hand is like a lotus in fire, naturally possessing a soaring-to-heaven energy. Arriving in the mutual: not falling into being or nonbeing, who dares to respond? Everyone entirely wants to leave the common stream; but when it is folded together, you return to sit in the coals. The record of Fushan Yuanlu says: This koan is the pattern of the Five Positions. If you understand one of them, the rest naturally are easy to understand. Yantou said: It is like a gourd on the water; press it and it turns. It does not take the slightest effort. Once a monk asked Dongshan: When Manjushri and Samantabhadra come to study, what then? Dongshan said: Drive them into the herd of water buffalo. The monk said: The master enters hell like an arrow. Dongshan said: It is entirely due to his power. Dongshan said: Why not go to the place with no cold and heat? This is the upright within the inclined. The monk said: What is the place with no cold and heat? Dongshan said: When it is cold, cold kills the venerable; when it is hot, heat kills the venerable one. This is the inclined within the upright. Though upright, it is inclined; though inclined, it is complete. In the Caodong Record it is recorded in detail. If it were under Linji, there would not be so many complications; such a case would be understood straightaway. Some say: Great, no cold and heat. What is there to grasp? The ancients said: If you walk on the blade of a sword, it is quick; if you look through feelings and consciousness, it is slow. Do you not see a monk asking Cuiwei: What is the meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West? Cuiwei said: Wait until no one is here, then I will tell you. Then he went walking into the garden. The monk said: Here there is no one. Please speak, master. Cuiwei pointed to the bamboo and said: This single stalk of bamboo Thus long—how did that single bamboo pole become thus short? At this the monk suddenly awakened. Again Caoshan asked a monk, “It’s so hot—where will you go to avoid it?” The monk said, “In a cauldron of boiling soup, in a brazier of coals to avoid it.” Caoshan said, “How do you avoid it in boiling soup and furnace coals?” The monk said, “All sufferings cannot reach there.” Look at the people of his own household—naturally they understand their own household’s way of speaking. Xuedou used this “household matter” and brought it out in verse.

Letting down a hand is still like a ten-thousand-fathom cliff. If you’re not a genuine hand, who can tell it apart? Where is it not perfectly interfused? Once the king’s edict goes forth, the feudal lords clear the road.

text_en: enter the world, one’s eyes gaze into the clouds and sky. If one enters the world, one is ash-headed and dirt-faced. Gazing into the clouds and sky is the peak-top of ten thousand fathoms; ash-headed and dirt-faced is the business of letting down a hand. Sometimes ash-headed and dirt-faced is right on the ten-thousand-fathom peak; sometimes the ten-thousand-fathom peak is precisely ash-headed and dirt-faced. In truth, entering the marketplace with lowered hands is the same as standing alone on a solitary peak. Returning to the source and realizing one’s nature is no different from discriminating wisdom. Absolutely avoid making two stakes of it. Therefore it is said: letting down a hand is still like a ten-thousand-fathom cliff—truly there is nowhere for you to cozy up and dock. Upright and inclined—why must it be arranged? When it comes time to use it, it is naturally like this; it is not a matter of arrangement. This verse praises the place where Dongshan answered. Later it says: the ancient crystal hall shines in the bright moon; unable to hold back a grin, the Han hound runs up the steps in vain. This directly praises this monk chasing after words. In the Dongshan school there are things like the stone woman, the wooden horse, the bottomless basket, the night-shining pearl, the dead snake, and eighteen such kinds. In general they only clarify the proper position, like the moon shining on the crystal hall—seeming to have a round reflection. Dongshan answered, “Why not go to the place without cold or heat?” That monk was just like the Han hound chasing a clod, hurrying up the steps to grab the moon’s reflection. He asked again, “What is the place without cold or heat?” Dongshan said, “When it’s cold, cold kills the monk; when it’s hot, heat kills the monk.” Like the Han hound chasing a clod, he ran up the steps, yet again did not see the moon’s reflection. The “Han hound” comes from the Strategies of the Warring States: it says the Han clan’s hound is a swift dog; Zhongshan’s rabbit is a crafty rabbit; only that hound can track that rabbit. Xuedou cites this as a metaphor for this monk. Now as for all of you— do you recognize where Dongshan meets people? After a long pause he said, “What rabbit are you hunting for?”

text_zh: 禾山垂示云。習學謂之聞。絕學謂之隣。過此 二者。是為真過。此一則語。出寶藏論。學至無 學。謂之絕學。所以道。淺聞深悟。深聞不悟。 謂之絕學。一宿覺道。吾早年來積學問。亦曾 討疏尋經論。習學既盡。謂之絕學無為閑道 人。及至絕學。方始與道相近。直得過此二學。 是謂真過。其僧也不妨明敏。便拈此語問禾 山。山云。解打鼓。所謂言無味語無味。欲明這 箇公案。須是向上人方能見此語不涉理性。 亦無議論處。直下便會。如桶底脫相似。方是 衲僧安穩處。始契得祖師西來意。所以雲門 道。雪峯輥毬。禾山打鼓。國師水碗。趙州喫 茶。盡是向上拈提。又問。如何是真諦。山云。 解打鼓。真諦更不立一法。若是俗諦萬物俱 備。真俗無二。是聖諦第一義。又問。即心即佛 即不問。如何是非心非佛。山云。解打鼓。即心 即佛即易求。若到非心非佛即難。少有人到。 又問。向上人來時如何接。山云。解打鼓。向上 人即是透脫灑落底人。此四句語諸方以為 宗旨。謂之禾山四打鼓。只如僧問鏡清。新年 頭還有佛法也無。清云。有。僧云。如何是新年 頭佛法。清云。元正啟祚萬物咸新。僧云。謝師 答話。清云。老僧今日失利。似此答話。有十八 般失利。又僧問淨果大師。鶴立孤松時如何。 果云。脚底下一場懡㦬。又問雪覆千山時如 何。果云。日出後一場懡㦬。又問。會昌沙汰 時。護法神向什麼處去。果云。三門外兩箇漢 一場懡㦬。諸方謂之三懡㦬。又保福問僧。殿 裏是什麼佛。僧云。和尚定當看。福云。釋迦老 子。僧云。莫瞞人好。福云。却是爾瞞我。又問 僧云。爾名什麼。僧云。咸澤。福云。或遇枯涸 時如何。僧云。誰是枯涸者。福云。我。僧云。和 尚莫瞞人好。福云。却是爾瞞我。又問僧。爾作 什麼業。喫得恁麼大。僧云。和尚也不小。福作 蹲身勢。僧云。和尚莫瞞人好。福云。却是爾瞞 我。又問浴主。浴鍋闊多少。主云。請和尚量 看。福作量勢。主云。和尚莫瞞人好。福云。却 是爾瞞我。諸方謂之保福四瞞人。又如雪峯 四漆桶。皆是從上宗師。各出深妙之旨接人 之機。雪竇後面引一落索。依雲門示眾。頌出 此公案。
text_en: these two is called true passing.” This saying comes from the Treatise on the Treasury. Learning reaches no learning—this is called cutting off learning. Therefore it is said, “Shallow hearing, deep awakening; deep hearing, no awakening.” This is called cutting off learning. In one night he awakened to the Way: “In my early years I accumulated learning, and also sought commentaries and searched sutras and treatises. When practiced learning is exhausted, it is called cutting off learning—an idle person of the Way without contrivance. Only upon reaching cutting off learning does one begin to be close to the Way, truly passing beyond these two learnings. This is called true passing. That monk was quite sharp, so he took up these words and asked Heshan. Heshan said, “Able to beat the drum.” This is what is meant by “words have no flavor, phrases have no flavor.” If you want to understand this koan, you must be a person of the upward way; only then can you see that these words do not touch principle or nature, and there is no place for argument. Understand it directly, like the bottom falling out of a bucket—only then is it the secure place for a patch-robed monk. Then you first accord with the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West. Therefore Yunmen said, “Xuefeng rolls a ball; Heshan beats a drum; the National Teacher’s water bowl; Zhaozhou drinks tea”—all of it is taking up and presenting the upward matter. He asked again, “What is true truth?” Heshan said, “Able to beat the drum.” True truth does not establish a single dharma. If it is conventional truth, all things are fully present. True and conventional are not two—this is the first principle of the holy truths. He asked again, “Mind itself is Buddha I won’t ask about. What is neither mind nor Buddha?” Heshan said, “Able to beat the drum.” Mind itself is Buddha is easy to seek; but when it comes to neither mind nor Buddha, it is difficult—few people reach it. He asked again, “When a person of the upward way comes, how do you receive him?” Heshan said, “Able to beat the drum.” A person of the upward way is one who is thoroughly free and unbound. These four lines are taken by the monasteries everywhere as the essential point, and are called Heshan’s “four drum-beatings.” For example, a monk asked Jingqing, “At the start of the New Year is there still Buddhadharma or not?” Jingqing said, “There is.” The monk said, “What is the Buddhadharma at the start of the New Year?” Jingqing said, “At the first of the year the mandate opens; all things are wholly renewed.” The monk said, “Thank you, master, for answering.” Jingqing said, “Today this old monk has lost profit.” With answers like this there are eighteen kinds of “lost profit.” Again, a monk asked Master Jingguo, “When a crane stands on a lone pine, how is it?” Jingguo said, “Under your feet—one ‘mo.’” He asked again, “When snow covers a thousand mountains, how is it?” Jingguo said, “After the sun rises—one ‘mo.’” He asked again, “During the Huichang suppression of Buddhism, where did the Dharma-protecting spirits go?” Jingguo said, “Two fellows outside the three gates— one ‘mo.’” The monasteries everywhere call these the “three mo’s.” Again, Baofu asked a monk, “In the hall what Buddha is it?” The monk said, “The master will surely see.” Baofu said, “Old Shakyamuni.” The monk said, “Don’t go fooling people.” Baofu said, “It’s you who are fooling me.” Again he asked the monk, “What’s your name?” The monk said, “Xianze.” Baofu said, “If you encounter drying up what then?” The monk said, “Who is the one dried up?” Baofu said, “Me.” The monk said, “Master, don’t go fooling people.” Baofu said, “It’s you who are fooling me.” Again he asked the monk, “What work do you do to eat so much and get so big?” The monk said, “The master isn’t small either.” Baofu took a squatting posture. The monk said, “Master, don’t go fooling people.” Baofu said, “It’s you who are fooling me.” Again he asked the bath manager, “How wide is the bath cauldron?” The manager said, “Please, master, measure it.” Baofu made a measuring gesture. The manager said, “Master, don’t go fooling people.” Baofu said, “It’s you who are fooling me.” The monasteries everywhere call these Baofu’s “four foolings.” And then there’s Xuefeng’s “four lacquer buckets.” All of these are from the ancient masters, each bringing forth profound and subtle intent to meet people according to the occasion. After this, Xuedou adds a single tightening pull; following Yunmen’s instruction to the assembly, he versifies this koan.

text_en: said, “To tug the stone.” Guizong said, “Tug the stone as you like, but you must not disturb the central tree.” Mujing, whenever a newcomer arrived, would first have him carry three rounds of earth. Mujing had a verse and told the assembly, “East Mountain’s road is narrow, West Mountain is low; newcomer, don’t refuse the three rounds of mud. Alas, you’ve been on the road for days on end—clearly you don’t understand, yet you end up confused.” Later a monk asked, “Inside the three rounds I won’t ask about; outside the three rounds, how is it?” Mujing said, “The Iron-Wheel King’s edict throughout the realm.” The monk had no words, and Mujing struck him. Therefore it is said: one tug at a stone, two kinds of earth; to release the trigger must be a thousand-jun crossbow. Xuedou uses the thousand-jun crossbow as a metaphor for these words—if you want to see where he meets people. Thirty jin make one jun; one thousand jun is thirty thousand jin. If it’s a savage dragon, tigers, wolves, and fierce beasts, only then do you use this crossbow. If it’s some tiny little thing like a wren, you surely must not release it lightly. Thus a thousand-jun crossbow is not triggered for a field mouse. “The elephant-boned old master once rolled a ball” refers to when Xuefeng one day saw Xuansha coming and rolled three wooden balls at once. Xuansha immediately made a chopping-the-plaque gesture; Xuefeng deeply approved of it. Although all of it is the full functioning of great use, none of it compares to Heshan who can beat the drum—so direct and cutting through. It’s just hard to understand. Therefore Xuedou said, “How could it compare to He- shan who can beat the drum.” Yet he feared people would only stay on the phrase-head, making a living off it, not knowing the reason for it. Blundering and crude. Therefore it is said: I tell you, do not be reckless and crude. It too must truly reach this stage. If you want to not be crude, sweet is sweet, bitter is bitter. Though Xuedou thus toys with it, in the end he still cannot jump out of it.

text_zh: 垂示云。要道便道。舉世無雙。當行即行。全機 不讓。如擊石火。似閃電光。疾焰過風。奔流度 刃。拈起向上鉗鎚。未免亡鋒結舌。放一線道。 試舉看。

Sure enough, seven vertical and eight horizontal; he yanks down the net that fills the sky. Do you still see Zhaozhou? A patchrobed monk once pinched his nostrils—do you know where Zhaozhou lands? If you see it here, then it’s “above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored.” When water arrives, the channel forms; when wind moves, grass lies down. If not, this old monk is right under your heels.

text_zh: 若向一擊便行處會去。天下老和尚鼻孔一 時穿却。不奈爾何。自然水到渠成。苟或躊躇。 老僧在爾脚跟下。佛法省要處。言不在多。語 不在繁。只如這僧問趙州。萬法歸一。一歸何 處。他却答道。我在青州作一領布衫重七斤。 若向語句上辨。錯認定盤星。不向語句上辨。 爭奈却恁麼道。這箇公案。雖難見却易會。雖 易會却難見。難則銀山鐵壁。易則直下惺惺。 無爾計較是非處。此話與普化道來日大悲 院裏有齋話。更無兩般。一日僧問趙州。如何 是祖師西來意。州云。庭前柏樹子。僧云。和尚 莫將境示人。州云。老僧不曾將境示人。看他 恁麼向極則轉不得處轉得。自然蓋天蓋地。 若轉不得。觸途成滯。且道他有佛法商量也 無。若道他有佛法。他又何曾說心說性。說玄 說妙。若道他無佛法旨趣。他又不曾辜負爾 問頭。豈不見。僧問木平和尚。如何是佛法大 意。平云。這箇冬瓜如許大。又僧問古德。深山 懸崖逈絕無人處。還有佛法也無。古德云。有。 僧云。如何是深山裏佛法。古德云。石頭大底 大小底小。看這般公案。誵訛在什麼處。雪竇 知他落處。故打開義路。與爾頌出。
text_en: pierced through at once, and there is nothing they can do to you. Naturally, when water arrives, the channel is formed. But if you hesitate, this old monk is right beneath your heels. The essentials of Buddhadharma are not in many words; speech is not in being elaborate. Just consider this monk asking Zhaozhou: All dharmas return to the one; where does the one return? He instead answered: In Qingzhou I made a cloth robe; it weighed seven jin. If you discriminate in the words and phrases, you mistake the fixed pole star. If you do not discriminate in the words and phrases, then how will you deal with his speaking like this? This koan: though hard to see, it is easy to understand; though easy to understand, it is hard to see. Hard means silver mountains and iron cliffs; easy means directly clear and awake. There is no place for your calculating right and wrong. These words are just like Puhua saying, Tomorrow at the Great Compassion Monastery there will be a meal; there is nothing else. One day a monk asked Zhaozhou: What is the meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West? Zhaozhou said, The cypress in the courtyard. The monk said, Master, do not use a thing as a scene to point it out to people. Zhaozhou said, This old monk has never used a scene to point it out to people. See how he thus can turn right at the utmost, where turning is impossible; naturally it covers heaven and covers earth. If you cannot turn, then wherever you go you get stuck. Tell me: does he have any Buddhadharma to discuss or not? If you say he has Buddhadharma, when did he ever speak of mind or speak of nature, speak of the mysterious or speak of the subtle? If you say he has no purport of Buddhadharma, he never let down your question. Haven't you seen: a monk asked Master Muping, What is the great meaning of Buddhadharma? Muping said, This winter melon is this big. Another monk asked an ancient worthy: In the deep mountains, on sheer cliffs, in a remote place with no people, is there still Buddhadharma or not? The ancient worthy said, There is. The monk said, What is Buddhadharma in the deep mountains? The ancient worthy said, Stones: the big are big, the small are small. Look at such koans: where is the distortion? Xuedou knew where it lands, so he opened up the road of meaning and gave you a verse.
Bianbi once pressed the old ancient awl; a seven-jin robe, heavy. Why must you press this old fellow? Where are you trying to shove and press him to?

text_zh: 十八問中。此謂之編辟問。雪竇道。編辟曾挨 老古錐。編辟萬法。教歸一致。這僧要挨拶他 趙州。州也不妨作家。向轉不得處有出身之 路。敢開大口便道。我在青州作一領布衫。重 七斤。雪竇道。這箇七斤布衫能有幾人知。如 今拋擲西湖裏。萬法歸一。一亦不要。七斤布 衫亦不要。一時拋在西湖裏。雪竇住洞庭翠 峯。有西湖也。下載清風付與誰。此是趙州示 眾。爾若向北來。與爾上載。爾若向南來。與爾 下載。爾若從雪峯雲居來。也是箇擔板漢。雪 竇道。如此清風堪付阿誰。上載者。與爾說心 說性。說玄說妙。種種方便。若是下載。更無許 多義理玄妙。有底擔一擔禪。到趙州處。一點 也使不著。一時與他打疊。教灑灑落落無一 星事。謂之悟了還同未悟時。如今人盡作無 事會。有底道。無迷無悟。不要更求。只如佛未 出世時。達磨未來此土時。不可不恁麼也。用 佛出世作什麼。祖師更西來作什麼。總如此 有什麼干涉。也須是大徹大悟了。依舊山是 山水是水。乃至一切萬法悉皆成現。方始作。 箇無事底人。不見龍牙道學道。先須有悟由。 還如曾鬪快龍舟。雖然舊閣閑田地。一度贏 來方始休。只如趙州這箇七斤布衫話子。看 他古人恁麼道。如金如玉。山僧恁麼說。諸人 恁麼聽。總是上載。且道作麼生是下載。三條 椽下看取。
text_en: the old ancient awl. Bianbi means to marshal the ten thousand dharmas and make them return to one. This monk wanted to press Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou too was a seasoned hand: where turning is impossible, he has a road of coming forth. He dared to open his big mouth and say: In Qingzhou I made a cloth robe; it weighed seven jin. Xuedou said: This seven-jin cloth robe, how many people can know it? Now toss it into West Lake. All dharmas return to one, and even the one is not wanted. The seven-jin cloth robe is not wanted either. In one stroke toss it into West Lake. Xuedou lived at Dongting, on Cuifeng; he too has a West Lake. Below, the clear wind: to whom will it be entrusted? This is Zhaozhou instructing the assembly: If you come from the north, I will give you the upper load; if you come from the south, I will give you the lower load. If you come from Xuefeng or Yunju, you are also a plank-carrying fellow. Xuedou said: Such a clear wind, to whom is it fit to entrust? The upper load means I speak to you of mind and speak of nature, speak of the mysterious and the subtle, all kinds of expedients. If it is the lower load, there is no such mass of abstruse principle and mystery. Some carry a load of Zen; when they arrive at Zhaozhou, they cannot use even the slightest bit. All at once he packs it up for them, making it open and loose, with not a single speck of business. This is called: after awakening, still the same as before awakening. People nowadays all take it as meaning there is nothing to do. Some say: no delusion, no awakening; do not seek further. But just consider: before the Buddha appeared in the world, before Bodhidharma came to this land, you could not help but be like this. What use is it for the Buddha to appear in the world? What use for the Patriarch to come from the West? If it is all like this, what does it matter? Yet you must have great penetration and great awakening; then as before, mountains are mountains and waters are waters, and all the ten thousand dharmas entirely appear. Only then do you begin to be a person of no affairs. Haven't you seen Longya say: Studying the Way, first you must have a cause for awakening. It is like you once raced dragon boats: though it is an old pavilion and idle ground, you must win once before you can rest. Take Zhaozhou's phrase about the seven-jin cloth robe: see how the ancients spoke like this, like gold, like jade. This mountain monk speaks like this; you all listen like this: it is all the upper load. Tell me then, what is the lower load? Under three rafters, look and see.

text_zh: 垂示云。一槌便成超凡越聖。片言可折。去縛 解粘。如氷凌上行。劍刃上走。聲色堆裏坐。聲 色頭上行。縱橫妙用則且置。剎那便去時如 何。試舉看。
text_en: and loosening sticking. Like walking on icicles, running on a sword edge. Sit amid heaps of sound and form; walk upon the heads of sound and form. Set aside the wondrous functioning of freedom; when in an instant you must go, how is it then? Try bringing it up and see.

text_zh: 【四六】舉。鏡清問僧。門外是什麼聲等閑垂一釣。不患聾問什麼 僧云。雨滴聲不妨實頭。也好箇消息清云。眾生顛倒迷 己逐物事生也。慣得其便。鐃鈎搭索。還他本分手脚僧云。和尚作麼 生果然納敗缺。轉槍來也。不妨難當。却把槍頭倒刺人清云。洎不迷己咄直得分 疎不下僧云。洎不迷己意旨如何拶著這老漢。逼殺人。前箭 猶輕後箭深清云。出身猶可易。脫體道應難養子之緣。雖 然如是。德山臨濟向什麼處去。不喚作雨滴聲。喚作什麼聲。直得分疎不下洎巨至切及也。
text_en: The monk said, The sound of raindrops. Jingqing said, Sentient beings are inverted, deluded It can be downright real. That’s also good news. about themselves and chase after things. The monk said, Master, then how Trouble arises. Used to taking advantage, he hooks and lassoes with a jingling hook—return his proper hands and feet. should it be? Jingqing said, Then do not be deluded about yourself. The monk said, If one is not deluded about oneself, what is the meaning? Jingqing said, Coming forth is still easy; speaking the Way after shedding the body is hard indeed. Sure enough he takes in the flaw and turns the spear around. It’s hard to handle—and then he reverses the spearhead to stab people. Tsk! So straight you can separate but can’t get any distance. Pressing this old fellow, he forces people to death. The first arrow is still light; the later arrow strikes deep. The affinity of raising a child—although it is so, where did Deshan and Linji go? If you don’t call it the sound of raindrops, what do you call it? So straight you can’t separate or keep apart. It is enormous—right up close and immediate.

text_zh: 只這裏也好薦取。古人垂示一機一境。要接 人。一日鏡清問僧。門外是什麼聲。僧云。雨滴 聲。清云。眾生顛倒迷己逐物。又問。門外什麼 聲。僧云。鵓鳩聲。清云。欲得不招為間業。莫 謗如來正法輪。又問。門外什麼聲。僧云。蛇咬 蝦䗫聲。清云。將謂眾生苦。更有苦眾生。此語 與前頭公案。更無兩般。衲僧家於這裏透得 去。於聲色堆裏不妨自由。若透不得。便被聲 色所拘。這般公案。諸方謂之煅煉語。若是煅 煉只成心行。不見他古人為人處。亦喚作透 聲色。一明道眼。二明聲色。三明心宗。四明忘 情。五明展演。然不妨子細。爭奈有窠臼在。鏡 清恁麼問。門外什麼聲。僧云。雨滴聲。却道。 眾生顛倒迷己逐物。人皆錯會。喚作故意轉 人。且得沒交涉。殊不知鏡清有為人底手脚。 膽大不抅一機一境。忒殺不惜眉毛。鏡清豈 不知是雨滴聲。何消更問。須知古人以探竿 影草。要驗這僧。這僧也善挨拶便道。和尚又 作麼生直得。鏡清入泥入水向他道。洎不迷 己。其僧迷己逐物。則故是鏡清為什麼也迷 己。須知驗他句中便有出身處。這僧太懞懂 要勦絕此話。更問道。只箇洎不迷己意旨如 何。若是德山臨濟門下棒喝已行。鏡清通一 線道。隨他打葛藤。更向他道。出身猶可易。脫 體道應難。雖然恁麼。古人道。相續也大難。他 鏡清只一句。便與這僧明脚跟下大事。雪竇 頌云。
text_en: people. One day Jingqing asked a monk, What sound is outside the gate? The monk said, The sound of raindrops. Jingqing said, Sentient beings are inverted, deluded about themselves and chase after things. He asked again, What sound is outside the gate? The monk said, The sound of a turtledove. Jingqing said, If you want not to invite karmic obstruction, do not slander the Tathagata's true Dharma wheel. He asked again, What sound is outside the gate? The monk said, The sound of a snake biting a shrimp. Jingqing said, You think sentient beings suffer, yet there are sentient beings who suffer even more. These words are no different from the previous koan. If a patch-robed monk breaks through here, then amid heaps of sound and form he can be free. If he cannot break through, he is bound by sound and form. Koans like this are called in all quarters forging phrases. If you forge and refine, you only make mental activity. You do not see where the ancients worked for people. It is also called passing through sound and form: first, clarify the eye of the Way; second, clarify sound and form; third, clarify the mind school; fourth, clarify forgetting feelings; fifth, clarify unfolding and displaying. Still, you can examine it closely. Yet there are grooves and ruts in it. Jingqing asked like this, What sound is outside the gate? The monk said, The sound of raindrops. Then he said, Sentient beings are inverted, deluded about themselves and chase after things. Everyone misunderstands it, calling it deliberately turning people. That has nothing to do with it. They do not know that Jingqing had hands and feet for working for others. Bold, he is not constrained by one device or one situation; he is utterly careless of his eyebrows. How could Jingqing not know it was the sound of raindrops? Why ask again? You must know the ancients used a probing pole to stir the grass and startle the snakes, to test this monk. This monk too was good at pressing; he then said, Master, then how does it go straight? Jingqing entered mud and entered water and said to him, Then do not be deluded about yourself. If that monk is deluded about himself and chases after things, then why is Jingqing also deluded about himself? You must know: within the testing phrase there is already a place to come forth. This monk was too muddled; wanting to cut it off, he asked further: Just this, not being deluded about oneself, what is the meaning of it? If it were Deshan or Linji, the stick and shout would already have been applied. Jingqing let one thread of the Way run through, letting him spin vines; then he said to him, Coming forth is still easy; shedding the body and speaking the Way should be hard. Even so, the ancients said continuity is also very hard. Jingqing with just one sentence made clear for this monk the great matter beneath his heels. Xuedou versified, saying:

text_zh: 虛堂雨滴聲。作者難酬對。若喚作雨聲。則是 迷己逐物。不喚作雨聲。又如何轉物。到這裏。 任是作者也難酬對。所以古人道。見與師齊 減師半德。見過於師方堪傳授。又南院道。棒 下無生忍。臨機不讓師。若謂曾入流。依前 還不會。教中道。初於聞中。入流忘所。所入既 寂。動靜二相了然不生。若道是雨滴聲。也不 是。若道不是雨滴聲。也不是。前頭頌。兩喝與 三喝作者知機變。正類此頌。若道是入聲色 之流。也不是。若喚作聲色。依前不會他意。譬 如以指指月。月不是指。會與不會。南山北山 轉𩃎霈也。
text_en: losing yourself and chasing after things. If you do not call it the sound of rain, then how do you turn things around? When it comes to this, even a seasoned hand finds it hard to respond. Therefore the ancients said: if your view equals the teacher's, you diminish the teacher by half a virtue. Only when your view surpasses the teacher are you fit to receive the transmission. And Nanyuan said: under the staff, there is the forbearance of the unborn. Facing the moment, do not yield to the teacher. If you say you have entered the stream, still you do not understand. In the teachings it says: first, within hearing, enter the stream and forget what is heard; once what is entered is quiet, the two appearances of motion and stillness clearly do not arise. If you say it is the sound of raindrops, that also is not it. If you say it is not the sound of raindrops, that also is not it. The earlier verse about two shouts and three shouts, where a seasoned hand knows the shifts of the moment, is exactly like this verse. If you say it is entering the stream of sound and form, that also is not it. If you call it sound and form, still you do not understand his meaning. It is like using a finger to point at the moon: the moon is not the finger. Whether you understand or not, South Mountain and North Mountain are still swirling with rain.

text_zh: 【四七】舉。僧問雲門。如何是法身多少人疑著。千聖跳不出。漏逗 不少門云。六不收斬釘截鐵。八角磨盤空裏走。靈龜曳尾朕兆未分時薦得。已是第 二頭。朕兆已生後薦得。又落第三首。若更向言語上辨得。且喜沒交涉。
text_en: is not a little. Cut nails and slice iron—an eight-sided millstone runs in empty space. If you realize it when the numinous tortoise drags its tail and the signs are not yet divided, that is already the second head. If you realize it after the signs have arisen, you fall into a third turn. If you go on distinguishing in words, well then—gladly, it has nothing to do with it.
Yunmen said, "The six do not take in"—it is truly hard to put together. If you try to put it together before the faint signs have even divided,

text_zh: 雲門道。六不收。直是難搆。若向朕兆未分時 搆得。已是第二頭。若向朕兆已生後薦得。又 落第三首。若向言句上辨明。卒摸索不著。且 畢竟以何為法身。若是作家底。聊聞舉著。剔 起便行。苟或佇思停機。伏聽處分。太原孚上 座本為講師。一日登座講次。說法身云。竪窮 三際。橫亘十方。有一禪客。在座下聞之失笑。 孚下座云。某甲適來有甚短處。願禪者為說 看。禪者云。座主只講得法身量邊事。不見法 身。孚云。畢竟如何即是。禪者云。可暫罷講於 靜室中坐。必得自見。孚如其言。一夜靜坐。忽 聞打五更鐘。忽然大悟。遂敲禪者門云。我會 也。禪者云。爾試道看。孚云。我從今日去。更 不將父母所生鼻孔扭揑也。又教中道。佛真 法身。猶若虛空。應物現形。如水中月。又僧問 夾山。如何是法身。山云。法身無相。如何是 法眼。山云。法眼。無瑕。雲門道。六不收。此公 案有者道。只是六根六塵六識。此六皆從法 身生。六根收他不得。若恁麼情解。且喜沒交 涉。更帶累雲門。要見便見。無爾穿鑿處。不見 教中道。是法非思量分別之所能解。他答話 多惹人情解。所以一句中。須具三句。更不辜 負爾問頭。應時應節。一言一句。一點一畫。不 妨有出身處。所以道。一句透。千句萬句一時 透。且道是法身。是祖師。放爾三十棒。雪竇頌 云。
text_en: that is already a second head. If you realize it after the faint signs have already arisen, then you fall into a third. If you try to sort it out in phrases, in the end you cannot lay a hand on it. So then, ultimately, what do you take as the dharma body? If you are a seasoned hand, as soon as you hear it raised, you lift it up and move at once. If you linger in thought and stop the workings, bowing to await orders, Taiyuan Fu, the senior seat, was originally a lecturer. One day he mounted the seat and, in the course of lecturing, spoke of the dharma body, saying: vertically it exhausts the three times; horizontally it spans the ten directions. A Chan traveler in the audience heard this and burst out laughing. Fu came down from the seat and said, "Where was I lacking just now? I ask the Chan traveler to explain." The Chan traveler said, "Seat master, you have only spoken of the edges and measures of the dharma body—you have not seen the dharma body." Fu said, "So what, ultimately, is it?" The Chan traveler said, "You may suspend your lectures for a while and in a quiet room sit; you will certainly see for yourself." Fu did as he said. One night, sitting in silence, he suddenly heard the fifth-watch bell, and suddenly had great awakening. Then he knocked on the Chan traveler's door and said, "I understand !" The Chan traveler said, "Try saying it." Fu said, "From today on, I will no longer twist and pinch the nostrils my parents gave me." And in the teachings it also says: the Buddha's true dharma body is like empty space; responding to things, it manifests forms, like the moon in water. And a monk asked Jiashan, "What is the dharma body?" Jiashan said, "The dharma body has no appearance." "What is the dharma eye?" Jiashan said, "The dharma eye is without flaw." Yunmen said, "The six do not take in." In this case, some say it is simply the six sense faculties, six sense objects, and six consciousnesses. These six all arise from the dharma body; the six faculties cannot take it in. If you make that kind of emotional interpretation, fine—at least it has nothing to do with it, but it drags Yunmen down with it. If you want to see, then see—there is no place for your forced contrivances. If you do not see, the teachings say: this dharma is not something that thinking and discriminating can understand. His replies often provoke people's emotional interpretations. Therefore within one phrase there must be three phrases, so as not to fail your question. Responding to time and season, one word, one phrase, one dot, one stroke—does not prevent there being a way out. Therefore it is said: if one phrase penetrates, a thousand phrases and ten thousand phrases penetrate at once. Now tell me: is it the dharma body, or is it the patriarch? I grant you thirty blows. text_zh: 一二三四五六周而復始。滴水滴凍。費許多工夫作什麼　碧眼胡 僧數不足三生六十劫。達磨何曾夢見。闍黎為什麼知而故犯少林謾道 付神光一人傳虗萬人傳實。從頭來已錯了也卷衣又說歸天竺 賺殺一船人。懡㦬不少天竺茫茫無處尋在什麼處。始是太平。如今在什 麼處夜來却對乳峯宿刺破爾眼睛。也是無風起浪。且道是法身是佛身。 放爾三十棒
text_en: monk's count is not enough. Three lives, sixty kalpas—when did Bodhidharma ever dream of this? Venerable, why do you knowingly commit it on purpose? Shaolin vainly says it was handed to Shenguang. One person passes on the empty, ten thousand pass on the solid—right from the start it has already been wrong. Rolling up his robe, he again says he returned to India. Duping a whole boatload of people to death—no small matter. Vast and boundless India—there is nowhere to search. Where is it that peace begins? Now it is in what place? Last night he instead lodged facing Rufu Peak. To stab out your eyes is also raising waves when there is no wind. Tell me— is it the dharma body or the Buddha body? I’ll let you off with thirty blows.

text_zh: 雪竇善能於無縫罅處。出眼目頌出教人見。 雲門道。六不收。雪竇為什麼却道。一二三四 五六。直是碧眼胡僧也數不足。所以道。只許 老胡知。不許老胡會。須是還他屋裏兒孫始 得。適來道。一言一句。應時應節。若透得去。 方知道不在言句中。其或未然。不免作情解。 五祖老師道。釋迦牟尼佛。下賤客作兒。庭前 柏樹子。一二三四五。若向雲門言句下。諦當 見得。相次到這境界。少林謾道付神光。二祖 始名神光。及至後來。又道歸天竺。達磨葬於 熊耳山之下。時宋雲奉使西歸。在西嶺見達 磨手携隻履歸西天去。使回奏聖。開墳惟見 遺下一隻履。雪竇道。其實此事。作麼生分付。 既無分付。卷衣又說歸天竺。且道為什麼。此 土却有二三。遞相恁麼傳來。這裏不妨誵訛。 也須是搆得始可入作。天竺茫茫無處尋。夜 來却對乳峯宿。且道即今在什麼處。師便打 云。瞎。
text_en: Yunmen said, "The six do not take in." Why then does Xuedou say, "One, two, three, four five, six"? It is that even the blue-eyed barbarian monk's count is not enough. Therefore it is said: only allow the old barbarian to know; do not allow the old barbarian to understand. You must return it to the children and grandchildren in his own house, and only then will it do. Just now it was said: one word, one phrase, responding to time and season—if you can pass through, only then will you know it is not in phrases. If not, you cannot avoid making an emotional interpretation. The master Fifth Patriarch said: Shakyamuni Buddha, a lowly guest acting as a child; the cypress tree in the courtyard; one, two, three, four, five. If under Yunmen's words you can clearly and rightly see it, then in due course you reach this realm. Shaolin vainly says it was handed to Shenguang—the Second Patriarch was first named Shenguang. And later they again say he returned to India. Bodhidharma was buried beneath Mount Xiong'er. At that time Song Yun was sent as envoy to the west; on the western ridge he saw Bodhi- dharma carrying a single sandal, returning to the western heaven. When the envoy returned he reported to the throne; they opened the tomb and only saw a single sandal left behind. Xuedou said: in truth, how is this matter to be handed down? Since there is no handing down, he rolls up his robe and again says he returned to India—now tell me, why? In this land, there are two or three versions, passed along in this way. Here it is not a problem if there are errors and distortions— but you still must be able to put it together before you can enter and work. Vast and boundless India—there is nowhere to search. Last night he instead lodged facing Rufu Peak. Now tell me, where is he right now? The master then struck and said, "Blind!"

If you want to know the meaning of buddha-nature, you should observe the causes and conditions of time and season. Grand Preceptor Wang governed Quanzhou.

text_zh: 欲知佛性義。當觀時節因緣。王太傅知泉州。 久參招慶。一日因入寺。時朗上座煎茶次。翻 却茶銚。太傅也是箇作家。纔見他翻却茶銚。 便問上座。茶爐下是什麼。朗云。捧爐神。不妨 言中有響。爭柰首尾相違失却宗旨傷鋒犯 手。不惟辜負自己。亦且觸忤他人。這箇雖是 無得失底事。若拈起來。依舊有親疎有皂白。 若論此事。不在言句上。却要向言句上辨箇 活處。所以道。他參活句。不參死句。據朗上座 恁麼道。如狂狗逐塊。太傅拂袖便去。似不肯 他。明招云。朗上座喫却招慶飯了。却去江外 打野榸。野榸即是荒野中。火燒底木橛。謂之 野榸。用明朗上座不向正處行。却向外邊走。 朗拶云。和尚又作麼生。招云。非人得其便。明 招自然。有出身處。亦不辜負他所問。所以道。 俊狗咬人不露牙。溈山哲和尚云。王太傅大 似相如奪璧直得鬚鬢衡冠。蓋明招忍俊不 禁難逢其便。大溈若作朗上座。見他太傅拂 袖便行。放下茶銚。呵呵大笑。何故。見之不 取。千載難逢。不見寶壽問胡釘鉸云。久聞胡 釘鉸。莫便是否。胡云。是壽云。還釘得虛空 麼。胡云。請師打破將來。壽便打。胡不肯。壽 云。異日自有多口阿師。為爾點破在。胡後 見趙州。舉似前話。州云爾因什麼被他打。胡 云。不知過在什麼處。州云。只這一縫。尚不 奈何。更教他打破虛空來。胡便休去。州代云。 且釘這一縫。胡於是有省。京兆米七師行脚 歸。有老宿問云。月夜斷井索。人皆喚作蛇。未 審七師見佛時。喚作什麼。七師云。若有所見 即同眾生。老宿云。也是千年桃核。忠國師問 紫璘供奉。聞說供奉解註思益經。是否。奉云。 是師云。凡當註經。須解佛意始得。奉云。若不 會意。爭敢言註經。師遂令侍者將一椀水七 粒米一隻筯在椀上送與供奉。問云。是什麼 義。奉云。不會。師云。老師意尚不會。更說甚 佛意。王太傅與朗上座。如此話會不一。雪竇 末後却道。當時但與踏倒茶爐。明招雖是如 此。終不如雪竇。雪峯在洞山會下作飯頭。一 日淘米次。山問。作什麼。峯云。淘米。山云。淘 米去沙。淘沙去米。峯云。沙米一時去。山云。 大眾喫箇什麼。峯便覆却盆。山云。子因緣不 在此。雖然恁麼。爭似雪竇云當時但踏倒茶 爐。一等是什麼時節。到他用處。自然騰今煥 古有活脫處。頌云。
text_en: He had long studied with Zhaoqing. One day he entered the monastery; at that time Senior Seat Lang was brewing tea and overturned the teapot. The Grand Preceptor too was a seasoned hand; as soon as he saw him overturn the teapot, he asked the senior seat, "Under the tea brazier what is it?" Lang said, "The brazier-bearing spirit." Not bad— there is an echo in the words. But alas, beginning and end contradict, losing the essential point, dulling the edge and injuring the hand. It not only betrays himself, it also offends others. Although this is a matter without gain or loss, if you pick it up, there are still nearness and distance, black and white. If you discuss this matter, it is not in words; yet you must use words to discern a living place. Therefore it is said: he studies living phrases, not dead phrases. As for Senior Seat Lang speaking like that, it is like a mad dog chasing a clod. The Grand Preceptor flicked his sleeves and left, as if unwilling to accept him. Mingzhao said, "Senior Seat Lang has eaten Zhaoqing's rice, and then goes outside the river to beat wild stumps." A wild stump is a charred wooden stake out in the wilderness, burned by fire; it is called a wild stump. This shows that Senior Seat Lang does not proceed in the proper place, but instead goes off to the outside. Lang pressed him, saying, "Master, then what about it?" Mingzhao said, "A non-person gets his advantage." Ming- zhao naturally had a way out, and did not fail the question. Therefore it is said: A keen dog bites without showing its teeth. Master Weishan Zhe said: Grand Preceptor Wang greatly resembles Xiangru seizing the jade—he went so far his whiskers and beard bristled and his cap was askew. It was that Mingzhao could not restrain his amusement and could scarcely find such an opening. If Great Weishan were in Senior Seat Lang's place, seeing the Grand Preceptor flick his sleeves and go, he would put down the teapot and laugh aloud. Why? Seeing it and not taking it up— hard to meet in a thousand years. Do you not see how Baoshou asked Hu Dingjiao, saying, "I have long heard of Hu Dingjiao—are you the one?" Hu said, "I am." Baoshou said, "Can you nail empty space too?" Hu said, "Please, master, break it open and bring it." Baoshou struck. Hu would not accept it. Baoshou He said, One day there will be some loudmouthed master who will spell it out for you. Later Hu went to see Zhaozhou and brought up the earlier story. Zhaozhou said, Why did he beat you? Hu said, I do not know where the fault was. Zhaozhou said, With just this one crack, you still cannot manage? How could you deal with it? Would you have him smash open empty space too? Hu stopped and left. Zhaozhou spoke on his behalf: Just nail down this one crack. Hu then had an awakening. In Jingzhao, Master Miqi went traveling on pilgrimage, and on his return an old veteran asked, On a moonlit night, a broken well-rope—everyone calls it a snake. When Master Miqi sees the Buddha, what does he call it? Master Miqi said, If there is anything seen, then it is the same as ordinary beings. The old veteran said, That too is a thousand-year peach pit. National Teacher Zhong asked Court Attendant Zilin, I have heard you can explain and annotate the Siyi Sutra—is it so? The attendant said, Yes. The teacher said, Whoever annotates a sutra must first understand the Buddha’s intent. The attendant said, If I did not understand the intent, how would I dare speak of annotating sutras? The teacher then had an attendant bring a bowl of water, seven grains of rice, and a single chopstick laid across the bowl, and present it to the attendant. He asked, What does it mean? The attendant said, I do not understand. The teacher said, If you still do not understand the teacher’s intent, what are you talking about Buddha’s intent? Grand Tutor Wang and Senior Seat Lang did not agree in their understanding of such talk. Xuedou in the end said instead, Back then one should simply have kicked over the tea brazier. Though Mingzhao was like that, in the end he was not as good as Xuedou. Xuefeng, in Dongshan’s community, served as head cook. One day while washing rice, Dongshan asked, What are you doing? Xuefeng said, Washing rice. Dongshan said, Washing rice to remove sand, or washing sand to remove rice? Xuefeng said, Sand and rice removed all at once. San Sheng received confirmation from Linji and traveled everywhere; all treated him as an honored guest. Look at how he sets up this question—how many people cannot even grope their way to it. It does not touch principle, nature, or Buddha-dharma; instead he asks: the golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net—what does it take as food? Tell me, what is his intent? Since the golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net normally does not eat fragrant bait, one does not know what it takes as food. Xuefeng is an adept, as if at leisure; he answers him with just a bit. He says to him, Wait until you come out of the net, and then I will tell you. Fenyang called this a question that presents an understanding; in the Dongshan line it is called borrowing an affair to ask. One must transcend the ordinary and surpass categories to gain great use; only with an eye in the crown of the head can one be called a golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net. Yet Xue feng is an adept and does not mind cutting down a man’s reputation; he says, Wait until you come out of the net and then I will tell you. Look at these two households: they hold the border firmly; they stand like a sheer wall ten thousand fathoms high. If it were not San Sheng, with just this one sentence he could not move on. Yet San Sheng is also an adept; only then can he say to him, A thousand five hundred people, good teachers— yet they do not even recognize the topic of conversation. Xuefeng then says, This old monk’s abbot affairs are many. These words are that stubborn and insolent. When adepts meet, one seizes, one releases; meeting the strong, one becomes weak; encountering the lowly, one becomes noble. If you make it into a contest of winning and losing, you have not even dreamed of Xuefeng. Look at these two men: at first solitary, perilous, steep and severe; at the end both are slack and careless. Tell me, is there still gain and loss, victory and defeat? Their exchange between adepts surely does not know such things. When San Sheng was head of the monastery under Linji, Linji at his passing gave this instruction: After I am gone, do not extinguish my treasury of the true dharma eye. San Sheng stepped forward and said, How would I dare extinguish the master’s treasury of the true dharma eye? Linji said, Later, if someone asks you, what will you do? San Sheng gave a shout. Linji said, Who would have known my treasury of the true dharma eye would be extinguished by this blind donkey! San Sheng then bowed. He was Linji’s true son, and only then dared to exchange like that. In the end, Xuedou only versified the golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net, revealing where adepts meet. Verse says:

text_en: solitary. A holeless iron hammer drives the wedge down hard. After that he again praised Mazu’s cutting off the four propositions and severing the hundred negations: The river’s head is white, the sea’s head is black. Even a clear-eyed patchrobed monk won’t be able to make sense of it. If you penetrate this case, then you’ll see this verse. Right at the start Xuedou says, Rice in the bowl, water in the bucket. In the words there is an echo; in the phrase the pivot is revealed. This talkative master is hard to answer. Right after that he gives you a footnote. If you seek subtle marvels and doctrines here, the more you calculate the harder it is to speak. Xuedou is fine stopping right here. He likes to pin it down at the outset, fearing that among the assembly there may be those with eyes who would see through it. When he reaches the later part he must let one move go through, bending down for beginners, opening up the verse so people can see: the Northern Dipper is still in the north; the Southern Star is still only in the south. Hence he says, The Northern Dipper and the Southern Star—positions not different. White waves flood the sky—on level ground they rise. Suddenly, on flat ground, waves surge—what then? If you look in the realm of events, it’s easy; if you search beneath the root of thought, in the end you can’t find it. This is like an iron stake—you can’t budge it, you can’t get a word in, you can’t interrupt. If you speculate, wanting to understand yet not understanding; stopping yet not stopping—confusedly presenting your muddled bag—that’s exactly each one a rich man’s son with no trousers. Hanshan’s poem says: The six directions constantly nurse suffering; the nine dimensions are discussed in vain. With talent you’re cast aside in the wilds; without influence you shut the brushwood door. The sun rises yet the cliffs are still dark; the smoke clears yet the valleys remain dim. Among them, these rich men’s sons—each one has no trousers at all.

text_zh: 垂示云。纔有是非。紛然失心。不落階級。又無 摸索。且道放行即是。把住即是。到這裏。若有 一絲毫解路。猶滯言詮。尚拘機境。盡是依草 附木。直饒便到獨脫處。未免萬里望鄉關。還 搆得麼。若未搆得。且只理會箇理成公案。試 舉看。
text_en: to grope for—tell me, is letting go right, or is holding fast right? When you come here, if there is the slightest route of explanation, you’re still stuck in words, still bound by circumstances and objects—all of it is clinging to grass and attaching to trees. Even if you reach the place of solitary release, you still can’t avoid gazing toward your home pass from ten thousand miles away. Can you connect with it? If you haven’t connected with it, just understand this case made from a principle. Try presenting it.
Case 51. When Xuefeng was living in a hut, two monks came to pay respects. What for? Take one charge and carry it through.

text_zh: 【五一】舉。雪峯住庵時。有兩僧來禮拜作什麼。一狀領過 峯見來。以手托庵門。放身出云。是什麼 鬼眼睛。無孔笛子。擎頭戴角僧亦云。是什麼泥彈子氈拍板。箭鋒相拄 峯低頭歸庵爛泥裏有刺。如龍無足。似蛇有角。就中難為措置僧後到 巖頭也須是問過始得。同道方知頭問。什麼處來也須是作家始得。這漢 往往納敗闕。若不是同參。洎乎放過僧云。嶺南來傳得什麼消息來。也須是通 箇消息。還見雪峯麼頭云。曾到雪峯麼勘破了多時。不可道不到僧 云。曾到實頭人難得。打作兩橛頭云。有何言句便恁麼去也僧 舉前話便恁麼去也。重重納敗闕頭云。他道什麼好劈口便打。失却 鼻孔了也僧云。他無語低頭歸庵又納敗闕。爾且道他是什麼頭 云。噫我當初悔不向他道末後句洪波浩渺白浪滔天 若向伊道。天下人不奈雪老何癩兒牽伴。不必。須彌也須 粉碎。且道他圈繢在什麼處僧至夏末。再舉前話請益已是不惺 惺。正賊去了多時。賊過後張弓頭云。何不早問好與掀倒禪床。過也僧 云。未敢容易這棒本是這僧喫。穿却鼻孔。停囚長智。已是兩重公案頭云。 雪峯雖與我同條生。不與我同條死漫天網地要 識末句後。只這是賺殺一船人。我也不信。洎乎分疎不下。

Raising the head, wearing horns. Mud pellets, felt clappers. Arrowheads braced against each other. Xuefeng lowered his head and returned to the hut. In general, to uphold and establish the teaching of the school, you must discern what fits the moment, and know advance and retreat, right and wrong.

text_zh: 大凡扶竪宗教。須是辨箇當機。知進退是非。 明殺活擒縱。若忽眼目迷黎麻羅。到處逢問 便問。逢答便答。殊不知鼻孔在別人手裏。只 如雪峯巖頭。同參德山。此僧參雪峯。見解只 到恁麼處。及乎見巖頭。亦不曾成得一事。虛 煩他二老宿。一問一答。一擒一縱。直至如 今。天下人成節角誵訛。分疎不下。且道節角 誵訛。在什麼處。雪峯雖遍歷諸方。末後於鰲 山店。巖頭因而激之。方得勦絕大徹。巖頭後 值沙汰。於湖邊作渡子。兩岸各懸一板。有人 過敲板一下。頭云。爾過那邊。遂從蘆葦間。舞 棹而出。雪峯歸嶺南住庵。這僧亦是久參底 人。雪峯見來。以手托庵門。放身出云。是什 麼。如今有底。恁麼問著。便去他語下咬嚼。這 僧亦怪。也只向他道是什麼。峯低頭歸庵。往 往喚作無語會去也。這僧便摸索不著。有底 道。雪峯被這僧一問直得。無語歸庵。殊不 知雪峯意有毒害處。雪峯雖得便宜。爭奈藏 身露影。這僧後辭雪峯。持此公案。令巖頭判。 既到彼。巖頭問。什麼處來。僧云。嶺南來。頭 云。曾到雪峯麼。若要見雪峯。只此一問。也好 急著眼看。僧云。曾到。頭云。有何言句。此語 亦不空過。這僧不曉。只管逐他語脈轉。頭云。 他道什麼。僧云。他低頭無語歸庵。這僧殊 不知。巖頭著草鞋。在他肚皮裏行。幾回了也。 巖頭云。噫我當初悔不向他道末後句。若向 他道。天下人不奈雪老何。巖頭也是扶強不 扶弱。這僧依舊黑漫漫地。不分緇素。懷一肚 皮疑。真箇道。雪峯不會。至夏末。再舉前話。 請益巖頭。頭云。何不早問。這老漢。計較生 也。僧云。未敢容易。頭云。雪峯雖與我同條 生。不與我同條死。要識末後句。只這是巖頭 太殺不惜眉毛。諸人畢竟作麼生會。雪峯在 德山會下作飯頭。一日齋晚。德山托鉢下至 法堂。峯云。鐘未鳴鼓未響。這老漢。托鉢向什 麼處去。山無語低頭歸方丈。雪峯舉似巖頭。 頭云。大小德山。不會末後句。山聞令侍者喚 至方丈問云。汝不肯老僧那頭密啟其語。山 至來日上堂。與尋常不同。頭於僧堂前。撫 掌大笑云。且喜老漢會末後句。他後天下人。 不奈他何。雖然如是。只得三年。此公案中。如 雪峯見德山無語。將謂得便宜。殊不知著賊 了也。蓋為他曾著賊來。後來亦解做賊。所以 古人道。末後一句。始到牢關。有者道。巖頭勝 雪峯。則錯會了也。巖頭常用此機示眾云。明 眼漢沒窠臼。却物為上。逐物為下。這末後句。 設使親見祖師來。也理會不得。德山齋晚。老 子自捧鉢下法堂去。巖頭道。大小德山。未會 末後句在。雪竇拈云。曾聞說箇獨眼龍。元來 只具一隻眼。殊不知。德山是箇無齒大蟲。若 不是巖頭識破。爭知得昨日與今日不同。諸 人要會末後句麼。只許老胡知。不許老胡會。 自古及今。公案萬別千差。如荊棘林相似。爾 若透得去。天下人不奈何。三世諸佛。立在下 風。爾若透不得。巖頭道。雪峯雖與我同條生。 不與我同條死。只這一句自然有出身處。雪 竇頌云。
text_en: Be clear about killing and giving life, capturing and releasing. If your eyes suddenly get muddled and confused, then wherever you go, when you meet a question you question; when you meet an answer you answer—without realizing your nostrils are in someone else’s hands. Just like Xuefeng and Yantou, who together studied under Deshan. These monks visited Xuefeng; their understanding only reached this point. When they came to see Yantou, they still didn’t accomplish a single thing, vainly troubling those two old worthies—one question, one answer; one capture, one release—down to today. People everywhere make knots and corners of garbled errors, unable to sort them out. Tell me—these knots and corners of garbled error—where are they? Though Xuefeng traveled everywhere, in the end at the Ao Mountain inn, Yantou provoked him, and only then did he cut it off completely and awaken greatly. Later Yantou encountered persecution and became a ferryman by a lake. On each bank he hung a board; when someone crossed, they struck the board once. Yantou would say, You cross to that side—then from among the reeds he would swing the oar and come out. Xuefeng returned to Lingnan to live in a hut. These monks too were long-time practitioners. When Xuefeng saw them come, he braced the hut door with his hand, stuck his body out, and said, What is this? Nowadays some, when asked like this, go and chew on his words. These monks too found it strange, and only replied to him, What is this? Xuefeng lowered his head and returned to the hut. People often call this understanding as silence. The monks then couldn’t grasp it. Some say, Xuefeng was pressed by the monks’ question and had to return to the hut in silence. They do not know that Xuefeng’s intent has a poisonous bite. Though Xuefeng gained the advantage, how could he avoid hiding his body yet revealing his shadow? Later the monks took leave of Xuefeng, carried this case, and asked Yantou to judge it. When they arrived there, Yantou asked, Where have you come from? The monks said, From Lingnan. Yantou said, Have you been to Xuefeng? If you want to see Xuefeng, just this one question is enough—and it’s also good to look sharply. The monks said, We have. Yantou said, What words did he say? This line also does not pass by in vain. The monks didn’t understand and simply followed the drift of his words. Yantou said, What did he say? The monks said, He lowered his head, was silent, and returned to the hut. These monks truly didn’t know that Yantou, wearing straw sandals, had already walked around inside their bellies several times over. Yantou said, Alas! I regret that at the time I didn’t tell him the final phrase. If I had told him, people everywhere would have been unable to do anything with old man Xue. Yantou too supports the strong and does not support the weak. These monks remained in total darkness, unable to distinguish black from white, carrying a bellyful of doubts. They truly said, Xuefeng doesn’t understand. At summer’s end they again raised the earlier exchange to ask Yantou. Yantou said, Why didn’t you ask sooner? This old fellow—calculations arise. The monks said, I didn’t dare be casual. Yantou said, Though Xuefeng and I are on the same branch in birth, we are not on the same branch in death. If you want to know the final phrase—just this is it. Yantou was utterly reckless, not sparing his eyebrows. Ultimately, how will you understand it? When Xuefeng was under Deshan, he served as head cook. One day after the evening meal, Deshan carried his bowl down to the Dharma hall. Xuefeng said, The bell hasn’t rung, the drum hasn’t sounded—where is this old man carrying his bowl going? Deshan, without a word, lowered his head and returned to the abbot’s quarters. Xuefeng told this to Yantou. Yantou said, Great Deshan doesn’t understand the final phrase. When Deshan heard this, he had an attendant summon him to the abbot’s quarters and asked, You won’t approve the old monk—then privately reveal your words. Deshan When he ascended the hall the next day, it was unlike the usual. In front of the monks’ hall, he stroked his palms and laughed loudly, saying: Good—this old fellow understands the last phrase. Later, people throughout the world will be unable to do anything about him. Even so, he only lasted three years. In this public case, it is like Xuefeng seeing Deshan left speechless and thinking he had gained an advantage—without realizing he had been robbed by a thief already. Because he had once been robbed by a thief, later he also knew how to be a thief. Therefore the ancients said: Only the last phrase reaches the solid barrier. If someone says Yantou surpasses Xuefeng, then they have misunderstood. Yantou often used this device to instruct the assembly, saying: A clear-eyed person has no ruts; turning away from things is above, chasing things is below. This last phrase— even if you personally met the patriarchs coming, you still could not grasp it. One evening after the meal, old Deshan himself carried his bowl down to the Dharma hall. Yantou said: Big Deshan still has not understood the last phrase. Xuedou raised it, saying: I had heard of a one-eyed dragon—turns out it really only has one eye. Little did he know: Deshan is a toothless great beast. If Yantou had not seen through it, how would one know that yesterday and today are different? All of you, do you want to understand the last phrase? Only allow the old barbarian to know; do not allow the old barbarian to understand. From ancient times to the present, public cases differ in ten thousand ways, like a thicket of brambles. If you can pass through, people throughout the world cannot do anything about you; the Buddhas of the three times stand downwind. If you cannot pass through, Yantou said: Though Xuefeng and I were born on the same branch, he does not die on the same branch as I. Just this one line naturally has its own place to come forth. text_en: but a verse is just a verse—it only praises a bit of surface color. If you want to penetrate and see through, it still is not there. Yet he dares open his mouth wide and say: At the time when light and dark come as a pair, it opens a single thread of a road for you—and with that one line it also kills you. Finally, he gives you another explanation. For instance, one day Zhaoqing asked Luoshan: Yantou said so-and-so, so-and-so; not so-and-so, not so-and-so—what is the purport? Luo- shan called: Great Master! The master responded. Luoshan said: Both bright, and also both dark. Zhaoqing bowed in thanks and left. Three days later he asked again: The other day I received the master’s compassion, but I still cannot see through it. Luoshan said: I have told you fully. Zhaoqing said: The master is like carrying fire as he walks. Luoshan said: If that is so, then take the place where you doubt and ask it forth. Zhaoqing said: What is both bright and also both dark? Luoshan said: Born together, also die together. Zhaoqing at that time bowed in thanks and left. Later a monk asked Zhaoqing: When born together and also dying together, how is it? Zhaoqing said: Shut the dog’s mouth. The monk said: Great Master, gather up your mouth and eat your rice. That monk then came and asked Luoshan: When born together but not dying together, how is it? Luoshan said: Like an ox without horns. The monk said: When born together and also dying together, how is it? Luoshan said: Like a tiger wearing horns. The last phrase is precisely this principle. In Luoshan’s assembly there was a monk who used this idea to question Zhaoqing. Zhaoqing said: Each side knows the other. Why? If I speak one line in the Eastern Victorious Body Continent, the Western Aparagodaniya Continent also knows. If I speak one line in the heavens, the human realm also knows. Mind knows mind, and eye illuminates eye. Being born on the same branch is still easy to see; not dying on the same branch is still utterly different—Shakyamuni and Bodhidharma cannot grope it out. North, south, east, and west—returning and coming—there is a bit of fine scenery here: deep in the night, together watching the snow on a thousand crags. Now tell me: is it both bright and both dark? Is it born on the same branch, is it dying on the same branch? A clear-eyed patched-robed monk, try sorting it out and see.
