One cast of the net and it is done—so that no one under heaven has any place to breathe. Once dead, never alive again. over. Truly urgent.
Zhaozhou has a stone bridge, built by Li Ying, and to this day it is famous throughout the world. A plank

text_zh: 趙州有石橋。蓋李膺造也。至今天下有名。略 彴者。即是獨木橋也。其僧故意減他威光問 他道。久響趙州石橋。到來只見略彴。趙州便 道。汝只見略彴。且不見石橋。據他問處。也只 是平常說話相似。趙州用去釣他。這僧果然 上鉤。隨後便問。如何是石橋。州云。渡驢渡 馬。不妨言中自有出身處。趙州不似臨濟德 山。行棒行喝。他只以言句殺活。這公案好好 看來。只是尋常鬪機鋒相似。雖然如是。也 不妨難湊泊。一日與首座看石橋。州乃問首 座。是什麼人造。座云。李膺造。州云。造時向 什麼處下手。座無對。州云。尋常說石橋。問著 下手處也不知。又一日州掃地次。僧問。和尚 是善知識。為什麼有塵。州云。外來底。又問。 清淨伽藍。為什麼有塵。州云。又有一點也。又 僧問。如何是道。州云。牆外底。僧云。不問這 箇道。問大道。州云。大道透長安。趙州偏用此 機。他到平實安穩處。為人更不傷鋒犯手。自 然孤峻。用得此機甚妙。雪竇頌云。
text_en: bridge is a single-log bridge. That monk intentionally tried to diminish his majesty and asked him: For a long time I have heard of Zhaozhou’s stone bridge; coming here I only see a plank bridge. Zhaozhou then said: You only see the plank bridge; you still do not see the stone bridge. Judging from where he asked, it also seems like ordinary talk. Zhaozhou used it to fish him; and indeed this monk bit the hook. Right after, he asked: What is the stone bridge? Zhaozhou said: It lets donkeys cross and lets horses cross. It is not amiss—within the words there is a place to come forth. Zhaozhou is not like Linji or Deshan, wielding staff and shout; he only uses phrases to kill and enliven. Look well at this public case— it seems like an ordinary contest of sharpness. Even so, it is not amiss that it is hard to bring together. One day he was looking at the stone bridge with the head monk; Zhaozhou asked the head monk: Who built it? The head monk said: Li Ying built it. Zhaozhou said: When he built it, where did he set his hand to it? The head monk had no answer. Zhaozhou said: You usually talk about the stone bridge, but when asked where it began, you do not even know. Another day, as Zhaozhou was sweeping the ground, a monk asked: Master, you are a good spiritual friend—why is there dust? Zhaozhou said: It comes from outside. He asked again: In a pure monastery, why is there dust? Zhaozhou said: There is another bit of it too. Again a monk asked: What is the Way? Zhaozhou said: It’s outside the wall. The monk said: I am not asking about that Way; I ask about the Great Way. Zhaozhou said: The Great Way passes through Chang’an. Zhaozhou particularly used this device. When he arrived at plain, solid, safe ground, in guiding people he did not further injure with sharpness or offend by force; naturally he was solitary and steep. He used this device wonderfully. Xuedou composed a verse:
If you do not set up solitary peril, the Way is then lofty; entering the sea, You must reach this ground for it to work. The words are still in your ears—give him his proper fodder.

text_zh: 孤危不立道方高須是到這田地始得。言猶在耳。還他本分草料　入海 還須釣巨鼇坐斷要津不通凡聖。蝦蜆螺蚌不足問。大丈夫漢。不可兩兩三三堪 笑同時灌溪老也有恁麼人曾恁麼來。也有恁麼用機關底手脚解云劈 箭亦徒勞猶較半月程。似則似是則未是
text_en: you must still fish for a giant sea turtle. Sitting and cutting off the vital pass, letting neither ordinary nor sage through. Shrimp, clams, snails, and mussels are not worth asking about. A real man cannot come in twos and threes. Worthy of laughter is that old man Guanxi of the same time; There are also such people who have come like this; there are also such hands and feet that work the mechanisms. even if he could say “split” arrows, it would still be in vain. Still short by half a month's journey. It seems like it, seems right, yet it is not.
If you do not set up solitary peril, the Way is then lofty. Xuedou is praising how Zhaozhou usually guided people:

text_zh: 孤危不立道方高。雪竇頌趙州尋常為人處。 不立玄妙。不立孤危。不似諸方道打破虛空。 擊碎須彌。海底生塵。須彌鼓浪。方稱他祖師 之道。所以雪竇道。孤危不立道方高。壁立萬 仞。顯佛法奇特靈驗。雖然孤危峭峻。不如不 立孤危。但平常自然轉轆轆地。不立而自立。 不高而自高。機出孤危方見玄妙。所以雪竇 云。入海還須釣巨鼇。看他具眼宗師等閑垂 一語。用一機不釣鰕蜆螺蚌。直釣巨鼇。也不 妨是作家。此一句用顯前面公案。堪笑同時 灌溪老。不見僧問灌溪。久響灌溪。及乎到來。 只見箇漚麻池。溪云。汝只見漚麻池。且不見 灌溪。僧云。如何是灌溪。溪云。劈箭急。又僧 問黃龍。久響黃龍。及乎到來。只見箇赤斑蛇。 龍云。子只見赤斑蛇。且不見黃龍。僧云。如何 是黃龍。龍云。拕拕地。僧云。忽遇金翅鳥來時 如何。龍云。性命難存。僧云。恁麼則遭他食噉 去也。龍云。謝子供養。此總是立孤危。是則也 是不免費力。終不如趙州尋常用底。所以雪 竇道。解云劈箭亦徒勞。只如灌溪黃龍即且 致。趙州云。波驢渡馬。又作麼生會。試辨看。
text_en: he did not set up mystery, did not set up solitary peril. He was not like those around the land who say they smash empty space, shatter Mount Sumeru, raise dust on the ocean floor, and make Sumeru beat up waves—only then calling it the Patriarchs’ Way. Therefore Xuedou said: If you do not set up solitary peril, the Way is then lofty. A cliff standing ten thousand fathoms shows the Buddha-Dharma’s extraordinary efficacy. Even so, solitary peril and steepness are not as good as not setting up solitary peril. Simply in the ordinary, it naturally rolls along; not set up, yet it sets itself up; not lofty, yet it is lofty. When the mechanism comes forth from solitary peril, then you see the mystery. Therefore Xuedou said: Entering the sea, you must still fish for a giant sea turtle. Look—an accomplished master casually drops one line, uses one device: he does not fish for shrimp, clams, snails, or mussels—he directly fishes for a giant sea turtle. This too shows a master’s hand. This one line is used to illuminate the earlier public case. Worthy of laughter is that of the same time, old man Guanxi. Haven’t you seen a monk ask Guanxi: For a long time I have heard of Guanxi; when I finally arrive, I only see a retting-hemp pond. Guanxi said: You only see the retting-hemp pond; you still do not see Guanxi. The monk said: What is Guanxi? Guanxi said: Split arrows—swiftly! Again, a monk asked Huanglong: For a long time I have heard of Huanglong; when I finally arrive, I only see a red-spotted snake. Huanglong said: You only see the red-spotted snake; you still do not see Huanglong. The monk said: What is Huanglong? Huanglong said: Dragging along. The monk said: If I suddenly meet a golden-winged bird, then what? Huanglong said: Life is hard to keep. The monk said: Then I would be eaten by it. Huanglong said: Thanks for the offering. All of this is setting up solitary peril; it may be so, yet it is not without effort. In the end it is not as good as what Zhaozhou ordinarily used. Therefore Xue- Xuedou said, To explain it is like splitting an arrow—also futile labor. As for Guanxi and Huanglong, let that be for now; Zhaozhou said, A wave-ass ferries a horse. How will you understand that? Try to discern it.
53 Instruction said: Throughout the whole realm there is no hiding; the whole mechanism alone is revealed. Whatever road you touch, there is no obstruction; step by step

text_zh: 垂示云。遍界不藏。全機獨露。觸途無滯。著著 有出身之機。句下無私。頭頭有殺人之意。且 道古人。畢竟向什麼處休歇。試舉看。
text_en: there is a way to emerge. Under the phrase there is no partiality; in each and every point there is an intent that can kill. Tell me, where did the ancients finally rest and settle? Try to raise it and see.
Case 53. Master Ma was walking with Baizhang. They saw wild ducks fly past. Master Ma said, What is that? Two

text_zh: 【五三】舉。馬大師與百丈行次。見野鴨子飛過兩箇 落草漢草裏輥。驀顧作什麼大師云。是什麼和尚合知。這老漢鼻孔也不知 丈云。野鴨子鼻孔已在別人手裏。只管供欵。第二杓惡水更毒大師云。 什麼處去也前箭猶輕後箭深。第二回啗啄。也合自知丈云。飛過去 也只管隨他後轉。當面蹉過大師遂扭百丈鼻頭父母所生鼻孔 却在別人手裏。捩轉鎗頭。裂轉鼻孔來也丈作忍痛聲只在這裏。還喚作野鴨子得 麼。還識痛痒麼大師云。何曾飛去莫瞞人好。這老漢元來只在鬼窟裏作 活計。
text_en: outlaws rolling in the grass—why suddenly look back? The master should know; this old fellow does not even know his own nostrils. Baizhang said, Wild ducks. Master Ma said, His nostrils are already in someone else's hands, yet he keeps on confessing. The second ladle of foul water is even more poisonous. Where have they gone? Baizhang said, They’ve flown past. The first arrow is still light, the next arrow sinks deep. The second pecking and biting—you should know it yourself. Master Ma then twisted Baizhang’s nose. Baizhang cried out in pain. Master Ma said, When did they ever fly away? You just keep turning after him and miss it right in front of your face. The nostrils you were born with are instead in someone else's hands. Twist the spearhead around; wrench the nostrils back. It is only right here. Can you still call it a wild duck or not? Do you still know pain and itch? Do not hide it from people. This old fellow has all along been doing business only in a ghost cave, making his living.
Seen with the true eye, it is Baizhang who has the right cause; Master Ma stirred waves without any wind.

text_zh: 正眼觀來却是百丈具正因。馬大師無風起 浪。諸人要與佛祖為師。參取百丈。要自救不 了。參取馬祖大師。看他古人二六時中。未 甞不在箇裏。百丈丱歲離塵。三學該練。屬大 寂闡化南昌。乃傾心依附。二十年為侍者。及 至再參。於喝下方始大悟。而今有者道。本無 悟處。作箇悟門建立此事。若恁麼見解。如獅 子身中蟲。自食獅子肉不見古人道。源不深 者流不長。智不大者見不遠。若用作建立會。 佛法豈到如今。看他馬大師與百丈行次。見 野鴨子飛過。大師豈不知是野鴨子。為什麼 却恁麼問。且道他意落在什麼處。百丈只管 隨他後走。馬祖遂扭他鼻孔。丈作忍痛聲馬 祖云。何曾飛去百丈便省。而今有底錯會。纔 問著便作忍痛聲。且喜跳不出。宗師家為人 須為教徹。見他不會。不免傷鋒犯手。只要教 他明此事。所以道。會則途中受用。不會則世 諦流布。馬祖當時若不扭住。只成世諦流布。 也須是逢境遇緣。宛轉教歸自己。十二時中。 無空缺處。謂之性地明白。若只依草附木。認 箇驢前馬後。有何用處。看他馬祖百丈恁麼 用。雖似昭昭靈靈。却不住在昭昭靈靈處。百 丈作忍痛聲。若恁麼見去。遍界不藏頭頭成 現。所以道。一處透千處萬處一時透。馬祖 次日陞堂眾纔集。百丈出卷却拜蓆。馬祖便 下座。歸方丈次問百丈。我適來上堂。未曾說 法。爾為什麼。便卷却蓆丈云。昨日被和尚扭 得鼻孔痛。祖云。爾昨日向甚處留心。丈云。今 日鼻頭又不痛也。祖云。爾深知今日事。丈乃 作禮。却歸侍者寮哭。同事侍者問云。爾哭作 什麼。丈云。爾去問取和尚。侍者遂去問馬祖。 祖云。爾去問取他看。侍者却歸寮問百丈。丈 却呵呵大笑。侍者云。爾適來哭。而今為什麼 却笑。丈云。我適來哭。如今却笑。看他悟後。 阿轆轆地。羅籠不住。自然玲瓏。雪竇頌云。
text_en: If you all want to take the Buddhas and Patriarchs as your teachers, study Baizhang. If you want to be unable to save yourselves, study Master Mazu. Look at those ancients: through the twelve hours of the day, they were never not right here. Baizhang left the dust while still young, fully trained in the three trainings. When Great Ji was teaching in Nanchang, he devoted himself and attached himself to him, serving as attendant for twenty years. When he came again to study, it was only under a shout that he finally had great awakening. Yet now some say there is fundamentally no place of awakening, and that establishing a gate of awakening is setting this matter up. If you see it like that, it is like worms within a lion’s body, eating the lion’s flesh themselves. Have you not seen the ancients say: if the source is not deep, the stream is not long; if wisdom is not great, vision is not far. If you take it as something to be established and understood, how could the Buddha Dharma have reached us today? Look at Master Ma walking with Baizhang: they saw wild ducks fly past. Would the master not know they were wild ducks? Why, then, did he ask like that? Tell me, where does his intent fall? Baizhang simply followed along behind him. Mazu then twisted his nostrils. Baizhang cried out in pain. Mazu said, When did they ever fly away? Baizhang immediately understood. But now there are those who misunderstand: as soon as they are questioned, they make a cry of pain. Luckily, they cannot jump out of it. In the house of a lineage master, to help people one must teach through. Seeing that they do not understand, one cannot avoid bruising the edge and hurting the hand; one only wants to make them clearly understand this matter. Therefore it is said: if you understand, you make use of it on the road; if you do not understand, it spreads as worldly truth. If Mazu had not seized him by twisting, it would only have become worldly-truth circulation. You must meet circumstances and conditions and, by turns, teach it back to oneself. Throughout the twelve hours, there is no gap. This is called clarity on the ground of nature. If you only cling to grass and attach to wood, recognizing some donkey-before, horse-behind, what use is it? Look at how Mazu and Baizhang used it like this: though it seems bright and numinous, it does not abide in the bright and numinous. Baizhang cried out in pain. If you see it like that, throughout the whole realm there is no hiding, and everywhere it is made manifest. Therefore it is said: penetrate in one place, and a thousand places, ten thousand places are penetrated at once. The next day Mazu ascended the hall; as soon as the assembly gathered, Baizhang rolled up the mat and bowed at the seat. Mazu then descended from the seat. Returning to the abbot’s quarters, he asked Baizhang, Just now I went up to the hall and did not speak the Dharma. Why did you roll up the mat? Baizhang said, Yesterday the master twisted my nostrils so they hurt. The patriarch said, Where did you set your mind yesterday? Baizhang said, Today my nose no longer hurts. The patriarch said, You deeply know today’s matter. Baizhang then made a bow and returned to the attendants’ quarters, crying. A fellow attendant asked, Why are you crying like that? Baizhang said, Go ask the master. The attendant then went to ask Mazu. Mazu said, Go ask him and see. The attendant returned to the quarters and asked Baizhang. Baizhang burst into hearty laughter. The attendant said, You were crying just now—why are you laughing now? Baizhang said, I was crying just now; now I am laughing. Look at him after awakening: rolling and rolling—no net can cage him. Naturally, he is clear and perfectly formed. Xuedou’s verse says:
Who knows where the wild ducks are? When Mazu sees them, Forming into flocks and teams, and there is yet another one. What use is it? Like hemp, like millet.

text_zh: 野鴨子成群作隊又有一隻　知何許用作什麼。如麻似粟　馬祖見來 相共語打葛藤有什麼了期。說箇什麼。獨有馬祖識箇俊底話盡山雲海 月情東家杓柄長。西家杓柄短。知他打葛藤多少依前不會還飛去 㘞。莫道他不會言。飛過什麼處去欲飛去鼻孔在別人手裏。已是與他下注脚了也 却把住老婆心切。更道什麼　道道什麼道。不可也教山僧道。不可作野鴨子叫。 蒼天蒼天。脚跟下好與三十棒。不知向什麼處去
text_en: they speak together, What end is there to vine-tangling? What are you even saying? Only Mazu recognized the one who was sharp. and the talk exhausts mountain clouds and sea moon-feelings. The east household's ladle-handle is long; the west household's ladle-handle is short. Who knows how much vine-tangling he has done? Still not understanding as before, they fly off again. Do not say he cannot speak—where did it fly off to? About to fly off, The nostrils are in someone else's hands—already you have supplied him with a footing. he seizes them and says, say! With an old woman's anxious heart, what more is there to say? What saying? You cannot even make this mountain monk say it. Do not make it cry like a wild duck. Blue sky, blue sky. Under your heels you deserve thirty blows—you do not know where you are going.
Xuedou, right at the start, versified: Who knows where the wild ducks are? Tell me, how many are there?

text_zh: 雪竇劈頭便頌道。野鴨子知何許。且道有多 少。馬祖見來相共語。此頌馬祖問百丈云。是 什麼。丈云。野鴨子。語盡山雲海月情。頌再問 百丈什麼處去。馬大師為他意旨自然脫體。 百丈依前不會。却道飛過去也。兩重蹉過欲 飛去。却把住。雪竇據欵結案。又云。道道。此 是雪竇轉身處。且道。作麼生道。若作忍痛聲 則錯。若不作忍痛聲。又作麼生會。雪竇雖然 頌得甚妙。爭奈也跳不出。
text_en: When Mazu sees them, they speak together. This versifies Mazu asking Baizhang, What is that? Baizhang said, Wild ducks. The talk exhausts mountain clouds and sea moon-feelings. The verse then asks again where they have gone. For Master Ma, his intent naturally drops away from the body. Baizhang still does not understand as before, and says, They flew past. Twice he misses it. About to fly away, he seizes them. Xuedou decides the case on the evidence, and again says, Say, say! This is where Xuedou turns around. Tell me, how do you say it? If you make a cry of pain, you are wrong. If you do not make a cry of pain, then how do you understand it? Although Xuedou versified it wonderfully, he still cannot jump out of it.
54 Instruction said: Penetrate birth and death; flip the mechanism; casually cut iron and sever nails.

text_zh: 垂示云。透出生死。撥轉機關。等閑截鐵斬釘。 隨處蓋天蓋地。且道是什麼人行履處。試舉 看。
text_en: Wherever you are, it covers heaven and covers earth. Tell me, whose tracks are these? Try to raise it and see.
Case 54. Yunmen asked a monk, Where have you just come from? Do not say "West Chan," do not probe with pole and shadow the grass; do not speak of east, west, south, or north.

text_zh: 【五四】舉。雲門問僧近離甚處不可也道西禪。探竿影草。不可道東西南北 僧云。西禪果然。可殺實頭。當時好與本分草料門云。西禪近日 有何言句欲舉恐驚和尚。深辨來風。也似和尚相似寐語僧展兩手敗闕 了也。勾賊破家。不妨令人疑著門打一掌據令而行。好打。快便難逢僧云。 某甲話在爾待要翻欵那。却似有攙旗奪鼓底手脚門却展兩手嶮駕 與青龍不解騎僧無語可惜門便打不可放過。此棒合是雲門喫。何故。當斷 不斷返招其亂。闍黎合喫多少。放過一著。若不放過合作麼生。
text_en: The monk said, Xichan. Yunmen said, Recently at Xichan Sure enough—damnably solid. At that time, it was best to give him his proper fodder. what sayings are there? The monk spread both hands. Yunmen struck one palm. The monk said, Wanting to bring it up, he fears startling the master. He discerns the incoming wind deeply; it is like the master talking in his sleep. A blunder. It is ruined. Luring thieves to wreck the house—no wonder it makes people suspicious. Act according to the order. A fine beating—such swift decisiveness is hard to meet. My words are with you, master. Yunmen again spread both hands. The monk had nothing to say, and Yunmen struck. You want to overturn the verdict, but you seem to have the moves to snatch the banner and seize the drum. A perilous ride. Even with a green dragon, he does not know how to ride. What a pity. He must not be let off. This staff should land on Yunmen. Why? When it should be cut off, if you do not cut it off, you invite disorder. How many blows should the senior monk take? Letting him off once—if you do not let him off, then what?
Yunmen asked this monk, Where have you just come from? The monk said, Xichan. This is talk right

text_zh: 雲門問這僧。近離甚處。僧云。西禪。這箇是當 面話。如閃電相似。門云。近日有何言句。也只 是平常說話。這僧也不妨是箇作家。却倒去 驗雲門。便展兩手。若是尋常人遭此一驗。便 見手忙脚亂。他雲門有石火電光之機。便打 一掌。僧云。打即故是。爭奈某甲話在。這僧有 轉身處。所以雲門放開。却展兩手。其僧無語。 門便打。看他雲門自是作家。行一步知一步 落處。會瞻前亦解顧後。不失蹤由。這僧只解 瞻前不能顧後。頌云。
text_en: in your face, like a flash of lightning. Yunmen said, Recently what sayings are there? That is also just ordinary talk. This monk, too, is not without being a capable one—he turned it around to test Yunmen, and spread both hands. If an ordinary person met such a test, they would immediately be flustered and scrambling. But Yunmen had the opportunity of stone-spark and lightning-flash, and struck one palm. The monk said, Striking is indeed so, but what about my words being here? This monk had a place to turn around. Therefore Yunmen loosened up and again spread both hands. The monk had nothing to say. Yunmen then struck. See how Yunmen is truly a master of the craft: with each step he knows where it lands; he can look ahead and also look back, never losing the trail. This monk only knew how to look ahead and could not look back. The verse says:
Tiger head and tiger tail gathered in at once—chilling A knife that kills, a sword that brings to life—only this monk will do. A thousand soldiers are easy to get; one general is hard to find.

text_zh: 雪竇頌得此話極易會。大意只頌雲門機鋒。 所以道。虎頭虎尾一時收。古人云。據虎頭收 虎尾。第一句下明宗旨。雪竇只據欵結案。愛 雲門會據虎頭。又能收虎尾。僧展兩手。門便 打。是據虎頭。雲門展兩手。僧無語。門又打。 是收虎尾。頭尾齊收。眼似流星。自然如擊石 火。似閃電光。直得凜凜威風四百州。直得盡 大地世界風颯颯地。却問。不知何太嶮。不妨 有嶮處。雪竇云。放過一著。且道如今不放過 時又作麼生。盡大地人。總須喫棒。如今禪和 子。總道等他展手時。也還他本分草料。似則 也似。是則未是。雲門不可只恁麼教爾休。也 須別有事在。
text_en: Therefore he says, Tiger head and tiger tail gathered in at once. The ancients said, Seize the tiger head and gather the tiger tail. Under the first line the central meaning is made clear. Xuedou only decides the case on the evidence, delighting that Yunmen can seize the tiger head and also gather the tiger tail. The monk spread both hands and Yunmen struck—this is seizing the tiger head. Yunmen spread both hands; the monk had nothing to say; Yunmen struck again—this is gathering the tiger tail. Head and tail gathered together, eyes like shooting stars—naturally like striking stone for sparks, like a flash of lightning. It reaches the point of chilling majesty over four hundred prefectures; it reaches the point that the whole world is swept by wind. Yet he asks back, Not knowing why it is so perilous. It is no harm that there is a perilous place. Xuedou said, Let one move pass. Tell me, if one does not let it pass now, then what? Everyone on the great earth would have to eat the staff. Nowadays Zen monks all say that when he spreads his hands, you should return his own proper fodder to him. It seems so, and it also seems so, but though it is so, it is not yet so. Yunmen cannot just teach you to rest in that way; there must be something else in it.

On the way back, Yuan said: The master, quickly tell me. If Too alert. you do not tell me, I will beat the master. I said: If you beat me, then beat me; if you want me to speak, then I will not speak. Yuan then struck him. Yet he falls short by a bit. Rare to meet a guest who pierces the ear; often you meet those who notch the boat. A fellow like this cannot speak a word. Entering hell like an arrow. Again and again, it must be made weighty—right on the body he is robbed. This old fellow is covered head to toe in mud and water; his first intention does not change. A fine beating—now tell me, why beat him? It turns out someone is taking the unjust staff. Later Daowu passed away. Yuan went to Shishuang and brought up the previous words. Shishuang said: I will not speak of life; I will not speak of death. Yuan said: Why not speak? Shishuang said: Not speaking, not speaking. Knowing and yet deliberately offending—do you know whether it is so or not? If it is, then it is very strange indeed. Damnably fresh. This kind of tea and rice—turns out someone is eating it. Though the words are the same, the meaning is not twofold. Tell me: compared with the earlier question, is it the same or different? In heaven and on earth—Caoqi's waves seem alike. text_en: dead? I said: I will not speak of life; I will not speak of death. If you enter right under the phrase, then you enter. Right at the words you know where to return. This right here is the key point for passing through life and death. If it is not so, you often miss it head-on. Look at how the ancients, in walking, standing, sitting, and lying down, kept this matter in mind. As soon as they arrived at a home to offer condolences, Jian- yuan patted the coffin and asked Daowu: Alive, or dead? Daowu did not shift by a hair, and replied to him: I will not speak of life; I will not speak of death. Jianyuan, right in front of him, missed it, chasing after the words and saying: Why not speak? I said: Not speaking, not speaking. I could be said to have a heart of pure sincerity, going along with the mistake to meet the mistake. Yuan still did not wake up. On the way back he again said: The master, quickly tell me. If you do not tell me, I will beat the master. What does this fellow know of what is good or bad? So-called: a good heart does not get a good return. Daowu still had an old woman’s anxious heart and again said to him: If you beat me, then beat me; if you want me to speak, then I will not speak. Yuan then struck him. Although it was like this, he still gained a point. Daowu did this for him with blood-dripping earnestness, yet Jianyuan took it without even a glance. After Daowu was struck by him, he then said to Jianyuan: You go for now; I fear the monastery officials will find out and bring trouble upon you. He secretly sent Jianyuan out. Daowu was far too compassionate. Later Yuan came to a small temple and heard an attendant reciting the Guanyin Sutra, saying: If one should be saved by the body of a monk, then one manifests the body of a monk and teaches the Dharma. Suddenly he had a great awakening and said: At that time I wrongly blamed my former teacher. How could I have known this matter is not in words and phrases? The ancients said: A boundless great person gets turned around within the pulse of words. Some with emotional interpretations say: Daowu’s Not speaking, not speaking—this is already speaking. They call it striking the back and turning the tendons, making people unable to grope it out. If you understand it like that, how will you ever be steady and secure? If your feet tread the real ground, not separated by a hair, then you see the Seven Worthy Ladies roaming the charnel ground. They pointed to a corpse and asked: The corpse is here—where is the person? The eldest sister said: What, what! The whole assembly together realized the patience of the unborn Dharma. Tell me, how many is that? A thousand, ten thousand—just one. Later Jianyuan arrived at Shishuang and raised the earlier words. Shishuang as before said: I will not speak of life; I will not speak of death. Yuan said: Why not speak? Shishuang said: Not speaking, not speaking. Then he awakened. One day he took a shovel and, in the Dharma hall, went from east to west and from west to east. He meant to present his own understanding. Shishuang indeed asked: What are you doing? Yuan said: Seeking the former teacher’s sacred bones. Shishuang then cut off his heels, saying: Here with me the floodwaters are vast, the white waves surge to the sky—what former teacher’s sacred bones are you seeking? Since he was seeking the former teacher’s sacred bones, why did Shishuang speak like that? When you get here, if at the place of I will not speak of life; I will not speak of death, you can be confirmed right at the words—only then do you know from beginning to end you can fully use the whole function. If you make it into doctrine, weighing and thinking, then it truly is hard to see. Jianyuan said: Now is exactly the time to apply effort. See how after awakening he spoke with natural strangeness: Daowu’s skull was like golden color; when struck it made a bronze sound. Xuedou added a remark: Blue heaven, blue heaven. The meaning fell on two sides. Taiyuan Fu said: The former teacher’s sacred bones are still here—naturally spoken with steadiness. With this one slip, it is all taken to one side at once. Tell me, what is the essential point of insight here? What is the place to apply effort? Haven’t you heard: when one place is penetrated, a thousand places, ten thousand places are penetrated all at once. If you can penetrate through at the place of not speaking, not speaking, then you cut off the tongues of all people under heaven. If you cannot penetrate, you still must investigate and awaken by yourself; you cannot let the days pass casually. What a pity, all that time. Xuedou’s verse says:

Waves arise on level ground—right to your nostrils. The golden sacred bones are still here today. Cut off the tongue; block up the throat. Toss it to one side—only afraid no one will recognize it. With white waves surging to the sky, where can you set it down? Letting it off once: it slips right under your heel; in your eyes, in your ears— it cannot be lodged. text_zh: 雪竇偏會下注脚。他是雲門下兒孫。凡一句 中。具三句底鉗鎚。向難道處道破。向撥不開 處撥開。去他緊要處頌出。直道兔馬有角。牛 羊無角。且道兔馬為什麼有角。牛羊為什麼 却無角。若透得前話。始知雪竇有為人處。有 者錯會道。不道便是道。無句是有句。兔馬無 角。却云有角。牛羊有角。却云無角。且得沒交 涉。殊不知。古人千變萬化。現如此神通。只為 打破爾這精靈鬼窟。若透得去。不消一箇了 字。兔馬有角牛羊無角。絕毫絕氂。如山如嶽。 這四句。似摩尼寶珠一顆相似。雪竇渾淪地。 吐在爾面前了也。末後皆是據欵結案。黃金 靈骨。今猶在。白浪滔天何處著。此頌石霜 與大原孚語。為什麼無處著。隻履西歸曾失 却。靈龜曳尾。此是雪竇轉身為人處。古人 道。他參活句不參死句。既是失却。他一火為 什麼。却競頭爭。
text_en: there are the tongs and hammer of three phrases. He speaks through what is hard to say; he pries open what cannot be pried open. He takes its crucial point and chants it out, saying straight: rabbits and horses have horns; oxen and sheep have no horns. Tell me, why do rabbits and horses have horns? Why do oxen and sheep instead have no horns? If you penetrate the earlier words, only then do you know Xuedou has a way of working for people. Some mistakenly understand it and say: not speaking is speaking; having no phrase is having a phrase. Rabbits and horses have no horns, yet they say they have horns; oxen and sheep have horns, yet they say they have no horns. That is still irrelevant. They do not realize that the ancients, transforming in a thousand ways, manifest such spiritual powers only to smash your goblin cave of cleverness. If you can penetrate through, there is no need for a single finished word. Rabbits and horses have horns; oxen and sheep have no horns. Cut off hair and down entirely—like mountains, like peaks. These four lines are like a single mani jewel. Xuedou, all in one lump, spits it out right in front of you. At the end it is all deciding the case by the evidence. The golden sacred bones are still here today; with white waves surging to the sky, where can you set it down? This verses Shishuang’s words together with Taiyuan Fu’s. Why is there nowhere to set it down? The single sandal going back to the West was once lost altogether. The spirit tortoise drags its tail—this is where Xuedou turns around to work for people. The ancients said: he investigates the living phrase, not the dead phrase. Since it was lost, why does he in one blaze still scramble and contend?

text_zh: 垂示云。諸佛不曾出世。亦無一法與人。祖師 不曾西來。未甞以心傳授。自是時人不了。向 外馳求。殊不知自己脚跟下。一段大事因緣。 千聖亦摸索不著。只如今見不見聞不聞。說 不說知不知。從什麼處得來。若未能洞達。且 向葛藤窟裏會取。試舉看。
text_en: never came from the West, and never transmitted mind to mind. It is only that people of the time do not understand, and run outward in search, not realizing that beneath their own heels lies a great matter of causes and conditions. A thousand sages also cannot grope it out. Right now, do you see or not see, hear or not hear—tell me, do you speak or not speak, know or not know—where does it come from? If you do not understand, then do not make principle-calculations. Do you not see Touzi Zongdao? Under Xuedou he served as a scribe. Xuedou had him investigate The supreme Way is not difficult, it only dislikes choosing and selecting. From this he gained understanding. One day Xuedou asked him, “The supreme Way is not difficult; it only dislikes choosing and picking—what do you make of that?” Zong said, “Beast, beast!” Later he lived in seclusion at Touzi. Whenever he went to take up abbacy, he wrapped his kashaya around straw sandals and sutra texts. A monk asked, “What is the household style of a person of the Way?” Zong said, “A kashaya wrapped around straw sandals.” The monk said, “I don’t yet understand the meaning—how is it?” Zong said, “Barefoot down in Tongcheng.” Therefore it is said: offering to the Buddha is not a matter of much incense. If you can penetrate through and cast it off, granting and seizing are in my hands. Since it is a single question and a single answer, it is plainly present—why then did Zhaozhou say, “For five years I couldn’t get it out”? Tell me—was that the pits and holes of the people of the time or not? Zhaozhou answered him from within the pits and holes; he answered him from outside the pits and holes. You must know this matter is not in words and phrases. If there is someone who penetrates to bone and marrow and can believe it through, it is like a dragon gaining water, like a tiger leaning on a mountain. The verse says:

text_en: Where do the mountains, rivers, and great earth come from?” If you say there is, you are blind; if you say there is not, you Dead. Do you still see where Yunmen worked for people? Give me back my staff. Nowadays people do not understand Yunmen’s uniquely revealed point, and instead say, “Using form to illuminate the mind,” “attaching to things” to manifest principle.” Take Shakyamuni for example: for forty-nine years he preached the Dharma; one cannot fail to know this line of talk. Why? Then they bring up the holding up of a flower and Kashyapa’s faint smile. This old fellow then smears on a beard and says, “I have the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, the wondrous mind of nirvana; I entrust it to Mahakashyapa.” What need is there, then, to speak of a separate transmission of the mind-seal? Since you are all guests under the Patriarchs’ gate, do you understand the mind that is singly transmitted? If there is a single thing in your chest, mountains, rivers, and the great earth abruptly appear before you. If there is not a single thing in your chest, then outwardly there is not the slightest trace. What talk is there of principle and wisdom, dark merging, or spirit meeting? Why? One understanding is all understandings; one clarity is all clarity. Changsha said, “Students of the Way do not recognize the real, only because from the start they have recognized the spirit.” The root of birth and death from measureless kalpas—fools call it the original person. If you suddenly smash through the realm of the aggregates, body and mind are one; within the body and outside it there is nothing left over—still you have not gotten even half of it. What talk is there of “using form to illuminate the mind,” “attaching to things” to manifest principle”? The ancients said, “As soon as a single mote arises, the whole earth is gathered in.” Tell me: what is that single mote? If you recognize this single mote, then you recognize the staff. The moment you raise the staff, you immediately see its wondrous functioning in every direction. Talking like this is already tangled vines. How much more if you go on and turn it into a dragon. Storekeeper Qing said, “In the five thousand four hundred and eighteen fascicles, was there ever talk like this?” Yunmen always, with the staff, would pick up the whole device and the great function, working for people in a vividly alive way. Bajiao addressed the assembly and said, “The nostrils of patch-robed monks are all on the tip of the staff.” Yongjia also said, “It is not an empty matter of outward marks; the Tathagata’s jeweled staff is his own trace.” In the past, when the Tathagata was with Dipankara Buddha, he spread out his hair and covered the mud to await that Buddha. Dipankara said, “In this place there should be built a monastery.” At that time a deva prince took a single blade of grass and marked it, saying, “Build a monastery right here.” Tell me, everyone: where did this news come from? The Patriarch said, “Take realization at the end of the staff; take it up under the shout.” Tell me, what is it that you take up? Suddenly someone asks, “What is the staff? Is it doing a somersault? Is it a single clap of the hands?” All of that is just playing with spirits—and luckily it has nothing to do with it. Xuedou versified: Stripping away. the sound races.
The staff swallows heaven and earth—mere talk, like peach-blossom waves surging. What are you saying? Only use it to beat the dog. Push open upward

text_en: a dragon: no need to say it that way. It is only that the staff swallows heaven and earth. Xuedou in the main point spares people sentimental interpretations; he further says it is mere talk of the peach-blossom waves surging. There is even less need to speak of turning into a dragon. Yu Gate has three tiers of waves; every third month, when the peach blossoms bloom, the waves rise. If a fish can swim against the current and leap over the waves, it immediately turns into a dragon. Xuedou says: even if it turns into a dragon, it is still mere talk. The one whose tail is scorched is not about grasping clouds and seizing mist. When the fish passes Yu Gate, there is naturally heavenly fire that scorches its tail; then it grasps clouds and seizes mist and goes off. Xuedou's meaning is: even if it turns into a dragon, it still is not in grasping clouds and seizing mist either. Why must one who exposes his gills lose courage and soul? The Preface to the Qingliang Commentary says: those who have amassed practice as bodhisattvas still expose their gills at Dragon Gate. The general meaning is to clarify that the Avatamsaka realm is not something small virtue and small wisdom can reach. It is like a fish passing Dragon Gate: if it cannot get through, it bumps its forehead and turns back, trapped in dead water and sandy flats, exposing its gills there. Xuedou's meaning is: once it bumps its forehead and turns back, it will surely lose courage and soul. He has brought it up too. Did you hear or not? He adds another footnote, and in one stroke sweeps it all clean for you. You all must go straight on open and unencumbered; do not get tangled up in a mass of fuss and confusion. If you get tangled up again, you will lose the staff. Seventy-two blows are still lenient; Xuedou sets aside the heavy and takes the light for your sake. The ancients spoke of seventy-two blows, and turned it into one hundred and fifty. People nowadays misunderstand and only count the numbers. It should be seventy-five blows. Why? They only see seventy-two blows, not realizing the ancients' meaning is beyond the words. Therefore it is said: This matter is not in words and phrases, lest later people go drilling and chiseling at it. That is why Xuedou cites it. Even if you truly are open and unencumbered, it would be just right to give you seventy-two blows; that is still leniency. Even if you had it all, a hundred and fifty would not let you off. With one verse he has finished it, yet he again picked up the staff, helping in layer upon layer. Even so, not a single one of you has blood under the skin. blood.

text_en: a single mote of dust, the household and the nation perish. Tell me: is establishing a single mote of dust it, or is not establishing a single mote of dust it? When you reach here, great functioning must appear before you can. Therefore it is said: even if you awaken to it in front of words, you still cling to the shell and are deluded by the seal. Even if you thoroughly understand beneath the phrase, you still cannot avoid wild views whenever you meet it. He is a venerable elder under Linji, who directly uses his proper fodder. If you establish a single mote of dust, the household and the nation flourish: the old rustic frowns, for the intent is to found the state and pacify the realm; you must rely on scheming ministers and fierce generals, and only then do qilin appear and phoenixes soar, as auspicious signs of great peace. He is a man of some backwater hamlet; how would he know such a thing? If you do not establish a single mote of dust, the household and the nation perish: the wind rustles and whistles; why would the old rustic come out singing? Only because the household and the nation perish. In the Caodong house this is called a place of transformation: there is no Buddha and no sentient beings, no right and no wrong, no good and no evil, cutting off sound and traces. Therefore it is said: though gold dust is precious, if it gets in the eye it becomes a cataract. And it is also said: gold dust in the eye is a cataract; the pearl in the robe is dust upon the Dharma. If your own spirit is still not weighty, who are Buddhas and patriarchs? Seven penetrations and eight openings, spiritual powers and wondrous function, are not taken as extraordinary. When you reach here, cover your head with your patch robe and all affairs cease. At this point, this mountain monk does not understand at all. If you further speak of mind and speak of nature, speak of the mysterious and the subtle, none of it is of any use. Why is that? Their own house has its realm of immortals. Nanquan instructed the assembly, saying: At Huangmei there were seven hundred eminent monks, all of them people who understood Buddhadharma; yet none obtained his robe and bowl. Only the layman Lu did not understand Buddhadharma, and so obtained his robe and bowl. He also said: the buddhas of the three times do not know it is; the civet cat and the white ox do know it is. The old rustic may frown, or may sing; tell me, how do you understand it? Tell me, what kind of eyes does he have, that he is like this? You must know: in front of the old rustic's gate there are other statutes. Xuedou picked up both. Then he picked up his staff and said: Are there any patch-robed monks who live together and die together? At that time, if there had been a fellow who came forth and spoke a single sentence, making guest and host for each other, it would have spared old Xuedou from, behind, pointing at his own chest.

text_en: the mountain of form. Tell me, was Yunmen's intent on the tip of the fishing pole, or on the lantern? This is several lines from Master Zhao's Treatise on the Treasury of Treasures; Yunmen picked them up to show the assembly. Master Zhao, in the Later Qin, composed the treatise at Xiaoyao Garden and wrote out the Vimalakirti Sutra; only then did he realize Zhuangzi and Laozi had not exhausted its subtlety. Zhao then paid respects to Kumarajiva as his teacher, and also visited the Waguansi with the bodhisattva Bhadrapala, transmitting the mind-seal from the twenty-seventh patriarch of the Western Heavens. Zhao deeply entered its inner chambers. One day Zhao met with calamity; at the time of execution, he begged for seven On a certain day, Jia wrote the Treatise on the Precious Treasury. Yunmen then picked up four lines from the treatise and presented them to the assembly. The general meaning says: how can a priceless treasure be hidden within the realm of the skandhas? The language in the treatise all accords with the way the school speaks. Do you not see Jingqing ask Caoshan, "As for the principle of pure emptiness, what is it like when ultimately there is no body?" Caoshan said, "The principle is just like that." "Then what about the matter?" Jingqing said, "As the principle, so the matter." Caoshan said, "Deceiving Caoshan alone is fine—what can you do about the eyes of all the sages?" Jingqing said, "If there were no eyes of the sages, how would you know it is not like this?" Caoshan said, "In public, not even a needle is allowed; in private, carts and horses pass through." Therefore it is said: within heaven and earth, within the universe, there is a single treasure, hidden in the body- mountain. The general meaning makes clear that everyone is fully endowed, each one perfectly complete. Yunmen then picked it up and presented it to the assembly—already completely ready-made. Do not be like a seat master again, going to annotate it. Out of compassion, he even added a footnote for you, saying: carry the lantern into the Buddha hall. Bring the three gates onto the lantern. Now tell me—when Yunmen speaks like this, what is his meaning? Do you not see the ancients say: the true nature of ignorance is buddha-nature. The illusory, empty body of transformation is the dharma body. And they also say: within the ordinary mind one sees the buddha mind. The body- mountain is the four elements and five skandhas. Within it there is a single treasure, hidden in the body-mountain. Therefore it is said: the buddhas are in the mind; deluded people seek outward. Within you carry a priceless treasure and do not recognize it—your whole life is wasted. And it is also said: buddha-nature stands forth plainly manifest; those who abide in appearances, sentient beings, find it hard to see. If you awaken to sentient beings having no self, how is my face any different from the Buddha's face? Mind is the original mind; face is the face born of mother. Even aeon-stones can be moved, yet within this there is no change. Some only take that bright and numinous awareness as the treasure, but they do not get its function, nor do they get its subtlety. Therefore they cannot move or turn; they cannot open or set it in motion. The ancients said: when pressed to the limit, you change; when you change, you come through. Carry the lantern into the Buddha hall—if it were something ordinary feelings could measure, then bringing the three gates onto the lantern—could you still measure it? Yunmen, all at once, smashes your emotional consciousness, your imaginings, your gain and loss, right and wrong. Xuedou said: I love Shaoyang's newly set mechanism—his whole life he has been pulling nails and drawing out wedges for people. He also said: how much can a crooked piece of wood know, sitting in the seat? A sharp blade cuts it off, and makes people love it. He said: carry the lantern into the Buddha hall—this one line already cuts it off. And then: bring the three gates onto the lantern. If you speak of this matter, it is like striking sparks from flint, like the flash of lightning. Yunmen said: if you are to meet it, first find a way in. Buddhas as numerous as motes of dust are under your heels; the holy teachings of the Tripitaka are on your tongue. Better to awaken. You students of the master, do not indulge in deluded thoughts. Heaven is heaven; earth is earth. Mountains are mountains; waters are waters. Monks are monks; laypeople are laypeople. After a long while he said, "Bring me the mountain right in front and set it here for me to see." Then a monk came forward and asked, "When a student sees mountains as mountains and waters as waters, how is it?" Yunmen said, "Why do the three gates pass through here?" Fearing you would die, he drew a stroke with his hand and said, "When you recognize it, it is the finest flavor of ghee. If you do not recognize it, it instead becomes poison." Therefore it is said: when it is thoroughly clear, there is nothing left to clear up; in the most mysterious place, you must directly give a shout. Xuedou again picked it up, saying: within heaven and earth, within the universe, there is a single treasure hidden in the body-mountain. It hangs on the wall. For nine years Bodhidharma did not dare look at it straight on, yet now if a patch-robed monk wants to see, he gets a staff across the back. Look at that master of the essential ground— in the end he never ties people up with any real dharma. Xuansha said: penned in, it will not stay; called to, it does not turn its head back. Even so, it is still the spirit turtle dragging its tail. Xuedou's verse says:
Look, look—on the ancient bank, who is holding the fishing rod? Hold your eyes high—what use is looking? The black dragon plays with the pearl. Solitary and perilous—how solitary and perilous.

The ancients said: the numinous light shines alone, far removed from sense faculties and sense objects. The essence reveals true constancy, not bound by words. Mind-nature is unstained, originally complete. Only depart from deluded conditions, and you are thusness itself, Buddha. If you only sit yourself to death in the place of glowering and glaring, how could you ever escape sense faculties and objects? Xuedou said: look, Look: Yunmen is like one holding a fishing rod on an ancient bank. The clouds drift slowly; the waters spread vast and wide. The bright moon reflects the reed blossoms; the reed blossoms reflect the bright moon. Right at such a time, tell me: what realm is this? If you see it straightaway, then before and after are only one phrase alike—stare! Chou-geng-qie: to stare straight.

text_en: intent? This story of cutting the cat—throughout the monasteries under heaven, people discuss it in a great flood. Some say, “It was right at the lifting.” Others say, “It was in the cutting.” In any case, it is all irrelevant. If he had not lifted it up, they would still have spun around and around, making up every kind of reasoning. They do not realize that those ancients had eyes that could settle heaven and earth, and a sword that could settle heaven and earth. Tell me: in the end, who cut the cat? Just consider: when Nansen lifted it and said, “If you can speak, I won’t cut it,” if at that moment someone had spoken—tell me, would Nansen cut or not cut? Therefore it is said: When the true command is carried out, the ten directions are cut off as you sit; go out beyond the heavens and look—who is the person within this? In truth, at that time he never cut it. This talk is also not found in cutting or not cutting. This matter is plainly known—so clear—do not seek it in emotional dust and opinions. If you seek it in emotional dust and opinions, you will betray Nansen. Just look on the edge of the sword where you meet it head-on: “is” also works, “is not” also works, neither is nor is not also works. So the ancients said: When pressed to the limit, you change; when you change, you pass through. People today do not understand adaptation; they only keep running after phrases. When Nansen lifted it like that, it was not to make people utter some particular line on the spot; he only wanted to make people present themselves. Each uses it for himself and knows it for himself. If you do not understand it like this, in the end you will grope and not find it. Xuedou, right on the spot, composed this verse:

text_en: In the evening Nansen again brought up the earlier story and asked Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou was an old hand, so he took off his straw sandals, put them on his head, and went out. Nansen said, “If you had been there, you would have saved the cat.” Tell me: is it truly like this or not like this? Nansen said, “If you can speak, I won’t He cut it down—like striking sparks from stone, like a flash of lightning. Zhaozhou then took off his straw sandals and, putting them on his head, went out. He studied living phrases, not dead phrases. Day after day new, moment after moment new. A thousand sages cannot shift it by even a hair. You must bring forth your own family treasure. Only then do you see his whole functioning and great use. He said, I am a Dharma king, free within the Dharma. Many people misread it, saying Zhaozhou temporarily took the straw sandals as a cat. Some say, Since he said, If you can speak, I will not cut, he then wore the straw sandals on his head and went out, meaning, You cut the cat; it has nothing to do with me—so he stays uninvolved. This is just playing tricks with the spirit. They do not realize the intent of the ancients: like heaven universally covering, like earth universally supporting. That father and son matched each other; their pivot-points and edge met. The moment one raised the head, the other understood the tail. Students today do not recognize where the ancients turn; they vainly speculate along the road of ideas. If you want to see it, just go to where Nanquan and Zhaozhou turn, and you will see. text_zh: 公案圓來問趙州。慶藏主道。如人結案相似。 八棒是八棒。十三是十三。已斷了也。却拈來 問趙州。州是他屋裏人。會南泉意旨。他是透 徹底人。𡎺著磕著便轉。具本分作家眼腦。纔 聞舉著。剔起便行。雪竇道。長安城裏任閑遊。 漏逗不少。古人道。長安雖樂。不是久居。又 云。長安甚閙。我國晏然也。須是識機宜別休 咎始得。草鞋頭戴無人會。戴草鞋處。這些 子。雖無許多事。所以道。唯我能知。唯我能 證。方見得南泉趙州雪竇同得同用處。且道 而今作麼生會。歸到家山即便休。什麼處是 家山。他若不會。必不恁麼道。他既會。且道家 山在什麼處。便打。

Xuedou said, In Chang’an city, he may wander at leisure. Not a bit was leaked or fumbled. The ancients said, Though Chang’an is pleasant, it is not a place to stay long. Also they said, Chang’an is very noisy; my country is at peace. You must recognize the right moment and stop blaming before it will do. Straw sandals worn on the head—no one understands. As for the wearing of straw sandals, these fellows, though there is not all that much going on—so it is said, Only I can know; only I can certify. Only then do you see where Nanquan, Zhaozhou, and Xuedou share the same attainment and the same use. Tell me, how do you understand it now? Returning to the home mountain, he immediately rests. What place is the home mountain? If he did not understand, he surely would not speak like that. Since he did understand, tell me, the home mountain is in what place? He strikes.

text_en: phrases? Some say wordlessness is it—then what need was there for the patriarch to come from the West at all? And as for all those cases from of old, in the end how do you see their landing place? There are not a few who can talk about understanding this case. Some call it a long silence; some call it sitting firm; some call it silent and not answering. Fortunately, none of that is relevant— when have they ever actually grasped it? In truth, this matter is not on words and phrases. Yet it is not apart from words and phrases. If there is the slightest conjecturing, you are off by thousands upon thousands of miles. Look—after the non-Buddhist awakened, only then did he know it is not here, and not there; not in yes, and not in no. Tell me, what is it? Venerable Tian yi Huai the master versified it: Vimalakirti was not silent, not long in silence; sitting firm and deliberating becomes a fault. In the hair-splitting sword case, cold light is chill; non-Buddhists and heavenly demons all fold their hands. Venerable Baizhang Chang visited Fayan; Fayan had him look into these words. One day Fayan asked, What case are you looking into? Chang said, The non-Buddhist asking the Buddha. Fayan said, Try raising it. Chang was about to open his mouth. Fayan said, Stop, stop. You are trying to understand it in the long-silence place, aren’t you? At those words, Chang suddenly had a great awakening. Later he instructed the assembly, Baizhang has three tips: Drink tea—take care. Rest. If you speculate and think it over again, I know you still have not penetrated. Cuiyan Zhen, patting his chest, said: In the six directions there are nine; there are blue, yellow, red, and white. Each one is interwoven. The non-Buddhist understood the four Vedas and treatises, and said of himself, I am an all knowing person. Everywhere he went he sought people to debate. He brought up this question to cut off Shakyamuni the old fellow’s tongue. The World-Honored One did not spend the slightest effort, and he immediately awakened. He praised him, saying, World-Honored One, of great compassion and great pity, you have opened my deluded cloud and allowed me to enter. Tell me, how is this the place of great compassion and great pity? The World-Honored One, with a single eye, penetrates the three times; the non-Buddhist, with both pupils, spans the five heavens. Weishan Zhenru raised it and said, The non-Buddhist carried a supreme treasure within; the World-Honored One personally lifted it high. The myriad things appear; all phenomena are clearly distinct. But in the end, what did the non-Buddhist awaken to? It is like chasing a dog up against a wall—when it reaches the extreme, there is no road; it must turn back. Then it becomes lively and nimble. If you calculate right and wrong, at once set it down—feelings exhausted, views removed—naturally it becomes thoroughly clear. After the non-Buddhist left, Ananda asked the Buddha, What did the non-Buddhist realize that he says he entered? The Buddha said, It is like a fine horse in the world that moves when it sees the shadow of the whip. Later, all sorts of expedient talk got blown into a different tune. And it said, Dragon head, snake tail. Where is the World-Honored One’s whip-shadow? Where is the place of seeing the whip-shadow? Xuedou said, Not distinguishing crooked and correct—the fault is due to the whip-shadow. Zhenru said, Ananda strikes the golden bell again; the four assemblies hear together. Even so, it is very much like two dragons fighting over a pearl, increasing the wise one’s fierce authority. Xuedou’s verse says:

text_en: falls into “there isn’t.” If not east, then west. Left eye half a jin, right eye eight liang. A bright mirror suddenly comes before the stand; Do you still see old Shakyamuni? One flick and it turns—broken too, broken too. Ruined—ruined, ruined. right on the spot it distinguishes fair and foul. The whole great earth is a gate of liberation. He deserves thirty blows. Do you still see old Shakyamuni? When fair and foul are distinguished, the deluded cloud opens. I let out a single line and allow you a place to turn around—yet what can you do, you’re still just an outsider. From the gate of compassion, where could dust and grime arise? Throughout the whole realm it has never been hidden. Back up, back up—Bodhidharma is coming! Therefore think of the fine horse that spies the whip shadow— I have my staff; I don’t need you to give it to me. Tell me, where is the place of the whip’s shadow? Where is the place of the fine horse? a thousand miles chasing the wind, called back. Ride the Buddha hall and go out through the three gates. Turn around and you’re wrong; let it pass and you can’t. Then he strikes. Called back—snap the fingers three times. Ahead you don’t reach a village; behind you don’t make the inn. Snap the staff in two—where will you go? Xuedou’s thunder is very loud, but there are no raindrops at all.

text_en: is the lifeline of all people since the very beginning. Have you not seen the ancients say, The numinous pivot of a thousand sages is not easy to approach; when a dragon gives birth to a dragon’s child, do not dally. Zhaozhou seized the matchless jade of a whole city; the King of Qin and Xiangru both lost themselves. The non-Buddhist, however, could hold it fast and take charge of it, without ever being moved. Why? He said, I do not ask about words that affirm; I do not ask about words that deny. Is this not the whole functioning? The World-Honored One knew how to read the wind and set the sail, to meet the illness with the medicine. Therefore he remained silent for a long time, raising the whole functioning. The non-Buddhist understood it with his whole body. The pivot-wheel then turned with a rumbling roll. It does not turn toward affirmation, and does not turn toward denial. It does not fall into gain and loss, and is not bound by ordinary or sage. Both sides are cut off at once. As soon as the World-Honored One fell silent for a long time, he bowed. People today mostly fall into denial; otherwise they fall into affirmation. They keep running to both ends in affirmation and denial. Xuedou said, A bright mirror suddenly comes before the stand. Right on the spot it distinguishes fair and foul. This never moved at all; it only took a single long silence, like a bright mirror before the stand—ten thousand forms cannot escape their shape and substance. The non-Buddhist said, World-Honored One, of great compassion and great pity, you have opened my deluded cloud and allowed me to enter. Tell me, what place is this? It is the place where the non-Buddhist entered. When you come here, each person must investigate for himself, awaken for himself, understand for himself—only then. Then in every place, walking, standing, sitting Lying down—without asking of high or low—it is all complete at once, not shifting or altering by even the slightest bit. The moment you start calculating, if there is even the slightest trace of reasoning, it blocks you up and kills you—there is no way in at all. Later, the verse says, The World-Honored One’s great compassion and great mercy open my cloud of delusion and let me enter. Right then, suddenly, beauty and ugliness are distinguished; when beauty and ugliness split apart, the cloud of delusion opens. From where could dust arise in the gate of compassion? The whole great earth is the World-Honored One’s gate of great compassion and great mercy. If you penetrate it, it won’t take even a pinch—this too is a gate that has been thrown wide open. Haven’t you seen how, during the twenty-one days, the World-Honored One contemplated such matters: I would rather not teach the Dharma and quickly enter nirvana. Then he thought of the fine horse that glimpses the shadow of the whip—over a thousand miles it chases the wind and can be called back. The wind-chasing horse, seeing the whip’s shadow, immediately goes a thousand miles. Told to return, it returns. Xuedou’s intent is to praise this: only if you find a swift one can it turn with a single flick, come back with a single call. If you can call it back, then snap your fingers three times. Now tell me, is that exposing it, or is it throwing sand?

text_en: before it will do. This monk’s eyes were like shooting stars, yet Yantou still saw through him and strung him up in one chain. If he had been a real fellow then—whether killing or giving life—he would have used it the moment it was raised. This monk was sloppy and careless, yet said, I recovered it. Traveling like this, if old King Yama asks you, Where’s the money for your meals? Who knows how many straw sandals you’ve worn through. When he got to Xuefeng, if he had even a bit of eye-muscle, he would have known to vanish in a flash—wouldn’t that have been a delight? In this set of circumstances there are knots and corners of garbled error. Though in this matter there is no gain or loss, the gain and loss are very great. Though there is no choosing, when you come here you still must choose with eyes. Look at how Longya traveled and brought up this question to Deshan: A student wields the Moye sword, and is about to take the master’s head—what then? Deshan stretched out his neck and came close. Longya said, Master, your head has fallen off. Deshan then returned to the abbot’s quarters. Later Longya brought this up to Dongshan. Dongshan said, What did Deshan say at the time? Longya said, He was silent. Dongshan said, Put his silence aside for now—lend me Deshan’s fallen head so I can have a look. At these words Longya had a great awakening. He then burned incense, gazed from afar toward Deshan, bowed, and repented. A monk carried the news to Deshan. Deshan said, Dongshan— that old fellow—doesn’t know good from bad. This man has been dead for who knows how long; saving him, what use is it? This case is just like Longya’s. Deshan returning to the abbot’s quarters is, in the dark, most wonderful. Yantou’s loud laughter—within his laughter there is poison. If someone can discern it, they can stride across the world. If this monk had discerned it then, for ages to come he would have been spared blame. Under Yantou’s gate it was already one great misstep. See how old man Xuefeng was a fellow student—he knew where it landed, yet did not explain it for him; he only gave thirty blows and drove him out of the monastery. That can illuminate the past and cut off the future. This is the method of grasping an adept patchrobed monk by the nostrils and helping people—further not doing anything else to him, letting him awaken on his own. A true master in helping people sometimes encloses and covers, not letting him show his head; sometimes lets him go along dead and sloppy— yet there must be a way to step out. Great Yantou and Xuefeng were instead seen through by this meal-eating Chan fellow. Just take Yantou’s words: After Huang Chao passed through, did you still recover the sword? Now tell me, what phrase fits right here, so you avoid his laughter, and also avoid Xuefeng’s staff driving you out? Here is the garbling: if you have not personally realized and personally awakened, then even if your tongue is sharp, in the end you still cannot penetrate and break free from birth and death. This mountain monk usually teaches people to look at where this mechanism turns; if you speculate, you are far, far away. Haven’t you seen Touzi ask Yanping’s monk, After Huang Chao passed through, did you recover the sword? The monk pointed to the ground with his hand. Touzi said, For thirty years I played at riding horses; today I got thrown by a donkey. Look at this monk—he’s not bad; he may well be an adept. He neither says recovered nor says not recovered. text_en: even received the abdication of Qi. After taking the throne he wrote separate notes and lectures on the Five Classics, and was deeply devoted to Huang-Lao, and by nature extremely filial. One day he wished to obtain a supramundane Dharma to repay his parents’ toil. Thus he set aside Daoist ways and served the Buddha, receiving the bodhisattva precepts from Dharma Master Louyue. Donning the Buddha’s kasaya, he personally lectured on the Radiant Prajna Sutra to repay his parents. At that time the layman Zhigong, by displaying marvels and bewildering the crowd, was confined in prison. Zhigong then divided his body and traveled to teach in towns and cities. One day the emperor learned of it, was deeply moved and awakened, and esteemed him greatly. Zhigong often went about protecting him; his hidden and manifest workings were beyond measure. At that time, in Wuzhou there was a layman who lived on Yunhuang Mountain. With his own hands he planted two trees, calling them the Twin Groves, and claimed he would be the future Layman Shanhui. One day he wrote a letter and ordered his disciple to submit a memorial to the emperor. At the time the court refused it because it lacked the proprieties of ruler and minister. text_en: and the old fellow with no front teeth met in the same way. When Bodhidharma first arrived in Jinling, he met Emperor Wu. The emperor asked, What is the first meaning of the holy truths? Bodhidharma said, Vast and empty, no holiness. The emperor said, Who is it that faces me? Bodhidharma said, I do not know. The emperor did not accord, so he crossed the river to Wei. Emperor Wu raised this and asked Master Zhi. The master said, Does Your Majesty recognize this person or not? The emperor said, I do not recognize him. Master Zhi said, This is the Great Being Avalokiteshvara, transmitting the Buddha’s mind-seal. The emperor regretted it, and then sent envoys to fetch him. Master Zhi said, Do not say Your Majesty sent envoys to fetch him; even if the whole country went, he still would not return. Therefore Xuedou said: If at that time he had not met old Master Zhi, he too would have been a restless man driven from the country. If at that time it were not Master Zhi giving Layman Fu an outlet, he would have had to be driven out of the country. Master Zhi was indeed long-tongued, and Emperor Wu was thoroughly hoodwinked by him. Xuedou’s great intent says: no need for him to come to the Liang court, preaching the sutra and pounding the table. So it says, why not lodge this body in the Twin Groves, eat gruel and eat rice, pass the time according to circumstances? Instead he came to the Liang court; like this, he pointed and pounded the table once, then stepped down from the seat. This is exactly where he stirred up dust and grime. If you want something extraordinary, then gaze into the clouds; above you do not see any Buddha. Below you do not see any sentient beings. If you speak of matters beyond the world, you cannot avoid a head of ash and a face of dust, taking what is not and making it be, taking what is and making it not, taking what is right and making it wrong, taking what is coarse and making it fine. A fish moving through a wine shop, grabbing sideways and using upside down, making everyone understand this matter. If you do not let it go like this, then even until Maitreya is born in the world, there will not be a single half one. Since Layman Fu was dragging mud and trailing water, it is fortunate there was someone who understood the tune. If he had not met old Master Zhi, he nearly would have been driven out of the country. Tell me, right now, where is it located?

text_zh: 三聖是臨濟下尊宿。少具出群作略。有大機 有大用。在眾中。昂昂藏藏。名聞諸方。後辭臨 濟。遍遊淮海。到處叢林。皆以高賓待之。自向 北至南方。先造雪峯便問。透網金鱗。未審以 何為食。峯云。待汝出網來。即向汝道。聖云。 一千五百人善知識。話頭也不識。峯云。老僧 住持事繁。峯往寺莊。路逢獼猴。乃云。這獼猴 各各佩一面古鏡。聖云。歷劫無名。何以彰為 古鏡。峯云。瑕生也。聖云。一千五百人善知 識。話頭也不識。峯云。罪過。老僧住持事繁。 後至仰山。山極愛其俊利。待之於明窓下。一 日有官人來參仰山。山問。官居何位。云推官。 山竪起拂子云。還推得這箇麼。官人無語。眾 人下語。俱不契仰山意。時三聖病在延壽堂。 仰山令侍者持此語問之。聖云。和尚有事也。 再令侍者問未審有什麼事。聖云。再犯不容。 仰山深肯之。百丈當時。以禪板蒲團付黃檗。 拄杖拂子付溈山。溈山後付仰山。仰山既大 肯三聖。聖一日辭去。仰山以拄杖拂子付三 聖。聖云。某甲已有師。仰山詰其由。乃臨濟的 子也。只如仰山問三聖。汝名什麼。他不可不 知其名。何故更恁麼問。所以作家。要驗人得 知子細。只似等閑。問云。汝名什麼。更道無計 較。何故三聖不云惠然。却道惠寂。看他具眼 漢。自然不同。三聖恁麼。又不是顛。一向攙旗 奪鼓。意在仰山語外。此語不墮常情。難為摸 索。這般漢手段。却活得人。所以道。他參活 句。不參死句。若順常情。則歇人不得。看他古 人念道如此。用盡精神。始能大悟。既悟了用 時還同未悟時人相似。隨分一言半句。不得 落常情。三聖知他仰山落處。便向他道。我名 惠寂。仰山要收三聖。三聖倒收仰山。仰山只 得就身打劫道。惠寂是我。是放行處。三聖云。 我名惠然。亦是放行。所以雪竇後面頌云。雙 收雙放若為宗。只一句內一時頌了。仰山呵 呵大笑。也有權有實。也有照有用。為他八面 玲瓏。所以用處得大自在。這箇笑與巖頭笑 不同。巖頭笑有毒藥。這箇笑。千古萬古。清風 凜凜地。雪竇頌云。
text_en: and great function. Among the assembly he carried himself proudly and concealed himself deeply; his name was known in all directions. Later he took leave of Linji and traveled throughout Huai and Hai. Wherever he went among the monasteries, all treated him as an honored guest. From the north to the south, he first visited Xuefeng and asked, A golden-scaled fish that passes through the net, what do you take as food? Xuefeng said, Wait until you come out of the net, then I will tell you. Sansheng said, A teacher of fifteen hundred people, and you do not even recognize the topic of conversation. Xuefeng said, This old monk has many duties as abbot. Xuefeng went to the temple estate; on the road he met monkeys and said, These monkeys each wear an ancient mirror. Sansheng said, Through kalpas without a name, how can it be displayed as an ancient mirror? Xuefeng said, A flaw has arisen. Sansheng said, A teacher of fifteen hundred people, and you do not recognize the topic of conversation. Xuefeng said, My fault. This old monk has many duties as abbot. Later he went to Yangshan. Yangshan greatly loved his sharp brilliance and received him beneath a bright window. One day an official came to visit Yangshan. Yangshan asked, What office do you hold? He said, Investigating officer. Yangshan held up his whisk and said, Can you investigate this? The official had no words. The assembly offered remarks, but none matched Yangshan’s intent. At the time Sansheng was ill in the Yanshou Hall. Yangshan had an attendant take these words and ask him. Sansheng said, The master has business. Again he had the attendant ask, what business is it exactly? Sansheng said, A second offense will not be tolerated. Yangshan deeply approved. In Baizhang’s time, he entrusted the meditation board and sitting cushion to Huangbo; the staff and whisk to Guishan; Guishan later entrusted them to Yangshan. Since Yangshan greatly approved of Sansheng, one day Sansheng took leave. Yangshan gave the staff and whisk to Sansheng. Sansheng said, I already have a teacher. Yangshan questioned him about why, and it turned out he was truly Linji’s heir. Now, when Yangshan asked Sansheng, What is your name, he could not not have known his own name. So why ask like this? Because a genuine adept wants to test a person and find out precisely. It seems casual, asking, What is your name, as if there were no calculation; so why did Sansheng not say Huiran, but instead say Huiji? Look at him, a man with eyes, naturally different. Sansheng was like this, yet it was not craziness. He was always disrupting banners and snatching drums; his intent lay outside Yangshan’s words. These words do not fall into ordinary sentiment, hard to grasp. The methods of such a fellow bring people to life. Therefore it is said, he studies living phrases, not dead phrases. If you follow ordinary sentiment, you cannot stop people. See how the ancients thought like this, exhausting their spirit, only then able to awaken greatly. Once awakened, when they use it it is still like someone not yet awakened. According to circumstance, with a word or half a phrase, they must not fall into ordinary sentiment. Sansheng knew where Yangshan would land, so he said to him, My name is Huiji. Yangshan wanted to seize Sansheng, but Sansheng instead seized Yangshan. Yangshan only managed to rob him on the spot, saying, Huiji is me. That is the releasing point. Sansheng said, My name is Huiran. That too is release. Therefore Xuedou later composed this verse: double gathering, double releasing, how can it be the principle? In a single line he versified it all at once. Yangshan laughed heartily. There is expedient and there is real; there is illumination and there is function. Because he was crystal-clear on all sides, his functioning attained great freedom. This laughter is different from Yantou’s laughter. Yantou’s laughter has poison. This laughter, through a thousand ages and ten thousand ages, is a clear wind sharp and bracing. Xuedou’s verse says:
Double gathering, double releasing, how can it be the principle? Riding a tiger, How many know it? Shining from eight sides—you’d think there really was such a thing.

text_zh: 雙收雙放若為宗。放行互為賓主。仰山云。汝 名什麼。聖云。我名惠寂是雙放。仰山云。惠寂 是我。聖云。我名惠然是雙收。其實是互換之 機。收則大家收。放則大家放。雪竇一時頌盡 了也。他意道。若不放收。若不互換。爾是爾我 是我。都來只四箇字。因甚却於裏頭。出沒卷 舒。古人道。爾若立我便坐。爾若坐我便立。 若也同坐同立。二俱瞎漢。此是雙收雙放。可 以為宗要。騎虎由來要絕功。有如此之高風 最上之機要。要騎便騎。要下便下。據虎頭亦 得。收虎尾亦得。三聖仰山。二俱有此之風。笑 罷不知何處去。且道他笑箇什麼。直得清風 凜凜為什麼。末後却道。只應千古動悲風。也 是死而不弔。一時與爾注解了也。爭柰天下 人啗啄不入。不知落處。縱是山僧。也不知落 處。諸人還知麼。
text_en: what is your name? Sansheng said, My name is Huiji, that is double release. Yangshan said, Huiji is me. Sansheng said, My name is Huiran, that is double gathering. In truth it is the pivot of mutual exchange. If gathering, everyone gathers; if releasing, everyone releases. Xuedou, all at once, versified it completely as well. His intent says: if you do not release and gather, if you do not exchange, you are you and I am I. Altogether just four characters. Why then within it do you come and go, roll and unroll? The ancients said: if you stand, I sit; if you sit, I stand. If you sit together and stand together, both are blind men. This is double gathering and double releasing; it can be taken as the essential principle. Riding a tiger has always required cutting off achievement. With such lofty style and the supreme pivot, ride when you want to ride, dismount when you want to dismount. Grasp the tiger’s head and it works; seize the tiger’s tail and it works. Sansheng and Yangshan both had this style. After laughing, he did not know where he went. Tell me, what was he laughing at? It made the clear wind sharp and bracing—why? In the end it says, it only makes the mournful wind stir through a thousand ages. That too is dying without mourning. All at once I have annotated it for you. But what can be done? People under heaven cannot bite into it, do not know where it lands. Even this mountain monk does not know where it lands. Do you all know?

text_zh: 當時馬祖盛化於江西。石頭道行於湖湘。忠 國師道化於長安。他親見六祖來。是時南方 擎頭帶角者。無有不欲升其堂入其室。若不 爾。為人所恥。這老漢三箇。欲去禮拜忠國師。 至中路。做這一場敗缺。南泉云。恁麼則不去 也。既是一一道得。為什麼却道不去。且道古 人意作麼生。當時待他道恁麼則不去也。劈 耳便掌。看他作什麼伎倆。萬古振綱宗。只是 這些子機要。所以慈明道。要牽只在索頭邊。 撥著點著便轉。如水上捺葫蘆子相似。人多 喚作不相肯語。殊不知。此事到極則處。須離 泥離水。拔楔抽釘。爾若作心行會。則沒交涉。 古人轉變得好。到這裏。不得不恁麼。須是有 殺有活。看他一人去圓相中坐。一人作女人 拜。也甚好。南泉云。恁麼則不去也。歸宗云。 是什麼心行。孟八郎漢。又恁麼去也。他恁麼 道。大意要驗南泉。南泉尋常道。喚作如如。早 是變了也。南泉歸宗麻谷。却是一家裏人。一 擒一縱。一殺一活。不妨奇特。雪竇頌云。
text_en: Teacher Zhong taught in Chang’an. He had personally seen the Sixth Patriarch come. In those days in the south, none of those who “raised their heads and wore horns” failed to want to ascend his hall and enter his room; if they did not, they would be shamed by others. These three old fellows wanted to go pay respects to National Teacher Zhong. Halfway there, they staged this botched affair. Nansen said, “If so, then we won’t go.” Since each has spoken, why then say, “we won’t go”? Tell me: what were the ancients’ intentions? If at that moment, when he said, “If so, then we won’t go,” you were to slap him right across the ear—see what tricks he has. The teaching that shakes the lineage for ten thousand ages is just these key points. Therefore Ciming said, “If you want to lead it, it’s right at the end of the rope.” Touch it and it turns; it is like pressing down a gourd on water. Many people call it words of non-acceptance. They do not realize that when this matter reaches the ultimate point, you must leave mud and leave water, pull out the wedge and draw the nail. If you understand it as mind-conduct, then it has nothing to do with it. The ancients were good at turning and changing. When you reach here, you cannot but be this way. There must be killing and there must be giving life. Look: one person sits inside the circle; one person acts like a woman and bows—also quite fine. Nansen said, “If so, then we won’t go.” Guizong said, “What kind of mind-conduct is that?” That Mengbalang fellow went and did it that way too. When he said it like that, his main intent was to test Nansen. Nansen usually says, “Call it suchness.” It has already changed. Nansen, Guizong, and Mogu were, after all, people of one household. One Capture one, release one; one kill, one let live—no harm in its strangeness. Xuedou’s verse says:
Youji’s arrow shoots the gibbon—circling the tree, why so straight? Right in front on a single road—who dares step forward? Everywhere it touches it’s wondrous; before it’s released, it hits.

text_zh: 由基箭射猿當頭一路誰敢向前。觸處得妙。未發先中　遶樹何太直 若不承當爭敢恁麼。東西南北一家風。已周遮多時也千箇與萬箇如麻似粟。野 狐精一隊。爭奈得南泉何是誰曾中的一箇半箇。更洛一箇。一箇也用不得　相 呼相喚歸去來一隊弄泥團漢。不如歸去好。却較些子曹溪路上 休登陟大勞生想料。不是曹溪門下客。低低處平之有餘。高高處觀之不足。
text_en: If you didn’t take responsibility, how would you dare be like this? East, west, south, north—one family wind. It has covered all around for a long time. A thousand, and ten thousand— Like hemp and millet. A band of wild fox spirits—what can they do to Nanquan? who has ever truly hit the mark? One or half of one, add another—none of them can be used. Calling to each other, they shout: come back, go home. A whole crew of mud-ball fellows—better to go home. That would be a bit better. On the Caoxi road, do not climb. Great toil, giving rise to calculating thoughts. Not a guest under Caoxi’s gate. In low places he levels them with ease; in high places, viewing is not enough. Again,

text_zh: 復 云。曹溪路坦平。為什麼休登陟不唯南泉半路抽身。雪 竇亦乃半路抽身。好事不如無。雪竇也患這般病痛
text_en: he says: the Caoxi road is level—why do you say do not climb? Not only did Nanquan pull back halfway; Xue- dou also pulled back halfway. Better no good thing than one. Xuedou too suffered this kind of illness.
“Youji’s arrow shoots the gibbon; circling the tree, why so straight?” Youji was a man of Chu in ancient times.

text_zh: 由基箭射猿。遶樹何太直。由基乃是楚時人。 姓養。名叔。字由基。時楚莊王出獵。見一白 猿。使人射之。其猿捉箭而戲。勅群臣射之。莫 有中者。王遂問群臣。群臣奏曰。由基者善射。 遂令射之。由基方彎弓。猿乃抱樹悲號。至箭 發時。猿遶樹避之。其箭亦遶樹中殺。此乃神 箭也。雪竇何故却言太直。若是太直則不中。 既是遶樹。何故却云太直。雪竇借其意。不妨 用得好。此事出春秋。有者道。遶樹是圓相。若 真箇如此。蓋不識語之宗旨。不知太直處。三 箇老漢。殊途而同歸一揆。一齊太直。若是 識得他去處。七縱八橫。不離方寸。百川異流。 同歸大海。所以南泉道。恁麼則不去也。若是 衲僧正眼覷著。只是弄精魂。若喚作弄精魂。 却不是弄精魂。五祖先師道。他三人是慧炬 三昧。莊嚴王三昧。雖然如此。作女人拜。他終 不作女人拜會。雖畫圓相。他終不作圓相會。 既不恁麼會。又作麼生會。雪竇道。千箇與萬 箇。是誰曾中的。能有幾箇。百發百中。相呼相 喚歸去來。頌南泉道恁麼則不去也。南泉從 此不去。故云。曹溪路上休登陟。滅却荊棘林。 雪竇把不定。復云。曹溪路坦平。為什麼休登 陟。曹溪路絕塵絕迹。露裸裸赤灑灑。平坦坦 翛然地。為什麼却休登陟。各自看脚下。
text_en: His surname was Yang, personal name Shu, style name Youji. When King Zhuang of Chu went hunting, he saw a white gibbon and had someone shoot it. The gibbon caught the arrow and toyed with it. He ordered the assembled ministers to shoot, but none could hit it. The king then asked his ministers, and they replied: Youji is skilled at archery. So he commanded him to shoot. As Youji began to draw his bow, the gibbon clung to the tree and cried mournfully. When the arrow was released, the gibbon circled the tree to evade it, and the arrow also circled the tree and struck, killing it. This was a miraculous arrow. Why, then, does Xuedou say “too straight”? If it were too straight, it would not hit. Since it circled the tree, why say “too straight”? Xuedou borrows the idea—no harm in using it well. This story comes from the Spring and Autumn records. Some say that circling the tree is a circle emblem. If it were really so, they simply do not understand the point of the words; they do not know where the “too straight” lies. The three old fellows take different roads yet return to the same principle—together, all “too straight.” If you recognize where they go, then seven times loose, eight times free, you do not leave a square inch of mind. The hundred rivers flow differently, yet all return to the great sea. Therefore Nanquan said: if it is so, then I will not go. If a patched-robed monk looks with the true eye, it is only playing with the spirit. If you call it playing with the spirit, then it is not playing with the spirit. The former master, Fifth Patriarch, said: those three are the Samadhi of the torch of wisdom, and the Samadhi of the Adornment King. Even so, if you take it as a woman’s bow, in the end they will not understand it as a woman’s bow. Though a circle emblem is drawn, they will never understand it as a circle emblem. If you do not understand it that way, then how will you understand it? Xuedou says: a thousand, and ten thousand—who has ever hit it? How many could there be? A hundred shots, a hundred hits—calling to each other, they shout: come back, go home. This praises Nanquan’s “if it is so, then I will not go.” From then on Nanquan did not go; hence it says: on the Caoxi road, do not climb—wipe out the thornbush grove. Xuedou cannot quite pin it down, and again says: the Caoxi road is level—why do you say do not climb? The Caoxi road is beyond dust and beyond tracks—bare and open, stark and unadorned, level and free and easy—why, then, say do not climb? Each of you, look under your own feet.
70 The pointer says: a swift man—one word; a swift horse—one whip. Ten thousand years—one thought, thought
