Weishan, Wufeng, and Yunyan were attending Baizhang, standing by his side. Baizhang asked Weishan: seal up

text_zh: 溈山五峯雲巖。同侍立百丈。百丈問溈山。併 却咽喉唇吻。作麼生道。山云。却請和尚道。丈 云。我不辭向汝道。恐已後喪我兒孫。百丈 雖然如此。鍋子已被別人奪去了也。丈復問 五峯。峯云。和尚也須併却。丈云。無人處斫額 望汝。又問雲巖。巖云。和尚有也未。丈云。喪 我兒孫。三人各是一家。古人道。平地上死人 無數。過得荊棘林者。是好手。所以宗師家。以 荊棘林驗人。何故若於常情句下。驗人不得。 衲僧家須是句裏呈機。言中辨的。若是擔板 漢。多向句中死却。便道。併却咽喉唇吻。更無 下口處。若是變通底人。有逆水之波。只向問 頭上有一條路。不傷鋒犯手。溈山云。却請和 尚道。且道他意作麼生。向箇裏如擊石火似 閃電光相似。拶他問處便答。自有出身之路。 不費纖毫氣力。所以道。他參活句。不參死句。 百丈却不采他。只云。不辭向汝道。恐已後喪 我兒孫。大凡宗師為人。抽釘拔楔。若是如 今人便道。此答不肯他不領話。殊不知。箇裏 一路生機處。壁立千仞。賓主互換。活鱍鱍 地。雪竇愛他此語風措。宛轉自在。又能把定 封疆。所以頌云。
text_en: your throat and your lips—how will you speak? Weishan said: I ask the master to speak. Baizhang said: I do not refuse to tell you, but I fear that later I will lose my sons and grandsons. Baizhang added: even so, the pot has already been seized by someone else. Baizhang again asked Wufeng. Wufeng said: the master must seal it up too. Baizhang said: in a place with no one, I break my brow and look to you. He also asked Yunyan. Yunyan said: does the master have it or not? Baizhang said: I have lost my sons and grandsons. The three men each make a school. The ancients said: on level ground, the dead are beyond number; the one who can pass through the thornbush grove is a good hand. Therefore, in the house of the lineage masters, they use the thornbush grove to test people. Why? Under phrases of ordinary feelings, you cannot test people. In the patched-robed family, you must reveal the pivot within the phrase and discern the target within the words. If you are a plank-shouldered fellow, you mostly die inside the phrase, and then say: seal up the throat and lips—there is no place to open your mouth. But if you are someone who can adapt, you have waves against the current—right in the question head there is a road; you do not nick the blade or cut the hand. Weishan said: I ask the master to speak. Tell me, what is his intent? Here it is like striking sparks from stone, like a flash of lightning—pressing at the place of the question, he answers at once, and has his own way out. It does not cost the slightest bit of effort. Therefore it is said: he studies living phrases, not dead phrases. Yet Baizhang does not accept him; he only says: I do not refuse to tell you, but I fear that later I will lose my sons and grandsons. In general, when lineage masters deal with people, they pull nails and extract wedges. If you were like people today, you would say: this answer does not approve of him, it does not take up the words. You do not realize that here there is a whole living road—sheer cliffs a thousand fathoms high; guest and host exchange places, lively and unrestrained. Xuedou loved the style of this phrase—flexible and free, and also able to hold the boundary. Therefore his verse says:
I ask the master to speak: horns grow from a tiger’s head, emerging from wild grass. The case covers heaven and earth—already the blade has hurt and cut the hand.

text_zh: 却請和尚道函蓋乾坤。已是傷鋒犯手　虎頭生角出荒草 可殺驚群。不妨奇特十洲春盡花凋殘觸處清涼讚歎也不及　珊瑚 樹林日杲杲千重百匝。爭柰百草頭上尋他不得。答處蓋天蓋地
text_en: Terrifying enough to startle the crowd—no harm in being singular. When spring ends on the ten isles, blossoms wither and fall; the coral Wherever it touches is cool and refreshing—praise can’t reach it. grove stands bright in the blazing sun. A thousand layers, a hundred turns—yet on the tips of a hundred grasses you can’t find it. Where it answers, it covers heaven and covers earth.
In how these three answered, each was different. There is sheer cliff like a thousand fathoms; there is

text_zh: 此三人答處。各各不同。也有壁立千仞。也有 照用同時。也有自救不了。却請和尚道。雪竇 便向此一句中。呈機了也。更就中輕輕拶。令 人易見云。虎頭生角出荒草。溈山答處。一似 猛虎頭上安角。有什麼近傍處。不見僧問羅 山。同生不同死時如何。山云。如牛無角。僧 云。同生亦同死時如何。山云。如虎戴角。雪竇 只一句頌了也。他有轉變餘才。更云。十洲春 盡花凋殘。海上有三山十洲。以百年為一春。 雪竇語帶風措。宛轉盤礴。春盡之際。百千萬 株花。一時凋殘。獨有珊瑚樹林。不解凋落。與 大陽相奪。其光交映。正當恁麼時。不妨奇特。 雪竇用此。明他却請和尚道。十洲皆海外諸 國之所附。一祖洲。出反魂香。二瀛洲。生芝草 玉石泉如酒味。三玄洲。出仙藥。服之長生。四 長洲。出木瓜玉英。五炎洲。出火浣布。六元 洲。出靈泉如蜜。七生洲。有山川無寒暑。八鳳 麟洲。人取鳳喙麟角。煎續弦膠。九聚窟洲。出 獅子銅頭鐵額之獸。十檀洲一作流洲出琨吾石。作 劍切玉如泥。珊瑚外國雜傳云。大秦西南。漲 海中。可七八百里。到珊瑚洲。洲底盤石。珊瑚 生其石上。人以鐵網取之。又十洲記云。珊瑚 生南海底。如樹高三二尺。有枝無皮。似玉而 紅潤。感月而生。凡枝頭皆有月暈此一則與八卷首公案同看。
text_en: illumination and function at once; there is also one who cannot even save himself. “I ask the master to speak”—Xuedou right within this single phrase already presents the pivot. Then within it he lightly presses, making it easy to see: “horns grow from a tiger’s head, emerging from wild grass.” Weishan’s answer is like fixing horns onto the head of a fierce tiger—where is there anywhere nearby? Haven’t you seen a monk ask Luo shan: when living together but not dying together, how is it? Luoshan said: like an ox with no horns. The monk said: when living together and dying together, how is it? Luoshan said: like a tiger wearing horns. Xuedou finishes it with a single line of verse. He has extra talent for turning and shifting, and adds: when spring on the ten isles ends, flowers wither and fall. In the sea there are three mountains and ten isles; a hundred years counts as one spring. Xuedou’s words carry style and flair, winding and ranging freely. At spring’s end, hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands of blossoms wither at once. Only the coral grove does not know how to wither and fall; it contends with the great sun, their lights reflecting each other. Right at such a time, no harm in its strangeness. Xuedou uses this to illuminate “I ask the master to speak.” The ten isles all belong to various lands beyond the seas. First, Zuzhou: it produces soul-returning incense. Second, Yingzhou: it grows magic fungi and herbs. Its jade-stone spring tastes like wine. Third, Xuanzhou: it produces elixir; take it and you live long. Fourth, Changzhou: it yields wood-melon jade essence. Fifth, Yanzhou: it yields fire-washed cloth. Sixth, Yuanzhou: it yields a numinous spring like honey. Seventh, Shengzhou: it has mountains and rivers, with no cold or heat. Eighth, Fenglinzhou: people take phoenix beaks and qilin horns, boil them to make glue to mend broken strings. Ninth, Juku Zhou: it produces beasts like lions with bronze heads and iron foreheads. Tenth, Tanzhou produces Kunwu stone; made into One version reads “Liuzhou.” swords, it cuts jade like mud. In Miscellaneous Traditions of Foreign Lands on coral it says: southwest of Great Qin, in the vast sea, some seven or eight hundred li out, you reach Coral Isle. The bottom of the isle is bedrock; coral grows upon that stone, and people take it with iron nets. And Records of the Ten Isles says: coral grows on the seabed of the Southern Sea, like a tree two or three feet high, with branches but no bark, like jade and red and glossy. It grows in response to the moon; every branch tip has a lunar halo. This case should be read together with the first koan of volume eight.

Seize the banner, snatch the drum—one phrase cuts off the stream. The ten thousand workings are quieted and pared away. The land is vast and people are few; those who meet are rare—this case, together with the end of volume seven, should be viewed as one.

text_zh: 溈山把定封疆。五峯截斷眾流。這些子。要是 箇漢當面提掇。如馬前相撲。不容擬議。直 下便用緊迅危峭。不似溈山盤礴滔滔地。如 今禪和子。只向架下行。不能出他一頭地。所 以道。欲得親切。莫將問來問。五峯答處。當頭 坐斷。不妨快俊。百丈云。無人處斫額望汝。且 道是肯他。是不肯他。是殺是活。見他阿轆轆 地。只與他一點。雪竇頌云。
text_en: a man who lifts it up right in your face, like wrestling in front of a horse—no room for conjecture, directly applying it tight, swift, perilous, and steep. Not like Weishan, winding on and on. Like today’s Zen companions, who only walk under the rack and cannot get their head above it. Therefore it is said: if you want intimacy, do not take a question and ask it as a question. Wufeng’s answer cuts it off right where it stands—no harm in how sharp and swift it is. Baizhang said: in a place with no one, I break my brow and look to you. Tell me, is he approving him or not approving him? Is it killing or is it letting live? Seeing him rolling along like that, he gives him just a single point. Xuedou’s verse says:
The master too has swept it all away; on the dragon-and-snake battle line, watch the strategy. It is already before the words; it cuts off all streams.

text_zh: 和尚也併却已在言前了。截斷眾流　龍蛇陣上看謀略 須是金牙始解七事隨身。慣戰作家令人長憶李將軍妙手無多子。匹馬 單鎗。千里萬里。千人萬人萬里天邊飛一鶚大眾見麼。且道落在什麼處。中 也。打云。飛過去也
text_en: It takes golden fangs to understand the seven things that follow the body—an adept seasoned in battle. It makes one long remember General Li. Skilled hands are not many; a single horse and a lone spear—over a thousand miles, ten thousand miles; a thousand people, ten thousand people. At the edge of the sky ten thousand miles away, a single hawk flies. Do you all see it? Tell me, where does it land? In the middle as well. He strikes and says: It has flown past.
The master too has swept it away. Within one line, Xuedou presses once, saying: Dragon and snake

text_zh: 和尚也併却。雪竇於一句中。拶一拶云。龍蛇 陣上看謀略。如排兩陣突出突入。七縱八橫。 有鬪將底手脚。有大謀略底人。匹馬單鎗。向 龍蛇陣上。出沒自在。爾作麼生圍繞得他。若 不是這箇人。爭知有如此謀略。雪竇此三頌。 皆就裏頭。狀出底語如此。大似李廣神箭。萬 里天邊飛一鶚。一箭落一雕定也。更不放過。 雪竇頌百丈問處如一鶚。五峯答處如一箭 相似。山僧只管讚歎五峯。不覺渾身入泥水 了也。
text_en: on the battle line, watch the strategy—like setting out two armies, breaking out and charging in, seven advances and eight crossings. There are the moves of a dueling general, and there are people of great strategy—one horse, one spear, heading toward the dragon-and-snake battle line, coming and going freely. How could you possibly surround him? If he were not this sort of person, how would he know such strategy? These three verses of Xuedou all go straight to the inside; the words he draws out are like this—just like Li Guang’s miraculous arrows, ten thousand miles to the sky’s edge a single hawk flies—one arrow drops one eagle for sure, and he does not let it slip away. Xuedou’s verse: Baizhang’s asking is like a hawk; Wufeng’s answering is like an arrow. This monk only keeps praising Wufeng, and without noticing, my whole body has entered mud and water already.

text_zh: 【七二】舉。百丈又問雲巖。併却咽喉唇吻。作麼 生道蝦䗫窟裏出來。道什麼巖云。和尚有也未粘皮著骨。拕泥帶水。 前不搆村後不迭店丈云。喪我兒孫灼然有此答得半前落後。
text_en: will you speak? Yunyan said: Master, do you have it or not? Baizhang said: You’ve killed my sons and grandsons. Coming out of a shrimp hole—what are you saying? Skin stuck to bone, dragging mud and trailing water. Ahead it does not reach a village; behind it does not catch a shop. Clearly there is such an answer—half ahead, falling behind.
Yunyan served as Baizhang’s attendant for twenty years. Later, along with Daowu, he went to Yaoshan.

text_zh: 雲巖在百丈。二十年作侍者。後同道吾至藥 山。山問云。子在百丈會下。為箇什麼事。巖 云。透脫生死。山云。還透脫也未。巖云。渠無 生死。山云。二十年在百丈。習氣也未除。巖辭 去見南泉。後復歸藥山。方契悟。看他古人。二 十年參究。猶自半青半黃。粘皮著骨。不能頴 脫。是則也是。只是前不搆村。後不迭店。不見 道。語不離窠臼。焉能出蓋纏。白雲橫谷口。迷 却幾人源。洞下謂之觸破。故云。躍開仙仗 鳳凰樓。時人嫌觸當今號。所以道。荊棘林須 是透過始得。若不透過。終始涉廉纖。斬不斷。 適來道。前不搆村。後不迭店。雲巖只管去。點 檢他人底。百丈見他如此。一時把來打殺了 也。雪竇頌云。
text_en: Yaoshan asked: While you were in Baizhang’s assembly, what was it for? Yunyan said: To transcend birth and death. Yaoshan said: Have you transcended yet or not? Yunyan said: It has no birth and death. Yaoshan said: Twenty years with Baizhang, and your habits still aren’t gone. Yunyan took leave and went to see Nanquan. Later he returned to Yaoshan and only then accorded and awakened. Look at the people of old—twenty years of investigation, and still half green, half yellow—skin stuck to bone, unable to break free cleanly. It is so, yes, but: ahead he did not reach a village, behind he did not make it to an inn. Don’t you see it said: If words do not leave their ruts, how can one escape the covering tangle? White clouds stretch across the valley mouth, confusing the source for how many people. The Dongshan line calls it breaking through by contact. Hence it is said: Leaping past the immortal guard, you reach Phoenix Tower. People of the time disliked such “contact” and called it a present-day style. Therefore it is said: A thicket of thorns must be passed through. If you do not pass through, from start to finish you brush against trifles, unable to cut them off. Just now I said: ahead he did not reach a village, behind he did not make it to an inn. Yunyan just kept going, checking other people. Seeing him like this, Baizhang at once seized him and killed him off on the spot. Xuedou’s verse says:
Master, do you have it or not? The golden-haired lion does not crouch The case is ready-made: following the waves, chasing the surf, mixing mud and blending water.

text_zh: 和尚有也未公案現成。隨波逐浪。和泥合水　金毛獅子不踞 地灼然。有什麼用處。可惜許兩兩三三舊路行併却咽喉唇吻。作麼生 道。轉身吐氣。脚跟下蹉過了也大雄山下空彈指一死更不再活。可悲可 痛。蒼天中更添怨苦
text_en: on the ground. Clearly—what use is it? A pity, indeed, In pairs and in threes, they walk the old road. to block off throat, lips, and mouth—how can you speak? Turn around and exhale—already you have slipped past beneath your heels. Below Great Hero Mountain, he snaps his fingers in vain. Once dead, you will not live again. Pitiful and painful—adding more grievance and suffering under the blue sky.
Master, do you have it or not? Xuedou lays out the charge and closes the case: it is so, yes—but as for the golden-

text_zh: 和尚有也未。雪竇據欵結案。是則是。只是金 毛獅子。爭柰不踞地。獅子捉物。藏牙伏爪。踞 地返擲。物無大小。皆以全威。要全其功。雲巖 云。和尚有也未。只是向舊路上行。所以雪竇 云。百丈向大雄山下空彈指。
text_en: haired lion, what can you do that it does not crouch? When a lion seizes prey, it hides its fangs and crouches its claws; when it crouches on the ground it flings it back. Whether the thing is large or small, it uses full power. Wanting the full achievement, Yunyan said: Master, do you have it or not?—he was only walking along the old road. Therefore Xuedou said: Baizhang below Great Hero Mountain snaps his fingers in vain.
73 In his instruction he said: As for one who speaks the Dharma, there is no speaking and no showing; and for one who hears the Dharma, there is no hearing

text_zh: 垂示云。夫說法者。無說無示。其聽法者。無聞 無得。說既無說無示。爭如不說。聽既無聞無 得。爭如不聽。而無說又無聽。却較些子。只如 今諸人。聽山僧在這裏說。作麼生免得此過。 具透關眼者。試舉看。
text_en: and no attaining. If speaking is already without speaking and without showing, how is that compared to not speaking? If hearing is already without hearing and without attaining, how is that compared to not hearing? Yet with no speaking and also no hearing, it still falls short a bit. For example, all of you now are listening to this monk speak here—how will you avoid this fault? Whoever has eyes that penetrate the barrier, try to raise it and see.
Case 73. Raised: A monk asked Master Ma: Leaving the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations, I ask the master to directly

text_zh: 【七三】舉。僧問馬大師。離四句絕百非。請師直 指某甲西來意什麼處得這話頭來。那裏得這消息馬師云。我今 日勞倦。不能為汝說。問取智藏去退身三步蹉過也不知。 藏身露影。不妨是這老漢推過。與別人僧問智藏也須與他一拶。蹉過也不知藏 云。何不問和尚草裏焦尾大蟲出來也。道什麼。直得草繩自縛。去死十分 僧云。和尚教來問愛人處分。前箭猶輕後箭深藏云。我今日 頭痛。不能為汝說。問取海兄去不妨是八十四員善知識。 一樣患這般病痛僧問海兄轉與別人。抱贜叫屈海云。我到這裏 却不會不用忉忉。從教千古萬古黑漫漫僧舉似馬大師這僧却有些子 眼睛馬師云。藏頭白海頭黑寰中天子勅。塞外將軍令。
text_en: point out the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West. Master Ma said: Today I From what place did you get this topic of talk? From where did you get this news? am weary and cannot speak for you. Go ask Zhizang. The monk asked Zhizang. Zhizang Step back three paces and you slip past it without knowing. Hiding the body yet showing the shadow—no harm if this old fellow shoves it off; but as for others, you must also give them a squeeze; they slip past it without knowing. said: Why not ask the master? From the grass comes a scorched-tailed great beast. What are you saying? It goes so far as to bind itself with a rope of grass—go die, all the way. The monk said: The master told me to ask. Zhizang said: Today I Cherishing people by dealing with them: the first arrow is light, the later arrow sinks deep. have a headache and cannot speak for you. Go ask Elder Hai. The monk asked Elder Hai. Hai said: When it comes to this, It is no harm if there are eighty-four good knowing advisors. They all suffer the same illness. Hand it off to others—hugging stolen goods and crying injustice. I do not understand. The monk reported this to Master Ma. Master Ma said: Zang’s head is white, Hai’s head is black. No need for endless chatter; let a thousand ages, ten thousand ages be pitch-black. This monk, though, has a bit of eyes. Within the realm, the Son of Heaven's edict; beyond the passes, the general's command.
This public case—back in the day, when this monk studied Zhenjue in Chengdu, Zhenjue said: Just

text_zh: 這箇公案。山僧舊日。在成都參真覺。覺云。只 消看馬祖第一句。自然一時理會得。且道這 僧。是會來問。不會來問。此問不妨深遠。離四 句者。有。無。非有。非無。非非有。非非無。離此 四句。絕其百非。只管作道理。不識話頭。討頭 腦不見。若是山僧。待馬祖道了。也便與展坐 具。禮三拜。看他作麼生道。當時馬祖。若見這 僧來。問離四句絕百非。請師直指某甲西來 意。以拄杖劈脊便棒趕出。看他省不省。馬 大師只管與他打葛藤。以至這漢。當面蹉過。 更令去問智藏。殊不知馬大師來風深辨。這 僧懞懂。走去問智藏。藏云。何不問和尚。僧 云。和尚教來問。看他這些子。拶著便轉。更無 閑暇處。智藏云。我今日頭痛。不能為汝說得。 問取海兄去。這僧又去問海兄。海兄云。我到 這裏却不會。且道為什麼。一人道頭痛。一人 云不會。畢竟作麼生。這僧却回來。舉似馬大 師。師云。藏頭白海頭黑。若以解路卜度。却謂 之相瞞。有者道。只是相推過。有者道。三箇總 識他問頭。所以不答。總是拍盲地。一時將 古人醍醐上味。著毒藥在裏許。所以馬祖道。 待汝一口吸盡西江水。即向汝道。與此公案 一般。若會得藏頭白海頭黑。便會西江水話。 這僧將一檐懞𢤦。換得箇不安樂。更勞他三 人尊宿。入泥入水。畢竟這僧不瞥地。雖然一 恁麼。這三箇宗師。却被箇擔板漢勘破。如 今人只管去語言上。作活計云。白是明頭合。 黑是暗頭合。只管鑽研計較。殊不知。古人一 句截斷意根。須是向正脈裏。自看始得穩當。 所以道。末後一句。始到牢關。把斷要津。不通 凡聖。若論此事。如當門按一口劍相似。擬議 則喪身失命。又道。譬如擲劍揮空。莫論及之 不及。但向八面玲瓏處會取。不見古人道。這 漆桶。或云。野狐精。或云。瞎漢。且道與一棒 一喝。是同是別。若知千差萬別。只是一般。自 然八面受敵。要會藏頭白海頭黑麼。五祖先 師道。封后先生。雪竇頌云。
text_en: look at Mazu’s first line, and naturally you will understand it all at once. Now tell me—this monk—did he come asking with understanding, or asking without understanding? This question can be quite deep and far-reaching. “Leaving the four propositions” means: is, is not, not is, not is not, not not is, not not is not. Leaving these four propositions, cutting off its hundred negations—he only keeps making it into principle, not recognizing the topic, seeking a head and not seeing a brain. If it were this monk, once Mazu had spoken, I would immediately spread out my sitting cloth and bow three times, to see how he would speak. At that time, if Mazu saw this monk come asking: Leaving the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations, please directly point out the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West— he should have split his back with the staff, beaten him, and chased him out, to see whether he woke up or not. Master Ma only kept tangling vines with him, so that this fellow slipped past right in front of him. Then he sent him to ask Zhizang. Little did he know Master Ma’s incoming breeze was deeply discerning; this monk was muddled and ran off to ask Zhizang. Zhizang said: Why not ask the master? The monk said: The master told me to ask. Look at this—pressed, he turns immediately, with not a spare moment. Zhizang said: Today I have a headache; I cannot speak it for you. Go ask Elder Hai. This monk then went to ask Elder Hai. Elder Hai said: When it comes to this, I do not understand. Now tell me—why? One says “headache,” one says “don’t understand.” In the end, how is it? This monk then came back and reported it to Master Ma. The master said: Zang’s head is white, Hai’s head is black. If you measure it by the route of interpretation, it is called mutual deception. Some say it is merely shoving it off onto each other. Some say all three knew the point of his question, so they did not answer. All of that is just slapping at the dark. It takes the ancients’ finest ghee-flavor and mixes poison into it. Therefore Mazu said: When you swallow the waters of the West River in one gulp, then I will tell you. It is just like this public case: if you understand “Zang’s head is white, Hai’s head is black,” then you will understand the talk about the West River’s water. This monk took a shoulder-load of confusion and traded it for unrest, further troubling three venerable elders to enter mud and water. In the end, this monk did not catch it in a flash. Even so, in this way, these three lineage masters were instead seen through by a plank-shouldered fellow. People nowadays only work at it in language, saying: White means it matches the bright head; black means it matches the dark head—drilling and calculating nonstop. Not realizing that the ancients, with one line, cut off the root of intention—you must look for yourself within the true pulse to be secure. Therefore it is said: Only the last phrase reaches the solid barrier, blocking the crucial ford, not allowing passage to ordinary or holy. Speaking of this matter, it is like pressing a sword point at the gate—if you speculate, you lose body and life. It is also said: It is like throwing a sword and slashing empty space—do not argue whether it reaches or does not reach; just understand it where it is crystal-clear on all eight sides. Haven’t you seen the ancients say: This lacquer bucket—or some say wild-fox spirit, some say blind fellow—tell me, compared with one blow and one shout, is it the same or different? If you know the thousand differences and ten thousand distinctions are only the one, then naturally you meet enemies on all sides. Want to understand “Zang’s head is white, Hai’s head is black”? The Fifth Patriarch, former master, said: Mister Fenghou. Xuedou’s verse says:
Zang’s head is white, Hai’s head is black—clear-eyed patched-robed monks Half closed, half open; one hand lifts, one hand grips—golden tones, jade-like resonance.

text_zh: 藏頭白海頭黑半合半開。一手擡一手搦。金聲玉振　明眼衲僧會 不得更行脚三十年。終是被人穿却爾鼻孔。山僧故是口似匾檐馬駒踏殺天 下人叢林中也須是這老漢始得。放出這老漢臨濟未是白拈賊癩兒 牽伴。直饒好手。也被人捉了也離四句絕百非道什麼。也須是自點檢看。 阿爺似阿爹天上人間唯我知用我作什麼。奪却拄杖子。或若無人無我無得 無失。將什麼知
text_en: cannot understand it. Travel on foot another thirty years, and in the end someone will still pierce your nostrils. This mountain monk's mouth is indeed like a flat eave. The colt tramples to death the people of the world. In the monasteries it still has to be this old fellow. Let this old fellow loose— Linji still wasn’t a barehanded thief. a leper child dragging companions. Even if you have good hands, you still get caught. Leave the four propositions, cut off the hundred negations— What are you saying? You must examine it yourself. Granddad is like dad. in heaven above and among humans below, only I know. All this vine-tangling is already a matter of necessity; the ancients only slightly revealed a bit of it. edge and point. If you are someone who has pierced through, then you pierce seven times and bore eight holes, gaining great freedom and ease. If you have not pierced through, from the start there has been no place to awaken or enter, and the more you talk the farther you go. The colt tramples everyone under heaven to death. In the West, Prajñātāra prophesied; Bodhidharma foretold, saying: Though the land of China is vast, there is no other road; it must be walked under the feet of sons and grandsons. A golden rooster can carry in its beak a single grain of millet and make offerings to the arhat monks of the ten directions. And the Sixth Patriarch said to Master Rang, In the future, the Buddha Dharma will go out from your side. Later there will arise a colt that will trample everyone under heaven to death. After that, the Dharma heirs of Jiangxi spread throughout the world, and he was called Mazu. Bodhidharma and the Sixth Patriarch both foretold Mazu in advance. Look at his conduct—indeed it was different. Just say, The mountain head is white, the sea head is black, and you will see the place where he tramples everyone under heaven to death. Just this one black-and-white line—thousands upon tens of thousands cannot bite through it. Linji was not yet a daylight robber. One day Linji addressed the assembly, saying: Within this red lump of flesh there is a true person of no rank, always coming and going through the gate of your face. Those who have not verified it, look! At that time a monk came forward and asked, What is the true person of no rank? Linji got down from the meditation seat, grabbed him, and said, Speak, speak! The monk had no words. Linji shoved him away and said, The true person of no rank— what kind of dried shit-stick is that! Later Xuefeng heard of it and said, Linji really seems like a daylight robber. Xuedou wanted Linji to meet him, to observe Mazu’s edge and devices. They surpass Linji even more. This truly is a daylight robber; Linji was not yet a daylight robber. Xuedou pierced it through in one go, and then versified this monk’s saying: Depart from the four propositions, cut off the hundred negations—through heaven and earth, only I know. Do not set up shop in a ghost cave. The ancients said, The question is in the answer; the answer is in the question—already extraordinary. How will you depart from the four propositions and cut off the hundred negations? Xuedou said, This matter, only I can know. Even the Buddhas of the three times cannot see it. Since it is known by me alone, what are you all still coming up here to seek? Great Weishan Zhenru raised it and said: The monk asked like this; Mazu answered like this—depart from the four propositions, cut off the hundred negations—and even Zhizang and Hai the elder brother do not know at all. Want to understand? Have you not seen it said: the colt tramples everyone under heaven to death—tsk! At the start, it is especially tightly restrained.

text_en: in front of the monks’ hall, dance, laughing loudly, saying, Bodhisattva children, come eat! He did this for twenty years. Tell me, where was his intent? If you just call it eating, ordinarily striking the wooden fish and beating the drum already announces it—so why would he need to bring the rice bucket himself and perform so many tricks? Was he crazy? Or was he proclaiming and setting this up? If he was proclaiming this matter, why not go up to the jeweled-flower king seat, strike the bench and raise the whisk? Why must he do it like this? People today truly do not know: the ancients’ intent is beyond words. Why not first look at what the patriarch’s original topic was when he first came: it plainly says, A separate transmission outside the teachings, a direct transmission of the mind seal. The ancients’ expedients only taught you to take it up directly. Later people vainly guessed and divined, saying there are not so many things: when cold, go to the fire; when hot, enjoy the shade; when hungry, eat; when tired, sleep. If you explain it in this way with ordinary feelings, interpreting and glossing by meanings, Bodhidharma’s lineage would be swept away like dust. You do not know that the ancients, through the twelve hours, never let it go, thought after thought, wanting to make this matter clear. Xuedou said, Although this is so, Jinniu is not acting from a good heart. Just this one line—how many people misunderstand it! What is called the finest flavor of ghee is treasured by the world, yet when it meets such people, it turns into poison. text_zh: 僧從定州和尚會裏來到烏臼。臼亦是作家。 諸人若向這裏。識得此二人一出一入。千箇 萬箇只是一箇。作主也恁麼。作賓也恁麼。二 人畢竟合成一家。一期勘辨。賓主問答。始 終作家。看烏臼問這僧云。定州法道何似這 裏。僧便云。不別。當時若不是烏臼。難奈這僧 何。臼云。若不別。更轉彼中去。便打。爭奈這 僧是作家漢。便云。棒頭有眼不得草草打人。 臼一向行令云。今日打著一箇也。又打三下。 其僧便出去。看他兩箇轉轆轆地。俱是作家。 了這一事。須要分緇素別休咎。這僧雖出去。 這公案。却未了在。烏臼始終。要驗他實處看 他如何。這僧却似撐門拄戶。所以未見得他。 烏臼却云。屈棒元來有人喫在。這僧要轉身 吐氣。却不與他爭。輕輕轉云。爭奈杓柄在和 尚手裏。烏臼是頂門具眼底宗師。敢向猛虎 口裏橫身云。汝若要山僧回與汝。這漢是箇 肘下有符底漢。所謂見義不為無勇也。更不 擬議。近前奪烏臼手中棒。打臼三下。臼云。屈 棒屈棒。爾且道意作麼生。頭上道。屈棒元來 有人喫在。及乎到這僧打他。却道屈棒屈棒。 僧云。有人喫在。臼云。草草打著箇漢。頭上道 草草打著一箇也。到末後自喫棒。為什麼亦 道草草打著箇漢。當時若不是這僧卓朔地。 也不奈他何。這僧便禮拜。這箇禮拜最毒。也 不是好心。若不是烏臼。也識他不破。烏臼云。 却恁麼去也。其僧大笑而出。烏臼云。消得 恁麼消得恁麼。看他作家相見。始終賓主分 明。斷而能續。其實也只是互換之機。他到這 裏。亦不道有箇互換處。自是他古人。絕情塵 意想。彼此作家。亦不道有得有失。雖是一期 間語言。兩個活鱍鱍地。都有血脈針線。若 能於此見得。亦乃向十二時中。歷歷分明。其 僧便出是雙放。已下是雙收。謂之互換也。雪 竇正恁麼地。頌出。
text_en: If you all, here, recognize these two people—one going out and one coming in—then a thousand and ten thousand are just one. Acting as host is like this; acting as guest is like this. The two people, in the end, form one household. In one round of examination, guest-and-host questions and answers, from beginning to end, are the work of masters. Look: Wujiu asked this monk, How is Dingzhou’s Dharma way compared to here? The monk immediately said, Not different. If at that time it had not been Wujiu, it would have been hard to deal with this monk. Wujiu said, If it is not different, then turn back there—and he struck. But what can be done? This monk was a capable one, so he said, The staff tip has eyes; you must not strike people carelessly. Wujiu carried out his command straight through, saying, Today I’ve hit one—and he struck three more times. The monk then went out. Look at the two of them rolling and turning—both are masters of the craft. To settle this one matter, you must distinguish monk from lay, and discern blame from innocence. Though this monk went out, this case was still not finished. From start to finish, Wujou wanted to test him and see where he was real, to see how he would be. But this monk was like bracing the door and propping the house, so his true face was not yet seen. Wujou then said: So it turns out someone has taken a beating from this staff. This monk wanted to turn around and breathe out, yet he did not contend with him; he lightly turned it, saying: But what can you do, the ladle-handle is in the master’s hand. Wujou was a lineage teacher with eyes atop his head; he dared to throw himself across a fierce tiger’s mouth and say: If you want this mountain monk to hand it back to you. This fellow was one who carried a tally under his elbow; as the saying goes, to see what is right and not do it is to lack courage. Without the least hesitation, he stepped up, snatched the staff from Wujou’s hand, and struck Wujou three times. Wujou said: Bent staff, bent staff! Tell me, what is the meaning? Earlier he said: So it turns out someone has taken a beating. Yet when this monk struck him, he instead said: Bent staff, bent staff. The monk said: Someone has taken a beating. Wujou said: Carelessly you struck this fellow. Earlier he said: Carelessly you struck one. In the end he himself took the staff—why did he also say, Carelessly you struck this fellow? If at that time it were not this monk standing firm and direct, there would have been no way to deal with him. The monk then bowed. This bow was the most venomous; it was not from a good heart. If it were not Wujou, he would not have recognized it and broken through. Wujou said: And you go off like that? The monk burst into loud laughter and left. Wujou said: It can digest like this, it can digest like this. See how master hands meet: from start to finish host and guest are clearly distinguished; cut off yet able to continue. In truth it is only the pivot of mutual exchange. When he came to here, he also did not say there was some place of exchange. Such are the ancients: cutting off emotional dust and ideation. Both sides were master hands, and neither spoke of gain or loss. Though it was a single bout of words, the two were lively and quick, each with bloodlines and stitches. If you can see it here, then throughout the twelve double-hours it is vividly clear. This monk’s leaving is a double release; what follows is a double gathering. This is called mutual exchange. Xue- dou chanted it just like this.

Calling is easy; sending off is hard. Everyone under heaven keeps doubting. Stinking flesh draws flies; patch-robed monks throughout the land still do not know where it lands. No harm in wiping it out. On the sea

text_zh: 呼即易天下人總疑著。臭肉引來蠅。天下衲僧總不知落處　遣即難不妨勦絕。海 上明公秀互換機鋒子細看一出一入。二俱作家。一條拄杖兩人扶。且道在阿 誰邊劫石固來猶可壞袖裏金鎚如何辨取。千聖不傳　滄溟深處 立須乾向什麼處安排。棒頭有眼。獨許他親得烏臼老烏臼老可惜 許。這老漢不識好惡幾何般也是箇無端漢。百千萬重　與他杓柄太 無端已在言前。洎合打破蔡州。好與三十棒。且道過在什麼處
text_en: there is the eminent one, outstanding and refined. Look closely at the sharp pivot of mutual exchange. One goes out, one comes in—both are adepts. One staff, two people supporting it. Tell me, on whose side is it? Though the aeon-stone is solid, it can still be worn away; in the deep of the vast sea, How do you discern the golden hammer in the sleeve? A thousand sages do not transmit it. it would have to dry up at once. Where can you place it? The tip of the staff has eyes; only he is allowed to obtain it personally. Old Wujou, old Wujou, A pity indeed. This old fellow does not recognize good and bad. what is it, after all, to hand him the ladle-handle so He is also a pointless fellow, a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand layers without cause? already before the words. He should have smashed Caizhou—best to give him thirty blows. Tell me, where is the fault?
Calling is easy; sending off is hard. Either way, it is falling into the weeds. Xuedou was far too compassionate.

text_zh: 呼即易遣即難。一等是落草。雪竇忒殺慈悲。 尋常道。呼蛇易遣蛇難。如今將箇瓢子吹來。 喚蛇即易。要遣時即難。一似將棒與他却易。 復奪他棒。遣去却難。須是有本分手脚。方能 遣得他去。烏臼是作家。有呼蛇底手脚。亦有 遣蛇底手段。這僧也不是瞌睡底。烏臼問。定 州法道何似這裏。便是呼他。烏臼便打。是遣 他。僧云。棒頭有眼。不得草草打人。却轉在這 僧處。便是呼來。烏臼云。汝若要山僧回與汝。 僧便近前奪棒。也打三下。却是這僧遣去。乃 至這僧大笑而出。烏臼云。消得恁麼消得恁 麼。此分明是遣得他恰好。看他兩箇機鋒互 換。絲來線去。打成一片。始終賓主分明。有時 主却作賓。有時賓却作主。雪竇也讚歎不及。 所以道。互換之機。教人且子細看。劫石固 來猶可壞。謂此劫石。長四十里。廣八萬四千 由旬。厚八萬四千由旬。凡五百年乃有天人 下來。以六銖衣袖拂一下。又去至五百年。又 來如此拂。拂盡此石。乃為一劫。謂之輕衣拂 石劫。雪竇道。劫石固來猶可壞。石雖堅固。尚 爾可消磨盡。此二人機鋒。千古萬古。更無有 窮盡。滄溟深處立須乾。任是滄溟。洪波浩渺 白浪滔天。若教此二人。向內立地。此滄溟也 須乾竭。雪竇到此。一時頌了。末後更道。烏臼 老烏臼老。幾何般。或擒或縱。或殺或活。畢竟 是幾何般。與他杓柄太無端。這箇拄杖子。三 世諸佛也用。歷代祖師也用。宗師家也用。與 人抽釘拔楔。解粘去縛。爭得輕易分付與人。 雪竇意要獨用。賴值這僧當時只與他平展。 忽若旱地起雷。看他如何當抵。烏臼過杓柄 與人去。豈不是太無端。
text_en: They commonly say: calling a snake is easy; sending a snake off is hard. Now he brings a gourd ladle in by blowing. To call the snake is easy; to send it away is hard. It is like handing him the staff is easy, but then snatching the staff back and sending him off is hard. You must have fundamental hands and feet, only then can you send him off. Wujou was a master hand: he had the skill to call the snake, and also the means to send the snake away. This monk was no sleepyhead either. Wujou asked: How is Dingzhou’s Dharma Way compared to here? That was calling him in. Wujou then struck him—that was sending him off. The monk said: The staff-tip has eyes; you must not carelessly strike people. That turned it over onto this monk—this was calling him in. Wujou said: If you want this mountain monk to hand it back to you. The monk then stepped forward and snatched the staff, and also struck three times—this was the monk sending him off. Then this monk burst into loud laughter and left. Wujou said: It can digest like this, it can digest like this. This clearly is sending him off just right. Look at these two, their sharp points mutually exchanging—thread coming, line going—beating it into one piece. From start to finish host and guest are clear. Sometimes the host becomes the guest; sometimes the guest becomes the host. Even Xuedou could not praise it enough. Therefore he said: the pivot of mutual exchange—people must look closely. Though the aeon-stone is solid, it can still be worn away. This aeon-stone is said to be forty li long, and eighty-four thousand yojanas wide, and eighty-four thousand yojanas thick. Every five hundred years a heavenly being comes down and brushes it once with a sleeve of a six-zhu robe, then leaves; after another five hundred years, again comes to brush it like this. When this stone is brushed away entirely, that counts as one aeon. This is called the light-robe brushing- stone aeon. Xuedou said: though the aeon-stone is solid, it can still be worn away. Though the stone is hard, it still can be ground down to nothing. But the sharp exchange of these two people, for a thousand ages, ten thousand ages, has no end. In the deep of the vast sea, it would have to dry up at once. Even if it is the vast sea, with floodwaters broad and white waves surging to the sky, if you let these two stand firmly within, then this vast sea too would have to run dry. When Xuedou got to this, he chanted it all at once. At the end he added: Old Wujou old Wujou old—what is it, after all? Sometimes capturing, sometimes releasing; sometimes killing, sometimes enlivening—ultimately what is it? To hand him the ladle-handle was too uncaused. This staff: all Buddhas of the three times use it; patriarchs of successive generations also use it; lineage teachers’ households also use it. It is used to pull nails and remove pegs for people, to undo sticking and remove bonds—how could one lightly hand it over to others? Xuedou’s intent was to use it alone. Luckily, at that time this monk only laid it out evenly with him. If suddenly thunder rose from dry ground, see how he would meet it. Wujou passed the ladle-handle off to another—was that not too uncaused?

text_zh: 垂示云。細如米末。冷似氷霜。畐塞乾坤。離明 絕暗。低低處觀之有餘。高高處平之不足。把 住放行。總在這裏許還有出身處也無。試舉 看　畐拍逼切滿也。
text_en: and cutting off darkness. Seen from low places it is more than enough; leveled from high places it is not enough. Grasp it and release it—everything is right here. Is there still a way out or not? Try raising it and see. Fu. Clapping and pressing—tight and full.
Case 76. Danxia asked a monk: Where have you come from? Indeed you cannot entirely lack a place it came from. To know the source is not hard.

text_zh: 【七六】舉。丹霞問僧。甚處來正是不可總沒來處也。要知來處也不難 僧云。山下來著草鞋入爾肚裏過也。只是不會。言中有響諳含來。知他是黃是綠 霞云。喫飯了也未第一杓惡水澆。何必定盤星。要知端的僧云。 喫飯了果然撞著箇露柱。却被旁人穿却鼻孔。元來是箇無孔鐵鎚霞云。將 飯來與汝喫底人。還具眼麼雖然是倚勢欺人。也是據欵結案。當 時好掀倒禪床。無端作什麼僧無語果然走不得。這僧若是作家。向他道。與和尚眼一 般長慶問保福。將飯與人喫。報恩有分。為 什麼不具眼也只道得一半。通身是遍身是。一刀兩段。一手擡一手搦福 云。施者受者二俱瞎漢據令而行。一句道盡。罕遇其人長慶 云。盡其機來。還成瞎否識甚好惡。猶自未肯。討什麼碗福 云。道我瞎得麼兩箇俱是草裏漢。龍頭蛇尾。當時待他道盡其機來。還成瞎否。只 向他道瞎。也只道得一半。一等是作家。為什麼前不搆村。後不迭店。
text_en: The monk said: From below the mountain. Put on straw sandals and walk through your belly. You just do not understand. There is an echo in the words, coming hidden and familiar—how will you know whether it is yellow or green? Danxia said: Have you eaten yet? The monk said: Pour the first ladle of foul water—why insist on a fixed north star? If you want to know precisely, I have eaten. Danxia said: The one who sure enough you crash into a bare pillar, yet someone else pierces your nostrils. It turns out to be a holeless iron hammer. brought the food for you to eat—does he still have eyes? The monk had no words. Changqing asked Baofu: Bringing food for people to eat, there is a share in repaying kindness; why Though it relies on power to bully people, it is still closing the case by the evidence. At that time it was best to flip over the meditation bench—why act for no reason? Sure enough, he cannot run. If this monk were an adept, he would say to him: You have eyes like the master's, the same. is it that he does not have eyes? Baofu Even then, that only says half. The whole body is it, every part is it—one knife, two sections; one hand lifts, one hand grips. said: Giver and receiver are both blind fellows. Changqing Act in accord with the command. One sentence says it all—rare to meet such a person. said: If one exhausts the whole function, is one still blind? Baofu What do you know of good and bad? Still you will not agree—what bowl are you begging for? said: Tell me, am I blind? Both are grass-dwelling fellows: dragon head, snake tail. If at that time you waited for him to speak out his whole mechanism, would you still end up blind? Only tell him "blind," and you still say only half. Both are of the same rank as adepts—so why does it not reach a village ahead, and not catch a shop behind?
Chan Master Danxia Tianran of Dengzhou—no one knows where he was from. At first he studied Confucian learning.

text_zh: 鄧州丹霞天然禪師。不知何許人。初習儒學。 將入長安應舉。方宿於逆旅。忽夢白光滿室。 占者曰。解空之祥。偶一禪客問曰。仁者何往。 曰。選官去。禪客曰。選官何如選佛。霞云。選 佛當往何所。禪客曰。今江西馬大師出世。是 選佛之場。仁者可往。遂直造江西。才見馬 大師。以兩手托幞頭脚。馬師顧視云。吾非 汝師。南嶽石頭處去。遽抵南嶽。還以前意投 之。石頭云。著槽廠去。師禮謝。入行者堂。隨 眾作務。凡三年。石頭一日告眾云。來日剗佛 殿前草。至來日。大眾各備鍬鋤剗草。丹霞獨 以盆盛水淨頭。於師前跪膝。石頭見而笑之。 便與剃髮。又為說戒。丹霞掩耳而出。便往江 西。再謁馬祖。未參禮。便去僧堂內。騎聖僧 頸而坐。時大眾驚愕。急報馬祖。祖躬入堂。視 之曰。我子天然。霞便下禮拜曰。謝師賜法號。 因名天然他古人天然。如此頴脫。所謂選官 不如選佛也。傳燈錄中載其語句。直是壁立 千仞。句句有與人抽釘拔楔底手脚。似問這 僧道。什麼處來。僧云。山下來。這僧却不通來 處。一如具眼倒去勘主家相似。當時若不是 丹霞。也難為收拾。丹霞却云。喫飯了也未。頭 邊總未見得。此是第二回勘他。僧云。喫飯了 也。懵𢤦漢元來不會。霞云。將飯與汝喫底 人。還具眼麼。僧無語。丹霞意道。與爾這般漢 飯喫。堪作什麼。這僧若是箇漢。試與他一劄。 看他如何。雖然如是。丹霞也未放爾在。這 僧便眼眨眨地無語。保福長慶。同在雪峯會 下。常舉古人公案商量。長慶問保福。將飯與 人喫。報恩有分。為什麼不具眼。不必盡問公 案中事。大綱借此語作話頭。要驗他諦當處。 保福云。施者受者二俱瞎漢。快哉到這裏。只 論當機事。家裏有出身之路。長慶云。盡其機 來。還成瞎否。保福云。道我瞎得麼。保福意 謂。我恁麼具眼。與爾道了也。還道我瞎得麼。 雖然如是。半合半開。當時若是山僧。等他道 盡其機來。還成瞎否。只向他道瞎。可惜許。保 福當時。若下得這箇瞎字。免得雪竇許多葛 藤。雪竇亦只用此意頌。
text_en: He was going to Chang’an to take the examinations, and stayed at an inn. Suddenly he dreamed of white light filling the room. A diviner said: An auspice of understanding emptiness. By chance a Chan traveler asked: Worthy one, where are you going? He said: To be selected as an official. The Chan traveler said: How does selecting officials compare to selecting Buddhas? Danxia said: To select Buddhas, where should one go? The Chan traveler said: Now in Jiangxi, Master Ma has appeared in the world; that is the place for selecting Buddhas. Worthy one, you can go there. So he went straight to Jiangxi. As soon as he saw Master Ma, he lifted up the feet of Ma’s head-wrapped cap with both hands. Master Ma looked back and said: I am not your teacher. Go to Shitou at Nanyue. He hurried to Nanyue and again offered his former intent. Shitou said: Go to the work shed. The master bowed in thanks, entered the practitioners’ hall, and together with the assembly labored for three years. One day Shitou told the assembly: Tomorrow, clear the grass in front of the Buddha hall. When the next day came, the great assembly each prepared shovels and hoes to clear the grass. Danxia alone brought a basin of water to wash his head, knelt before the teacher, and Shitou saw this and smiled. He then shaved his hair and also explained the precepts to him. Danxia covered his ears and left, then went to Jiang- xi to visit Mazu again. Before paying respects, he went into the monks’ hall and sat astride the neck of the holy monk statue. The great assembly was startled and rushed to report to Mazu. The patriarch personally entered the hall and looked at him, saying: My son Tianran. Danxia then came down and bowed, saying: I thank the master for granting me a Dharma name. Thus he was named Tianran. Those ancients were naturally like this—so outstanding and unbound. This is what is meant by: selecting officials is not as good as selecting Buddhas. The Transmission of the Lamp records his sayings; they are truly like sheer cliffs a thousand fathoms high. Every line has the skill to pull nails and remove pegs for people. It is like asking this monk: Where have you come from? The monk says: From below the mountain. Yet this monk did not understand his coming place at all—like someone with eyes going in upside down to assess the household. If at that time it were not Danxia, it would have been hard to clean up. Danxia then said: Have you eaten yet? From the start he still had not been seen through. This was the second round of testing him. The monk said: I have eaten. The dullard never understood. Danxia said: The one who brought the food for you to eat— person. Do you still have eyes? The monk had no words. Danxia meant: With fellows like you, you eat rice, but what is it good for? If this monk were a real man, try giving him one jab and see what he does. Even so, Danxia still would not let you off. This monk just blinked and said nothing. Baofu and Changqing were together in Xuefeng’s assembly and often brought up the ancients’ cases to discuss. Changqing asked Baofu: Giving rice to people to eat, there is a share of repaying kindness; why is it that one does not have eyes? There is no need to ask every detail of the case; broadly speaking, he borrows these words as a topic, to test where it truly hits. Baofu said: Giver and receiver are both blind men. Excellent, right here. Just speak of what meets the situation; at home there is a road of emergence. Changqing said: If you exhaust his mechanism and it comes forth, does it still become blind? Baofu said: Are you saying I am blind? Baofu’s intent was: I have eyes like this, I have told you, and you still say I am blind? Even so, it is half closed and half open. If it had been this mountain monk back then, when he said, If you exhaust his mechanism and it comes forth, does it still become blind? I would only tell him: Blind. What a pity. If Baofu back then could have delivered that one word blind, it would have spared Xuedou all this much vine and creeper. Xuedou also versified only using this intent.

Exhausting the mechanism does not become blind; pressing the ox’s head to make it eat grass. You have only managed to say half of it. It still must be tested through. The words are still in the ear. Losing money,

text_zh: 盡機不成瞎只道得一半。也要驗他過。言猶在耳　按牛頭喫草失錢 遭罪。半河南半河北。殊不知傷鋒犯手四七二三諸祖師有條攀條。帶 累先聖。不唯只帶累一人寶器持來成過咎盡大地人換手搥胸。還我拄杖來。 帶累山僧也出頭不得過咎深可殺深。天下衲僧跳不出。且道深多少　無處尋 在爾脚跟下。摸索不著天上人間同陸沈天下衲僧一坑埋却。還有活底人 麼。放過一著。蒼天蒼天廠齒兩切馬屋無壁也　眨側洽切目動也
text_en: you incur punishment. Half Henan, half Hebei—without realizing you have nicked the blade and cut the hand. Four, seven, two, three: the various patriarchs and masters. Having a branch, you cling to a branch; dragging down the former sages—not merely dragging down one person. Bringing the precious vessel turns into a fault. Everyone on earth switches hands and pounds their chests: return my staff! It even drags this mountain monk down so I cannot lift my head. The fault is deep, with nowhere to search. Damnably deep. Patch-robed monks throughout the land cannot jump out. Tell me—how deep is it? Right under your heel—you cannot grope it out. In heaven above and among humans, all sink on dry land. Bury all the patch-robed monks in one pit—are there still any living people left? Letting it off once—blue heaven, blue heaven! Blink, blink. Horse-stall without walls. The eyes move.
Exhausting the mechanism does not become blind. Changqing said: If you exhaust his mechanism and it comes forth, does it still become blind? Bao-

text_zh: 盡機不成瞎。長慶云。盡其機來。還成瞎否。保 福云。道我瞎得麼。一似按牛頭喫草。須是等 他自喫始得。那裏按他頭教喫。雪竇恁麼頌。 自然見得丹霞意。四七二三諸祖師。寶器持 來成過咎。不唯只帶累長慶。乃至西天二十 八祖。此土六祖。一時埋沒。釋迦老子。四十九 年。說一大藏教。末後唯傳這箇寶器。永嘉道。 不是標形虛事褫。如來寶杖親蹤跡。若作保 福見解。寶器持來。都成過咎。過咎深無處尋。 這箇與爾說不得。但去靜坐。向他句中點檢 看。既是過咎深。因什麼却無處尋。此非小 過也。將祖師大事。一齊於陸地上平沈却。所 以雪竇道。天上人間同陸沈。
text_en: fu said: Are you saying I am blind? It is like pressing the ox’s head to make it eat grass. You must wait until it eats by itself. How could you press its head and teach it to eat? Xuedou versified it like this and naturally you see Danxia’s intent. Four, seven, two, three: the various patriarchs and masters. Bringing the precious vessel turns into a fault. It not only implicates Changqing, it even buries the twenty- eight patriarchs of the West, and the six patriarchs of this land, all at once. Old Shakyamuni, for forty-nine years, spoke the entire canon; in the end he only transmitted this precious vessel. Yongjia said: It is not an empty show of forms; the Tathagata’s jeweled staff has its own trace. If you take Baofu’s understanding, then bringing the precious vessel all turns into a fault. The fault is deep, with nowhere to search. This cannot be explained to you. Just go sit quietly, and check it within his lines, and see. Since the fault is deep, why is there nowhere to search? This is no small fault. It sinks the great affair of the patriarchs all at once, sinking it flat on dry land. Therefore Xuedou said: In heaven above and among humans, all sink on dry land.

In the house of patched-robes they ask about Buddha, ask about patriarchs, ask about Zen, ask about the Way, ask upward and downward, until there is nothing left to ask, and yet they still produce a question point, asking about talk that surpasses Buddhas and transcends patriarchs. Yunmen was an adept; as the water rises the boat floats high, as the mud grows the Buddha grows big, so he answered: A sesame cake. It can be said the Way is not practiced in vain, and effort is not applied wastefully. Yunmen again instructed the assembly, saying: You must not make up things. When you hear someone speak of the patriarchs’ meaning, you then ask about the principle of surpassing Buddhas and transcending patriarchs. You, first call what Buddha, call what patriarch, and then you speak of surpassing Buddhas and transcending patriarchs. Then you ask about leaving the three realms. Bring the three realms and look: what seeing, hearing, awareness, and knowing is obstructing you? What sounds, forms, Buddha-dharma are there for you to settle? Settle what bowl? Taking that as a view of differences, the ancient sages could do nothing with you. You throw yourself sideways to become a thing. Say: the whole body is entirely real, thing after thing meets it directly, and it cannot be gotten. I tell you: what matter is there right here? It is already buried. If you understand these words, then you recognize the sesame cake. The Fifth Patriarch said: Donkey dung is compared to musk. As the saying goes: directly cutting to the root is what the Buddha attested; picking leaves and searching branches, I cannot. When you reach here and want it intimate, do not take a question to ask a question. Look at this monk asking: What is talk that surpasses Buddhas and transcends patriarchs? Yunmen said: A ses- ame cake. Do you still know shame? Do you still sense leakage? There are some people who fabricate, saying: Yunmen saw a rabbit and released the hawk, so he said sesame cake. If you take sesame cake like that as the view of talk that surpasses Buddhas and transcends patriarchs, how could there be a living road? Do not take it as a A cake banquet. And if you do not make it a surpass-Buddhas-and-outdo-Patriarchs affair, then it is the living road. Like hemp the three pounds of hemp that can beat a drum: though it is only said as sesame cake, in truth it is hard to see. Later people often make doctrines of it, saying: coarse words and subtle words all return to the first meaning. If you understand it like that, then go be a lecturer; for a whole life you win much knowing and much explaining. Nowadays Zen fellows say: When you surpass Buddhas and transcend patriarchs, all Buddhas are trampled under your heels, and the patriarchs too are trampled under your heels. Therefore Yunmen only told him: sesame cake. Since it is sesame cake, how could it transcend Buddhas and patriarchs? Go investigate it carefully. There are extremely many verses in various places, all making words at the edge of the question. Only Xue- dou’s verse is the best. Try raising it and see. The verse says:
Zen guests asking about surpassing talk ask far too much; do you see the seams and gaps torn open, Each one that comes out at once makes this kind of understanding—like hemp, like millet.

text_en: Yunmen saying: You people shoulder your staffs crosswise and say you study Zen and learn the Way, and then you go looking for some principle of surpassing Buddhas and transcending patriarchs. Let me ask you: throughout the twelve hours, in walking standing sitting lying, in shitting and pissing, even for the bugs in the latrine and in the market buying and selling at the mutton stall, is there still any principle of surpassing Buddhas and transcending patriarchs? Speak it out if you can. If not, do not hinder me from going east or west, and then he stepped down from the seat. Some do not even know good from bad and make an enso, adding mud on dirt, adding cangues and chains. Do you see the seams and gaps torn open? Where he brings up the question, there are great and small seams and gaps. Yun- men saw that his question was torn open, so he used a sesame cake to block the seam and plug it tight. This monk still would not stop, and asked again. Therefore Xuedou said: Even when the sesame cake comes, you still will not stop. To this day, under heaven there are distortions. Nowadays Zen fellows only go on interpreting it from the sesame cake, or else they make doctrines in the place of surpassing Buddhas and transcending patriarchs. Since it is not in either of these two ends, where is it ultimately? After thirty years, wait until this mountain monk changes bones and comes out, then I will tell you.

text_en: pure conduct, and each spoke of the cause by which they realized the perfect penetration dharma gate. This too is one among the twenty- five perfect penetrations. He, because while bathing with the monks he entered the bath as usual, suddenly awakened to the water as the cause, and said: Since it does not wash dust, and also does not wash the body, tell me, what does it wash? If you can understand it, then in the middle it is at ease, gaining nothing at all; a thousand, ten thousand cannot even come near. As is said: taking no attainment as true prajna; if there is attainment, it is only similar prajna. Do you not see Bodhidharma saying to the Second Patriarch: Bring me your mind and I will set it at rest for you. The Second Patriarch said: When I searched for mind, it could not be found. Here is the very life-root of a patch-robed monk. In the end there is no need for so many entangling vines at all. Just say a sudden awakening to the cause of water, and it is naturally clear and settled. Since one does not wash away dust, one also does not wash the body. Tell me, awaken to what? When you reach this stage, not a speck can be attached. Even saying the word Buddha must be avoided. He said: wondrous contact makes it manifest, and the child of Buddha abides. Proclaim means reveal; wondrous contact is clarity. Once you awaken to wondrous contact, the child of Buddha abides, that is, abides on Buddha-ground. People nowadays also enter the bath and also wash with water, and they touch just like that; why then do they not awaken? They are all confused and obstructed by dusty objects and conditions, stuck to the skin and clinging to the bones, so they cannot at once go clear and awake. If in this place, washing gains nothing, touching gains nothing, and the cause of water gains nothing. Tell me: is it wondrous contact making it manifest, or is it not wondrous contact making it manifest? If right here you see it directly, that is wondrous contact making it manifest: the child of Buddha abides. People nowadays also touch; do they still see the wondrous place? Wondrous contact is not ordinary contact: when contact and the one who contacts unite, it is contact; when they separate, it is not. Xuansha crossing a ridge, stubbing his toe, and even Deshan's staff: are these not wondrous contact? Even so, you still must have seven penetrations and eight openings for it to work. If you only grope around on the body, what does it have to do with it? If you go with seven penetrations and eight openings, why need to enter a bath? Right on the tip of a single hair you manifest the jeweled king's land; within a mote of dust you turn the great Dharma wheel. If you penetrate in one place, in a thousand places and ten thousand places you penetrate at once. Do not merely guard one nest or one cave; everywhere is the gate by which Guanyin enters principle. The ancients too had awakening to the Way on hearing sound, and clarifying the mind on seeing form. If one person awakens, that is so; why did the sixteen great ones awaken all at the same time? Therefore the ancients practiced together and realized together, awakened together and understood together. Xuedou picked up the teaching's intent, making people go and understand at the place of wondrous contact. He brought forth his teaching eye in verse, to spare people from being netted by the teaching and caged, half drunk and half awake. He wants people to go directly open and unencumbered. text_en: Zen traveler, just hearing it raised, picks it up and goes. A patch-robed monk like this needs only one; why form crowds and teams? Stretched out on a long connected bed, he lies with legs extended. The ancients said: clearly there is no Dharma of awakening; once you awaken, it still confuses people. Stretch both legs out long and sleep. No false and no true; therefore in the breast there is not a single affair. When hungry, eat; when tired, sleep. Xuedou's meaning is: if you say that by entering the bath you awaken to wondrous contact making it manifest, as far as this kind of no-affairs patch-robed monk is concerned, it is only like speaking of a dream within a dream. Therefore he says: In a dream you once spoke of awakening perfect penetration; when the fragrant water is used to wash, suddenly spit in your face. Like this, it is merely filthy water suddenly poured over your head; what more is there to say about perfect penetration? Xuedou says: a fellow like this is just right for sudden spitting straight on his head and face. This mountain monk says: on dirt you add mud, another layer.

text_zh: 投子朴實頭。得逸群之辯。凡有致問。開口便 見膽。不費餘力。便坐斷他舌頭。可謂運籌帷 幄之中。決勝千里之外。這僧將聲色佛法見 解。貼在他額頭上。逢人便問。投子作家。來風 深辨。這僧知投子實頭。合下做箇圈繢子。教 投子入來。所以有後語。投子却使陷虎之機。 釣他後語出來。這僧接他答處道。和尚莫㞘 沸碗鳴聲。果然一釣便上。若是別人。則不奈 這僧何。投子具眼。隨後便打。咬猪狗底手脚。 須還作家始得。左轉也隨他阿轆轆地。右轉 也隨他阿轆轆地。這僧既是做箇圈繢子。要 來捋虎鬚。殊不知投子。更在他圈繢頭上。投 子便打。這僧可惜許。有頭無尾。當時等他 拈棒。便與掀倒禪床。直饒投子全機。也須倒 退三千里。又問。麁言及細語皆歸第一義是 否。投子亦云是。一似前頭語無異。僧云。喚和 尚作一頭驢得麼。投子又打。這僧雖然作窠 窟。也不妨奇特。若是曲彔木床上老漢。頂門 無眼。也難折挫他。投子有轉身處。這僧既做 箇道理。要攙他行市。到了依舊不奈投子老 漢何。不見巖頭道。若論戰也。箇箇立在轉處。 投子放去太遲。收來太急。這僧當時。若解轉 身吐氣。豈不作得箇口似血盆底漢。衲僧家 一不做二不休。這僧既不能返擲。却被投子 穿了鼻孔。頌云。
text_en: showed his guts. Without spending extra effort, he simply cut off their tongues while seated. It can be called planning within the curtain, deciding victory a thousand miles away. This monk took his views about sound and form and Buddhadharma and pasted them on his own forehead, asking everyone he met. Touzi was a seasoned hand, with sharp discernment; he saw through it deeply. This monk knew Touzi was a solid fellow, so from the start he made a trap, to make Touzi step into it, and so there was the follow-up line. But Touzi instead used a tiger-trapping mechanism, to fish out the monk's follow-up words. The monk, catching at Touzi's reply, said: Master, do not take the sound of a boiling bowl. Sure enough, one cast and he bit. If it were someone else, they could do nothing against this monk. Touzi had eyes; right after it he struck. Hands and feet that bite pigs and dogs must belong to a seasoned hand. Turning left, he rolls along with him; turning right, he rolls along with him. This monk, having made a trap, wanted to stroke the tiger's whiskers. He did not know that Touzi was even above his trap. Tou- zi immediately struck. Pity this monk: a head with no tail. At the time, if he had waited for Touzi to pick up the staff, then overturned the Zen bench, even if Touzi had the whole functioning, he would still have had to retreat three thousand miles. He asked again: Rough speech and subtle speech both return to the first meaning, is it so? Touzi also said yes. It was no different from the earlier line. The monk said, Can I call the mas- ter a donkey? Touzi struck again. Although this monk made nests and caves, it was not without something strange. If it were some old fellow on a crooked wooden bed, with no eyes on the crown of his head, it would be hard to break him down. Touzi had a place to turn around. This monk, having made a piece of reasoning, wanted to elbow into his trade; but when it came to it, he still could not do anything to old Touzi. Haven't you seen Yantou say: when it comes to battle, each one stands at a turning point. Touzi let him go too late, and pulled him in too fast. If at that time this monk had known how to turn his body and breathe out, would he not have made himself into a fellow with a mouth like a basin of blood? Patch-robed monks do it once and do not stop at twice. Since this monk could not throw it back, he was instead led by Touzi with his nostrils pierced. The verse says:

text_en: zi is solid and plain. Suddenly he goes three steps down the mountain; if someone asks you, say, what is Touzi's solid-plain place, how will you respond? The ancients said: where the wheel of function turns, the author is still deluded. His wheel of function turns rumbling without the least obstruction. Therefore Xuedou said: release one and get two. Haven't you seen a monk ask: What is Buddha? Tou- zi said, Buddha. He asked again: What is the Way? Touzi said, the Way. He asked again: What is Zen? Touzi said, Zen. He asked again: when the moon is not yet full, how is it? Tou- zi said, swallow three and four. After it is full, how is it? Spit out seven and eight. Touzi received people and always used this device. Answering this monk, it was only a single word yes. This monk was struck twice, so Xuedou said: the same there and the same here. In four lines at once he finished versifying Touzi. In the end he versified this monk, saying: pitiable are the countless people who play with the tide. This monk dared to seize the banner and snatch the drum, saying: Master, do not take the sound of a boiling bowl. And he also said: can I call the master a donkey? This is exactly where he plays with the tide. This monk exhausted his tricks, yet still died in Touzi's phrase as before. Touzi struck immediately. This monk is precisely one who in the end still falls and dies within the tide. Xue- dou spoke for this monk: if suddenly living, then overturn the Zen bench; Touzi too would have had to retreat three thousand miles, until a hundred streams roar as they flow backward. Not only would the Zen bench shake, but mountains and rivers would loom jagged; heaven and earth would suddenly darken. If each and every one were like this, this mountain monk would beat the retreat drum. You all: where would you go to settle your body and establish your life? Jagged, looming. Against. Against.

text_zh: 【八〇】舉。僧問趙州。初生孩子。還具六識也無 閃電之機。說什麼初生孩兒子趙州云。急水上打毬子過也。俊鷂趁 不及。也要驗過僧復問投子。急水上打毬子。意旨 如何也是作家同驗過。還會麼。過也子云。念念不停流打葛藤漢。
text_en: Zhaozhou said: hitting a ball on swift water. The monk again asked Touzi: hitting a ball on swift water, what is the meaning The moment of a flash of lightning—why talk about a newborn baby? Passed. A swift hawk cannot catch up. It too must be tested through. of it? Touzi said: thought after thought flows on without stopping. Experts also test it together. Do you understand? Passed. Beat the vine-and-creeper fellow.
These six consciousnesses are established by the teaching schools as the proper root. Mountains and rivers, the great earth, sun and moon and stars.

text_zh: 此六識。教家立為正本。山河大地。日月星辰。 因其所以生。來為先鋒。去為殿後。古人道。三 界唯心。萬法唯識。若證佛地。以八識。轉為四 智。教家謂之改名不改體。根塵識是三。前塵 元不會分別。勝義根能發生識。識能顯色分 別。即是第六意識。第七識末那識。能去執持 世間一切影事。令人煩惱。不得自由自在。皆 是第七識。到第八識。亦謂之阿賴耶識。亦謂 之含藏識。含藏一切善惡種子。這僧知教意。 故將來問趙州道。初生孩子。還具六識也無。 初生孩兒。雖具六識眼能見耳能聞。然未曾 分別六塵。好惡長短。是非得失。他恁麼時 總不知。學道之人要復如嬰孩。榮辱功名。逆 情順境。都動他不得。眼見色與盲等。耳聞聲 與聾等。如癡似兀。其心不動。如須彌山。這箇 是衲僧家。真實得力處。古人道。衲被蒙頭萬 事休。此時山僧都不會。若能如此。方有少分 相應。雖然如此。爭奈一點也瞞他不得。山依 舊是山。水依舊是水。無造作。無緣慮。如日月 運於太虛未嘗暫止。亦不道我有許多名相。 如天普蓋。似地普擎。為無心故。所以長養 萬物。亦不道我有許多功行。天地為無心故。 所以長久。若有心則有限齊。得道之人亦復 如是。於無功用中施功用。一切違情順境。皆 以慈心攝受。到這裏。古人尚自呵責道。了了 了時無可了。玄玄玄處直須呵。又道。事事通 兮物物明。達者聞之暗裏驚。又云。入聖超凡 不作聲。臥龍長怖碧潭清。人生若得長如此。 大地那能留一名。然雖恁麼。更須跳出窠窟 始得。豈不見。教中道。第八不動地菩薩。以無 功用智。於一微塵中。轉大法輪。於一切時中。 行住坐臥。不拘得失。任運流入薩婆若海。衲 僧家。到這裏。亦不可執著。但隨時自在。遇茶 喫茶遇飯喫飯。這箇向上事著箇定字也不 得。著箇不定字也不得。石室善道和尚示眾 云。汝不見小兒出胎時。何曾道我會看教。當 恁麼時。亦不知有佛性義。無佛性義。及至長 大。便學種種知解出來。便道我能我解。不知 是客塵煩惱。十六觀行中。嬰兒行為最。哆哆 啝啝時。喻學道之人離分別取捨心。故讚歎 嬰兒。可況喻取之。若謂嬰兒是道。今時人錯 會。南泉云。我十八上。解作活計。趙州道。我 十八上解破家散宅。又道。我在南方二十年。 除粥飯二時。是雜用心處。曹山問僧。菩薩定 中。聞香象渡河。歷歷地。出什麼經。僧云。涅 槃經。山云。定前聞定後聞。僧云。和尚流也。 山云。灘下接取。又楞嚴經云。湛入合湛入識 邊際。又楞伽經云。相生執礙。想生妄想。流 注生則逐妄流轉。若到無功用地。猶在流注 相中。須是出得第三流注生相。方始快活自 在。所以溈山問仰山云。寂子如何。仰山云。和 尚問他見解。問他行解。若問他行解。某甲不 知。若是見解。如一瓶水注一鉼水。若得如 此。皆可以為一方之師。趙州云。急水上打毬 子。早是轉轆轆地。更向急水上打時。眨眼便 過。譬如楞嚴經云。如急流水。望為恬靜。古人 云。譬如駛流水。水流無定止。各各不相知。諸 法亦如是。趙州答處。意渾類此。其僧又問 投子。急水上打毬子。意旨如何。子云。念念不 停流。自然與他問處恰好。古人行履綿密。答 得只似一箇。更不消計較。爾纔問他。早知爾 落處了也。孩子六識。雖然無功用。爭奈念念 不停。如密水流。投子恁麼答。可謂深辨來風。 雪竇頌云　駛音史疾也。
text_en: Because of how it arises: coming, it serves as the vanguard; going, it serves as the rearguard. The ancients said: the three realms are only mind; the ten thousand dharmas are only consciousness. If one realizes the Buddha-ground, the eight consciousnesses are transformed into the four wisdoms. The doctrinal schools call this changing the name without changing the substance. Root, dust, and consciousness are three; the external dust originally cannot discriminate. The supreme root faculty can give rise to consciousness; consciousness can manifest form and discriminate distinctions—this is the sixth, the mind-consciousness. The seventh consciousness, the manas consciousness, can grasp and hold all shadowy things of the world, causing people affliction and preventing freedom and ease. All of this is the seventh consciousness. As for the eighth consciousness, it is also called the alaya consciousness, and also called the storehouse consciousness, containing all wholesome and unwholesome seeds. This monk knew the doctrinal meaning, so he came to ask Zhaozhou: does a newborn child still have the six consciousnesses or not? A newborn child, though possessing the six consciousnesses—eyes can see, ears can hear—has not yet discriminated the six sense-objects: liking and disliking, long and short, right and wrong, gain and loss. At that time, it does not know any of it. A person learning the Way should return to being like an infant: honor and disgrace, merit and fame, adverse feelings and favorable circumstances cannot move him. Seeing forms with the eyes is the same as being blind; hearing sounds with the ears is the same as being deaf. Like a fool, like a stump, the mind does not move, like Mount Sumeru. This is where a patched-robed monk truly gains strength. The ancients said: with the patched robe covering your head, ten thousand matters cease. At such a time this mountain monk understands nothing at all. If you can be like this, only then is there a small measure of accord. Even so, you cannot hide even a bit from it. Mountains are still mountains, waters are still waters. No contrivance, no calculating thought—like the sun and moon moving through vast space without ever pausing. It does not say, I have so many names and marks. Like heaven universally covering, like earth universally supporting—because it is without mind, it nurtures and sustains all beings. It does not say, I have so many merits and practices. Heaven and earth, because they are without mind, endure for a long time. If there is mind, then there are limits. A person who has attained the Way is likewise like this: within no-doing, he applies doing. All adverse feelings and favorable circumstances are embraced with a compassionate heart. When you reach here, the ancients still scolded, saying: when it is utterly clear, there is nothing to be made clear. In the most mysterious place, you must scold straight through. They also said: in every matter it is open, in every thing it is bright; the one who has arrived hears this and is startled in the dark. And again: entering sagehood and surpassing the ordinary, it makes no sound; the crouching dragon is long feared, the green pool is clear. If a person could always be like this, how could the great earth keep even a single name? Yet even so, you must still leap out of the nest and the den before it is so. Have you not seen the doctrine say: the bodhisattva of the eighth, Immovable Ground, with no-doing wisdom, turns the great Dharma wheel within a single speck of dust, and in all times walking, standing, sitting, and lying down, is not bound by gain and loss, and naturally flows into the ocean of omniscience. In the patched-robed monk’s house, when you reach here, you must not cling even to this—just be free according to the time. Meet tea, drink tea; meet rice, eat rice. This matter of going beyond cannot be pinned with the word fixed, and cannot be pinned with the word not-fixed either. Venerable Shishi Shandao instructed the assembly, saying: do you not see that when a child comes out of the womb, it never says, I can read doctrine. At such a time, it does not know the meaning of having buddha-nature, or not having buddha-nature. When it grows up, it then learns all sorts of knowledge and interpretations, and then says, I can, I understand—without knowing these are guest-dust afflictions. Among the sixteen contemplative practices, infant conduct is best. Babbling and cooing are metaphors for a person learning the Way leaving behind the discriminating mind of grasping and rejecting. Therefore one praises the infant, and takes it as a metaphor. If one claims the infant is the Way, people today mis understand. Nanquan said, When I was eighteen and up, I knew how to make a living. Zhaozhou said, When I was eighteen and up, I knew how to break up a household and scatter the home. He also said, I was in the South for twenty years; aside from the two times of gruel and rice, it was mixed, busy mind. Caoshan asked a monk: in bodhisattva concentration, hearing a fragrant elephant crossing the river, vividly and clearly—what sutra is it from? The monk said, The Nir vana Sutra. Caoshan said, Heard before concentration, heard after concentration? The monk said, The master is flowing. Caoshan said, Catch it below the shoals. Also, the Shurangama Sutra says: the deep enters and merges; the deep enters into the boundary of consciousness. And the Lankavatara Sutra says: from marks arises grasping obstruction; from thought arise deluded thoughts; the flowing stream gives rise to becoming, and one follows delusion in turning. Even if you reach the no-doing ground, you are still within the flowing-stream phase; you must get out of the third phase of flowing-stream becoming before you are at ease and free. Therefore Weishan asked Yangshan, How is Jizi? Yangshan said, If the mas ter asks him about understanding, ask him about practice-understanding. If you ask about his practice-understanding, I do not know. If it is understanding, it is like pouring one bottle of water into one bowl of water. If it is like this, then he can serve as a teacher in one region. Zhaozhou said, Hitting a ball atop rushing water already rolls and spins. If you hit it again atop rushing water, in the blink of an eye it has passed by. It is like what the Shurangama Sutra says: like a swift current, it appears calm when seen from afar. The ancients said: like a fast-flowing stream, the water’s flow has no fixed stop; each does not know the other. The dharmas are also like this. In Zhaozhou’s reply, the intent is wholly like this. That monk again asked Touzi: hitting a ball atop rushing water—what is the meaning? Touzi said, Thought after thought does not stop flowing. Naturally it fits his question exactly. The ancients’ conduct was seamless and close-knit; their answers came out as if from a single one, with no need for calculation. The moment you asked him, he already knew where you would land. The child’s six consciousnesses, though without deliberate doing, still—thought after thought— do not stop, like hidden water flowing. Touzi answered like this—one could say he deeply discerned the wind that was coming. Xuedou’s verse says: Swift. Very swift.

The six consciousnesses, without deliberate doing, extend a single question; With eyes as if blind, with ears as if deaf. A bright mirror on its stand; a luminous pearl in the palm. One sentence says it all.

Beginning to end, one thread runs through—passed. Say what? Its landing never stops—who can see it? Look, and you pass by blindly. Receive it below the shoals.

text_zh: 六識無功伸一問。古人學道。養到這裏。謂之 無功之功。與嬰兒一般。雖有眼耳鼻舌身意。 而不能分別六塵。蓋無功用也。既到這般田 地。便乃降龍伏虎。坐脫立亡。如今人但將目 前萬境。一時歇却。何必八地以上。方乃如是。 雖然無功用處。依舊山是山水是水。雪竇前 面頌云。活中有眼還同死。藥忌何須鑒作家。 蓋為趙州投子是作家。故云。作家曾共辨來 端。茫茫急水打毬子。投子道。念念不停流。諸 人還知落處麼。雪竇末後教人自著眼看。是 故云。落處不停誰解看。此是雪竇活句。且道 落在什麼處。
text_en: the doing of no-doing. It is like an infant: though it has eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind, it cannot discriminate the six sense-objects—this is no deliberate doing. Once you reach this sort of field, then you subdue dragons and tame tigers, shed the body sitting, depart standing. People today only need to have the ten thousand present conditions cease all at once—why must it be only above the eighth ground for it to be so? Even at the place of no deliberate doing, mountains are still mountains and waters are still waters. Earlier Xuedou versified: In the living there are eyes, yet it is still like death; why must medicine-taboo use the mirror to assess adepts? Because Zhaozhou and Touzi were adepts, he said: adepts once together discerned the wind that came. Vast, vast, rushing water—hitting a ball. Touzi said, thought after thought does not stop flowing. All of you, do you still know the landing place? In the end Xuedou taught people to set their own eyes and see; thus he said: its landing never stops—who can see it? This is Xuedou’s living phrase. Tell me, where does it land?

text_en: to illuminate what is fit to the moment. A deer and a musk-deer are ordinarily easy to shoot; only the musk-deer among musk-deer is the king among deer, the hardest to shoot. This musk-deer often sharpens its horns on cliff rocks, like a keen blade. With its body it protects and cherishes the herd; even tigers cannot come near. This monk too seemed alert, coming to ask Yaoshan, to illuminate the first pivot. Yaoshan said, Watch the arrow. A true adept teacher is indeed remarkable—like striking sparks from stone, like a flash of lightning. Have you not seen how Sanping first visited Shigong? As soon as Shigong saw him coming, he made the posture of drawing a bow and said, Watch the arrow. Sanping opened his chest and said, Is this an arrow that kills people, or an arrow that brings people to life? Shigong flicked the bowstring three times, and Sanping bowed. Gong said: Thirty years. One bow, two arrows. Today I only shot half a sage, so I snapped the bow and arrows. Later Sanping brought it up to Dadian. Dadian said: If it is an arrow that brings living people to life, why do you discriminate on the bowstring? Sanping had no words. Dadian said: Thirty years from now, to find someone who can raise this saying will be hard. Fadeng has a verse: In old times there was Master Shigong, who sat with bow and arrows set. Thus for thirty years. Not one true knower. Sanping hit the mark. Father and son met in harmony. Carefully reflect again: from the start it was shooting at a target. Shigong's methods were just like Yaoshan's. Sanping had eyes in the crown of his head; under a single phrase he hit it at once. Just like Yaoshan saying "Watch the arrow"—that monk then made himself the deer and threw his body down. This monk too seemed like a capable hand. Only he had a head but no tail. Since he set the snare to trap Yaoshan, how could it help that Yaoshan was a true adept, pressing him on relentlessly. Yaoshan said: Attendant, drag out this dead fellow. It was like deploying the ranks and advancing. It was fine that the monk ran—fine, it is so. But he was not cleanly free, sticky-footed and sticky-handed. Therefore Yaoshan said: This mud ball fellow—what limit does he have? If Yaoshan at the time had no further words, for a thousand ages he would be picked over by people. Yaoshan said: Watch the arrow. The monk then fell. Now tell me: is this understanding or not understanding? If you say it is understanding, why did Yaoshan then speak like this? Mud-ball fellow—this is the worst. It is just like when a monk asked Deshan: A student wields the Moye sword—what if he intends to take the master's head? Deshan stretched out his neck, leaned forward, and said... The monk said: The master's head has fallen. Deshan lowered his head and returned to the abbot's room. Later Yantou asked the monk: Where do you come from? The monk said: From the Western Capital. Yantou said: After Huang Chao passed through, did you ever retrieve the sword? The monk said: I retrieved it. Yantou stretched out his neck, leaned forward, and said... The monk said: The master's head has fallen. Yantou laughed loudly. Cases like this are all mechanisms for trapping tigers, exactly like this. It was precisely because Yaoshan did not bother with him, only because he saw through it, that he kept pressing him. Xuedou said: This monk in three steps may live, but in five steps he must die. Though this monk really understood "watch the arrow," he simply threw his body down. Yaoshan said: Attendant, drag out this dead fellow. The monk then ran. Xuedou said: I only fear that beyond three steps he would not live. If at that time he had leapt beyond five steps, then under heaven no one could have done anything to him. When adepts meet, host and guest must from start to finish exchange roles without a break—only then is there a share of free ease. Since this monk at the time could not carry it through to the end, he was inspected by Xuedou. Later he also used his own words. The verse says:

text_en: Have the bearing of deer among deer; have mechanisms and tactics. Even if it is a fierce tiger with wings or a great beast with horns, it can only preserve its body and keep far from harm. This monk at that time threw himself down and said to himself: I am the deer. With the next arrow, run three steps. Yaoshan said: Watch the arrow. The monk then fell. This monk carried a load of crudity, and exchanged it for a load of muddle, bringing forth a questioning point, with no small flaws. If it were not Dalong, how could it cover heaven and cover earth? He asked like that; Dalong answered like that. In one fitting of forms, not shifting a hair's breadth. Like seeing a rabbit and releasing the hawk, seeing the hole and driving the wedge. In the three vehicles and the twelvefold teachings, is there still such a moment? It is not that it cannot be wondrous—only the words are tasteless, blocking people's mouths. Therefore it is said: A piece of white cloud lies across the valley mouth; how many returning birds at night lose their nests. Some say it is just an offhand answer. If you understand it that way, you are all fellows who wipe out the barbarian tribes. You do not know that the ancients, with one device and one situation, knocked the cangue and struck the lock—one phrase, one word, pure gold and uncut jade. If you have the eyes and brains of a patched-robed monk, sometimes you seize, sometimes you release; illumination and function are simultaneous; person and environment are both taken away; both released and both gathered; at the moment you adapt with ease. Without great function and great mechanism, how could one understand such a net over heaven and canopy over earth? It is like a bright mirror on its stand: barbarians come, barbarians appear; Chinese come, Chinese appear. This case is like the talk of flowers and the medicine railing, yet the intent is different. The place where this monk asked was unclear; Dalong's answering was just right. Do you not see a monk asking Yunmen: When the trees wither and the leaves fall, how is it? For eighty-four thousand immeasurable kalpas, falling into the Avici karma—you still have not returned even half of it.
