text_zh: 雪竇頌得。最有工夫。前來頌雲門話。却云。問 既有宗。答亦攸同。這箇却不恁麼。却云。問曾 不知。答還不會。大龍答處傍瞥。直是奇特。分 明是誰恁麼問。未問已前。早納敗缺了也。他 答處俯能恰好。應機宜道。山花開似錦。㵎 水湛如藍。爾諸人如今作麼生會大龍意。答 處傍瞥。直是奇特。所以雪竇頌出。教人知道 月冷風高。更撞著古巖寒檜。且道他意作麼 生會。所以適來道。無孔笛子撞著氈拍板。只 這四句頌了也。雪竇又怕人作道理。却云。堪 笑路逢達道人。不將語默對。此事且不是見 聞覺知。亦非思量分別。所以云。的的無兼帶。 獨運何依賴。路逢達道人。不將語默對。此是 香巖頌雪竇引用也。不見僧問趙州。不將語 默對。未審將什麼對。州云。呈漆器。這箇便同 適來話。不落爾情塵意想。一似什麼。手把白 玉鞭驪珠盡擊碎。是故祖令當行十方坐斷。 此是劍刃上事。須是有恁麼作略。若不恁麼。 總辜負從上諸聖。到這裏要無些子事。自有 好處。便是向上人行履處也。既不擊碎。必增 瑕纇。便見漏逗。畢竟是作麼生得是。國有憲 章三千條罪。五刑之屬三千。莫大於不孝。憲 是法章是條。三千條罪。一時犯了也。何故如 此。只為不以本分事接人。若是大龍必不恁 麼也。
text_en: has a lineage; the answer accords with it. But this one is not like that. Here he says: Asked—he never knew; answered—he still did not understand. Dalong's answer is a sideways glance—truly wondrous. Clearly who is it that asks like this? Before he even asked, he had already taken in the flaw. As for his answering, it can bow down and be just right, responding appropriately: Mountain flowers bloom like brocade. The water is deep and blue like indigo. All of you now, how will you understand Dalong's intent? The answer is a sideways glance—truly wondrous. Therefore Xuedou brought forth this verse to let people know: The moon is cold, the wind is high—further colliding with ancient cliff and cold cypress. Now tell me, how is his intent to be understood? Thus it was just said: A holeless flute runs into a felt clapper board. It is only these four lines of verse. Xuedou also feared people would make doctrine of it, so he said: Laughable— meeting a realized person on the road, not responding with speech or silence. This matter is not a matter of seeing Hearing, awareness, knowing—none of it is thinking or discriminating. Therefore it is said: plainly, it has no admixture. When it moves alone, what can it rely on? Meeting a realized person on the road, you do not answer with either speech or silence. This is what Xiangyan praised, which Xuedou quoted. Haven’t you seen a monk ask Zhaozhou: You do not answer with either speech or silence—so what will you answer with? Zhaozhou said: Present a lacquer vessel. This is the same as what was just said: it does not fall into your emotional dust and mental imagining. Like what? Holding a white jade whip, you smash the black pearl to bits. Thus the ancestral command is to be carried out: in the ten directions, sit and cut off. This is business on the sword’s edge. You must have such a tactic; if not, you wholly betray all the sages of old. When you reach here, there must not be the slightest thing; then there is a good place. This is precisely where a person of the Way walks. If you do not smash it, you will surely add blemishes and flaws, and then leaks will show. Ultimately, how can it be right? A state has statutes with three thousand articles of crime; the five punishments have three thousand categories—none is greater than unfiliality. The statute is the law; the chapter is the article. Even if you violate all three thousand crimes at once—why is it so ? Only because you do not meet people with the fundamental matter. If it were a great dragon, it would not be like this.

text_zh: 【八三】舉。雲門示眾云。古佛與露柱相交。是第 幾機三千里外沒交涉。七花八裂自代云東家人死。西家人助哀。一合相不可得 南山起雲乾坤莫覩。刀斫不入北山下雨點滴不施。半河南半河北。
text_en: what numbered pivot? He answered for himself: Three thousand miles away, it has nothing to do with it. Shattered into seven flowers and eight splits. The east neighbor dies; the west neighbor helps mourn. A single united form cannot be obtained. South Mountain raises clouds; North Mountain sends down rain. Heaven and earth cannot be seen; a knife chop cannot enter. Not a drop is applied—half Henan, half Hebei.
Great Master Yunmen produced more than eighty good spiritual guides. More than seventy

text_zh: 雲門大師。出八十餘員善知識。遷化後七十 餘年。開塔觀之。儼然如故。他見地明白。機境 迅速。大凡垂語別語代語。直下孤峻。只這公 案。如擊石火。似閃電光。直是神出鬼沒。慶藏 主云。一大藏教還有這般說話麼。如今人多 向情解上作活計。道佛是三界導師四生慈 父。既是古佛。為什麼却與露柱相交。若恁 麼會。卒摸索不著。有者喚作無中唱出。殊不 知宗師家說話。絕意識絕情量。絕生死絕法 塵。入正位更不存一法。爾纔作道理計較。便 纏脚纏手。且道他古人意作麼生。但只使心 境一如。好惡是非。撼動他不得。便說有也得 無也得。有機也得無機也得。到這裏拍拍是 令。五祖先師道。大小雲門元來膽小。若是山 僧。只向他道第八機。他道。古佛與露柱相交。 是第幾機。一時間且向目前包裹。僧問。未審 意旨如何。門云。一條絛三十文買。他有定乾 坤底眼。既無人會。後來自代云。南山起雲北 山下雨。且與後學通箇入路。所以雪竇只拈 他定乾坤處教人見。若纔犯計較露箇鋒鋩。 則當面蹉過。只要原他雲門宗旨。明他峻機。 所以頌出云。
text_en: years after his passing, they opened the stupa and saw him—solemn as before. His ground of seeing was clear; his pivots and situations were swift. In general, his pointing phrases, separate phrases, and substitute phrases were directly solitary and steep. This very public case is like striking stone for sparks, like a flash of lightning—truly appearing and vanishing like spirits and ghosts. Qingzang the abbot said: Does the whole canon even have talk like this? Nowadays people mostly make their living in emotional interpretations, saying the Buddha is the guide of the three realms, the compassionate father of the four kinds of birth. If he is an ancient Buddha, why then does he commune with a pillar? If you understand it like this, in the end you will not be able to find it. Some call it singing out of nothingness. But they do not know that the words of the masters cut off consciousness and cut off emotional measuring; cut off birth and death and cut off dharma dust. Entering the proper position, not a single thing is retained. The moment you start reasoning and calculating, you bind your feet and hands. Tell me: what was the intent of the ancients? They only made mind and environment one suchness; likes and dislikes, right and wrong—none can shake it. Then saying there is is fine; saying there isn’t is fine; having pivots is fine; having no pivots is fine. Here, a slap is the command. The ancestral master Wuzu said: Big and small, Yunmen was originally timid. If it were this mountain monk, I would just tell him: the eighth pivot. He said: An ancient Buddha communes with a pillar— what numbered pivot is it? For the moment, wrap it up right before your eyes. A monk asked: I wonder what is the purport? Yunmen said: One cord, bought for thirty coins. He has an eye that settles heaven and earth. Since no one understood, later he answered for himself: South Mountain raises clouds; North Mountain sends down rain—just to give later students a way in. Therefore Xuedou only picks up his place of settling heaven and earth to let people see. If you so much as fall into calculation and show a bit of sharpness, you miss it right in front of your face. You only need to trace Yunmen’s central aim and understand his steep pivot. Therefore the verse says:
South Mountain clouds, North Mountain rain—four seven, Heaven and earth cannot be seen; a knife chop cannot enter. Not a drop is applied—half Henan, half Hebei.

text_zh: 南山雲乾坤莫覩。刀斫不入　北山雨點滴不施。半河南半河北　四七 二三面相覩幾處覓不見。帶累傍人。露柱掛燈籠新羅國裏曾 上堂東湧西沒。東行不見西行利。那裏得這消息來大唐國裏未打鼓 遲一刻。還我話頭來。先行不到。末後太過苦中樂教阿誰知　樂中苦兩重公案。使 誰舉。苦便苦樂便樂。那裏有兩頭三面來誰道黃金如糞土具眼者辨。試 拂試看。阿剌剌。可惜許。且道是古佛是露柱
text_en: two three, faces meeting face to face; In several places you search and cannot find it, implicating those beside you. A dew pillar hangs a lantern. In Silla it once ascended the hall; It surges in the east and sinks in the west. Going east you do not see the benefit of going west. Where do you get this news? In Great Tang the drum has not yet been struck. Delay one moment—give me back my topic. The first move does not arrive; the last is too much. Joy within bitterness, bitterness within joy— Who are you going to make know? A double-layered case—make who raise it? Bitter is bitter, joyful is joyful—where do two heads and three faces come from? Who says gold is like dirt and dung? Those with eyes discern it. Try to brush it and test it. A-la-la! What a pity. Now tell me—is it an ancient Buddha or a dew pillar?
South Mountain clouds, North Mountain rain—Xuedou buys a hat to match the head, watching the wind and setting the sails. On

text_zh: 南山雲北山雨。雪竇買帽相頭。看風使帆。向 劍刃上與爾下箇注脚。直得四七二三面相 覩。也莫錯會。此只頌古佛與露柱相交。是第 幾機了也。後面劈開路。打葛藤要見他意。新 羅國裏曾上堂。大唐國裏未打鼓。雪竇向電 轉星飛處便道。苦中樂樂中苦。雪竇似堆一 堆七珍八寶。在這裏了。所以末後有這一句 子。云。誰道黃金如糞土。此一句是禪月行路 難詩。雪竇引來用。禪月云。山高海深人不測。 古往今來轉青碧。淺近輕浮莫與交。地卑只 解生荊棘。誰道黃金如糞土。張耳陳餘斷消 息。行路難行路難。君自看。且莫土曠人稀。雲 居羅漢。
text_en: the sword’s edge he gives you a footnote, straight to four seven, two three, faces meeting face to face. Don’t misunderstand: this only praises that an ancient Buddha communes with a pillar—what numbered pivot it is. After that he splits open a road; he tangles vines to make you see the intent. In Silla it once ascended the hall; in Great Tang the drum has not yet been struck. Xuedou, at the place where lightning turns and stars fly, then says: Joy within bitterness, bitterness within joy. Xuedou seems to heap up a pile of seven treasures and eight jewels right here. Therefore at the end there is this line: Who says gold is like dirt and dung? This line comes from Chan Yue’s poem The Road is Hard and Xuedou borrows it. Chan Yue said: Mountains are high, seas are deep—people cannot be fathomed. From ancient times to now they turn blue-green. Don’t associate with the shallow and flighty. Low ground only knows how to grow thorns. Who says gold is like dirt and dung? Zhang Er and Chen Yu cut off and ended the news. The road is hard, the road is hard—see for yourself. Also, don’t say the land is vast and people are few. Yun Ju, the arhat.

text_zh: 垂示云。道是是無可是。言非非無可非。是非 已去。得失兩忘。淨裸裸赤灑灑。且道。面前背 後是箇什麼。或有箇衲僧出來道。面前是佛 殿三門。背後是寢堂方丈。且道。此人還具眼 也無。若辨得此人。許爾親見古人來。
text_en: have already gone; gain and loss are both forgotten. Clean and naked, bare and bright. Tell me: what is in front and what is behind? Perhaps a patched monk comes forward and says: In front is the Buddha hall and the three gates; behind is the sleeping hall and the abbot’s quarters. Tell me: does this person have eyes or not? If you can discern this person, I will allow you to personally meet the ancients.
Case 84. Raised: Vimalakirti asked Manjushri, what This fellow is far too much—he should make a ruckus once. He should shut his mouth.

text_zh: 【八四】舉。維摩詰問文殊師利這漢太殺合閙一場。合取口何等 是菩薩入不二法門知而故犯文殊曰。如我意者道什 麼。直得分疎不下。擔枷過狀。把髻投衙於一切法喚什麼作一切法無言無 說道什麼無示無識瞞別人即得離諸問答道什麼是為 入不二法門用入作什麼。用許多葛藤作什麼於是文殊師利 問維摩詰。我等各自說已。仁者當說。何等 是菩薩入不二法門這一靠莫道金粟如來。設使三世諸佛。也開口不得。 倒轉鎗頭來也。刺殺一人。中箭還似射人時雪竇云。維摩道什麼咄。萬 箭攢心。替他說道理復云。勘破了也非但當時。即今也恁麼。雪竇也是賊過後 張弓。雖然為眾竭力。爭奈禍出私門。且道雪竇還見得落處麼。夢也未夢見。說什麼勘破。嶮。金毛 獅子也摸索不著。
text_en: is a bodhisattva’s entry into the Dharma gate of nonduality? Manjushri said: As I see it, toward all dharmas there is no speech, no Knowing it and deliberately offending. Say what ? It comes to the point you cannot sort it out. Carry the cangue and confession; tie up your hair and surrender at the yamen. What do you call all dharmas? speaking, no pointing, no knowing; apart from all question and answer—this is Say what? If you fool others, it works. Say what? entry into the Dharma gate of nonduality. Then Manjushri What use is it to bring it in? What use is all these entangling vines? asked Vimalakirti: We have each spoken; you, sir, should speak—what is a bodhisattva’s entry into the Dharma gate of nonduality? Xuedou said: What did Vimalakirti say? And again: It has been seen through. With this one leaning, do not say even the Tathagata Golden Millet—suppose all Buddhas of the three times—none can open their mouths. Turning the spearhead around. Stab and kill one person—being hit by an arrow is still like when you shot someone. Bah! Ten thousand arrows crowd the heart—explaining doctrine for him. Not only then—right now it is also like this. Xuedou too is like drawing a bow after the thief has passed. Though he exhausts himself for the assembly, disaster comes out of a private gate. Tell me, has Xuedou ever seen where it lands? He has not even dreamed it—what talk of seeing through? Perilous! Golden-maned even a lion cannot grope it out.
Vimalakirti had the great bodhisattvas each speak of the Dharma gate of nonduality. At the time, thirty-

text_zh: 維摩詰令諸大菩薩各說不二法門。時三十 二菩薩。皆以二見有為無為真俗二諦。合為 一見。為不二法門。後問文殊。文殊云。如我意 者。於一切法。無言無說。無示無識。離諸問 答。是為入不二法門。蓋為三十二人以言遣 言。文殊以無言遣言。一時掃蕩總不要。是為 入不二法門。殊不知靈龜曳尾。拂迹成痕。又 如掃󰆠掃塵相似。塵雖去。󰆠迹猶存。末後依 前除蹤跡。於是文殊却問維摩詰云。我等各 自說已。仁者當自說。何等是菩薩入不二法 門。維摩詰默然。若是活漢。終不去死水裏浸 却。若作恁麼見解。似狂狗逐塊。雪竇亦不說 良久。亦不說默然據坐。只去急急處云。維摩 道什麼。只如雪竇恁麼道。還見維摩麼。夢 也未夢見在。維摩乃過去古佛。亦有眷屬。助 佛宣化。具不可思議辯才。有不可思議境界。 有不可思議神通妙用。於方丈室中。容三萬 二千獅子寶座。與八萬大眾。亦不寬狹。且道 是什麼道理。喚作神通妙用得麼。且莫錯會。 若是不二法門。雖同得同證方乃相共證知。 獨有文殊。可與酬對。雖然恁麼。還免得雪竇 檢責也無。雪竇恁麼道。也要與這二人相見 云。維摩道什麼。又云。勘破了也。爾且道是什 麼處。是勘破處。只這些子。不拘得失。不落是 非。如萬仞懸崖。向上捨得性命。跳得過去。許 爾親見維摩。如捨不得。大似群羊觸藩。雪竇 故然是捨得性命底人。所以頌出云。
text_en: two bodhisattvas all used dual views—conditioned and unconditioned, true and conventional, the two truths—combining them into one view, as the Dharma gate of nonduality. Then he asked Manjushri. Manjushri said: As I see it, toward all dharmas: no speech, no speaking; no pointing, no knowing; apart from all question and answer—this is entry into the Dharma gate of nonduality. The thirty-two people used words to drive out words; Manjushri used wordlessness to drive out words—sweeping everything away at once, wanting none of it. This is entry into the Dharma gate of nonduality. Yet he did not know: the spirit tortoise drags its tail; brushing away traces makes a mark. Also it is like sweeping away dust: though the dust is gone, the traces remain. In the end, in accordance with what came before, remove even the tracks. Thus Manjushri again asked Vimalakirti: We each have spoken; you, sir, should speak yourself—what is a bodhisattva’s entry into the Dharma gate of nonduality? Vimalakirti remained silent. If you are a living person, you will never go soak in dead water. If you make such an interpretation, it is like a mad dog chasing a clod. Xuedou also does not say after a long time; he also does not say, silently sitting there. He only goes to the urgent spot and says: Vimalakirti said what? Just as Xuedou says it like this—have you seen Vimalakirti? Not even in a dream have you seen him. Vimalakirti is an ancient Buddha of the past, and also has a retinue, assisting the Buddha in proclaiming the teaching. He possesses inconceivable eloquence and inconceivable states. He has inconceivable spiritual powers and wondrous functions. In the abbot’s room, he accommodated thirty thousand two thousand lion-thrones and eighty thousand in the great assembly—yet it was neither cramped nor spacious. Tell me: what principle is this? Can you call it spiritual powers and wondrous function? Don’t misunderstand. If it is the Dharma gate of nonduality, then only by attaining together and realizing together can you mutually confirm and know it. Only Manjushri can respond in kind. Even so, can he avoid Xuedou’s scrutiny and blame or not? When Xuedou speaks like this, he also wants you to meet these two people face to face, saying: What did Vimalakirti say? And again: It has been seen through. Tell me: what place is the place of seeing through? Just this much: not bound by gain and loss, not falling into right and wrong—like a sheer cliff of ten thousand fathoms. Upward, you must be able to cast away your life and leap across; then I permit you to personally meet Vimalakirti. If you cannot let go, it is like a flock of sheep butting into a fence. Xuedou indeed is a person who can cast away his life. Therefore he versifies:
Bah! This old Vimalakirti—so pitiful, Why scold him? In the morning strike three thousand, in the evening strike eight hundred—scolding is useless. Better give him thirty blows.

text_zh: 咄這維摩老咄他作什麼。朝打三千暮打八百。咄得不濟事。好與三十棒　悲 生空懊惱悲他作什麼。自有金剛王寶劍。為他閑事長無明。勞而無功臥疾 毘耶離因誰致得。帶累一切人全身太枯槁病則且置。為什麼口似匾擔。 飯也喫不得。喘也喘不得七佛祖師來客來須看。賊來須打。成群作隊。也須是作家 始得一室且頻掃猶有這箇在。元來在鬼窟裏作活計　請問不二門 若有可說。被他說了也。打云。和闍黎。也尋不見當時便靠倒蒼天蒼天。道什麼 不靠倒死中得活。猶有氣息在　金毛獅子無處討咄。還見麼。 蒼天蒼天
text_en: troubled by empty notions, Why pity him? There is already the Diamond King precious sword. For his idle affairs, ignorance grows long—labor with no achievement. lying sick, Vaiśālī Who brought it about? It drags down everyone. His whole body is utterly withered. Set the illness aside for now—why is the mouth like a shoulder pole? You cannot even eat, and you cannot even catch your breath. The patriarch of the Seven Buddhas arrives. When guests come, you must watch; when thieves come, you must strike. Forming crowds and squads—you must also be an adept. Only then will it do. In a single room, swept again and again—pray ask about the gate of nonduality. This is still here. It turns out he has been making a living in a ghost cave. If there is anything that can be spoken, he has already spoken it. Striking, he says: And, acarya—still you cannot find it. Right then he collapsed. Blue heaven, blue heaven—say what? If he does not collapse, there is nowhere to seek the golden-maned lion. Gaining life within death—there is still breath in it. Bah! Do you still see? Blue heaven, blue heaven!
Xuedou said, Bah, this old Vimalakīrti—why throw out a Bah right at the start?

text_zh: 雪竇道。咄這維摩老。頭上先下一咄作什麼。 以金剛王寶劍。當頭直截。須朝打三千暮打 八百始得。梵語云維摩詰。此云無垢稱。亦云 淨名。乃過去金粟如來也。不見僧問雲居簡 和尚。既是金粟如來。為什麼却於釋迦如來 會中聽法。簡云。他不爭人我。大解脫人不拘 成佛不成佛。若道他修行務成佛道。轉沒交 涉。譬如圓覺經云。以輪迴心。生輪迴見。入於 如來大寂滅海。終不能至。永嘉云。或是或 非人不識。逆行順行天莫測。若順行則趣佛 果位中。若逆行則入眾生境界。壽禪師道。直 饒爾磨鍊得到這田地。亦未可順汝意在。直 待證無漏聖身。始可逆行順行。所以雪竇道。 悲生空懊惱。維摩經云。為眾生有病故。我 亦有病。懊惱則悲絕也。臥疾毘耶離。維摩示 疾於毘耶離城也。唐時王玄策使西域過其 居。遂以手板縱橫量其室得十笏。因名方丈。 全身太枯槁。因以身疾。廣為說法云。是身無 常無強無力無堅。速朽之法。不可信也。為苦 為惱。眾病所集。乃至陰界入所共合成。七 佛祖師來。文殊是七佛祖師。承世尊旨往彼 問疾。一室且頻掃。方丈內皆除去所有。唯留 一榻等文殊至。請問不二法門也。所以雪竇 道。請問不二門。當時便靠倒。維摩口似匾檐。 如今禪和子便道。無語是靠倒。且莫錯認定 盤星。雪竇拶到萬仞懸崖上。却云不靠倒。一 手擡一手搦。他有這般手脚。直是用得玲瓏。 此頌前面拈云維摩道什麼。金毛獅子無處 討。非但當時。即今也恁麼。還見維摩老麼。盡 山河大地草木叢林。皆變作金毛獅子。也摸 索不著。
text_en: With the vajra-king jeweled sword, cut straight down on the head; you must strike three thousand in the morning and strike eight hundred in the evening before it will do. In Sanskrit he is called Vimalakīrti; here it means Spotless Renown; also called Pure Name. He is the past Golden-Grain Tathāgata. Did you not see a monk ask Yunju Jian, the master, Since he is the Golden-Grain Tathāgata, why does he nonetheless, in Śākyamuni Tathāgata’s assembly, listen to the Dharma? Jian said, He does not contend over self and others. A person of great liberation is not bound by becoming a Buddha or not becoming a Buddha. If you say his practice aims at attaining Buddhahood, that only makes it irrelevant. For example, the Perfect Enlightenment Sutra says: with a mind of rebirth, you give rise to views of rebirth; entering the Tathāgata’s great sea of quiescent extinction, in the end you cannot arrive. Yongjia said: whether it is or whether it is not, people do not recognize it. Inverting the course or going with it—heaven cannot fathom it. If you go with the course, you head toward the Buddha fruit and its rank; if you invert the course, you enter the realm of sentient beings. Chan Master Shou said, Even if you grind and temper yourself until you reach this ground, it still will not follow what you have in mind. Only once you realize the stainless, holy body may you invert or go with the course. Therefore Xuedou said, Compassion arises from emptiness, and affliction. The Vimalakīrti Sutra says: because sentient beings are sick, I too am sick. When there is affliction, compassion is cut off. Lying ill in Vaiśālī—Vimalakīrti displayed illness in the city of Vaiśālī. In the Tang, the envoy Wang Xuance passed by his dwelling and measured the room lengthwise and crosswise with a hand-board, finding it ten cubits; thus it was named the abbot’s quarters. His whole body was utterly withered. Because of bodily illness, he broadly preached the Dharma, saying: this body is impermanent, without strength, without power, without firmness; a law of quick decay, not to be trusted. It is suffering, it is vexation, a gathering of many illnesses, even to the point that it is formed from the aggregates, realms, and sense-fields combined. The Seven Buddhas’ patriarch arrives. Mañjuśrī is the patriarch of the Seven Buddhas; receiving the World-Honored One’s command, he went there to inquire after the illness. In a single room, swept again and again: inside the abbot’s quarters, everything was cleared away, leaving only one couch, waiting for Mañjuśrī to arrive—so as to ask about the Dharma gate of nonduality. Therefore Xuedou said, Pray ask about the gate of nonduality. Right then he collapsed. Vimalakīrti’s mouth was like a flat eave. Nowadays the Chan crowd then says, Having no words is collapsing. Do not mistake it and fix it as the Pole Star. Xuedou pressed them to the edge of a ten-thousand-fathom cliff, then said, He does not collapse. With one hand he lifts, with one hand he grips. He has such hands and feet—truly he uses them with perfect finesse. Before this verse he brought it up, saying, What did Vimalakīrti say? There is nowhere to seek the golden-maned lion. Not only then—right now it is also so. Do you still see the old Vimalakīrti? The whole mountains and rivers, the great earth, grasses and forests, all transform into golden-maned lions—yet you still cannot lay hold of it.
85 The instruction said: Grasp the world firmly and do not let a single hair leak; people throughout the whole earth lose their edge

text_zh: 垂示云。把定世界不漏纖毫。盡大地人亡鋒 結舌。是衲僧正令。頂門放光。照破四天下。是 衲僧金剛眼睛。點鐵成金。點金成鐵。忽擒忽 縱。是衲僧拄杖子。坐斷天下人舌頭。直得無 出氣處。倒退三千里。是衲僧氣宇。且道總不 恁麼時。畢竟是箇什麼人。試舉看。
text_en: and tie up their tongues—this is the patch-robed monk’s true command. Light shines from the crown of the head, illuminating the four worlds—this is the patch-robed monk’s vajra eyes. Touch iron and it becomes gold; touch gold and it becomes iron. Now seize, now let go—this is the patch-robed monk’s staff. Sitting, he cuts off the tongues of all under heaven, until there is no place to breathe out; retreating three thousand miles—this is the patch-robed monk’s bearing. Tell me, when it is not like this at all, what sort of person is it, after all? Try to bring it up and see.

text_zh: 【八五】舉。僧到桐峯庵主處便問。這裏忽逢大蟲 時。又作麼生作家弄影漢。草窠裏一箇半箇庵主便作虎聲 將錯就錯。却有牙爪。同生同死。承言須會宗僧便作怕勢兩箇弄泥團漢。見機而 作。似則也似。是則未是庵主呵呵大笑猶較些子。笑中有刀。亦能放亦 能收僧云。這老賊也須識破。敗也。兩箇都放行庵主云。爭 奈老僧何劈耳便掌。可惜放過。雪上加霜又一重僧休去恁麼休去。二 俱不了。蒼天蒼天雪竇云。是則是兩箇惡賊。只解掩 耳偷鈴言猶在耳。遭他雪竇點檢。且道當時合作麼生免得點檢。天下衲僧不到。
text_en: what then? The hermitage master immediately made a tiger’s roar. Shadow-playing fellows of the adepts—one or half a one in a grass nest. The monk at once struck a frightened pose. The hermitage master laughed loudly. The monk said, You old bandit! The hermitage master said, What Take error as error—yet there are teeth and claws. Live together, die together. If you take up words, you must understand the lineage. Two mud-ball fellows—seeing the opportunity and acting. It seems like it, indeed it seems; if you say it is, it is not. Still a bit off. In the smile there is a knife. It can also release and it can also gather in. You must also see through it. Ruined. Let both go through. can you do about this old monk? The monk left. Xuedou said, Yes, they are two evil bandits, who only know how to cover A slap right across the ear—what a pity to let it pass. Frost on top of snow, one more layer. Let it rest like this. The two both do not finish it. Blue heaven, blue heaven! their ears and steal the bell. The words are still in the ear, yet he is inspected by Xuedou. Tell me, what should have been done then to avoid inspection? Patch-robed monks of the world cannot reach it—
In the Great Hero’s lineage there appeared four hermitage masters: Damei, Baiyun, Huxi, and Tongfeng.

text_zh: 大雄宗派下。出四庵主。大梅白雲。虎溪桐峯。 看他兩人恁麼眼親手辨。且道誵訛在什麼 處。古人一機一境。一言一句。雖然出在臨時。 若是眼目周正。自然活鱍鱍地。雪竇拈教人 識邪正辨得失。雖然如此。在他達人分上。雖 處得失。却無得失。若以得失見他古人。則 沒交涉。如今人須是各各窮到無得失處。然 後以得失辨人。若一向去揀擇言句處用心。 又到幾時得了去。不見雲門大師道。行脚漢 莫只空遊州獵縣。只欲得提搦閑言語。待老 和尚口動。便問禪問道。向上向下。如何若 何。大卷抄將去。𡎺向肚皮裏卜度。到處火爐 邊。三箇五箇聚頭舉口。喃喃地便道。這箇是 公才語。這箇是就身打出語。這箇是事上道 底語。這箇是體裏語。體爾屋裏老爺老娘。噇 却飯了。只管說夢。便道我會佛法了也。將知 恁麼行脚。驢年得休歇去。古人暫時間拈弄。 豈有勝負得失是非等見。桐峯見臨濟。其時 在深山卓庵。這僧到彼中遂問。這裏忽逢大 蟲時又作麼生。峯便作虎聲。也好就事便行。 這僧也會將錯就錯。便作怕勢。庵主呵呵大 笑。僧云。這老賊。峯云。爭奈老僧何。是則是 二俱不了。千古之下遭人點檢。所以雪竇道。 是則是兩箇惡賊。只解掩耳偷鈴。他二人雖 皆是賊。當機却不用。所以掩耳偷鈴。此二老 如排百萬軍陣。却只鬪掃󰆠。若論此事。須是 殺人不眨眼底手脚。若一向縱而不擒。一向 殺而不活。不免遭人怪笑。雖然如是。他古 人亦無許多事。看他兩箇恁麼。總是見機而 作。五祖道。神通遊戲三昧。慧炬三昧。莊嚴王 三昧。自是後人脚跟不點地。只去點檢古人 便道。有得有失。有底道。分明是庵主落節。且 得沒交涉。雪竇道。他二人相見皆有放過處。 其僧道。這裏忽逢大蟲時又作麼生。峯便作 虎聲。此便是放過處。乃至道。爭奈老僧何。此 亦是放過處。著著落在第二機。雪竇道。要 用便用。如今人聞恁麼道。便道當時好與行 令。且莫盲枷瞎棒。只如德山入門便棒。臨濟 入門便喝。且道古人意如何。雪竇後面。便只 如此頌出。且道畢竟作麼生免得掩耳偷鈴 去。頌云。
text_en: Watch how those two, with their own eyes and hands, made the distinctions. Tell me, where is the error located? The ancients—one device, one situation; one word, one phrase—though it emerged on the spot, if your eyes are proper, it is naturally lively and nimble. Xuedou picked this up to teach people to recognize crooked and straight and to distinguish gain and loss. Even so, for one who has arrived, even though he deals in gain and loss, there is no gain and loss. If you look at the ancients through gain-and-loss, then it has nothing to do with it. People today must each press through to the place of no gain and loss, and then use gain and loss to assess others. If you always apply your mind to picking and choosing in phrases and sentences, when will you ever finish? Did you not see Great Master Yunmen say: Pilgrims do not merely wander idly through prefectures and counties. You only want to grab hold of idle talk, waiting for the old master’s mouth to move, then you ask about Chan and ask about the Way—upward, downward, how this and how that. You copy off big volumes and take them away, divining with them in your belly. Everywhere, by the furnace you gather in threes and fives, heads together, mouths going, mumbling and saying, This one is words of public talent; this one is words struck out from the body; this one is words spoken on the matter; this one is words of principle; this one is words from within the essence. Essence—your old man and old woman at home have eaten their meal; you just keep talking in dreams, then say, I understand the Buddha-Dharma now. You should know that traveling like this, you will rest only in the year of the donkey. The ancients would toy with it for a moment— how could there be views of victory and defeat, gain and loss, right and wrong? Tongfeng met Linji; at that time he was in the deep mountains at a hermitage. This monk went there and asked, When you suddenly meet a great beast here, what then? Feng made a tiger’s roar. Fine—he acted right on the matter. This monk also knew how to turn mistake into mistake, and struck a frightened pose. The hermitage master laughed loudly. The monk said, You old bandit! Feng said, What can you do about this old monk? Yes, yes— neither of the two understood. For a thousand ages they have been inspected by others. Therefore Xuedou said, Yes, they are two evil bandits, who only know how to cover their ears and steal the bell. Though those two are both bandits, when the moment came they did not use it; thus, covering the ears and stealing the bell. These two old fellows are like deploying an army of a million—yet they only fought with broom and dustpan. If you speak of this matter, you must have hands and feet that kill without blinking. If you only let go and never seize, if you only kill and never give life, you will inevitably be mocked. Even so, those ancients had no such excess. Look at those two as they are—altogether it is acting upon the opportunity, doing. The Fifth Patriarch said: the samādhi of supernormal play; the samādhi of the torch of wisdom; the samādhi of the Adornment King. It is simply that later people’s heels do not touch the ground; they only go inspecting the ancients and say, There is gain, there is loss. Some say, Clearly the hermitage master fell into a cadence. Even so, it has nothing to do with it. Xuedou said, When those two met, each had a place of letting go. The monk said, When you suddenly meet a great beast here, what then? Feng then made a tiger’s roar—this is precisely the letting-go. And then, What can you do about this old monk? This too is letting-go. Step after step, they fell into the second device. Xuedou said, If you want to use it, then use it. People today hear this and say, At the time it would have been good to carry out the command. Do not be a blind cangue and a blind stick. Consider Deshan—enter the gate and he strikes; Linji— enter the gate and he shouts. Tell me, what was the ancients’ intent? After this, Xuedou then just put forth the verse like this. Tell me, after all, how do you avoid covering your ears and stealing the bell and leaving it at that? The verse says:

text_zh: 見之不取。思之千里。正當嶮處都不能使。等 他道爭奈老僧何。好與本分草料。當時若下 得這手脚。他必須有後語。二人只解放不解 收。見之不取。早是白雲萬里。更說什麼思之 千里。好箇斑斑爪牙未備。是則是箇大蟲。也 解藏牙伏爪。爭奈不解咬人。君不見。大雄山 下忽相逢。落落聲光皆振地。百丈一日問黃 檗云。什麼處來。檗云。山下採菌子來。丈云。 還見大蟲麼。檗便作虎聲。丈於腰下取斧作 斫勢。檗約住便掌。丈至晚上堂云。大雄山下 有一虎。汝等諸人出入切須好看。老僧今日 親遭一口。後來溈山問仰山。黃檗虎話作麼 生。仰云。和尚尊意如何。溈山云。百丈當時合 一斧斫殺。因什麼到如此。仰山云。不然。溈山 云。子又作麼生。仰山云。不唯騎虎頭。亦解收 虎尾。溈山云。寂子甚有嶮崖之句。雪竇引用 明前面公案。聲光落落振於大地也。這箇些 子轉變自在。要句中有出身之路。大丈夫見 也無。還見麼。收虎尾兮捋虎鬚。也須是本分。 任爾收虎尾捋虎鬚。未免一時穿却鼻孔。
text_en: he says, What can you do about this old monk?—then give him his proper fodder. If at that time you could have put down these hands and feet, he would surely have had a follow-up. The two only know how to let go, not how to gather in. Seeing it, do not take it, already it is white clouds for ten thousand miles—what more is there to say about thinking of it A thousand li. What a fine dappled one—its claws and fangs not yet fully formed. It is, to be sure, a great beast, yet it knows how to hide its fangs and tuck its claws; but it cannot bite people. Have you not seen? Below Great Hero Mountain, they suddenly met—clear and ringing, the sound and brilliance shook the earth. One day Baizhang asked Huang- bo: Where have you come from? Huangbo said: From below the mountain, gathering mushrooms. Baizhang said: Did you see the great beast? Huangbo then made a tiger’s roar. Baizhang drew an axe from his waist and made a chopping gesture. Huangbo grabbed him and slapped him. That evening Baizhang ascended the hall and said: Below Great Hero Mountain there is a tiger. All of you, when going in and out, must watch carefully. Today this old monk personally took a bite. Later Weishan asked Yangshan: How about Huangbo’s tiger talk— how was it? Yangshan said: What is the master’s honored intent? Weishan said: Baizhang at the time should have chopped him dead with one axe. Why did it come to this? Yangshan said: Not so. Weishan said: Then what would you do? Yangshan said: Not only would I ride the tiger’s head, I would also know how to gather the tiger’s tail. Weishan said: Jizi has a phrase from a sheer cliff. Xuedou cites this to illuminate the earlier case: the sound and brilliance, clear and ringing, shook the earth. This little bit turns and changes with ease, wanting a way out within the phrase. Does a true man see it or not? Do you see it? Gathering the tiger’s tail, stroking the tiger’s whiskers—this too must be fundamental. Even if you gather the tiger’s tail and stroke the tiger’s whiskers, you still cannot avoid, for a moment, having your nose pierced through.

You yourself know it is off by half—still a bit off.

text_zh: 雲門室中垂語接人。爾等諸人脚跟下。各各 有一段光明。輝騰今古逈絕見知。雖然光明。 恰到問著又不會。豈不是暗昏昏地。二十年 垂示。都無人會他意。香林後來請代語。門云。 厨庫三門。又云。好事不如無。尋常代語只一 句。為什麼這裏却兩句。前頭一句為爾略開 一線路教爾見。若是箇漢。聊聞舉著剔起便 行。他怕人滯在此。又云。好事不如無。依前與 爾掃却。如今人纔聞舉著光明。便去瞠眼云。 那裏是厨庫。那裏是三門。且得沒交涉。所以 道。識取鉤頭意。莫認定盤星。此事不在眼上。 亦不在境上。須是絕知見忘得失。淨裸裸赤 灑灑。各各當人分上究取始得。雲門云。日裏 來往日裏辨人。忽然半夜無日月燈光。曾到 處則故是。未曾到處取一件物。還取得麼。參 同契云。當明中有暗。勿以暗相覩。當暗中有 明。勿以明相遇。若坐斷明暗。且道是箇什麼。 所以道。心花發明。照十方剎。盤山云。光非照 境。境亦非存。光境俱忘。復是何物。又云。即 此見聞非見聞。無餘聲色可呈君。箇中若了 全無事。體用何妨分不分。但會取末後一句 了。却去前頭游戲。畢竟不在裏頭作活計。古 人道。以無住本。立一切法。不得去這裏弄光 影弄精魂。又不得作無事會。古人道。寧可起 有見如須彌山。不可起無見如芥子許。二乘 人多偏墜此見。雪竇頌云。
text_en: has a stretch of brightness, blazing through past and present, far beyond seeing and knowing. Though there is brightness, when you are asked, you do not understand—how is that not dark and murky? For twenty years he held it up, and no one understood his intent. Later Xianglin asked for a substitute phrase. Yunmen said: The kitchen and storeroom, the three gates. And he said: Better to have no good thing. Usually a substitute phrase is just one line—why are there two lines here? The first line slightly opens a single thread of a path so you can see. If you are a real fellow, hearing it raised, you pick it up and go. He feared people would get stuck here, so he added: Better to have no good thing, and as before swept it away for you. People today, as soon as they hear brightness raised, stare their eyes wide and say: Where is the kitchen and storeroom? Where are the three gates? That is entirely irrelevant. Therefore it is said: Recognize the meaning at the hook’s tip; do not take the fixed star as certain. This matter is not in the eyes. Nor is it in objects. You must cut off views and forget gain and loss—clean, naked, bare and bright. Each person must investigate it on their own share. Yunmen said: In daylight you come and go, in daylight you recognize people. Suddenly at midnight there is no sun, moon, or lamplight—of the places you have been to, of course they are so; but from a place you have never been to, take one thing—can you take it? The Cantongqi says: Within brightness there is darkness; do not take darkness as what you see. Within darkness there is brightness; do not meet it by means of brightness. If you cut off brightness and darkness, tell me, what is it? Therefore it is said: the mind-flower blossoms in illumination, shining on the lands of the ten directions. Panshan said: Light is not what illuminates objects; objects are not what remain. When light and objects are both forgotten, what is it then? He also said: This seeing and hearing are not seeing and hearing; there are no remaining sounds or colors to present to you. If within this you understand, there is nothing at all. Essence and function—what harm is there in dividing or not dividing? Only grasp the very last line, then go back and play in the earlier parts; in the end you are not making your living inside them. The ancients said: Taking non-abiding as the root, one establishes all dharmas. You must not go here and toy with light and shadow, toy with spirit. Nor must you take it as an understanding of nothing-to-do. The ancients said: Better to raise a view of being as big as Mount Sumeru than to raise a view of non-being as small as a mustard seed. People of the two vehicles people often fall one-sidedly into this view. Xuedou's verse says:
Self-illumination sets out a solitary brightness, opening one The myriad phenomena: host and guest interpenetrate. Nostrils turn in a row. What is a blind fellow doing?

text_zh: 自照列孤明森羅萬象。賓主交參。列轉鼻孔。瞎漢作什麼　為君通一 線何止一線。十日並照。放一線道即得花謝樹無影打葛藤有什麼了期。向什麼 處摸索。黑漆桶裏盛黑汁看時誰不見瞎。不可總扶籬摸壁。兩瞎三瞎　見不 見兩頭俱坐斷。瞎倒騎牛兮入佛殿中。三門合掌。還我話頭來。打 云。向什麼處去也。雪竇也只向鬼窟裏作活計。還會麼。半夜日頭出。日午打三更
text_en: thread for you. More than a single thread: ten suns shine together. Release one thread of the way and it is obtained. The flowers fall; the trees have no shadow. What end is there to tangling vines? Toward what place are you groping? A black lacquer bucket holds black sap. When you look, who does not see? See, not Blind. You must not always cling to the fence and feel the wall—two blind, three blind. see. Both ends are cut off and sat dead. Blind Riding the ox backward, enter the Buddha hall. within blindness. At the three gates, palms together. Give me back my topic. Strike and say: Where are you going? Xuedou too only makes a living in a ghost cave—do you understand? At midnight the sun comes out; at noon, you strike the third watch.
Self-illumination sets out a solitary brightness. Beneath your own heels, there has always been this stretch of brightness.

text_zh: 自照列孤明。自家脚跟下。本有此一段光明。 只是尋常用得暗。所以雲門大師。與爾羅列 此光明。在爾面前。且作麼生是諸人光明。厨 庫三門。此是雲門列孤明處也。盤山道。心月 孤圓光吞萬像。這箇便是真常獨露。然後與 君通一線。亦怕人著在厨庫三門處。厨庫三 門則且從却。朝花亦謝樹亦無影。日又落月 又暗。盡乾坤大地。黑漫漫地。諸人還見麼。看 時誰不見。且道是誰不見。到這裏。當明中有 暗。暗中有明。皆如前後步自可見。雪竇道。見 不見。頌好事不如無。合見又不見。合明又不 明。倒騎牛兮入佛殿。入黑漆桶裏去也。須是 爾自騎牛入佛殿。看道是箇什麼道理。
text_en: It is only that in ordinary use it becomes dark. Therefore Master Yunmen set out this brightness right in front of you. Now what is all of your brightness? The kitchen and storeroom, the three gates—this is where Yunmen sets out the solitary brightness. Panshan said: The mind-moon, solitary and round, its light swallows ten thousand forms. This is true constancy uniquely revealed. Then it opens one thread for you. He also feared people would stick to the kitchen and storeroom, the three gates. So the kitchen and storeroom, the three gates—set them aside for now. Morning flowers fall and trees have no shadow; the sun sets and the moon grows dark. All of heaven and earth, the great land, is pitch-black. Do you still see? When you look, who does not see? Tell me, who is it that does not see? When you get here, within brightness there is darkness; within darkness there is brightness—each can be seen by the earlier and later steps. Xuedou said: See, not see—he chanted Better to have no good thing. It should be seen, yet not seen; it should be bright, yet not bright. Riding the ox backward, enter the Buddha hall—go into a black lacquer bucket. You must yourself ride the ox into the Buddha hall and see what kind of principle it is.
87 The pointer said: A clear-eyed fellow has no ruts. Sometimes, atop a lone peak, grass is wild

text_zh: 垂示云。明眼漢沒窠臼。有時孤峯頂上草漫 漫。有時鬧市裏頭赤灑灑。忽若忿怒那吒。現 三頭六臂。忽若日面月面。放普攝慈光。於一 塵現一切身。為隨類人。和泥合水。忽若撥 著向上竅。佛眼也覻不著。設使千聖出頭來。 也須倒退三千里。還有同得同證者麼。試舉 看。
text_en: and sprawling; sometimes, in the busy marketplace, bare and bright. Suddenly like wrathful Nata, manifesting three heads and six arms; suddenly like Sun-Face and Moon-Face, releasing universally embracing compassionate light. Within a single speck of dust, manifest all bodies. To suit the type of person, mixing mud and blending water. Suddenly, if it is tapped into the upward aperture, even the Buddha-eye cannot spy it. Even if a thousand sages came forth, they would have to retreat three thousand li. Is there anyone who attains the same and verifies the same? Try raising it and see.
Case 87. Yunmen instructed the assembly, saying: Medicine and illness cure each other; throughout the great earth A single united form cannot be obtained.

text_zh: 【八七】舉。雲門示眾云。藥病相治一合相不可得盡大地 是藥苦瓠連根苦。擺向一邊那箇是自己甜瓜徹蔕甜。那裏得這消息來 治澄之切。攻理也。音持。
text_en: is medicine—what is the self Bitter gourd, bitter to the root—set it off to one side. Sweet melon, sweet through the stem—where do you get this news? that is cured? Cheng's note: qie. It means to attack the principle. Pronounced chi.
Yunmen said: Medicine and illness cure each other; throughout the great earth is medicine—what is the self?

text_zh: 雲門道。藥病相治。盡大地是藥那箇是自己。 諸人還有出身處麼。二六時中。管取壁立千 仞。德山棒如雨點。臨濟喝似雷奔。則且致。釋 迦自釋迦。彌勒自彌勒。未知落處者。往往 喚作藥病相投會去。世尊四十九年。三百餘 會。應機設教。皆是應病與藥。如將蜜果換苦 葫蘆相似。既淘汝諸人業根。令灑灑落落。盡 大地是藥。爾向什麼處插嘴。若插得嘴。許 爾有轉身吐氣處。便親見雲門。爾若回顧躊 躇。管取插嘴不得。雲門在爾脚跟底。藥病相 治。也只是尋常語論。爾若著有。與爾說無。爾 若著無。與爾說有。爾若著不有不無。與爾去 糞掃堆上。現丈六金身。頭出頭沒。只如今盡 大地森羅萬象乃至自己。一時是藥。當恁麼 時。却喚那箇是自己。爾一向喚作藥。彌勒佛 下生。也未夢見雲門在。畢竟如何。識取鉤頭 意。莫認定盤星。文殊一日。令善財去採藥云。 不是藥者採將來。善財遍採。無不是藥。却來 白云。無不是藥者。文殊云。是藥者採將來。善 財乃拈一枝草。度與文殊。文殊提起示眾云。 此藥亦能殺人。亦能活人。此藥病相治話。最 難看。雲門室中尋常用接人。金鵝長老。一 日訪雪竇。他是箇作家。乃臨濟下尊宿。與雪 竇論此藥病相治話。一夜至天光。方能盡善。 到這裏。學解思量計較。總使不著。雪竇後有 頌送他道。藥病相治見最難。萬重關鎖太無 端。金鵝道者來相訪。學海波瀾一夜乾。雪竇 後面頌得最有工夫。他意亦在賓亦在主。自 可見也。頌云。
text_en: Do you people still have a way out? In the twelve hours of day and night, you will surely be like a sheer wall a thousand fathoms high. Deshan’s staff is like raindrops; Linji’s shout is like rushing thunder—set those aside. Shakya is Shakya; Maitreya is Maitreya. Those who do not know where it lands often take it as an understanding of medicine and illness fitting together. For forty-nine years, the World-Honored One, in more than three hundred assemblies, set up teachings in response to capacities—all are medicine given in response to illness, like trading honeyed fruit for a bitter gourd. Having washed out the roots of your karmic habits, making you open and unbound, all the great earth is medicine—where will you stick in your mouth? If you can stick in your mouth, then I allow you a place to turn around and breathe out; then you personally see Yunmen. If you look back and hesitate, you will surely be unable to stick in your mouth. Yunmen is right beneath your heels. Medicine and illness curing each other is also just ordinary talk. If you cling to being, I tell you non-being. If you cling to non-being, I tell you being. If you cling to neither being nor non-being, I take you to a dung-and-sweepings heap and manifest a sixteen-foot golden body—head appearing, head disappearing. Right now, all the great earth’s dense array of myriad forms, up to and including yourself, are at once medicine. At such a time, what do you call the self? If you only keep calling it medicine, even if Maitreya Buddha descends, you still have not even dreamed of Yunmen being here. Ultimately, how is it? Recognize the meaning at the hook’s tip; do not take the fixed star as certain. One day Manjushri told Sudhana to gather medicine, saying: Gather what is not medicine and bring it back. Sudhana gathered everywhere—there was nothing that was not medicine. He came back and reported: There is nothing that is not medicine. Manjushri said: Gather what is medicine and bring it back. Sudhana then picked up a blade of grass and handed it to Manjushri. Manjushri lifted it up and showed the assembly, saying: This medicine can also kill people; it can also bring people to life. This talk of medicine and illness curing each other is the most difficult to see. Yunmen ordinarily used it to receive people in his room. Elder Jine arrived one day to visit Xuedou. He was a master hand, a venerable elder under Linji’s line, and with Xue- Xuedou discussed this talk of medicine and illness curing each other all night until daybreak, and only then could it be fully perfected. When you reach here, learned understanding, thinking, and calculating are of no use at all. Later Xuedou sent him off with a verse, saying: To see medicine and illness curing each other is hardest; ten thousand layered barriers and locks are far too boundless. The golden-goose man of the Way comes to visit; in one night the waves of the sea of learning dry up. Xuedou in the later part of his verse shows the most workmanship. His intent is in the guest and also in the host; it can be seen for yourself. The verse says:
The whole great earth is medicine, how terribly wrong from ancient times to now. Who can discern it? Scattering sand and dirt, setting it up on a high rack. In the words

text_zh: 盡大地是藥教誰辨的。撒沙撒土。架高處著　古今何太錯言中 有響。一筆句下。咄閉門不造車大小雪竇為眾竭力。禍出私門。坦蕩不掛一絲 毫。阿誰有閑工夫。向鬼窟裏作活計通途自寥廓脚下便入草。上馬見路。信 手拈來。不妨奇特錯錯雙劍倚空飛。一箭落雙雕　鼻孔遼天亦穿却 頭落也。打云。穿却了也
text_en: there is an echo. In a single stroke, under the line—bah! With the door shut, do not build a cart. Big and small, Xuedou strains himself for the crowd; calamity comes from the private gate. Open and level, not hanging by a single hair—who has spare time to make a living in a ghost den? The open road is naturally vast and wide. With one step you enter the weeds; mount the horse and you see the road. Freely, you pick it up at hand—it is fine to be strange. Wrong, wrong, even nostrils reaching the sky are pierced through. Twin swords fly leaning on empty space; one arrow brings down two hawks. The head drops. He struck and said: It has pierced through.
The whole great earth is medicine, how terribly wrong from ancient times to now. If you call it an understanding of medicine, then

text_zh: 盡大地是藥。古今何太錯。爾若喚作藥會。自 古自今。一時錯了也。雪竇云。有般漢不解截 斷太梅脚跟。只管道貪程太速。他解截雲門 脚跟。為雲門這一句惑亂天下人。雲門云。拄 杖子是浪。許爾七縱八橫。盡大地是浪。看爾 頭出頭沒。閉門不造車。通途自寥廓。雪竇道。 為爾通一線路。爾若閉門造車。出門合轍。濟 箇甚事。我這裏閉門也不造車。出門自然寥 廓。他這裏略露些子縫罅。教人見。又連忙却 道。錯錯。前頭也錯。後頭也錯。誰知雪竇開一 線路。也是錯。既然鼻孔遼天。為什麼也穿却。 要會麼。且參三十年。爾有拄杖子。我與爾拄 杖子。爾若無拄杖子。不免被人穿却鼻孔。
text_en: from of old until now, in one stroke it is all mistaken. Xuedou said: There are fellows who do not know how to cut off Taimei at the heels, and only keep saying he was too greedy and hurried. He knows how to cut off Yunmen at the heels, because Yunmen’s one line confuses people under heaven. Yunmen said: The staff is a wave. I allow you seven lunges and eight crosses. The whole great earth is a wave. Watch you bobbing up and down. With the door shut, do not build a cart; the open road is naturally vast and wide. Xuedou said: I have opened a single thread of a road for you. If you build a cart behind closed doors and when you go out it fits the ruts, what does that accomplish? Here I also shut the door and do not build a cart; when I go out, it is naturally vast and wide. Here he slightly reveals a seam and gap for people to see, and then he hurriedly says: Wrong, wrong. The front is also wrong, the back is also wrong. Who would know that when Xuedou opens a thread of a road, that too is wrong? Since the nostrils reach the sky, why are they also pierced through? Want to understand? Then investigate for thirty years. If you have a staff, I will give you a staff. If you have no staff, you cannot avoid having your nostrils pierced through by others.

text_zh: 垂示云。門庭施設。且恁麼。破二作三。入理深 談。也須是七穿八穴。當機敲點。擊碎金鎖玄 關。據令而行。直得掃蹤滅跡。且道誵訛在什 麼處。具頂門眼者。請試舉看。
text_en: and you still must have seven piercings and eight holes. Striking and pointing in response to the situation, you smash the dark gate of golden locks. Acting in accord with the command, you sweep away tracks and erase traces. Tell me, where is the distortion? Those who have the eye at the crown of the head, please try bringing it up and see.
Case 88. Xuansha instructed the assembly, saying: The old worthies in all quarters all speak of meeting beings and benefiting

text_zh: 【八八】舉。玄沙示眾云。諸方老宿。盡道接物利 生隨分開箇鋪席。隨家豐儉忽遇三種病人來。作麼生接 打草只要蛇驚。山僧直得目瞪口呿。管取倒退三千里患盲者。拈鎚竪拂。 他又不見端的瞎。是則接物利生。未必不見在患聾者。語言三 昧。他又不聞端的聾。是則接物利生。未必聾在。是那箇未聞在患啞者 教伊說。又說不得端的啞。是則接物利生。未必啞在。是那箇未說在且 作麼生接。若接此人不得。佛法無靈驗誠哉 是言。山僧拱手歸降。已接了也。便打僧請益雲門也要諸方共知。著雲 門云。汝禮拜著風行草偃。咄僧禮拜起這僧拗折拄杖子也雲 門以拄杖挃。僧退後。門云。汝不是患盲 端的瞎。莫道這僧患盲好復喚近前來。僧近前第二杓惡水澆。觀音來 也。當時好與一喝門云。汝不是患聾端的聾。莫道這僧患聾好門乃 云。還會麼何不與本分草料。當時好莫作聲僧云。不會兩重公案。蒼 天蒼天門云。汝不是患啞端的啞。口吧吧地。莫道這僧啞好僧 於此有省賊過後張弓。討什麼碗　瞪持陵切。怒目直視也　呿去伽切。 張口貌　挃陟栗切。音窒撞空也。
text_en: life. Suddenly, if three kinds of sick people come, how do you receive them? Spread the mat according to your share; each household with its own plenty or thrift. If one is blind, you lift the hammer and raise the whisk; Beating the grass only aims to startle the snake. This mountain monk is left staring, mouth agape—surely you will retreat three thousand miles. but he does not see. If one is deaf, you use the speech samadhi, Truly blind. If so, in meeting beings and benefiting life, it is not that he necessarily does not see. but he does not hear. If one is mute, Truly deaf. If so, in meeting beings and benefiting life, it is not that he is necessarily deaf—what is it that has not been heard? you tell him to speak, but he cannot speak. So Truly mute. If so, in meeting beings and benefiting life, it is not that he is necessarily mute—what is it that has not been spoken? how do you receive them? If you cannot receive such people, the Buddha-dharma has no efficacy. A monk asked Yunmen for instruction, and Yun- Indeed! Those words are true. This mountain monk folds his hands and surrenders—already received. Then strike. And you must let all quarters know. Hit. men said: You, bow. The monk bowed. He called him close again. The monk came near. Yunmen said: You are not deaf. Yunmen then Truly blind. Don’t say this monk’s blindness is good. The second ladle pours foul water. Guanyin arrives too. At that time, he deserved a shout. Truly deaf. Don’t say this monk’s deafness is good. said: Do you understand? The monk said: I do not understand. Yunmen said: You are not mute. The monk Why not give him his proper fodder? At that time, best not to make a sound. A double-layered public case. Blue heaven, blue heaven! Truly mute. His mouth gapes and babbles—don’t say this monk’s muteness is good. from this had an insight. Stare. Gape. Strike. Drawing the bow after the thief has passed—what bowl are you begging for? Xuansha studied until feelings, dust, and thoughts were cut off, reaching a place utterly naked and completely bare.

text_en: Only then could he speak like this. At that time, monasteries in all quarters faced one another; in ordinary instruction to the assembly he would say: The old worthies in all quarters all speak of meeting beings and benefiting life. Suddenly, if three kinds of sick people come, how do you receive them? If one is blind, you lift the hammer and raise the whisk, but he does not see. If one is deaf, you use the speech samadhi, but he does not hear. If one is mute, you tell him to speak, but he cannot speak. So how do you receive them? If you cannot receive such people, the Buddha-dharma has no efficacy. If people nowadays take it as blind, deaf, mute understanding, in the end they cannot find it at all. Therefore it is said: Do not die inside the lines; you must understand Xuansha’s intent for it to work. Xuansha often used these words to meet people. There was a monk who had long been with Xuansha. One day in the hall, the monk asked the master: Regarding the talk of the three kinds of sick people, do you still allow a student to speak doctrine or not? Xuansha said: I allow it. The monk then said farewell and went down. Xuansha said: No, no. This monk had understood Xuansha’s intent. Later Fayan said: I heard Dizang the master cite this monk’s words, and only then did I understand the talk of the three kinds of sick people. If you say this monk did not understand, then why did Fayan speak like that? If you say he understood, then why did Xuansha say no, no? One day Di- zang said: I have heard that the master has talk of the three kinds of sick people, is that so? Xuansha said: It is. Dizang said: Guichen now has eyes, ears, nose, and tongue. How do you receive him? Xuansha then stopped. If you understand Xuansha’s intent, how could it be in words and phrases? What he understood is naturally distinct. Later a monk brought it up to Yunmen, and Yunmen immediately understood his intent and said: You, bow. The monk bowed and rose. Yunmen struck with his staff. This monk stepped back. Yunmen said: You are not blind. He called him close again. The monk came near. Yunmen said: You are not deaf. Then he said: Do you understand? The monk said: I do not understand. Yunmen said: You are not mute. From this the monk had an insight. If at that time he had been a real man, the moment Yunmen said bow, he would have flipped over the meditation bench. How could you see so much vine and creeper? Tell me, where Yunmen and Xuansha understood, is it the same or different? Where those two understood is all just the same. Look at the ancients coming forth, making a thousand and ten thousand kinds of expedient means; the intent is on the hook point. How many bitter words, only to make everyone each clearly understand this one matter. The old master of the Fifth Patriarch said: One person can speak it, yet does not understand; one person understands, yet cannot speak it. If the two come to study, how do you discern them? If you cannot discern these two, then you can be sure you cannot remove others’ sticking and undo their binding. If you can discern them, only then do you see entry. I will put on straw sandals and walk through your belly several times, and still you will not awaken. Why go out begging for a bowl? Just do not take it as blind, deaf, mute understanding. If you calculate like that, therefore it is said: Eyes seeing forms are like the blind, and so on; ears hearing sounds are like the deaf, and so on. It also says: With eyes full you do not see forms; with ears full you do not hear sounds. Manjushri constantly meets what the eyes touch; Guanyin blocks the ear faculty. When you reach here, eyes seeing is like the blind, ears hearing is like the deaf; only then can you be not far from Xuansha’s intent. Do you all recognize where the blind, deaf, mute fellow lands? Look at Xuedou’s verse:
Blind, deaf, mute, cut off from all timing and appropriateness. Already before words. The three apertures are all clear—already made into a complete piece. Where will you grope for it?

text_zh: 盲聾瘖啞杳絕機宜。盡爾見與不見聞與不 聞說與不說。雪竇一時與爾掃却了也。直得 盲聾瘖啞見解。機宜計較。一時杳絕。總用不 著。這箇向上事。可謂真盲真聾真啞。無機 無宜。天上天下堪笑堪悲。雪竇一手擡一手 搦。且道笑箇什麼悲箇什麼。堪笑是啞却不 啞。是聾却不聾。堪悲明明不盲却盲。明明不 聾却聾。離婁不辨正色。不能辨青黃赤白。正 是瞎。離婁黃帝時人。百步外能見秋毫之末。 其目甚明。黃帝游於赤水沈珠。令離朱尋之 不見。令喫詬尋之亦不得。後令象罔尋之方 獲之。故云。象罔到時光燦爛。離婁行處浪 滔天。這箇高處一著。直是離婁之目亦辨他 正色不得。師曠豈識玄絲。周時絳州晉景公 之子。師曠字子野一云。晉平公之樂太師也善別五音六 律。隔山聞蟻鬪。時晉與楚爭󰊉。師曠唯鼓琴。 撥動風絃。知戰楚必無功。雖然如是。雪竇道。 他尚未識玄絲在。不聾却是聾底人。這箇高 處玄音。直是師曠亦識不得。雪竇道。我亦不 作離婁。亦不作師曠。爭如獨坐虛窓下。葉落 花開自有時。若到此境界。雖然見似不見。聞 似不聞。說似不說。飢即喫飯。困即打眠。任他 葉落花開。葉落時是秋。花開時是春。各各 自有時節。雪竇與爾一時掃蕩了也。又放一 線道云。還會也無。雪竇力盡神疲。只道得箇 無孔鐵鎚。這一句急著眼看方見。若擬議又 蹉過。師舉拂子云。還見麼。遂敲禪床一下云。 還聞麼。下禪床云。還說得麼。
text_en: hearing, speaking and not speaking, Xuedou sweeps away for you at once. Until blind-deaf-mute understandings, timing and appropriateness calculations, are all at once cut off and gone. None of it is of any use. This upward matter can be called true blind, true deaf, true mute, with no timing and no appropriateness. In heaven above and below heaven, fit to laugh, fit to grieve. Xuedou lifts one hand and grips with one hand. Tell me, what are you laughing at, what are you grieving over? Fit to laugh: mute yet not mute; deaf yet not deaf. Fit to grieve: clearly not blind yet blind; clearly not deaf yet deaf. Li Lou cannot distinguish true colors; he cannot distinguish blue, yellow, red, and white; that is truly blind. Li Lou was a man of the Yellow Emperor’s time; from a hundred paces away he could see the tip of an autumn hair. His eyes were extremely clear. When the Yellow Emperor roamed at the Red Water and sank a pearl, he ordered Li Zhu to search for it but he could not find it; he ordered Chi Gou to search and also could not obtain it. Later he ordered Xiangwang to search, and only then did he get it. Therefore it is said: When Xiangwang arrives, the light is dazzling; where Li Lou walks, the waves billow to the sky. At this one move from the heights, even Li Lou’s eyes cannot distinguish true colors. How could Shi Kuang recognize the mysterious strings? In the Zhou era, in Jiangzhou, Duke Jing of Jin son. Shi Kuang, styled Ziye, was skilled at distinguishing the five tones and the six One says: It was Jin Pinggong’s music master. pitch-pipes. He could hear ants fighting across a mountain. When Jin and Chu were at war, Shi Kuang only played the zither. Plucking the wind-strings, he knew that fighting Chu would surely achieve nothing. Even so, Xuedou said, he still had not recognized where the mysterious string is. Not deaf, yet he is a deaf person. This lofty mysterious sound at this place: even Shi Kuang could not recognize it. Xuedou said: I also do not play Li Lou, and I also do not play Shi Kuang. Better to sit alone beneath an empty window; leaves fall and flowers bloom each in their own time. If you reach this realm, though you see it is as if not seeing, though you hear it is as if not hearing, though you speak it is as if not speaking. Hungry, you eat; tired, you sleep. Let it be leaves fall and flowers bloom: when leaves fall, it is autumn; when flowers bloom, it is spring. Each and every thing has its own season. Xuedou has, in one stroke, swept it all clean for you. And again he let one thread of the Way loose, saying: do you understand or not? Xuedou is spent and weary, and can only say a holeless iron hammer. You must look with urgent eyes to see this line; if you form an idea, you miss it. The master raised his whisk and said: do you see? Then he struck the Zen bench once and said, do you hear? He stepped down from the Zen bench and said: can you speak it?

text_zh: 垂示云。通身是眼見不到。通身是耳聞不及。 通身是口說不著。通身是心鑒不出。通身即 且止。忽若無眼作麼生見。無耳作麼生聞。無 口作麼生說。無心作麼生鑒。若向箇裏撥轉 得一線道。便與古佛同參。參則且止。且道參 箇什麼人。
text_en: Your whole body is mouth, yet you cannot speak it; your whole body is mind, yet you cannot illuminate it. Whole body, for now set it aside. Suddenly, if there were no eyes, how would you see? If there were no ears, how would you hear? If there were no mouth, how would you speak? If there were no mind, how would you illuminate? If right here you can flip a single thread of the Way, then you participate together with the ancient buddhas. Participation aside for now, tell me: you participate with what person?

text_en: shan produced the Caodong school. There were three whose Dharma and Way flourished: from Yunyan came Dong- shan; from Daowu came Shishuang; from Chuanzhi came Jiashan. The Great Compassion Bodhisattva has eighty- four thousand mudra arms. Great Compassion has so many hands and eyes; do you all have them or not? Baizhang said: all language and writing all, by winding turns, return to oneself. Yunyan often followed Daowu to consult, inquire, and decide. One day he asked him, saying: what does the Great Compassion Bodhisattva use so many hands and eyes for? At the start it would have been good to split his back with a staff right then, sparing us from seeing so many entangling vines afterward. Daowu was compassionate and could not do that, so he explained the principle to him instead, intending to make him understand right away. So he said: like a person in the middle of the night, reaching back with the hand to feel for a pillow. In the deep of night with no lamplight, you reach with your hand to feel for the pillow; tell me, where are the eyes? Yunyan then said: I understand. Daowu said: how do you understand? Yunyan said: the whole body is hands and eyes. Daowu said: you have said far too much; you only said eighty percent. Yunyan said: then you, elder brother, how do you say it? Daowu said: the entire body is hands and eyes. Tell me: is whole body it, or is entire body it? Though it seems like rotten mud, it is clean and free. People nowadays mostly go and make sentimental interpretations, saying: whole body is not it, entire body is it. They keep chewing on the ancients' words and phrases, and die beneath the ancients' words. They do not realize that the ancients' meaning is not in words and phrases. All of this was used only because matters left no choice. People now add footnotes and set up rules, saying: if you penetrate this koan, then you can stop investigating and understanding. They use the hand to feel the whole body, feel the lantern and the exposed pillar, and make it all into an understanding of entire-body talk. If you understand like that, you ruin the ancients quite a lot. Therefore it is said: they investigate living phrases, not dead phrases. You must cut off emotional dust and imagining; clean, naked, bare, and open. Only then can you see the Great Compassion saying. Haven't you seen Caoshan ask a monk: responding to things and manifesting form like the moon in water, how is it? The monk said: like a donkey looking into a well. Caoshan said: you have said it to death, you only said eighty percent. The monk said: then how do you, master? Caoshan said: like a well looking at a donkey. It is the same meaning. If you go to see it in the words, you will never escape the traps of Daowu and Yunyan. Xuedou, a seasoned hand, does not die under the phrases either; he goes straight over your head. The verse says:
Whole body is, entire body is; pick it up Four limbs, eight joints—this is not the ultimate standard of a patch-robed monk. On the crown of the head there is half a side—still in the den. Blind.

text_en: the hand to feel the body is it, then with such a view you do business entirely in a ghost cave. In the end, whole body and entire body are both not it. If you want to use feelings and cognition to see the Great Compassion saying, it is truly still a hundred thousand miles off. Xuedou worked up one living phrase: pick it up and it is still a hundred thousand miles off. The later lines verse Yunyan and Daowu's marvelous place, saying: spreading its wings, the roc soars through the six directions, clouds; beating the wind, drumming up the waters of the four seas. The great roc swallows dragons, and with its wings beats wind and drums waves; the water opens three thousand miles, and then it takes the dragons and swallows them. Xuedou said: if your great roc can beat the wind and drum the waves, it is indeed too heroic. But if you look at it with Great Compassion's thousand hands and eyes, it is only like a bit of dust suddenly arising, and also like a tiny hairbreadth of wind that has not yet stopped. Xuedou said: if you use the hand feeling the body as hands and eyes, what use can it possibly be? As for the Great Compassion saying, you are simply not there. Therefore it says: what dust and grime is this, suddenly arising; that tiny hairbreadth that has not yet stopped. Xuedou, calling himself a seasoned hand, in one stroke wiped away the traces. Yet afterward he still leaks and hints, speaking a metaphor; as before it is still inside the trap. Do you not see: the net-pearls hang down as a model, reflections layered upon layers. Xuedou brings up Indra's net bright pearls to serve as a model. Tell me: hands and eyes fall where? In the Huayan school they establish four dharma realms: first, the realm of principle, clarifying that it is one flavor of equality; second, the realm of phenomena, clarifying that the whole principle becomes phenomena; third, the realm of nonobstruction between principle and phenomena, clarifying that principle and phenomena interpenetrate, with no obstruction of large and small; fourth, the realm of nonobstruction among phenomena, clarifying that one phenomenon pervades all phenomena, and all phenomena wholly contain all phenomena, mutually interpenetrating at the same time without obstruction. Therefore it is said: as soon as one speck is raised, the whole earth is gathered in; each and every speck contains boundless dharma realms. Since one speck is like this, all specks are likewise. The net-pearls are before the Hall of Good Dharma of the Heavenly Lord Shakra. He uses mani jewels as a net: within a single jewel appear hundreds and thousands of jewels, and the hundreds and thousands of jewels all appear within one jewel, mutually reflecting in layers, host and companion without end. This is used to clarify the realm of nonobstruction among phenomena. In the past, National Teacher Xianshou set it up as the mirror-and-lamp metaphor: arrange ten mirrors in a circle with a lamp in the middle. If you look at the eastern mirror, then in the nine mirrors the mirrors and lamp appear distinctly all at once; if you look at the southern mirror, each mirror is likewise. Therefore the World-Honored One, when he first attained perfect awakening, without leaving the bodhi site, universally ascended among the Trayastrimsa heavens, and even to all places, in seven locations and nine assemblies, taught the Avatamsaka Sutra. Xuedou uses Indra's net pearls to point out the realm of nonobstruction among phenomena. Yet the meaning of the six aspects is very clear: namely whole and parts, namely sameness and difference, namely formation and destruction. Raise one aspect, and all six are included. But sentient beings use it every day and do not know it. Xuedou picks up Indra's net bright pearls as a model; how much more this Great Compassion saying is exactly like this. If you If you can truly, within this jeweled net, make clear the staff—its miraculous powers and wondrous function—going in and out without obstruction, only then can you see the hands and eyes. Therefore Xuedou said: on the end of the staff, where do hands and eyes arise? He has you take verification at the staff’s end and take it up under the shout. Just like Deshan—enter the gate and he strikes. Tell me, where are the hands and eyes? Linji—enter the gate and he shouts. Tell me, where are the hands and eyes? And tell me, at the end, why did Xuedou still add that tut as something to investigate?

The crooked cannot hide the straight. Frost on top of snow—another layer. Retreat three thousand miles—what do you want to use it for? Zhimen said, A rabbit carries a fetus. Steep. text_zh: 智門道。蚌含明月兔子。懷胎。都用中秋意。雖 然如此。古人意却不在蚌兔上。他是雲門會 下尊宿。一句語須具三句。所謂函蓋乾坤句。 截斷眾流句。隨波逐浪句。亦不消安排。自然 恰好。便去嶮處。答這僧話。略露些子鋒鋩。不 妨奇特。雖然恁麼。他古人終不去弄光影。只 與爾指些路頭教人見。這僧問。如何是般若 體。智門云。蚌含明月。漢江出蚌。蚌中有明 珠。到中秋月出。蚌於水面浮。開口含月光。感 而產珠。合浦珠是也。若中秋有月則珠多。無 月則珠少。如何是般若用。門云。兔子懷胎。此 意亦無異。兔屬陰。中秋月生。開口吞其光。便 乃懷胎。口中產兒。亦是有月則多。無月則少。 他古人答處。無許多事。他只借其意。而答般 若光也。雖然恁麼。他意不在言句上。自是 後人。去言句上作活計。不見盤山道。心月孤 圓光吞萬象。光非照境境亦非存。光境俱亡 復是何物。如今人但瞠眼喚作光。只去情上 生解。空裏釘橛。古人道。汝等諸人。六根門頭 晝夜放大光明。照破山河大地。不只止眼根 放光。鼻舌身意亦皆放光也。到這裏直須打 疊六根下無一星事。淨裸裸赤灑灑地。方見 此話落處。雪竇正恁麼頌出。
text_en: so, the ancients’ intent is not on clam and rabbit. He was a venerable elder in Yunmen’s assembly; in one phrase he must have three phrases: the phrase that encloses and covers heaven and earth, the phrase that cuts off all streams, and the phrase that goes along with waves and follows the current. There is no need to arrange them; naturally it is just right. He went straight to the steep place to answer this monk, slightly revealing a bit of edge. It is indeed remarkable. Even so, the ancients never went to toy with light and shadow; they only point out some route for you so people can see. This monk asked, What is the substance of prajna? Zhimen said, A clam holds the bright moon. Clams come from the Han River; within the clam there is a bright pearl. When the mid-autumn moon rises, the clam floats to the surface, opens its mouth and takes in moonlight; stirred by it, it produces a pearl—these are the Hepu pearls. If there is moon at mid-autumn, there are many pearls; if there is no moon, there are few. What is the function of prajna? Zhimen said, A rabbit carries a fetus. This meaning is also no different. The rabbit belongs to yin; when the mid-autumn moon is born, it opens its mouth and swallows its light, and then it becomes pregnant, giving birth from its mouth. Again, if there is moon there are many; if there is no moon there are few. In the ancients’ reply there is not all that much; they only borrow that meaning to answer the prajna light. Even so, their intent is not on words and phrases. It is only later people who make a living on words and phrases. Have you not seen Panshan say: the mind-moon, solitary and round, its light swallows all forms. Light does not illumine objects, and objects do not abide; when both light and objects are gone, what then is it? People today only stare their eyes and call it light, and then generate interpretations from feelings—driving a peg into emptiness. The ancients said: all of you, at the gateways of the six faculties, day and night emit great light, shining through mountains, rivers, and the great earth—not only the eye faculty emits light; nose, tongue, body, and mind also all emit light. When you reach here, you must simply fold up the six faculties so there is not the slightest thing. Clean nakedness, bare and plain—only then do you see where these words land. Xuedou versified it exactly like this.

text_en: you can see the ancients’ intent. The six faculties are clear and still—what is it? Just this single piece, empty-bright and congealed-still. No need to seek it in heaven, and no need to ask it from others. Naturally constant light appears before you; everywhere is a sheer cliff a thousand fathoms high. What is called feeling is precisely cut off— that is, the dust of feeling. Fayan’s verse on the perfected real nature says: when principle reaches the utmost, one forgets feeling and speech—how can it be explained evenly? At the end, the frosty night moon falls naturally into the stream before you. Fruit ripens and the monkeys grow heavy; the mountains are far and the road seems lost. Raise your head and the remaining glow is there—it was always dwelling in the west. Therefore it is said: mind is the root, dharmas are the dust—these two are like a stain upon a mirror. When dust and grime are exhausted, light first appears; when mind and dharmas are both forgotten, the nature is true. Also it says: in three bays of thatched hut I have always lived; one path of numinous light and ten thousand conditions are at ease. Do not take right and wrong to judge me; the meddling of this floating life is not connected. In this very verse too you see that single piece, empty and congealed, cutting off what is called feeling. Humans and devas from this see emptiness arise. Have you not seen how Subhuti sat in silent ease in a cave, and the devas rained flowers in praise? The venerable one said, In emptiness flowers rain and praise—who is it? The deva said, I am Brahma. The venerable one said, How do you praise? Brahma said, I esteem the venerable one for well expounding prajnaparamita. The venerable one said, I have never spoken a single word about prajna—how do you praise? Brahma said, The venerable one has no speaking; I therefore have no hearing. No speaking and no hearing are true prajna. And again the earth shook and flowers rained down. Look at how Subhuti well expounded prajna—without even speaking of substance and function. If you see it here, then you can see Zhimen saying, A clam holds the bright moon, a rabbit carries a fetus. Though the ancients’ intent is not in words and phrases, still the reply carries a deep, deep purport, which drew out Xuedou’s saying: the clam holds the dark rabbit’s deep, deep meaning. Coming to this, it has once made battle with the Chan folk. The Chan crowd under heaven makes a huge racket debating, yet not one has ever even dreamed of it. If you want to investigate together with Zhimen and Xuedou, you must set your own eyes to it first.

text_zh: 鹽官一日喚侍者。與我將犀牛扇子來。此事 雖不在言句上。且要驗人平生意氣作略。又 須得如此藉言而顯。於臘月三十日著得力。 作得主。萬境摐然。覩之不動。可謂無功之 功。無力之力。鹽官廼齊安禪師。古時以犀牛 角為扇。時鹽官豈不知犀牛扇子破。故問侍 者。侍者云。扇子破也。看他古人。十二時中常 在裏許撞著磕著。鹽官云。扇子既破。還我犀 牛兒來。且道他要犀牛兒作什麼。也只要驗 人知得落處也無。投子云。不辭將出。恐頭角 不全。雪竇云。我要不全底頭角。亦向句下便 投機。石霜云。若還和尚即無也。雪竇云。犀牛 兒猶在。資福畫一圓相。於中書一牛字。為他 承嗣仰山。平生愛以境致接人明此事。雪竇 云。適來為什麼不將出。又穿他鼻孔了也。保 福云。和尚年尊。別請人好。此語道得穩當。前 三則語却易見。此一句語有遠意。雪竇亦打。 破了也。山僧舊日在慶藏主處理會。道。和尚 年尊老耄。得頭忘尾。適來索扇子。如今索犀 牛兒。難為執侍。故云。別請人好。雪竇云。可 惜勞而無功。此皆是下語格式。古人見徹此 事。各各雖不同。道得出來。百發百中。須有出 身之路。句句不失血脈。如今人問著。只管作 道理計較。所以十二時中。要人咬嚼教滴水 滴凍。求箇證悟處。看他雪竇頌一串云。摐 七恭切撞也。
text_en: though it is not on words and phrases, still tests a person’s lifelong spirit and tactics. Also, it must be made manifest by relying on words like this. On the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month, you must gain real strength and be able to take charge. Though ten thousand conditions crash and clatter, you see them without moving—this is called the achievement of no-achievement, the strength of no-strength. Yanguan was Chan Master Qian of Qi’an. In ancient times they used rhinoceros horn as a fan. At that time, how could Yanguan not know the rhinoceros fan was broken? Therefore he asked the attendant. The attendant said, The fan is broken. Look at the ancients—through the twelve hours they are always right there, colliding and striking. Yanguan said, If the fan is broken, return my rhi noceros to me. Tell me, what does he want the rhinoceros for? He only wants to test whether a person knows the landing place or not. Touzi said, I do not refuse to bring it out, but I fear the head and horns are not whole. Xuedou said, I want head and horns that are not whole—also, right under the phrase he met the pivot. Shishuang said, If it is returned to the master, then there is none. Xuedou said, The rhinoceros is still here. Zifu drew a circular form and wrote within it the character ox—because he inherited Yangshan, and throughout his life loved using circumstances to meet people and make this matter clear. Xuedou said, Just now, why did you not bring it out?—again piercing his nostrils. Bao fu said, The master is advanced in years—better ask someone else. These words were spoken steadily. The previous three replies are easy to see; this one sentence has a far-reaching intent. Xuedou also shattered it. This mountain monk once, at Steward Qing’s place, worked it out, saying: The master is advanced in years and senile—getting the head and forgetting the tail. Just now he asked for the fan; now he asks for the rhi noceros. It is hard on those serving him, so he said, Better ask someone else. Xuedou said, What a pity—labor with no achievement. These are all patterns of giving a concluding phrase. The ancients, seeing through this matter, though each different, could speak it forth—one hundred shots, one hundred hits. There must be a way out the road of one’s very body. Sentence after sentence never loses the living lineage. Nowadays when people are asked, they only keep making doctrinal calculations. Thus, through the twelve hours of the day, they make people chew it over until drops of water freeze drop by drop, searching for some place of realization. Look at how Xuedou strung his verse together, saying: 。 Striking and colliding.
The rhinoceros fan has been used a long time; Meeting summer it is cool; meeting winter it is warm. Everyone fully has it—why do they not know? Who has never used it?

text_en: a rhinoceros fan; through the twelve hours of the day we wholly rely on its power. Why is it that when asked we always go on not knowing? The attendant, Touzi, and even Baofu as well—none of them knew either. Tell me, did Xuedou know or not? Haven’t you seen how Wuzhuo visited Manjushri, and while drinking tea, Manjushri raised a glass cup and said, In the south, is there still this or not? Wuzhuo said, No. Manjushri said, What do you ordinarily use to drink tea? Wuzhuo was silent. If you know where this case lands, then you know that the rhinoceros fan has boundless pure breeze, and you also see the rhinoceros horn rising rugged and sharp. Those four old fellows spoke like that, as if morning clouds and evening rain—once gone, hard to chase. Xuedou again said, If you want the pure breeze to return and the horn to be born again, I ask each Zen traveler to give a turning word. He asked, The fan is already broken—return my little rhinoceros to me. At the time a Zen traveler came forward and said, Everyone, go to the hall for practice. This monk seized the householder’s authority; what he said was deadly indeed, yet he only got it to eighty percent. If you want one hundred percent, then you must overturn the meditation bench. Now tell me, did this monk understand the little rhinoceros or not? If he didn’t understand, how could he say it like that? If he did understand, why didn’t Xuedou approve him? Why did he say, Casting a hook to fish for a great whale, he only caught a shrimp? Tell me, in the end, how is it? You all, if you have nothing to do, try picking it up and bringing it forth.

text_zh: 世尊未拈花已前。早有這箇消息。始從鹿野 苑。終至拔提河。幾曾用著金剛王寶劍。當 時眾中。若有衲僧氣息底漢。綽得去。免得他 末後拈花。一場狼藉。世尊良久間。被文殊一 拶。便下座。那時也有這箇消息。釋迦掩室。淨 名杜口。皆似此這箇。則已說了也。如肅宗問 忠國師。造無縫塔話。又如外道問佛。不問有 言。不問無言之語。看他向上人行履。幾曾入 鬼窟裏作活計。有者道。意在默然處。有者道。 在良久處。有言明無言底事。無言明有言底 事。永嘉道。默時說說時默。總恁麼會。三生 六十劫。也未夢見在。爾若便直下承當得去。 更不見有凡有聖。是法平等無有高下。日日 與三世諸佛。把手共行。後面看雪竇自然見 得頌出。
text_en: at the beginning to the Bhadrā River at the end, when did he ever need the vajra-king precious sword? At that time, if among the assembly there had been a fellow with the breath of a patchrobed monk, he would have snatched it away, sparing us the later holding up of the flower and the whole messy affair. When the World-Honored One sat silent for a long time, Manjushri pressed him with a shove, and he stepped down from the seat. At that moment too there was this message. Shakyamuni closing the room, Vimalakirti sealing his mouth—both are like this: it has already been spoken. It is like Emperor Suzong asking National Teacher Zhong about making a seamless stupa; and like an outsider asking the Buddha for a word that is not asked with words and not asked with silence. Look at how those above tread and conduct themselves—when did they ever enter a ghost cave to make a living? Some say the intent lies in silence; some say it lies in the long pause. With words they clarify what is beyond words; without words they clarify what is within words— and Yongjia said, Silent while speaking, speaking while silent. If you understand it all like that, for three lives and sixty kalpas you still won’t even dream of it. If you can straightaway take it up and accept it, you will no longer see any ordinary or any sage. This Dharma is equal, with no high or low. Day after day you walk hand in hand with all buddhas of the three times. Later, look at Xuedou and you will naturally see the verse emerge.

text_en: The Dharma King’s decrees are not like this. Those who just follow him are like hemp and millet—three heads and two faces. Clearly, how many can reach here? But the second and third blows you do not want at all. In the moment, how do you speak a single sentence? Perilous!

text_zh: 列聖叢中作者知。靈山八萬大眾。皆是列聖。 文殊普賢。乃至彌勒。主伴同會。須是巧中之 巧。奇中之奇。方知他落處。雪竇意謂。列聖叢 中。無一箇人知有。若有箇作家者。方知不恁 麼。何故文殊白槌云。諦觀法王法。法王法 如是。雪竇道。法王法令不如斯。何故如此。當 時會中。若有箇漢。頂門具眼。肘後有符。向世 尊未陞座已前。覻得破。更何必文殊白槌。涅 槃經云。仙陀婆一名四實。一者鹽。二者水。三 者器。四者馬。有一智臣。善會四義。王若欲灑 洗。要仙陀婆。臣即奉水。食索奉鹽。食訖奉 器飲漿。欲出奉馬。隨意應用無差。灼然須是 箇伶俐漢始得。只如僧問香嚴。如何是王索 仙陀婆。嚴云。過這邊來。僧過嚴云。鈍置殺 人。又問趙州。如何是王索仙陀婆。州下禪床。 曲躬叉手。當時若有箇仙陀婆。向世尊未陞 座已前透去。猶較些子。世尊更陞座。便下 去。已是不著便了也。那堪文殊更白槌。不妨 鈍置他世尊一上提唱。且作麼生是鈍置處。
text_en: Manjushri and Samantabhadra, up to Maitreya—host and companions gathered together. It must be skill within skill, marvel within marvel, to know where it lands. Xuedou’s intent is that among the array of sages not a single one knows it is there. If there is an adept, only then does he know it is not like that. Why did Manjushri strike the gavel and say, Contemplate well the Dharma of the Dharma King; the Dharma King’s Dharma is just so? Xuedou says, The Dharma King’s decrees are not like this. Why is it like this? At that time, if in the assembly there had been a fellow with eyes on the crown of his head and a talisman behind his elbow, before the World- Honored One even ascended the seat he would have seen through it—what need would there be for Manjushri to strike the gavel? The Nirvana Sutra says: Xiantuopo is one name with four realities: first, salt; second, water; third, a vessel; fourth, a horse. There was a wise minister who understood these four meanings well. If the king wished to sprinkle and wash and asked for xiantuopo, the minister would present water. If food was requested, he would present salt. After eating, he would present a vessel to drink broth. If the king wished to go out, he would present a horse. Responding according to intent without error—clearly it requires a sharp fellow. For example, a monk asked Xiangyan, What is it like when the king asks for xiantuopo? Xiangyan said, Come over here. The monk came over. Xiangyan said, You are so dull it kills people. He also asked Zhaozhou, What is it like when the king asks for xiantuopo? Zhaozhou stepped down from the meditation bench and bowed, hands folded. If at that time there had been a xiantuopo in the assembly, before the World-Honored One ascended the seat he would have passed through—still somewhat better. But the World-Honored One ascended the seat and immediately stepped down— that already misses the mark. How much more when Manjushri also strikes the gavel—it does not hinder, but it makes that one lifting-and-proclaiming of the World-Honored One dull. Now tell me, what is the place where it is made dull?

Yangshan instructed the assembly, All of you, each return the light and reflect it back; do not memorize my words. From beginningless kalpas you have turned your backs on the bright and thrown yourselves into darkness; delusive thoughts have deep roots and are hard to pull out all at once. Therefore I set up provisional means to take away your coarse knowing. It is like using yellow leaves to stop a child’s crying; like using sweet fruit to trade for bitter gourds. Like this. The ancients provisionally set up skillful means for people; once the crying stops, yellow leaves are not gold. The World-Honored One’s teaching throughout a lifetime was also just talk to stop the crying. This wild-fox goblin only wants to swap out their karmic consciousness. Within it there is also provisional and real, and also illumination and function. Only then do you see the snout of a patch-robed monk. If you understand it, it is like a tiger with wings; the Caoxi waves are like that as well. But if, from all directions, students suddenly just keep everyone dancing like this—always like this—countless ordinary people get sunk. What is there to save them?
